author: max2
claim: Changing symmetric PSD contractions, even with all pairwise cocoercivity and an exact GD step, do not ensure one legal smooth-convex function: an explicit two-dimensional three-point counterexample.
evidence: Status: refuted. Normalize L=1, x_*=g_*=0. Let x_0=(1,0), g_0=(1/2,1/2), h_0=1, x_1=(1/2,-1/2), g_1=(1/2,0). Then x_1=x_0-h_0 g_0. For every pair i,j in {*,0,1}, <g_i-g_j,x_i-x_j>=||g_i-g_j||^2 (values for (*,0),(*,1),(0,1) are 1/2,1/4,1/4). The gradients are radial PSD-contraction images: g_0=P_0 x_0 with P_0=(1/2)[[1,1],[1,1]], and g_1=P_1 x_1 with P_1=diag(1,0); both are orthogonal projections. Nevertheless no convex differentiable 1-smooth f can interpolate these gradients and have 0 as minimizer. Necessity of smooth-convex interpolation gives f_i-f_j >= <g_j,x_i-x_j>+(1/2)||g_i-g_j||^2. Taking both directions against * forces f_0-f_*=1/4 and f_1-f_*=1/8. Taking (i,j)=(0,1) forces f_0-f_1 >= (1/2,0) dot (1/2,1/2)+1/8=3/8, whereas the forced difference is 1/8. Equivalently the cycle *->1->0->* has positive total lower-increment weight 1/8+3/8-1/4=1/4. Thus all pairwise two-cycle tests omit a decisive three-cycle. Source for the necessary interpolation inequality: Taylor, Hendrickx, Glineur, Smooth Strongly Convex Interpolation and Exact Worst-case Performance of First-order Methods, arXiv:1502.05666, Theorem 4 / Corollary 1; downloaded paper and read proof. This is a mechanism counterexample, not a verified fact or a resolution of (P).

author: max3
claim: C1 refuted: arbitrarily long recent chronology, even together with the initial jet and every sampled point and gradient, need not determine feasible future objective values. A one-dimensional fixed-schedule example has a factor-16 difference after forgetting one old function value.
evidence: Normalize L=1 and x_*=0, f_*=0. Define F by F(x)=x^2/2 for x<=0, 0 for 0<=x<=1, (x-1)^2/2 for 1<=x<=3, and 2x-4 for x>=3. Define G(x)=integral_0^x q(t)dt, where q(t)=t for t<=1/2; q(t)=1/2 for 1/2<=t<=11/6; q(t)=t-4/3 for 11/6<=t<=10/3; q(t)=2 for t>=10/3. Both derivatives are continuous, nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz; 0 is a minimizer with value 0. At x=4 both jets are (value,gradient)=(4,2). At x=3/2 both gradients are 1/2, but F=1/8 and G=5/8. Both functions agree on the entire negative half-line. For arbitrary integer m>=1, take h=(5/4,5,1/2 repeated m times,1+(5/4)2^m). Both functions, starting at x0=4, generate exactly the same sampled points and gradients through the cut: x1=3/2; x_{2+j}=-2^{-j}, 0<=j<=m. The final step sends the common cut x=-2^{-m} to y=5/4. All steps are positive, finite and predetermined. Any convex 1-smooth function interpolating the full F-prefix obeys f(y)<=1/32: on [5/4,3/2], f'(t)>=1/2-(3/2-t)=t-1, hence f(y)<=1/8-integral_{5/4}^{3/2}(t-1)dt=1/32; F attains equality. Any function interpolating the full G-prefix has f(y)=1/2: on [0,3/2], convexity and smoothness imply f'(t)<=min(t,1/2); the integral of this upper envelope equals 5/8=f(3/2), so continuity forces equality everywhere, giving f(5/4)=1/2. Thus conditional terminal maxima differ by 16 despite the same initial jet, minimizer, radius, entire schedule, all points and gradients, and any prescribed fixed-length recent history (choose m large). In W normalization the two conditional values are 1/256 and 1/16 because ||x0||^2=16. The only differing sampled datum is the forgotten old value at x1=3/2. This refutes exact gluing or conditional-state kernels that discard that datum without an equivalent encoding. It does NOT refute all finite-dimensional sufficient statistics, determine the unrestricted worst case of this schedule, or resolve (P). Explicit self-contained construction, not verifier-accepted yet.

author: max2
claim: The full smooth-convex worst-case W cannot be a function of the terminal scalar schedule polynomial: for every real H>2, W_2(H,1)=(H-1)^2/3 > W_2(1,H), although both terminal polynomials are (1-z)(1-Hz).
evidence: Complete self-contained proof: research/max2_order_sensitivity.md. Normalize L=1, x_*=0, f_*=0, ||x_0||=1. The smooth-convex inequality I follows directly by applying the descent lemma to f-<grad f(v),.>, whose minimum is at v; thus no unverified external lemma is used. For one unit GD step y=x-u, u=grad f(x), v=grad f(y), I gives f(y)<=<u,x>-||u||^2-||v||^2/2 and f(y)<=<v,x>-<v,u>-||v||^2/2. Averaging, with w=(u+v)/2, yields f(y)<=<w,x>-(3/2)||w||^2-(1/8)||u-v||^2<=||x||^2/6. Combining the first bound with f(y)>=||v||^2/2 also yields ||v||^2<=||x||^2/4. Hence for H>=2 descent from the first unit step gives W_2(1,H)<=1/3+(H^2-2H)/4. Conversely a first H-step satisfies ||x_0-Hg_0||^2<=1+H(H-2)||g_0||^2<=(H-1)^2 by cocoercivity and ||g_0||<=1. The subsequent unit-step bound gives W_2(H,1)<=(H-1)^2/3. Equality is attained by delta=(H-1)/3 and the globally convex differentiable 1-smooth asymmetric Huber function f(x)=x^2/2 for x>=-delta and f(x)=-delta x-delta^2/2 for x<=-delta. Its derivative max(x,-delta) is nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz; minimizer is 0. From x_0=1 the iterates are x_1=-3delta,x_2=-2delta, giving 2f(x_2)=3delta^2=(H-1)^2/3. The gap between this exact value and the opposite order's upper bound is H(H-2)/12>0. For H=3 this reads W_2(3,1)=4/3>13/12>=W_2(1,3). Status: explicit refutation of an order-blind exact characterization, not a refutation of (P) or of every order-blind lower bound; not submitted under selective-verification policy.

glossary.H: An arbitrary real long step greater than 2 in the two-step permutation example.
glossary.delta: The asymmetric Huber threshold (H-1)/3 in this example.

evidence: Set x_star=0, x_0=(1,0), x_1=(-1,0), x_2=(2,0), g_0=(1,0), g_1=(-1,0), g_2=(1/2,sqrt(3)/2). Exact GD holds for h=(2,3). Norms of all gradients are1 and <x_i,g_i>=1. author: max
claim: Random full-curvature symmetric Huber thresholds cannot prove the target lower bound: descending binary steps give the exact restricted-family worst case 1/(2^{n+1}-1), uniformly over all threshold distributions, rotations, and direct sums.
evidence:
UNVERIFIED COMPLETE FAMILY CALCULATION. Normalize L=1 and initial distance1. For tau>0 define H_tau(x)=x^2/2 for |x|<=tau and tau|x|-tau^2/2 otherwise, minimized at0. Its derivative clips x to [-tau,tau], hence is nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz, so the function is a legal smooth convex instance. It is even, so x_0=1 suffices for both normalized initial signs.

For a>=0 define M_a(z)=z-a clip(z,-1,1). Let D_n be the composition of these maps in chronological order 2^{n-1},2^{n-2},...,1, and put S_n=2^n-1. Claim D_n(z)=sign(z)(|z|-S_n)_+ for every real z. For n=1, M_1(z) has exactly this form. Suppose the identity holds at n-1 and set A=2^{n-1}, so S_{n-1}=A-1. The maps are odd, so take z>=0. If 0<=z<=1, M_A(z)=(1-A)z lies in[-(A-1),0]. If 1<=z<=2A-1, M_A(z)=z-A lies in[-(A-1),A-1]. The induction hypothesis sends both ranges to0. If z>2A-1, then M_A(z)=z-A>A-1, so D_{n-1}(M_A(z))=z-A-(A-1)=z-S_n. Oddness treats z<0. This proves the exact identity.

For the GD schedule d^(n)=(2^{n-1},...,1), rescale z=x/tau. The identity gives x_n=(1-tau S_n)_+. Write S=S_n. If tau>=1/S then x_n=0. For 0<tau<=1/(S+1), the endpoint is in the affine Huber region and
2H_tau(x_n)=2tau-(2S+1)tau^2<=1/(2S+1),
with equality at tau=1/(2S+1). For 1/(S+1)<=tau<=1/S, the endpoint lies in the quadratic region and
2H_tau(x_n)=(1-S tau)^2<=1/(S+1)^2<=1/(2S+1).
Consequently
sup_{tau>0} 2H_tau(x_n)=1/(2^{n+1}-1).
This holds for every n>=1. Thus for every law on tau (even one selected after seeing the entire binary schedule), its expected normalized error is at most1/(2^{n+1}-1). No minimax interchange is used: the deterministic pointwise upper bound is integrated.

Translations and orthogonal embeddings preserve the scalar trajectory and the normalization. Radial Hubers H_tau(||x-x_star||) have collinear GD trajectories, so the same identity holds for any starting displacement; after scaling its length to1 the parameter is tau/||x0-x_star||. A finite direct sum of these full-curvature scalar/radial components has a normalized error equal to the initial-squared-distance weighted average of component normalized errors. Hence it has the same cap; any distribution over these direct sums does too.

This is a limitation of full-curvature symmetric Huber thresholds, embeddings, and separable direct sums. It does not include arbitrary lower core curvatures, asymmetric tails, sums of overlapping ridge Hubers, or general convex functions. The schedule d^(n) is not claimed to have small unrestricted W_n; other legal functions can make it unstable. In particular this is not a negative answer to P. For a benchmark comparison one may use the already verified fact b98bb807d514e80d, which proves B_n=1/U_n^ZJ<=1+4n^{log_2 3}; the restricted-family ratio is consequently at most (1+4n^{log_2 3})/(2^{n+1}-1), tending to0.

author: max3
claim: The verified C6 functional alone cannot match the ZJ profile: for the explicit half-linear schedules h_t=(t+1)/2, every feasible chain has at most one checkpoint, so F_ray_n=K_n=O(n^-2) and F_ray_n/U_n^ZJ tends to0.
evidence:
# Quantitative tests of the verified alternating-ray functional

Status: new analytic candidate findings based on verified fact
1fca3e5dd555cb4a; not independently verifier-accepted. Worker: max3.

## A precise obstruction to the ray functional alone

For every n>=1 define h_t=(t+1)/2 for 0<=t<n. Then the alternating-ray
functional F_ray_n of fact 1fca3e5dd555cb4a equals the single-cut functional
K_n: no selected chain with two or more checkpoints is feasible.
For n>=2,

\[
F_{\rm ray,n}(h)=K_n(h)\leq16/n^2,
\qquad
\frac{F_{\rm ray,n}(h)}{U_n^{ZJ}}
\leq16(1+4n^{\log_2 3})/n^2\longrightarrow0.
\]

This refutes the exact uniform-profile comparison for F_ray_n alone. It does
not refute the same comparison after adding quadratic witnesses, and it is
not a negative solution of the minimax problem.

### General first-return obstruction

For any selected first two checkpoints at original indices i<j, let
P=sum_{t<i}h_t and M=sum_{i<t<j}h_t. The first two magnitudes in the verified
recurrence, if the second is positive, are

\[
m_0=1/(1+P),\quad
m_1=(h_i-1)/[(1+P)(1+M)],\quad O_1=P/(1+P).
\]

The available distance after the second checkpoint, before dividing by the
next ordinary-block mass, is therefore

\[
(h_j-1)m_1-O_1
=\frac{(h_i-1)(h_j-1)/(1+M)-P}{1+P}.
\tag{1}
\]

Every feasible chain with at least two checkpoints must have both h_i>1
and h_j>1. If the second checkpoint is nonterminal, otherwise m_1 or m_2
would be nonpositive. If it is terminal, its feasible final magnitude must
be at least m_0>0, forcing the same strict positivity.

If

\[
(h_i-1)(h_j-1)\leq P(1+M),
\tag{2}
\]

then (1) is nonpositive. This contradicts either the required positive m_2
when more checkpoints follow, or the terminal lower bound
z_term>=(1+s_2)m_0>0 when these are the only two checkpoints.
Consequently, if (2) holds for every eligible pair i<j, all feasible chains
have at most one checkpoint.

### The half-linear schedule satisfies every pair inequality

For h_t=(t+1)/2, an eligible i has i>=2. Write j=i+1+d with integer d>=0.
Then P=i(i+1)/4, M>=d(i+2)/2, and

\[
4(h_i-1)(h_j-1)=(i-1)(i+d).
\]

On the other hand

\[
4P(1+M)\geq i(i+1)[1+d(i+2)/2].
\]

At d=0, the right side minus the left is2i>0. Its coefficient of d is
i(i+1)(i+2)/2-(i-1)>0 for i>=2. Thus (2) holds strictly for all eligible
pairs, proving F_ray_n=K_n.

### Uniform bound on K_n for this family

The total step sum is n(n+1)/4, so the global Huber term is at most2/n^2.
For a cut j write P_j=j(j+1)/4 and
T_j=[n(n+1)-(j+1)(j+2)]/4. If j>=n/2, then
(h_j-1)_+<=j/2 and P_j>=j^2/4, so the cut term is at most4/j^2<=16/n^2.
If j<n/2, the inequalities
j+1<=(n+1)/2 and j+2<=(n+3)/2 give

\[
1+2T_j\geq(3n^2+5)/8\geq n^2/4.
\]

Also (h_j-1)_+<=1+P_j. Thus this cut term is at most4/n^2. Combining
the cases proves the stated16/n^2 estimate. Verified fact b98bb807d514e80d
supplies the exact-recursion estimate 1/U_n^ZJ<=1+4n^(log_2 3), which gives
the vanishing comparison without importing an asymptotic numerical constant.

## What the obstruction says about the mechanism

The alternating-ray construction demands that the second crossing can return
beyond the already visited positive-ray record. Inequality (2) prevents even
that first return, regardless of any later selected checkpoints. A genuine
GD trajectory can first return inside its old range and later expand. The
verified construction does not describe that behavior. Quadratic witnesses
are one way to capture it; arbitrary inner returns would require a new legal
extension of the state, rather than deleting the ray-feasibility conditions.

No bound on the full W_n of the half-linear schedules is claimed. Their
quadratic behavior may be large, so this construction is not evidence against
the combined functional max(F_ray_n,Q_n), where Q_n is the exact quadratic
worst-case polynomial functional.

## A second exact necessary condition for any adjacent checkpoint pair

For consecutive selected checkpoints b_i,b_{i+1}, the verified recurrence and
O_{i+1}=O_i+s_i m_i imply that a feasible next same-ray magnitude at least
m_i requires

\[
(b_i-1)(b_{i+1}-1)\geq
(1+s_{i+1})(1+s_i+s_{i+2})
 +\frac{b_{i+1}+s_{i+1}}{m_i}O_i.
\tag{3}
\]

For a nonterminal next visit this follows by multiplying its recurrence by
1+s_{i+1}, substituting m_{i+1}, and using m_{i+2}>=m_i. For a terminal
next visit, replace m_{i+2} by its allowed upper endpoint z_term/(1+s_{i+2});
the same feasibility inequality follows. Every quantity retained on the right
is nonnegative. Equation (3) is a useful local obstruction, not a sufficient
condition for a complete legal chain and not a profile theorem.

evidence:
# Exact hostile test for the reset-doubling family

Status: self-contained unverified counterexample package. No further fact submission under the current allocation. It excludes every seed depth k >= 6 in the stated family, uniformly over subsequent doublings. It does not exclude the small remaining seed depths or all endpoint-potential constructions.

Use the notation of research/max4_reset_seed_boundary_certificate.md. Put lambda=1+sqrt(2), sigma=1/lambda, A=lambda^k, B=beta_k-1, R=A+B+2. Then A=2B^2+B, and the actual seed is [pi^(k),B+1,1]. Let H_j=q^(k,j), with shifted sum R_j=lambda^j R, and H_(j+1)=[H_j,1+sigma R_j,H_j]. Every H_j ends with the same two steps (B+1,1). Its length satisfies len(H_j)+1=2^j(2^k+2).

For k>=6 we have A>=lambda^6=99+70sqrt(2)>197>171, hence B>9. In particular a=B/2>lambda. Define a one-dimensional smooth convex function by
f(x)=x^2/2 for -a<=x<=1;
f(x)=x-1/2 for x>=1;
f(x)=-a x-a^2/2 for x<=-a.
Its derivative clip(x,-a,1) is continuous, monotone, and 1-Lipschitz, and f(0)=0=min f.

Fix j>=0 and start H_(j+1) at x_0=R_j-B-2>0. The prefix of its first H_j before the last two steps has total sum R_j-B-3. All steps are nonnegative, so every sampled point of that prefix stays in the right affine region, and the prefix ends exactly at x=1. The (B+1)-step then reaches -B=-2a. The unit step reaches -a, with terminal gradient -a.

The following central step 1+sigma R_j sends -a to y=sigma R_j a. Since sigma a>1, we have y>R_j. The second H_j has total sum R_j-1. Every one of its iterates therefore stays in the right affine region with gradient1, and its final point is
x_N=R_j(sigma a-1)+1>1.
Consequently the exact normalized objective of this legal instance is

W_N(H_(j+1)) >= [R_j(B/lambda-2)+1]/(R_j-B-2)^2,
N+1=2^(j+1)(2^k+2).

This is a genuine lower bound for the proposed schedules; it is not an upper bound or a negative answer to (P).

Comparison with the exact benchmark, without decimal replacements:
Let P_m=S_circle(m)+1. The original recursion gives P_(2m+1)>=lambda P_m and P_(m+1)>=P_m. Thus P_(2^r-1)>=lambda^r. Since the dominant recurrence permits the split (n-1,0), B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1>=2P_(n-1)-1. Hence B_n>=2lambda^r-1 whenever n>=2^r. Here N>=2^(k+j+1), so B_N>=2lambda^(k+j+1)-1.

The displayed lower bound is strictly larger than (B/lambda-2)/R_j. Multiplication by B_N yields
W_N(H_(j+1))/U_N^ZJ > (A/R)(2B-4lambda) - (B/lambda-2)/(lambda^j R).
For B>9, A=2B^2+B>9(B+2), so A/R>9/10. Also lambda<5/2, hence 2B-4lambda>8. Finally,
(B/lambda-2)/(lambda^j R)<B/A=1/(2B+1)<1/19.
Therefore the ratio is greater than 36/5-1/19=679/95>7 for every k>=6 and j>=0.

The sharper asymptotic lower constant for each fixed seed depth is
liminf_(j->infinity) W_(len H_(j+1))(H_(j+1))/U_(len H_(j+1))^ZJ >= (A/R)(2B-4lambda).
It tends to infinity as k tends to infinity. Large reset seeds cannot be rescued by increasing the number of balanced doublings in this family.

Scope and next obligation:
This exact test does not close k<=5. In particular the previously interesting k=4 seed has B/2<lambda, so the central jump in this witness lands inside the region the second block can traverse. No upper certificate or successful recursion is known for that remaining case. A later candidate must either establish a concrete boundary-variable inequality for it or change the block rule; claiming that a unit step controls terminal gradients is invalid.

evidence:
# A recursive family defeats the combined ray, quadratic, and single-cap channels

Status: complete symbolic candidate, not verifier-accepted. Worker: max3.
No extra verifier allocation is assumed. The result bounds specified lower-bound
functionals from above. It does not bound the true smooth-convex worst case from
above and does not decide the project's minimax target.

## Statement and definitions

Put c=13/5 and a=c^(-17). Define the ordered lists H_0=() and

    H_m=(H_(m-1), a c^(m-1), H_(m-1)),   m>=1.

checkpoints follow, the next magnitude must be positive; if these are the

j lies strictly after i, since j-i is a positive multiple of 2^v; hence

then M>=s_v and P>=s_u, with the same conclusion. Otherwise i lies inside

copies of H_u on each side of i give

    P_loc>=s_u, M>=s_u, P_loc+M=s_v-b_u, P>=P_loc.

their product is at least s_u(s_v-b_u-s_u). This follows by factoring

    D_(u+1)=s_u^2-c b_u^2>=0.

radius domain here only makes this upper bound more permissive.

asymptotic decimal constant. Put C_n=S_circle(n)+1. Their shifted joins are

    Omega(A,D)=(A+D+sqrt((A+D)^2+4AD))/2,
    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

The first joins C_k,C_(n-k-1), and the second joins C_k,B_(n-k-1).
Both are increasing in their nonnegative arguments.

For 0<=t<=1,

    t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1.

      <=[729 c^13/a] c^(-m)[1+4(2^m-1)^(4/3)] ->0,

## Structural consequence and next mechanism

This family has recursive large steps separated by substantial symmetric
blocks. Those blocks prevent the first outward return in the ray construction
and damp every quadratic scale; the prefix damping also defeats a lone terminal
cap. A next witness must permit nonlinear changes followed by additional
returns and further changes, or use a genuinely different multidimensional
interaction. This result does not establish that these schedules perform well
on that richer class. No conclusion about W_(N_m)(H_m) from above is made.

For r<=4 this is at most c^12/(a c^u). For r>=5, 2^(r-1)>=3r and
c<e make its extra factor at most1. This proves the bound for every u.

Now consider any feasible single-cap checkpoint j in H_m. Maximizing over
all real r, rather than only its legal interval, gives the rigorous upper bound

    2 lambda r A-lambda(1+2lambda T)r^2
                           <=lambda A^2/(1+2lambda T).

Let u=m-1, and consider the central step b_u. If j precedes it, the tail
contains b_u, so T>=b_u, while |A|<=27. The cap payoff is at most
729/(2b_u). If j is central or follows it, the prefix contains the complete
block (H_u,b_u), followed by a prefix of H_u. Hence |A|<=27|R_u| and
the cap payoff is at most lambda A^2<=729 c^12/(a c^u).
Both cases are bounded by 729 c^13/(a c^m). All signed-record and radius
feasibility constraints were retained in defining the family; enlarging the
radius domain here only makes this upper bound more permissive.

## 6. A sufficient bound on the exact benchmark recurrence

This part uses the exact phi/psi recursions in fact b98bb807d514e80d, not an
asymptotic decimal constant. Put C_n=S_circle(n)+1. Their shifted joins are

    Omega(A,D)=(A+D+sqrt((A+D)^2+4AD))/2,
    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

The first joins C_k,C_(n-k-1), and the second joins C_k,B_(n-k-1).
Both are increasing in their nonnegative arguments.

For 0<=t<=1,

    t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1.

To prove this, put x=t^(1/3), y=(1-t)^(1/3). Then x^3+y^3=1 and

    1-x^4-y^4-x^4y^4
      =x^3y^3[1/(1+x+x^2)+1/(1+y+y^2)-xy]>=0.

Each reciprocal is at least1/3, and xy<=2^(-2/3)<2/3; the latter strict
inequality follows by cubing, since1/4<8/27. Endpoints cause no division
problem. Since Omega is the positive root of X^2-(A+D)X-AD=0, this proves

    Omega(A,D)<=(A^(3/4)+D^(3/4))^(4/3).

Induction in the exact primitive recursion now gives C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3).
Also sqrt(D^2+8AD)<=D+4A, hence G(A,D)<=D+4A. Induction in the exact
dominant recursion gives

    B_n<=1+4[(n-k-1)^(4/3)+(k+1)^(4/3)]<=1+4n^(4/3)

for every split, so it holds for the maximum. The base values are C_0=B_0=1.

Combining Sections2--5 with this recurrence bound gives

    max(F_ray,Q,F_cap)(H_m)/U_(N_m)^ZJ
      <=[729 c^13/a] c^(-m)[1+4(2^m-1)^(4/3)] ->0,

because 2^(4/3)<c. This completes the candidate restricted-channel result.

## Structural consequence and next mechanism

This family has recursive large steps separated by substantial symmetric
blocks. Those blocks prevent the first outward return in the ray construction
and damp every quadratic scale; the prefix damping also defeats a lone terminal
cap. A next witness must permit nonlinear changes followed by additional
returns and further changes, or use a genuinely different multidimensional
interaction. This result does not establish that these schedules perform well
on that richer class. No conclusion about W_(N_m)(H_m) from above is made.

Literature retrieval: a Matlas search for the displayed recursive-product
claim returned unrelated results, none used. Every new estimate above is
proved in the text. Correctness status remains unverified.

## 7. The same family controls every two-curvature homogeneous objective

This extension is part of the same unverified candidate proof. It does not
assume correctness of a separate unverified finding. For u,v in (0,1], define

    f_(u,v)(x)=u x^2/2 for x>=0, and v x^2/2 for x<=0.

Its derivative is continuous, monotone, and 1-Lipschitz, including across zero;
zero is a minimizer. Write F_two_n(h) for the supremum of normalized terminal
error on this family with either initial point +1 or -1. The claim is

    F_two_(N_m)(H_m)<=c/(a c^m),   m>=18.

Scaling or reflecting the initial point adds no larger case, by positive
homogeneity and by allowing both initial signs. Random mixtures and separable
direct sums of such objectives cannot exceed their supremum, since their
normalized errors are convex combinations of component errors.

It suffices first to consider u<=v, with neither reciprocal equal to a step
level. The reverse order follows by reflecting the objective. The exceptional
parameter pairs follow by continuity: each finite GD update and final objective
is continuous in (u,v), even at a sign change or zero iterate. All bounds are
uniform in the parameters. The cases with a zero curvature follow by the same
limit if they are included in the definition.

Let I be the first integer level with b_I v>1, and J the first with b_J u>1.
Then 18<=I<=J. A whole block H_l maps each starting sign to a deterministic
ending sign and nonnegative magnitude. Represent these two magnitudes by the
columns of a two-state map. Before level I, both signs are preserved, and the
whole-block magnitudes are P_l(u),P_l(v), both positive. If m<=I, the two
trajectories are ordinary quadratics, already bounded by Section4.

### 7a. Different first-crossing levels: I<J

The step b_I crosses from the negative side to the positive side but leaves
the positive side positive. Thus H_(I+1) sends both initial signs to the
positive side. Its amplitudes, from positive and negative starts respectively,
are

    A_(I+1)=(1-b_I u)P_I(u)^2,
    D_(I+1)=(b_I v-1)P_I(u)P_I(v).

Every larger whole block also ends positive from both starting signs, because
the last copy of the preceding block has this property. Put

    r_0=D_(I+1)/A_(I+1)>0.

The ratio D_l/A_l stays equal to r_0. Indeed composition with the central
step yields

    (A_(l+1),D_(l+1))=(1-b_l u)(A_l^2,A_l D_l),  l<J,
    (A_(l+1),D_(l+1))=(b_l u-1)(A_l D_l,D_l^2),  l>=J.

In particular, for I+1<=l<=J,

    A_l=P_l(u),
    D_l=(b_I v-1)P_I(v) P_l(u)/[(1-b_I u)P_I(u)].

All factors of P_l(u) in this range are positive. Dividing by
(1-b_I u)P_I(u) removes a submultiset of its factors with total step mass
b_I+s_I. Since 1-t<=exp(-t), it follows that

    A_l<=exp(-u s_l),
    D_l<=exp(-u s_l) exp(u(s_I+b_I)-v s_I+log(b_I v-1)).

Set S=s_I/b_I>=eta>1, t_u=b_I u<1 and t_v=b_I v>1. The exponent in
the latter extra factor is at most

    (S+1)-S t_v+log(t_v-1)
       =1-S(t_v-1)+log(t_v-1)<=-log S<=0.

Here the maximum of log w-Sw over w>0 is -1-log S, found by differentiating.
Consequently both whole-block amplitudes obey exp(-u s_l) up to l=J.
Their common terminal side has curvature u, so for I< m<=J the error is

    <=u exp(-2u s_m)<=1/(2e s_m)<=1/(a c^m),

using s_m>=eta a c^m.

For l>=J, put E_l=max(A_l,D_l). The exact recurrence gives

    E_(l+1)<=E_l^2(b_l u-1),    E_J<=exp(-u s_J).

Let t=b_J u in (1,c) and m=J+r with r>=1. Expanding this scalar recursion,

    log E_m / 2^(r-1)
      <=-2u s_J+sum_(j=0)^(r-1)2^(-j)log(c^j t-1)
      <=-2eta t+2log c+2log t
      <=-2eta+2<-1.

The series bound uses log(c^j t-1)<=j log c+log t and sums the nonnegative
upper bounds to infinity. The last inequality uses log c<1 and the fact that
-2eta t+2log t decreases on t>=1 because eta>1. Thus

    u E_m^2<=u exp(-2^r)
       <=[c/(a c^m)] c^r exp(-2^r)<=c/(a c^m),

since u<c/(a c^J), log c<1, and r<=2^r. This covers I<J completely.

### 7b. Equal first-crossing levels: I=J

At level I both signs cross, so H_(I+1) interchanges the two starting signs.
Every larger block also interchanges them: an interchange, the central
interchange, and another interchange compose to an interchange. Let A_l be
the amplitude from a positive start and D_l the amplitude from a negative
start. Then

    A_(I+1)=(b_I u-1)P_I(u)P_I(v),
    D_(I+1)=(b_I v-1)P_I(u)P_I(v),
    A_(l+1)=A_l^2(b_l v-1),
    D_(l+1)=D_l^2(b_l u-1),     l>=I+1.

Put S=s_I/b_I>=eta, t_u=b_I u>1, t_v=b_I v>1. Both t_u,t_v are less
than c. All earlier factors are positive, so P_I(w)<=exp(-w s_I).
For m=I+r, r>=1, the exact recursion therefore implies

    log A_m / 2^(r-1)
      <=log(t_u-1)-S(t_u+t_v)
                   +sum_(j=1)^(r-1)2^(-j)log(c^j t_v-1)
      <=[-S t_u+log(t_u-1)]+[-S t_v+log t_v]+2log c.

For any t>1, -St+log(t-1)<=-S-1-log S. Also -St+log t<=-S, because
S>1. The displayed bound is consequently

    <=-2S-1-log S+2log c<=-2eta+1=-9/4<-2.

The identical estimate for D_m follows after interchanging u,v. Thus both
amplitudes are at most exp(-2^r). Their terminal curvatures are at most
v<c/(a c^I), giving normalized error at most

    [c/(a c^m)] c^r exp(-2^(r+1))<=c/(a c^m).

This proves the asserted two-curvature bound. In conjunction with Sections1--6,
the maximum of F_ray, Q, F_cap, and F_two still has ratio tending to zero
relative to the exact ZJ benchmark along N_m=2^m-1.

### Scope of the stronger exclusion

The proof controls a continuous two-parameter nonlinear family, with repeated
sign changes and inner returns. It does not control a derivative whose slope
changes more than once along either ray, nor a genuinely coupled multidimensional
function. Such changes remain concrete mechanisms to investigate. Six fixed
curvature pairs were checked using only forty compositions of a two-state map
(about0.1 seconds, no long trajectory stored); those checks suggested the proof
but are not used in it. No numerical sweep or asymptotic computation is evidence
for the claimed bound.

The reversed schedule (6/5,2,17/10), with the same sum and quadratic multiplier, is a distinct unresolved candidate. The displayed flat-interval test does not refute it. evidence:
# A recursive family defeats the combined ray, quadratic, and single-cap channels

Status: complete symbolic candidate, not verifier-accepted. Worker: max3.
No extra verifier allocation is assumed. The result bounds specified lower-bound
functionals from above. It does not bound the true smooth-convex worst case from
above and does not decide the project's minimax target.

## Statement and definitions

Put c=13/5 and a=c^(-17). Define the ordered lists H_0=() and

    H_m=(H_(m-1), a c^(m-1), H_(m-1)),   m>=1.

Their lengths are N_m=2^m-1. Write b_u=a c^u for the step at level u and
s_m=sum H_m. Directly from the recursion,

    s_m=a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2),    s_(m+1)=2s_m+b_m.

F_ray is precisely the verified functional of fact 1fca3e5dd555cb4a, including
all its sign, remote-offset, old-slope, and retained-area constraints. K is the
functional of fact b98bb807d514e80d. Define the full quadratic functional by

    Q_n(h)=max_{0<=lambda<=1} lambda product_(t<n)(1-lambda h_t)^2.

For clarity, define also the algebraic single-cap functional F_cap_n. For each
lambda in (0,1], sigma in {-1,1}, and checkpoint j<n, put

    p_t=product_(v<t)(1-lambda h_v),
    R=max(0,sigma p_t:0<=t<=j), A=sigma p_(j+1), T=sum_(v>j)h_v.

Take the supremum of

    2 lambda r A - lambda(1+2 lambda T)r^2

over A>0 and radii R<=r<=A/(1+lambda T), and include zero. This is exactly
the candidate quadratic-core/terminal-cap family, but its upper bounds below
use only this displayed definition, not any unverified prior lemma. It is a
legal lower-bound family directly: integrate the derivative of lambda x^2/2
until sigma x=r and continue with constant derivative sigma lambda r beyond
that point. The record constraint preserves the quadratic prefix, while
A-lambda rT>=r preserves the affine suffix. The derivative is continuous,
nondecreasing, and lambda-Lipschitz; the minimum is zero at zero and x_0=1.

For every m>=18 the candidate conclusions are

    F_ray_(N_m)(H_m)=K_(N_m)(H_m)<=1/(1+s_(m-1))
                                      <=8/(5a c^m),
    Q_(N_m)(H_m)<=1/(a c^m),
    F_cap_(N_m)(H_m)<=729 c^13/(a c^m).

In addition the exact benchmark recursions satisfy

    S_circle(n)+1<=(n+1)^(4/3),
    B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1<=1+4n^(4/3).

Consequently, since c^3=2197/125>16,

    max(F_ray_(N_m), Q_(N_m), F_cap_(N_m))(H_m) / U_(N_m)^ZJ -> 0.

Thus even adding the one-terminal-cap extension to the verified ray functional
and all convex quadratic witnesses cannot give the desired uniform comparison.
The comparison fails along an explicit subsequence of horizons, which suffices
to refute a proposed comparison uniform over all horizons and all schedules.

## 1. Elementary scale estimates

Let d=2/c=10/13. Since d^3<1/2 and d^2<4/5,
d^17=d^15 d^2<1/40. Therefore for u>=17,

    s_u/b_u=(1-d^u)/(c-2)>=(39/40)/(3/5)=13/8.

Write eta=13/8. Then eta>1, eta^2=169/64>13/5=c.
Every step b_u>1 has u>=18, so this estimate applies to every eligible
checkpoint. At ineligible levels b_u<=1, the inequality s_u>=b_u-1 also
holds. Thus s_u>=b_u-1 for every level u, and s_u>=eta b_u whenever u>=17.

## 2. Every feasible ray chain has at most one checkpoint

The j-th step of H_m, indexed here by 1<=j<2^m, is b_u where u is the
largest integer for which 2^u divides j. Each such occurrence has an exact
copy of H_u immediately before it and an exact copy immediately after it.

Consider proposed first two checkpoints at indices i<j, with step levels
u and v. Both steps must exceed one for a feasible chain: otherwise the
verified first crossing or second return has nonpositive distance budget.
Let P be the sum before i, and M the sum strictly between i and j.
The verified recurrence gives the distance budget after the second crossing as

    [(b_u-1)(b_v-1)/(1+M)-P]/(1+P).

Any chain of at least two checkpoints needs this budget positive. If more
checkpoints follow, the next magnitude must be positive; if these are the
only two, the terminal old-slope constraint is at least m_0>0. It therefore
suffices to show P M >= b_u b_v, which is a stronger obstruction.

If u>=v, the copy of H_u before i yields P>=s_u. The copy of H_v before
j lies strictly after i, since j-i is a positive multiple of 2^v; hence
M>=s_v. Thus P M>=s_u s_v>=b_u b_v.

Suppose u<v. If i lies before the copy of H_v immediately preceding j,
then M>=s_v and P>=s_u, with the same conclusion. Otherwise i lies inside
that copy. Let P_loc be the sum in that copy strictly before i. The local
copies of H_u on each side of i give

    P_loc>=s_u, M>=s_u, P_loc+M=s_v-b_u, P>=P_loc.

For two nonnegative numbers with this fixed sum and each at least s_u,
their product is at least s_u(s_v-b_u-s_u). This follows by factoring
(P_loc-s_u)(M-s_u)>=0.

For fixed u, put D_v=s_u(s_v-b_u-s_u)-b_u b_v. At v=u+1,

    D_(u+1)=s_u^2-c b_u^2>=0.

For v>=u+1, using s_(v+1)-s_v=s_v+b_v and b_(v+1)=c b_v,

    D_(v+1)-D_v=s_u(s_v+b_v)-(c-1)b_u b_v
                  >=(3-c)b_u b_v>0,

because s_u>=b_u and s_v>=b_v. Thus D_v>=0 for all v>u. This proves the
pair obstruction and rules out every chain with two or more checkpoints.
No offset or retained-area term has been dropped from a feasible chain;
the exact first-return condition prevents such a chain from existing.

## 3. Bound on all remaining single cuts

At an occurrence of b_u, prefix and tail sums P,T satisfy

    P,T>=s_u, P+T=s_m-b_u.

Put V=s_m-b_u-s_u. Since b_u+s_u increases with u,

    V>=s_m-b_(m-1)-s_(m-1)=s_(m-1).

On P in [s_u,V], the logarithm of
(1+P)^2[1+2(s_m-b_u-P)] is concave. Its minimum is therefore at an
endpoint. If b_u>1, the two endpoint values for the cut ratio are bounded by

    (b_u-1)^2/[(1+s_u)^2(1+2V)] <=1/(1+2V),
    (b_u-1)^2/[(1+V)^2(1+2s_u)]
                               <=b_u/(1+V)^2.

Here s_u>=b_u-1. Also b_u<=b_(m-1)<=1+s_(m-1) and V>=s_(m-1),
so both ratios are at most 1/(1+s_(m-1)). Ineligible cuts give zero. The
global Huber term 1/(1+2s_m) obeys the same bound. Fact1fca3e5dd555cb4a
therefore gives F_ray=K<=1/(1+s_(m-1)). For m>=18 the scale estimate yields
1/(1+s_(m-1))<=c/(eta a c^m)=8/(5a c^m).

## 4. Exact quadratic-product damping

For lambda in (0,1], put z=a lambda. The whole-block polynomial is

    P_m(lambda)=product_(u=0)^(m-1)(1-b_u lambda)^(2^(m-u-1)).

Choose the integer k>=17 such that c^k z<=1<c^(k+1)z, and set
y=c^k z in (1/c,1]. If a factor is zero, the following whole-block bounds
are immediate. Otherwise, when m>k,

    log|P_m| / 2^(m-k-1)
       =sum_(j=-k)^(m-k-1) 2^(-j) log|1-c^j y|.

For j<0 use log(1-c^j y)<=-c^j y. For j>=1 use
log|1-c^j y|<=log(c^j y)=j log c+log y; these latter upper bounds are
nonnegative because c^j y>1. Extending only these nonnegative bounds to an
infinite series gives

    log|P_m| / 2^(m-k-1)
       <=-2y(1-d^k)/(c-2)+log[y(1-y)]+2log c
       <=-(13/4)y+log(1/4)+2log c
       <=-5/4+log(169/100)
       <=-5/4+69/100=-14/25<-1/2.

The endpoint y=1 gives a zero factor when m>k and was already handled.
We have proved

    |P_m(lambda)|<=exp(-2^(m-k-2))  if m>k.

If m<=k, every factor has b_u lambda<=1, so |P_m|<=1. In particular
|P_m(lambda)|<=1 for every m and lambda in [0,1].

If lambda<=1/(a c^m), the desired weighted bound follows immediately.
Otherwise m>k. Put r=m-k>=1. Then

    lambda |P_m|^2
       <=(1/(a c^m)) c^r exp(-2^(r-1))
       <=1/(a c^m).

The last inequality uses c<e, hence r log c<r<=2^(r-1). For example,
e>1+1+1/2+1/6=8/3>13/5, so no decimal estimate is required. Taking the
maximum over lambda proves the Q bound. This is also the full quadratic
class: diagonalizing a positive semidefinite Hessian with spectrum in [0,1]
makes normalized terminal error a weighted average of these scalar errors.

## 5. Uniform prefix bound and the entire one-cap extension

Define R_u(lambda)=P_u(lambda)(1-b_u lambda), a prefix block of length2^u.
Every prefix of H_m of length ell, 0<=ell<=2^m-1, has polynomial equal to
the product of R_u over the nonzero binary digits of ell. This follows by
successively consuming its largest complete block (H_u,b_u), of length2^u;
the remaining list begins another copy of the same lower-level pattern.

For u<=k, all factors of R_u have b_v lambda<=1, so |R_u|<=1. For
u=k+r with integer r>=1, the damping estimate gives

    |R_u|<=c^r exp(-2^(r-2)).

For r>=4, 2^(r-2)>=r and c<e, so this bound is at most1. For r=1,2,3
it is less than3: for r=1 use c<3; for r=2,3 use e>8/3 and respectively
c^2/(8/3)<3 and c^3/(8/3)^2<3. There are therefore at most three factors
exceeding one in any prefix, each less than3. Every prefix satisfies

    |p_t(lambda)|<=27.

We also need the weighted bound

    lambda |R_u(lambda)|^2 <= c^12/(a c^u).

If lambda<=1/(a c^u), it follows from |R_u|<=1. Otherwise u=k+r with
r>=1, and the left side is at most

    (1/(a c^u)) c^(3r) exp(-2^(r-1)).

For r<=4 this is at most c^12/(a c^u). For r>=5, 2^(r-1)>=3r and
c<e make its extra factor at most1. This proves the bound for every u.

Now consider any feasible single-cap checkpoint j in H_m. Maximizing over
all real r, rather than only its legal interval, gives the rigorous upper bound

    2 lambda r A-lambda(1+2lambda T)r^2
                           <=lambda A^2/(1+2lambda T).

Let u=m-1, and consider the central step b_u. If j precedes it, the tail
contains b_u, so T>=b_u, while |A|<=27. The cap payoff is at most
729/(2b_u). If j is central or follows it, the prefix contains the complete
block (H_u,b_u), followed by a prefix of H_u. Hence |A|<=27|R_u| and
the cap payoff is at most lambda A^2<=729 c^12/(a c^u).
Both cases are bounded by 729 c^13/(a c^m). All signed-record and radius
feasibility constraints were retained in defining the family; enlarging the
radius domain here only makes this upper bound more permissive.

## 6. A sufficient bound on the exact benchmark recurrence

This part uses the exact phi/psi recursions in fact b98bb807d514e80d, not an
asymptotic decimal constant. Put C_n=S_circle(n)+1. Their shifted joins are

    Omega(A,D)=(A+D+sqrt((A+D)^2+4AD))/2,
    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

The first joins C_k,C_(n-k-1), and the second joins C_k,B_(n-k-1).
Both are increasing in their nonnegative arguments.

For 0<=t<=1,

    t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1.

To prove this, put x=t^(1/3), y=(1-t)^(1/3). Then x^3+y^3=1 and

    1-x^4-y^4-x^4y^4
      =x^3y^3[1/(1+x+x^2)+1/(1+y+y^2)-xy]>=0.

Each reciprocal is at least1/3, and xy<=2^(-2/3)<2/3; the latter strict
inequality follows by cubing, since1/4<8/27. Endpoints cause no division
problem. Since Omega is the positive root of X^2-(A+D)X-AD=0, this proves

    Omega(A,D)<=(A^(3/4)+D^(3/4))^(4/3).

Induction in the exact primitive recursion now gives C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3).
Also sqrt(D^2+8AD)<=D+4A, hence G(A,D)<=D+4A. Induction in the exact
dominant recursion gives

    B_n<=1+4[(n-k-1)^(4/3)+(k+1)^(4/3)]<=1+4n^(4/3)

for every split, so it holds for the maximum. The base values are C_0=B_0=1.

Combining Sections2--5 with this recurrence bound gives

    max(F_ray,Q,F_cap)(H_m)/U_(N_m)^ZJ
      <=[729 c^13/a] c^(-m)[1+4(2^m-1)^(4/3)] ->0,

because 2^(4/3)<c. This completes the candidate restricted-channel result.

## Structural consequence and next mechanism

This family has recursive large steps separated by substantial symmetric
blocks. Those blocks prevent the first outward return in the ray construction
and damp every quadratic scale; the prefix damping also defeats a lone terminal
cap. A next witness must permit nonlinear changes followed by additional
returns and further changes, or use a genuinely different multidimensional
interaction. This result does not establish that these schedules perform well
on that richer class. No conclusion about W_(N_m)(H_m) from above is made.

Literature retrieval: a Matlas search for the displayed recursive-product
claim returned unrelated results, none used. Every new estimate above is
proved in the text. Correctness status remains unverified.

## 7. The same family controls every two-curvature homogeneous objective

This extension is part of the same unverified candidate proof. It does not
assume correctness of a separate unverified finding. For u,v in (0,1], define

    f_(u,v)(x)=u x^2/2 for x>=0, and v x^2/2 for x<=0.

Its derivative is continuous, monotone, and 1-Lipschitz, including across zero;
zero is a minimizer. Write F_two_n(h) for the supremum of normalized terminal
error on this family with either initial point +1 or -1. The claim is

    F_two_(N_m)(H_m)<=c/(a c^m),   m>=18.

Scaling or reflecting the initial point adds no larger case, by positive
homogeneity and by allowing both initial signs. Random mixtures and separable
direct sums of such objectives cannot exceed their supremum, since their
normalized errors are convex combinations of component errors.

It suffices first to consider u<=v, with neither reciprocal equal to a step
level. The reverse order follows by reflecting the objective. The exceptional
parameter pairs follow by continuity: each finite GD update and final objective
is continuous in (u,v), even at a sign change or zero iterate. All bounds are
uniform in the parameters. The cases with a zero curvature follow by the same
limit if they are included in the definition.

Let I be the first integer level with b_I v>1, and J the first with b_J u>1.
Then 18<=I<=J. A whole block H_l maps each starting sign to a deterministic
ending sign and nonnegative magnitude. Represent these two magnitudes by the
columns of a two-state map. Before level I, both signs are preserved, and the
whole-block magnitudes are P_l(u),P_l(v), both positive. If m<=I, the two
trajectories are ordinary quadratics, already bounded by Section4.

### 7a. Different first-crossing levels: I<J

The step b_I crosses from the negative side to the positive side but leaves
the positive side positive. Thus H_(I+1) sends both initial signs to the
positive side. Its amplitudes, from positive and negative starts respectively,
are

    A_(I+1)=(1-b_I u)P_I(u)^2,
    D_(I+1)=(b_I v-1)P_I(u)P_I(v).

Every larger whole block also ends positive from both starting signs, because
the last copy of the preceding block has this property. Put

    r_0=D_(I+1)/A_(I+1)>0.

The ratio D_l/A_l stays equal to r_0. Indeed composition with the central
step yields

    (A_(l+1),D_(l+1))=(1-b_l u)(A_l^2,A_l D_l),  l<J,
    (A_(l+1),D_(l+1))=(b_l u-1)(A_l D_l,D_l^2),  l>=J.

In particular, for I+1<=l<=J,

    A_l=P_l(u),
    D_l=(b_I v-1)P_I(v) P_l(u)/[(1-b_I u)P_I(u)].

All factors of P_l(u) in this range are positive. Dividing by
(1-b_I u)P_I(u) removes a submultiset of its factors with total step mass
b_I+s_I. Since 1-t<=exp(-t), it follows that

    A_l<=exp(-u s_l),
    D_l<=exp(-u s_l) exp(u(s_I+b_I)-v s_I+log(b_I v-1)).

Set S=s_I/b_I>=eta>1, t_u=b_I u<1 and t_v=b_I v>1. The exponent in
the latter extra factor is at most

    (S+1)-S t_v+log(t_v-1)
       =1-S(t_v-1)+log(t_v-1)<=-log S<=0.

Here the maximum of log w-Sw over w>0 is -1-log S, found by differentiating.
Consequently both whole-block amplitudes obey exp(-u s_l) up to l=J.
Their common terminal side has curvature u, so for I< m<=J the error is

    <=u exp(-2u s_m)<=1/(2e s_m)<=1/(a c^m),

using s_m>=eta a c^m.

For l>=J, put E_l=max(A_l,D_l). The exact recurrence gives

    E_(l+1)<=E_l^2(b_l u-1),    E_J<=exp(-u s_J).

Let t=b_J u in (1,c) and m=J+r with r>=1. Expanding this scalar recursion,

    log E_m / 2^(r-1)
      <=-2u s_J+sum_(j=0)^(r-1)2^(-j)log(c^j t-1)
      <=-2eta t+2log c+2log t
      <=-2eta+2<-1.

The series bound uses log(c^j t-1)<=j log c+log t and sums the nonnegative
upper bounds to infinity. The last inequality uses log c<1 and the fact that
-2eta t+2log t decreases on t>=1 because eta>1. Thus

    u E_m^2<=u exp(-2^r)
       <=[c/(a c^m)] c^r exp(-2^r)<=c/(a c^m),

since u<c/(a c^J), log c<1, and r<=2^r. This covers I<J completely.

### 7b. Equal first-crossing levels: I=J

At level I both signs cross, so H_(I+1) interchanges the two starting signs.
Every larger block also interchanges them: an interchange, the central
interchange, and another interchange compose to an interchange. Let A_l be
the amplitude from a positive start and D_l the amplitude from a negative
start. Then

    A_(I+1)=(b_I u-1)P_I(u)P_I(v),
    D_(I+1)=(b_I v-1)P_I(u)P_I(v),
    A_(l+1)=A_l^2(b_l v-1),
    D_(l+1)=D_l^2(b_l u-1),     l>=I+1.

Put S=s_I/b_I>=eta, t_u=b_I u>1, t_v=b_I v>1. Both t_u,t_v are less
than c. All earlier factors are positive, so P_I(w)<=exp(-w s_I).
For m=I+r, r>=1, the exact recursion therefore implies

    log A_m / 2^(r-1)
      <=log(t_u-1)-S(t_u+t_v)
                   +sum_(j=1)^(r-1)2^(-j)log(c^j t_v-1)
      <=[-S t_u+log(t_u-1)]+[-S t_v+log t_v]+2log c.

For any t>1, -St+log(t-1)<=-S-1-log S. Also -St+log t<=-S, because
S>1. The displayed bound is consequently

    <=-2S-1-log S+2log c<=-2eta+1=-9/4<-2.

The identical estimate for D_m follows after interchanging u,v. Thus both
amplitudes are at most exp(-2^r). Their terminal curvatures are at most
v<c/(a c^I), giving normalized error at most

    [c/(a c^m)] c^r exp(-2^(r+1))<=c/(a c^m).

This proves the asserted two-curvature bound. In conjunction with Sections1--6,
the maximum of F_ray, Q, F_cap, and F_two still has ratio tending to zero
relative to the exact ZJ benchmark along N_m=2^m-1.

### Scope of the stronger exclusion

The proof controls a continuous two-parameter nonlinear family, with repeated
sign changes and inner returns. It does not control a derivative whose slope
changes more than once along either ray, nor a genuinely coupled multidimensional
function. Such changes remain concrete mechanisms to investigate. Six fixed
curvature pairs were checked using only forty compositions of a two-state map
(about0.1 seconds, no long trajectory stored); those checks suggested the proof
but are not used in it. No numerical sweep or asymptotic computation is evidence
for the claimed bound.

## 8. Arbitrary monotone continuations after a quadratic-gradient prefix

One can enlarge the single-cap class substantially without changing this
obstruction. Consider any legal scalar convex1-smooth function with minimizer0,
initial point1, and a checkpoint j such that its sampled gradients through j
satisfy g_t=lambda p_t, where p_t=product_(v<t)(1-lambda h_v) and
lambda in(0,1]. Function values on the prefix need not equal quadratic values.
After step j, allow an arbitrary nonlinear continuation, with the sole
restriction that all subsequent iterates stay on the same side of zero. A
zero iterate makes every later iterate zero and can be discarded as trivial.
The supremum of terminal error over this enlarged class, for H_m, is at most

    1458 c^13/(a c^m),   m>=18.

Here is a direct proof, not an appeal to a prior unverified claim about the
continuation. Let A=|p_(j+1)| and T=sum_(t>j)h_t. Reflect the current side so
that its coordinates are positive. Convexity implies every later gradient is
nonnegative; the no-crossing assumption and nonnegative steps make the
coordinates and gradients nonincreasing. Let x_f and g_f be the final radius
and gradient magnitude. Then

    x_f+T g_f<=A,    0<=g_f<=x_f.

For a monotone1-Lipschitz derivative with endpoint value g_f and value zero
at the origin, its integral from0 to x_f is at most
x_f g_f-g_f^2/2. Indeed its pointwise upper bound there is min(r,g_f), whose
integral has that value. Consequently

    2f(x_f)<=2A g_f-(2T+1)g_f^2<=A^2/(2T+1).       (8.1)

Set u=m-1, so the central step is b_u. If j is at or before the central
step, then T>=s_u, while Section5 gives A<=27. Thus (8.1) is at most
729/(1+2s_u), below the asserted bound.

If j follows the central step, both p_j and p_(j+1) contain the complete
factor R_u and a prefix factor of H_u. Hence each has magnitude at most
27|R_u|. There are two cases.

If lambda h_j<=1, this checkpoint does not cross zero. Since every later
point is closer to zero on the same side as p_j, monotonicity of the global
derivative gives g_f<=lambda |p_j|. The integral bound, or just convexity,
then gives

    2f(x_f)<=2x_f g_f<=1458 lambda |R_u|^2
                               <=1458 c^13/(a c^m).

If lambda h_j>1, the checkpoint is a crossing. Its level v obeys b_v>1,
and its following exact copy of H_v is included in the suffix. Therefore
T>=s_v>=eta b_v>eta/lambda. Combining this with (8.1) yields

    2f(x_f)<=729|R_u|^2/(1+2T)
             <=[729/(2eta)]lambda |R_u|^2
             <=[729/(2eta)]c^13/(a c^m).

This proves the stated bound. It applies to every monotone continuation
consistent with all old gradient data, including many changes of curvature and
interior interpolation gaps; neither a constant tail nor a preserved quadratic
prefix value was assumed. It makes no assertion about a continuation with
further sign crossings. Thus adding arbitrary curvature changes on one final
ray does not repair the earlier restricted constructions on this family. The
new scalar mechanism must permit nonlinear changes followed by additional
crossings of the minimizer.

evidence:
# The optimal three-step objective schedule needs more than endpoint proof-weight corrections

Status: complete unverified counterexample to a proposed certificate template. This is not a counterexample to the schedule, which is a standard optimal recursive objective schedule. No verifier call.

For a schedule h of length n and sum S, consider the restrictive proof-weight template

  u_0=h_0+a,
  u_i=h_i for1<=i<n,
  u_n=b.

Here a,b are real, and actual weights must be nonnegative. If the weight mass is the Huber-tight value D=2S+1, then b=S+1-a. Write d=x_0-x_n, U=sum_i u_i g_i, e=U-d. This template has the exact linear relation

  e=a g_0+b g_n.                                    (1)

The intrinsic objective certificate is E_h(u)>=0, where

  E_h(u)=2sum_i u_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_i u_i||g_i||^2
          +2sum_i u_i<g_i,x_0-x_i>-||U||^2.

For L=1 and minimizer0 it satisfies the exact identity

  E_h(u)=||x_0||^2+2sum_i u_i Q_(i,star)
           -2D f_n-||x_n-e||^2.                    (2)

The template is attractive because a one-step optimal schedule h=(3/2) has weights(2,2), hence a=1/2,b=2, and E=4(-Q_10)>=0. But it already fails on a basic three-step objective schedule.

Set t=sqrt(2), lambda=1+t, and

  h=(t,lambda,3/2),
  S=5/2+2t,
  D=2S+1=6+4t=2lambda^2.

This schedule is ConPD((sqrt(2)),(3/2)). The bridge is lambda, by direct substitution in psi. The argument below only needs the explicit steps and two legal equality examples; it does not assume its optimality among all schedules.

## Quadratic equality fixes the sole free endpoint parameter

Use f(x)=x^2/2, x_0=1. All Q_(i,star)=0, and

  x_3=p=(1-t)(1-lambda)(1-3/2)
       =-1/(2+t)=-1/sqrt(D).

Thus2D f_3=Dp^2=1. From(1)–(2),

  E_h(u)=-[p-a-bp]^2.

Any valid nonnegative intrinsic energy must therefore have a+(b-1)p=0. Substituting b=S+1-a gives the unique value

  a=-Sp/(1-p)=S/(sqrt(D)+1)=lambda/2,
  b=S+1-a=(3/2)(2+t).                              (3)

The associated weights are

  u=((1+3t)/2,lambda,3/2,(3/2)(2+t)),

and all are positive.

## The middle-checkpoint Huber equality contradicts those weights

Put c=1/lambda and q=t/(4lambda). Define the one-dimensional convex1-smooth function

  f(x)=x^2/2 for -q<=x<=c,
  f(x)=cx-c^2/2 for x>=c,
  f(x)=-qx-q^2/2 for x<=-q.

Its derivative is x clipped to[-q,c], which is nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz; f is differentiable, f(0)=min f=0. Starting at x_0=1, the specified GD steps give

  x_1=c,
  x_2=c-1=-t/lambda=-4q,
  x_3=-4q+(3/2)q=-(5/2)q,
  (g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3)=(c,c,-q,-q).

Every sampled point is on an outer affine piece or its boundary. Therefore Q_(i,star)=f_i-g_i x_i+g_i^2/2=0 at all four samples. Also

  f_3=(5/2)q^2-q^2/2=2q^2,
  2f_3=4q^2=1/(2lambda^2)=1/D.

This is the middle-cut equality construction from accepted facts b98bb807d514e80d and1fca3e5dd555cb4a, with prefix sum t, checkpoint lambda, and tail sum3/2; all trajectory details are included here.

For the only possible template weights(3),

  U=(u_0+u_1)c-(u_2+u_3)q
    =(6+11t)/(8lambda),
  U-1=(3t-2)/(8lambda)>0.

Since e=U-(1-x_3), one has x_3-e=1-U. Equation(2) now yields

  E_h(u)=-[(3sqrt(2)-2)/(8(1+sqrt(2)))]^2<0.

Thus no choice of a,b in the endpoint-only template can certify the Huber-tight denominator D for this schedule: the quadratic forces(3), and a second legal equality witness refutes it. The original schedule remains valid with a different weight vector. In the usual ConPD construction, one may use the nonnegative weights

  (sqrt(2),2+sqrt(2),2+sqrt(2),2+sqrt(2)),

which have mass D and adjust internal indices as well as endpoints.

The scope is precise. This rules out modifying only the initial and terminal entries of the physical-step weight vector. It does not exclude all fixed-dimensional potentials, all gradient-aggregate residuals, or another certificate with internal anchor weights. It explains why retaining a single initial-gradient correction while insisting every internal weight equal the physical step is too narrow for the upper-construction program.

This tests the specific repair suggested after the minimum-reset and residual-sign obstructions: allow positive proximal function values, and check actual past-plane deficits even when the signed residual is positive.

## 1. A parameterized model
Fix a in(0,1), chi>=1, T>=2, and kappa in[0,T-2]. Assume
T>=2a chi,                                               (1)
(T-2-kappa)-(T-kappa)chi^2+T chi/a>=0.                     (2)
For any number m>=1 of blocks, in R^(m+1) set
zeta_0=e_0,
zeta_(i+1)=-a zeta_i+sqrt(1-a^2)e_(i+1).
Define alpha_i=chi for even i and alpha_i=1 for odd i, omega_i=alpha_i zeta_i. Thus
<zeta_i,zeta_j>=(-a)^|i-j|
and all omega_i are independent.

Each real block consists of one unit step followed by
b_i=T-1+(T/a)alpha_(i+1)/alpha_i.
Take the ONE finite max-affine function
J(z)=max{0,max_(0<=i<=m)(<omega_i,z>-kappa alpha_i^2)}
and f=env_1 J. Start at X_0=T alpha_0 zeta_0.
We prove that block i queries X_i and X_i-omega_i with gradient omega_i at both, and that
X_(i+1)=X_i-(1+b_i)omega_i.
The terminal point is X_m with gradient omega_m.

These need not be a legal new primal: they are a legitimate test of
PSD, which is required on ALL formal vectors.

Here U=1, V=1/16, Z=0, and R0=sqrt(78)/20.
Consequently the OLD FULL slack (2) is exactly zero.
On (6), equation(5) is exactly

M_new=eta(81 eta-344)/[1024(12+eta)].                (7)

It is negative for every 0<eta<344/81. In particular eta=1 is allowed
by (4), all actual multipliers remain nonnegative, but
M_new=-263/13312<0. There is therefore no sufficiently small positive
move of this unchanged transport that preserves PSD.

On the actual matching quadratic data from Section1, in contrast,
(5)/eta is 25/16-25/[4(12+eta)]>0. Thus checking only the
matching primal would falsely suggest a gain. The second full-kernel
direction is essential.

## 4. Scope and a different successful action on this example

This is NOT a stationary tuple and NOT a globally optimal schedule.
It does not refute some other simultaneous descent. Indeed one exists
with a different certificate re-selection.

First continuously undo the last zero-flow adjustment in Section1,
moving from (1) to its base certificate (3) at the SAME h,q.
Every intermediate actual multiplier is nonnegative, and every
intermediate slack is a convex combination of the PSD matrices (2)
and (3). The same legal quadratic remains matching throughout.
The base slack (3) has no extra kernel beyond that quadratic direction,
because zeta^2/16=39/200<1.

Now use the schedule h'=(2,28/13,3), corresponding to eta=1 in (4).
An explicit full certificate with value q'=900/169<25/4 is obtained
by keeping the first-step multiplier pattern
(mu_0,mu_1,nu_0,lambda_10)
=(2+zeta/2,zeta/2,zeta,2-zeta/2),
multiplying it by q'=4(15/13)^2, and then adding the two
function-growth identities from Section1:
four times the i=1 identity with r=15/13, and once the i=2
identity with r=2.

Its slack is

q'[||R0||^2-(zeta/2)<R0,U>+||U||^2]
 +4||(15/13)g_1+g_2||^2+||2g_2+g_3||^2 >=0,

all multiplier signs hold since15/13>1 and zeta<4, and its
function-value flow is exactly2e_3. The quadratic again attains q'.
This is a real fixed-length improvement for this example.

The obstruction therefore distinguishes two mechanisms:
the same sparse transport can fail at an unnecessarily degenerate
optimal dual certificate, whereas reselecting the dual certificate
inside the fixed-h optimum face can make a different descent available.
No theorem is claimed that such re-selection removes remote edges
for every schedule, nor that the maximal-rank dual face always has
the needed kernel structure.

Next action: analyze certificate re-selection together with the
inactive-interpolation costs before attempting a universal descent.
Do not add a remote-edge-absence hypothesis and call the original
extension repaired. The eventual exact-profile mass-cap issue remains
separate even if global Huber tightness were established.

evidence:
# Quantitative limit of the exact two-cut inner-return objective witness

Status: complete scoped candidate proof, not verifier-accepted. No new verifier
call. This bounds the explicit two-cut construction, not the entire scalar
class and not the unrestricted smooth-convex worst case.

## 1. The construction being bounded

Take a schedule split as (prefix,b,middle,d,tail), with nonnegative ordinary
block sums P,M,T and b,d>1. Choose 0<w<=1 and R>=w. The fixed derivative is

    g(x)=-v                 when x<=-v,
    g(x)=x                  when -v<=x<=w,
    g(x)=w                  when w<=x<=R,
    g(x)=x-R+w              when R<=x<=R+1-w,
    g(x)=1                  when x>=R+1-w,

where v=(b-1-R+w)/(1+M)>0. Start at X=P+R+1-w, and put z=(d-1)v.
Require (1+T)w<=z<=R. As in the complete construction proof, every ordinary
block stays on its indicated plateau, the checkpoints cross the minimum,
and the normalized terminal objective is

    J=[2wz-(2T+1)w^2]/X^2.                                  (1)

All inequalities below use just these displayed definitions. In particular
no unverified result is imported as a proof premise. An overall scaling of
the gradient/radii is immaterial to (1).

Since X>=P+R, z<=R, and completing the square gives
2wz-(2T+1)w^2<=z^2/(2T+1), we have

    J <= [z/(P+R)]^2/(2T+1) <= 1/(2T+1).                    (2)

Also w<=1 and R>=w imply b-1-R+w<=b, so z<=(d-1)b/(1+M).
The strict crossing and z<=R moreover give R<b and z<b: the latter follows
from z<=min(R,(d-1)(b-R)/(1+M)), where w<=1 was used. Consequently

    J <=2z/X^2 <=2b/P^2                                    (3)

when P>0. Combining the first inequality in (2) with the preceding bound on z
gives

    J <= [b(d-1)/(P(1+M))]^2/(2T+1)                        (4)

when P>0. These are distinct valid relaxations; the w<=1 restriction in (3)
is essential near the end of the schedule.

## 2. Uniform bound on the recursive hostile family

Put c=13/5, a=c^(-17), b_j=a c^j, and

    H_0=(),  H_(m+1)=(H_m,b_m,H_m),
    s_m=sum H_m=a(c^m-2^m)/(c-2).

For m>=19 let B=b_(m-1) be the central, largest step. Write eta=13/8.
Since (2/c)^17<1/40, direct substitution gives s_u>=eta b_u for all u>=17.
Any eligible selected step greater than1 has level u>=18. An occurrence of
b_u has a complete H_u immediately before and immediately after it, so its
entire prefix and tail sums are at least eta b_u.

Consider ANY feasible pair of selected checkpoints in H_m and ANY feasible
w,R in Section1. There are three exhaustive cases.

1. The first selected checkpoint is at or after the central B-step. Then
P>=s_(m-1)>=eta B and b<=B. Equation (3) gives

    J <=2/(eta^2 B).

2. The second selected checkpoint is at or before the central B-step. Then
T>=s_(m-1)>=eta B. Equation (2) gives

    J <=1/(1+2eta B) <=1/(2eta B).

3. The first selected checkpoint is strictly before the central step and the
second is strictly after it. The middle sum contains the central step, hence
M>=B. Also P>=eta b, T>=eta d, and d<=B/c. Equation (4) yields

    J <=d^2/[eta^2 B^2(1+2eta d)]
       <=d/(2eta^3 B^2)
       <=1/(2eta^3 c B).

Each bound is at most2/(eta^2 B). Thus, uniformly over every feasible pair,
every threshold, and every choice of ordinary blocks within H_m,

    sup J <=2/(eta^2 a c^(m-1))
           =[2c/(eta^2 a)] c^(-m).                        (5)

This covers the arbitrary lower-positive-plateau height and the retained old
positive ramp/area in the exact C10 object. It does not cover more than two
checkpoints, visits inside nonconstant ordinary blocks, or arbitrary core
curvatures; no such generalization is asserted.

## 3. The exact benchmark comparison, with an elementary bound included

Let C_n=S_circle(n)+1 and B_n=2S_bullet(n)+1 for the exact project recursions.
Their shifted joins are

    Omega(A,D)=(A+D+sqrt((A+D)^2+4AD))/2,
    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

We prove the sufficient rough bounds C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3) and
B_n<=1+4n^(4/3) directly here. For positive A,D put
Z=(A^(3/4)+D^(3/4))^(4/3). The inequality Z>=Omega(A,D) is equivalent,
after normalizing A^(3/4)+D^(3/4), to

    t^(4/3)+(1-t)^(4/3)+[t(1-t)]^(4/3)<=1,  0<=t<=1.

To prove it set x=t^(1/3), y=(1-t)^(1/3), so x^3+y^3=1. The difference
between the right and left sides equals

    x^3 y^3 [1/(1+x+x^2)+1/(1+y+y^2)-xy].

Each reciprocal is at least1/3, and xy<=2^(-2/3)<2/3, so the bracket is
nonnegative. This proves the join inequality and, by induction in the exact
primitive recursion, C_n<=(n+1)^(4/3).

Next G(A,D)<=D+4A follows from sqrt(D^2+8AD)<=D+4A. In the dominant recursion
each left subtree has k+1 leaves for k steps and the right subtree has n-k-1
steps. Induction, together with u^(4/3)+v^(4/3)<=(u+v)^(4/3), yields
B_n<=1+4n^(4/3). The empty-horizon initial values are C_0=B_0=1.

At n=2^m-1, (5) and U_n^ZJ=1/B_n imply

    (sup J)/U_(2^m-1)^ZJ
       <=[2c/(eta^2 a)] c^(-m) [1+4(2^m-1)^(4/3)] ->0,

because c^3=2197/125>16. Therefore the exact two-cut inner-return objective
channel also cannot repair the recursive-family profile gap.

This does not undo its primitive-energy counterexample: the latter includes
weighted old-area residuals absent from the last-iterate objective. Nor does
it imply that H_m has a small unrestricted worst case; the coupled-coordinate
construction already shared provides a genuine divergent lower bound there.

claim: Four explicit equality instances for the tight benchmark h=(sqrt2,1+sqrt2,3/2) force every PSD quadratic remainder in its intrinsic objective energy to be identically zero, for ANY nonnegative proof weights of mass D=6+4sqrt2. evidence:
# Four equality instances forbid positive intrinsic quadratic storage at a benchmark schedule

Status: unverified exact counterexample argument. No new solver or verifier call. This is a limitation of positive quadratic remainders in the intrinsic objective energy, not of all certificates or of the unrestricted minimax problem.

Put t=sqrt(2), lambda=1+t, and consider the known three-step schedule

    h=(t,lambda,3/2), S=5/2+2t, D=2S+1=6+4t=2lambda^2.

For nonnegative proof weights u=(u_0,u_1,u_2,u_3) with sum D, define

    d=x_0-x_3, U=sum_i u_i g_i, e=U-d,
    E_u=2sum_i u_i(f_i-f_3)+sum_i u_i||g_i||^2
          +2sum_i u_i<g_i,x_0-x_i>-||U||^2.

Use Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.

## Claim

If a symmetric PSD matrix P of size4 satisfies

    E_u >= sum_(i,j=0)^3 P_ij <g_i,g_j>               (1)

for every legal smooth convex trajectory of this schedule, then P=0.

This applies to any positive quadratic storage formed from fixed linear combinations of the four gradients: substituting those combinations into the storage matrix gives a PSD matrix P in (1). A nonzero matrix on redundant coordinates is possible only if its quadratic form vanishes identically on the GD coordinate subspace.

## 1. Why equality instances constrain every choice of proof weights

For every minimizer x_star, expansion gives

    ||x_0-x_star||^2+2sum_i u_i Q_(i,star)
       -2D(f_3-f_star)=||x_3-x_star-e||^2+E_u.      (2)

Each one-dimensional instance below has x_star=0, f_star=0, x_0=1, Q_(i,star)=0 at every query, and 2f_3=1/D. Thus (2) implies

    E_u=-|x_3-e|^2<=0.

Under (1), PSD gives E_u>=0, so E_u=0 and the gradient vector belongs to the kernel of P. This argument does not assume the standard proof-weight vector or any completeness theorem for interpolation certificates.

## 2. Four explicit legal equality instances

Every derivative displayed below is continuous, nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz. Its integral from zero is therefore differentiable, convex, 1-smooth and minimized at zero. The formulas also directly show f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2 at the sampled points, giving Q_(i,star)=0.

### A. Global Huber plateau

Let c=1/D and set g(x)=max(-c,min(x,c)). All four sampled points remain on the positive affine piece, so their gradients are(c,c,c,c). The endpoint is x_3=1-Sc=(S+1)/D, and 2f_3=1/D. After division by the nonzero initial gradient, the gradient row is

    v_H=(1,1,1,1).

### B. Full quadratic

Take f(x)=x^2/2. The gradient row, with g_0=1, is

    v_Q=(1,1-t,2-t,-1+t/2).

The last entry is -(2-t)/2=-1/(2+t), and (2+t)^2=D, so 2f_3=1/D.

### C. Middle-cut asymmetric Huber

Let c=1/lambda and a=t/(4lambda). Set g(x)=max(-a,min(x,c)). Its exact points are

    x_0=1, x_1=c, x_2=-4a, x_3=-(5/2)a,

and its gradients are(c,c,-a,-a). Hence f_3=2a^2 and 2f_3=4a^2=1/D. Dividing the gradients by c gives

    v_M=(1,1,-t/4,-t/4).

### D. Capped quadratic with an inner return

Again let c=1/lambda, but use the different fixed derivative

    g(x)=x for x<=c, and g(x)=c for x>=c.

The exact points are

    x_0=1, x_1=c, x_2=-tc, x_3=(t/2)c.

The first step stays on the upper affine piece; the bridge enters the quadratic core, and the last step returns to its positive side. All points from x_1 onward are in the quadratic piece. Thus f_3=t^2 c^2/8=c^2/4 and 2f_3=1/(2lambda^2)=1/D. Dividing the gradients by c gives

    v_C=(1,1,-t,t/2).

This fourth equality case is essential. Using only the previous three rows would incorrectly leave room for a square proportional to

    ||g_2-g_3-(3/2)(t-1)(g_0-g_1)||^2.

For the capped quadratic, g_0=g_1 but g_2-g_3=-(3t/2)c is nonzero, whereas E_u=0 under any certificate (1).

## 3. The kernel spans the entire gradient space

Form the4-by4 matrix whose rows are v_H,v_Q,v_M,v_C. Subtract its first row from the other three. Expansion down the first column gives determinant

    (-t)(-1-t/4)(3t/2)=3(1+t/4)>0.                  (3)

The four rows therefore span R^4. For a PSD matrix, v^T P v=0 implies P v=0, as follows by diagonalizing P with nonnegative eigenvalues. Part1 puts all four independent rows in its kernel, proving P=0.

## 4. The obstruction occurs at an actual valid tight certificate

The usual weights are

    u=(t,2+t,2+t,2+t), sum u_i=D.

Their intrinsic energy has the explicit identity

    E_u=2lambda(-Q_10)+2(-Q_01)+D(-Q_32)
          +2lambda(-Q_21)+2lambda(-Q_31).            (4)

All coefficients are positive, so E_u>=0 and (2) yields W<=1/D. The four instances above attain this bound. Equation(4) can be checked directly from the GD differences x_1=x_0-tg_0, x_2=x_1-lambda g_1 and x_3=x_2-(3/2)g_2. This is also the primitive-one-step/dominant-one-step ConPD certificate, but no external closure theorem is needed for the displayed identity.

## Implication for retained-state propagation

The finite pair residual in max4_finite_pair_residual_transport.md is valid: that two-step objective bound leaves room for a positive quadratic remainder. Such a remainder cannot be carried as a nonzero PSD intrinsic-energy term through every exactly calibrated dominant schedule. At this three-step benchmark it must disappear, or become a structural zero, regardless of which nonnegative tight proof weights are selected.

The result does not exclude an indefinite storage coupled to function values, a state retaining actual interpolation slacks, a certificate at a smaller denominator, a different schedule, or a complete objective certificate in which the initial-distance square is still present. It rules out the specific plan of obtaining exact benchmark calibration and retaining a uniformly positive, nontrivial quadratic penalty depending on gradient-history linear aggregates alone. The complete original minimax target remains unresolved.

evidence:
# A globally minimizing stationary schedule with an unavoidable forward edge

Status: UNVERIFIED exact counterexample package. No additional verifier call
is allocated. The two-step optimum is used here as a fully certified calibration
example for a FACE-LEVEL support claim, not as a solution to the asymptotic target.

## 1. The precise property being refuted

The proposed property is:

    At a globally minimizing positive schedule, one can reselect a tight
    full interpolation certificate with lambda_(i,j)=0 for every
    finite chronological forward pair i<j.

This property is false. The example below is BOTH globally minimizing
among all nonnegative two-step schedules AND a full matching stationary
primal-dual tuple. Its ENTIRE optimal certificate set is a singleton,
and its multiplier lambda_01 is strictly positive.

The forced edge0->1 is ADJACENT. This does NOT refute the narrower
unproved property that only nonadjacent remote forward edges can be removed.

## 2. Exact constants and a complete full certificate

Define

    u=sqrt(2), a=u-1,
    b=(-1+sqrt(9+8u))/4,
    r=a b, q=r^2,
    h=(u,1+b).                                      (1)

The useful exact identities are

    a^2+2a=1,  u=1+a,  1/a=a+2,
    2b^2+b=a+2,
    r(2b+1)=1,
    q=1/[1+2(u+1+b)].                               (2)

For example, r(2b+1)=a(2b^2+b)=a(a+2)=1, and
1+2(u+1+b)=2a+2b+5=(2b+1)^2.
Also 2/5<a<1/2, 3/4<b<1, 0<r<1/2.

Normalize L=1, x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Use the complete inequalities

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.

Set all unlisted multipliers to zero and take

    mu_0=lambda_(0,star)=2u r^2,
    mu_1=lambda_(1,star)=2u b r,
    mu_2=lambda_(2,star)=2r,

    lambda_01=2r^2,
    lambda_10=2r^2/a,
    lambda_21=2(1-r).                               (3)

All are positive. There are no star-outgoing multipliers.
The finite flow equations are

    mu_0+lambda_01=lambda_10,
    mu_1+lambda_10=lambda_01+lambda_21,
    mu_2+lambda_21=2.

They follow from (2); for example 2r^2/a+r=1 and
u r+u b+1=2b+1=1/r.

After x_1=x_0-u g_0 and x_2=x_1-(1+b)g_1, the FULL quadratic identity is

    q||x_0||^2-2f_2+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
         =||r x_0-u r g_0-u b g_1-g_2||^2.          (4)

One way to check all coefficients is to write its gradient block as

    A=(u r,u b,1)^T(u r,u b,1),

whose diagonals are (2r^2,2b^2,1) and off-diagonal entries are
A_01=2rb, A_02=u r, A_12=u b.
Its x_0 cross coefficients are minus the three mu_i from (3).
Thus every multiplier sign, flow, and full PSD entry is explicit.

This proves W_2(h)<=q.

## 3. Three exact matching legal functions

Each scalar function starts at x_0=1 and is minimized at zero.

H: the even Huber function of threshold q, with derivative
max(-q,min(q,x)). Its vector (x_0,g_0,g_1,g_2) is

    v_H=(1,q,q,q),

and its final value is f_2=q/2. At every sampled point its
star-outgoing slack is strictly positive:

    f_i-||g_i||^2/2=q[1-q(P_i+1)]>0,               (5)

where P_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, including P_2=u+1+b.
The strict inequality follows from P_i<=P_2 and
q=1/(2P_2+1), with P_2>0.

Q: the quadratic function x^2/2. Its transcript vector is

    v_Q=(1,1,-a,r),

and f_2=r^2/2=q/2.

C: the one-sided capped quadratic

    f_C(x)=x^2/2 for x<=a,
           a x-a^2/2 for x>=a.

Its derivative min(x,a) is continuous, nondecreasing, and 1-Lipschitz.
The trajectory is x_0=1, x_1=a, x_2=-r, with

    v_C=(1,a,a,-r),  f_2=q/2.                       (6)

All are actual globally legal smooth-convex functions. They establish
W_2(h)>=q and hence equality with the full certificate (4).

## 4. Global optimality among ALL two-step schedules

The only verified predecessor used here is fact b98bb807d514e80d:
its exact Huber and both single-cut lower bounds apply to arbitrary
nonnegative schedules. The elementary quadratic witness adds its own
explicit lower bound. Thus for every X,Y>=0,

    W_2(X,Y)>=max{
       1/(1+2X+2Y),
       (X-1)_+^2/(1+2Y),
       (Y-1)_+^2/(1+X)^2,
       (X-1)^2(Y-1)^2
    }.                                             (7)

The last term is the error on x^2/2; the other three are the verified
single-cut/Huber bounds. Suppose W_2(X,Y)<=q=r^2. The Huber term gives

    X+Y>=u+1+b=2+a+b>3.                            (8)

If X<=1, then Y>1 and the third term in (7) gives
Y-1<=r(1+X), whence X+Y<=2+2r<3, contradicting (8).
If Y<=1, then X>1 and the second term gives
X-1<=r sqrt(1+2Y)<=r sqrt(3), whence X+Y<3, again impossible.

We may therefore set U=X-1>0 and V=Y-1>0. Equation (7) implies

    U V<=r,
    V<=r(U+2),
    U^2<=r^2(2V+3).                                (9)

For U<=a, use the second inequality:

    U+V<=U+r(U+2)<=a+r(a+2)=a+b,

with equality only at U=a,V=b.
For U>=a, the first and third inequalities imply

    U^3-3r^2 U-2r^3<=0,
    (U-2r)(U+r)^2<=0,

so a<=U<=2r. Also V<=r/U. The strictly convex function
U+r/U attains its maximum on [a,2r] at an endpoint. Its values are

    a+r/a=a+b,
    2r+1/2.

The first is strictly greater, since

    (a+b)-(2r+1/2)=a^2(b-1/2)>0.

Thus U+V<=a+b, again with equality only at U=a,V=b.
Combining with (8), every schedule with W_2(X,Y)<=q is exactly
(X,Y)=(u,1+b). In particular (1) is the UNIQUE global minimizer, and

    W_2^*=q.                                       (10)

All nonnegative schedules, including zero steps and arbitrary large
steps, were included. This is an exact two-step argument, not an
asymptotic profile claim.

## 5. The ENTIRE optimal certificate set is a singleton

Take ANY full nonnegative-flow PSD certificate at this fixed h,q.
Every actual instance in Section3 attains q. Therefore PSD and the
interpolation signs force the certificate matrix M to annihilate
v_H,v_Q,v_C, and every multiplier to vanish on a strict interpolation
slack of any one of these instances.

The three transcript vectors are independent. Indeed, v_H-v_C has
equal, nonzero g_0 and g_1 coordinates, whereas v_Q-v_C has those
coordinates 1-a and -2a, which are unequal. Both differences have
x_0 coordinate zero, while v_C has x_0 coordinate one. The nonzero
claim uses q<a, which follows from a b^2=(1-r)/2<1/2.

Their common orthogonal complement is generated by

    N=(r,-u r,-u b,-1).

It annihilates v_Q and v_C by (2), and N dot v_H=0 follows from
u r+u b+1=1/r. Since M is PSD and its x_0,x_0 coefficient is q=r^2,

    M=N N^T.                                       (11)

This is the WHOLE matrix for every optimal certificate. No assumption
about a numerical maximal rank or a chosen observed kernel is used;
three explicit legal equality instances force it.

Equation (5) forces every star-outgoing multiplier nu_i to be zero.
The x_0 row of (11) fixes mu uniquely at the values in (3).
The final gradient diagonal satisfies

    A_22=out_2-1=1+in_2

by the full flow equation. In (11), A_22=1, so every incoming
terminal multiplier is zero: lambda_02=lambda_12=nu_2=0.

For function C a direct substitution gives

    Q_20=(a-1)(a+r)<0.

Therefore lambda_20=0 for every optimal certificate as well.
The first gradient diagonal now reads

    A_00=mu_0-(u-1)lambda_01
         =2u r^2-a lambda_01.

In (11) it equals 2r^2, hence

    lambda_01=2r^2=2q>0.                            (12)

Flow then forces lambda_10=2r^2/a and lambda_21=2(1-r), leaving
exactly (3). All directed pairs have now been accounted for.

Thus the optimal certificate set is a singleton, and re-selection,
relative-interior selection, and maximal-rank selection all leave
the positive adjacent forward edge unchanged.

## 6. An ACTUAL matching stationary primal, with no assumed regularity

To check stationarity directly, set

    omega_H=1/(1+a^2 b^3),
    omega_C=omega_H*a^2 b^2*(b-a)/(1+a^2),
    omega_Q=omega_H*a^3 b^2*(1+a b)/(1+a^2).          (13)

They are positive and sum to one:
omega_C+omega_Q=omega_H a^2 b^3.
Construct the actual three-dimensional function

    F(z_H,z_Q,z_C)
       =sum_(J in {H,Q,C}) omega_J f_J(z_J/sqrt(omega_J))

and start at (sqrt(omega_H),sqrt(omega_Q),sqrt(omega_C)).
It is convex and 1-smooth, the initial squared distance is one, and
its full trajectory Gram matrix is
G=sum_J omega_J v_J v_J^T. Its final normalized value is q.

For the certificate (3), the two formal matrix derivatives evaluated
on any scalar/vector realization are

    D_0=2b^2<g_0,g_1>+2r<g_0,g_2>-2r^2||g_0||^2,
    D_1=2<g_1,g_2>.                                (14)

Their values on the three equality instances are

              H              Q                C
    D_0       2r^4           -2a b^2           2a r^2
    D_1       2r^4           -2a r             -2a r.

These values are obtained from (14), not by differentiating a
nonsmooth family of extremal functions. In particular the fixed
capped function C has a gradient kink at x_1=a, so that shortcut
would be unsafe.

The identities

    omega_Q-a^2 omega_C=omega_H a^3 b^2,
    omega_Q+omega_C=omega_H a^2 b^3

make both weighted derivatives zero. Therefore

    <G,partial M/partial h_0>=<G,partial M/partial h_1>=0.

All primal interpolation inequalities, PSD, normalization, full
matrix complementarity, multiplier complementarity, and both
stepsize stationarity equations hold for this actual instance.
Moreover rank(G)=3, rank(M)=1, and the formal matrix size is4.
This example even has strict complementarity; a hidden nonphysical
common kernel is not responsible for the obstruction.

## 7. Consequences and precise limits

This is a complete counterexample to removing ALL forward finite
multipliers by re-selection, even at a positive globally minimizing
schedule with a full stationary matching instance and no extra
common kernel. It closes a possible attempt to turn the triangular
sufficient hypothesis in the earlier suffix-deformation candidate
into a universal property of optimal schedules.

It does not refute removal of ONLY nonadjacent remote forward
edges: lambda_02=0 in the example. It also has q equal to the
Huber value, every nu_i=0, and Z=0; consequently it is not a
counterexample to global Huber tightness. The asymptotic exact-profile
question and the mass-cap bridge remain unresolved.

No literature result beyond the verified predecessor b98bb807d514e80d
was used as a proof brick. The targeted Matlas query returned no
applicable statement. The global two-step calculation is included
solely to make the counterexample's global and stationary status
reviewable without relying on a numerical optimum.
