# The new two-checkpoint tail policy still misses the full profile

Status: UNVERIFIED joint proof candidate. No verifier or solver allocation.
All new estimates, including the recursive-schedule and benchmark estimates,
are reproved here. Shared unverified findings are not premises.

This is a limit of the explicit policy from
`research/max_profile_height_and_tail_cap.md`, not an upper bound on W_n.
The policy itself has a full fixed-function construction in that document.
The comparisons here concern its explicit numerical formulas and the
VERIFIED K and F_ray functionals, defined in facts `b98bb807d514e80d` and
`1fca3e5dd555cb4a` respectively.

## 1. The exact functionals to be tested

For any i<j with h_i,h_j>1, write

 P=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=sum_(i<t<j)h_t, T=sum_(t>j)h_t,
 A=(h_i-1)/(1+P), epsilon=(h_j-1)/(1+S), sigma=1+2T.

Define

    C_ij=A^2 min(epsilon^2,epsilon)/(4sigma),
    C_n^tail=max_(eligible i<j) C_ij,

with zero if there are no eligible pairs. Also set a=P/(1+P). For
0<kappa<=A/(1+epsilon), define

 V_ij(kappa)=[A kappa epsilon^2
    -a^2(kappa epsilon-sigma/(1+P))_+^2/
                 ((A-kappa)(A+2a)+a^2)]/sigma.

Let E_n^tail be the maximum of V_ij(kappa) over those pairs and angles,
or zero if there are no pairs. These are exactly the lower and optimized
upper formulas of the constructed family, with the explicit angle optimizer
given in the companion document. Purely algebraically,

    C_n^tail<=E_n^tail<=4 C_n^tail.                        (1)

For the upper bound discard the nonnegative correction and use
kappa<=A/(1+epsilon). If epsilon<=1 the result is at most
A^2 epsilon^2/sigma; if epsilon>=1 it is at most A^2 epsilon/sigma.
For the lower bound choose kappa=A/[2max(1,epsilon)]. With
D=(A-kappa)(A+2a)+a^2, the correction in V is no larger than
a^2 kappa^2 epsilon^2/D<=kappa^2 epsilon^2, so
V>=epsilon^2 kappa(A-kappa)/sigma>=C_ij.

## 2. The prescribed recursive schedules

Put c=13/5, a_rul=c^(-17), b_u=a_rul c^u and

    H_0=(), H_(m+1)=(H_m,b_m,H_m),
    n_m=2^m-1,
    s_m=sum H_m=a_rul(c^m-2^m)/(c-2).

The last identity follows by induction from s_(m+1)=2s_m+b_m. Define
eta=13/8. For u>=17,

    s_u/b_u=[1-(10/13)^u]/(3/5)>=eta.                    (2)

Indeed (10/13)^3<1/2 and (10/13)^2<4/5 imply
(10/13)^17<1/40. Every eligible checkpoint b_u>1 has u>=18, so (2)
applies to every eligible index below.

At each occurrence of b_u there is a full H_u immediately before it
and another immediately after it. In particular its complete preceding
and following masses are each at least s_u>=eta b_u. Its one-based
position has 2-adic valuation u; this also follows directly by induction.

## 3. Every new pair is controlled by an old single cut

Fix i<j, of levels u and v. Denote the corresponding individual K terms by

    K_i=(h_i-1)^2/[(1+P)^2(1+2(S+h_j+T))],
    K_j=(h_j-1)^2/[(1+P+h_i+S)^2(1+2T)].

If epsilon<=1, put x=1+S and d=h_j-1, so d/x<=1. Since
T>=eta h_j>d, the ratio is

 C_ij/K_i=(d/x)^2/4 *[1+(2x+2d)/(1+2T)]
           <=[2(d/x)^2+d/x]/4<=3/4.                     (3)

Now suppose epsilon>1, so x=1+S<d=h_j-1. Necessarily u<v and i lies
inside the copy of H_v immediately preceding j. If u>=v, that copy's
H_v before j lies strictly after i and gives S>=s_v>=eta h_j, a
contradiction. If u<v but i precedes that copy, the same contradiction
holds. Inside the copy, the H_u immediately after i is contained between
i and j, so S>=s_u>=eta h_i. Also, writing P_loc for the mass in that
copy before i, one has

    P>=P_loc=s_v-h_i-S.

Because u<v, h_i<=h_j/c. Using S<h_j-2 therefore yields

 P>(eta-1-1/c)h_j+2=(25/104)h_j+2,
 x/(1+P)<104/25,
 h_i/(1+P)<=1/eta<2/3.                                  (4)

Consequently

 (1+P+h_i+S)/(1+P)<1+2/3+104/25<6,
 (h_i-1)^2/(d x)<h_i^2/x^2<=1/eta^2<4/9.

The exact ratio to the second single cut is thus

 C_ij/K_j=[(h_i-1)^2/(4d x)]
                   *[(1+P+h_i+S)/(1+P)]^2<4.             (5)

Equations (3)--(5) cover EVERY eligible pair, not merely chosen large
checkpoints. They prove

    C_(n_m)^tail(H_m)<=4 K_(n_m)(H_m),
    E_(n_m)^tail(H_m)<=16 K_(n_m)(H_m).                   (6)

The cases epsilon approaching1, tiny initial levels and zero eligible
pairs cause no exception; the division into (3) and (5) is exhaustive.

## 4. Full ray comparison and a uniform K bound on these schedules

For completeness the same schedules obey F_ray=K. For proposed first
two ray checkpoints i<j, let their levels be u,v and retain P,S above.
The exact accepted ray recurrence would give a second-crossing budget

    [(b_u-1)(b_v-1)/(1+S)-P]/(1+P).

Any chain of at least two checkpoints requires this to be positive.
We show the stronger opposite estimate PS>=b_u b_v.

If u>=v, P>=s_u and S>=s_v. If u<v but i is before the H_v preceding
j, these same bounds hold. In either case PS>=b_u b_v by (2).
Otherwise i lies inside that H_v. The local copies of H_u give

    P_loc>=s_u, S>=s_u, P_loc+S=s_v-b_u.

Factoring (P_loc-s_u)(S-s_u)>=0 shows

    PS>=s_u(s_v-b_u-s_u).

For v=u+1, this is s_u^2>=c b_u^2=b_u b_v since eta^2=169/64>13/5.
For larger v, define D_v=s_u(s_v-b_u-s_u)-b_u b_v. Its successive
increment is

 D_(v+1)-D_v=s_u(s_v+b_v)-(c-1)b_u b_v
             >=(3-c)b_u b_v>0,

using s_u>=b_u and s_v>=b_v. Hence PS>=b_u b_v always. The second
crossing budget is nonpositive, which prevents both a subsequent positive
gradient and a terminal return with its positive old-slope constraint.
Only zero or one checkpoint remains, so F_ray=K by the accepted fact.

For m>=18 let s=s_(m-1), the mass of either child of the top checkpoint.
An eligible cut at or left of the top checkpoint has T>=s and
(h_i-1)/(1+P_i)<=1 by its preceding buffer. Its K term is <=1/(1+2s).
A cut right of the top checkpoint has P_i>=s and, from its own local
buffers, T_i>=h_i and P_i>=h_i. Thus its term is at most

    h_i/[2(1+P_i)^2]<=1/[2(1+P_i)]<=1/[2(1+s)].

The global Huber term is <=1/(1+s). Therefore

    F_ray_(n_m)(H_m)=K_(n_m)(H_m)<=1/(1+s_(m-1))
                          <=8/(5a_rul c^m).              (7)

In combination,

    E_(n_m)^tail(H_m)<=128/(5a_rul c^m).                 (8)

## 5. Comparison with the actual B_n sequence

The following elementary estimate of the VERIFIED benchmark recursions is
included so that no unverified stronger growth estimate is a premise:

    S_circle(n)+1<=(n+1)^(4/3),
    B_n<=1+4n^(4/3).                                    (9)

Write p=4/3 just within this section. The primitive join is

 Omega(a,b)=(a+b+sqrt((a+b)^2+4ab))/2.

We claim Omega(x^p,y^p)<=(x+y)^p for x,y>=0. After dividing by
(x+y)^p and using symmetry, it suffices to show, for 0<=t<=1/2,

    t^p+(1-t)^p+[t(1-t)]^p<=1.                          (10)

This is the condition that1 lies beyond the positive root of
z^2-[t^p+(1-t)^p]z-[t(1-t)]^p=0. At t=0 it is equality.
For t>0, Taylor's integral remainder and

    [(1-t)^p]''=(4/9)(1-t)^(-2/3)<3/4

on [0,1/2] give

    (1-t)^p<=1-4t/3+3t^2/8.

For the strict derivative bound, 2^(2/3)<27/16 follows on cubing.
The left side of (10) is at most

    1+t[-4/3+L(t)],
    L(t)=t^(1/3)(2-4t/3+3t^2/8)+3t/8.

The function L is increasing on (0,1/2]. Indeed its derivative times
t^(2/3) is

    2/3-16t/9+7t^2/8+3t^(2/3)/8.

For t<=3/8 the first two terms are nonnegative. For 3/8<=t<=1/2,
the first three terms are at least their value -1/288 at1/2, since
their derivative -16/9+7t/4 is negative; the last term is at least
3t/8>=9/64>1/288. Thus the derivative is positive throughout.
Finally 2^(-1/3)<4/5 gives

    L(1/2)<(4/5)(4/3+3/32)+3/16=319/240<4/3.

This proves (10), including every t. Induction in the exact primitive
recurrence now gives C_n=S_circle(n)+1<=(n+1)^p.

In the dominant recursion, writing a=C_k, d=B_(n-k-1), the denominator
join is

    G(a,d)=2a+d/2+sqrt(d^2+8ad)/2<=4a+d,

since sqrt(d^2+8ad)<=d+4a. Starting with B_0=1, induction gives

 B_n<=1+4[(k+1)^p+(n-k-1)^p]<=1+4n^p

for every split, proving (9). This is a bound on the full supplied
sequence, without a phase limit or dyadic-constant substitution.

As c^3=2197/125>16, one has 2^(4/3)/c<1. From (7)--(9),

 max(F_ray_(n_m)(H_m),E_(n_m)^tail(H_m)) B_(n_m)
       <=[128/(5a_rul c^m)] [1+4(2^m-1)^(4/3)] ->0.       (11)

Thus even the exact optimized three-cell policy together with the whole
verified ray functional fails the required uniform lower comparison.
All parameter choices and finite tail budgets were included before this
countertest. This does not bound unrestricted W from above and does not
decide the project target. In particular it is compatible with the known
shared, unverified coupled-coordinate construction giving very large true
errors on H_m; that construction is not used anywhere in this proof.

The precise remaining mechanism is repeated changes of direction and
creation of positive height across more than two selected checkpoints,
with all queried history retained. Optimizing only the final cap, or
choosing the two checkpoints more carefully, cannot overcome (11).

# All quadratic primitive tests and all single cuts still miss the capacity scale

Status: complete self-contained candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. No new
solver or fact_submit. Earlier ruler estimates are re-proved here, not used
as unverified premises. This concerns a necessary-test relaxation of
primitive validity; it does NOT prove that the constructed schedules are
primitive for general smooth convex functions.

## Statement

Put c_sc=13/5, a_sc=c_sc^(-17), bsc_j=a_sc c_sc^j, and

    Hsc_0=(),  Hsc_(j+1)=(Hsc_j,bsc_j,Hsc_j),
    ssc_m=sum Hsc_m=a_sc(c_sc^m-2^m)/(c_sc-2).

Consider TWO consecutive copies

    Gsc_m=(Hsc_m,Hsc_m),
    Lsc_m=2(2^m-1),   Dsc_m=1+2ssc_m.                (1)

For any finite nonnegative schedule h of sum S define the intrinsic
primitive energy on an actual smoothness-one GD trajectory by

    V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)
       +sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
       -S(S+1)||g_n||^2.                             (2)

The following assertions hold for every m:

(a) EVERY single-cut primitive test holds strictly for Gsc_m:

    Dsc_m(h_j-1)_+
      <(1+sum_(i<j)h_i)(1+sum_(i>j)h_i)              (3)

    for each actual step j.

(b) V_(Gsc_m)>=0 on EVERY finite-dimensional convex quadratic with a
    minimizer and gradient Lipschitz constant at most1, from every initial
    point. This tests every curvature, and the actual chronological
    primitive energy, not only the final polynomial or curvature1.

(c) With rho_sil=log_2(1+sqrt(2)),

    Dsc_m/(Lsc_m+1)^(rho_sil) -> infinity.             (4)

Consequently the conjunction of ALL quadratic primitive-energy tests and
ALL single-cut primitive tests cannot imply the proposed silver-power
capacity bound, or a constant multiple of that bound. The remaining
simplex/projection geometry is essential to any proof by such testing.
No claim is made here that V_(Gsc_m)>=0 for arbitrary nonlinear functions.

## 1. Meaning and necessity of the cut tests

For a selected step b>1 put A=1+sum before it and B=1+sum after it;
the total capacity is D=A+B+b-1. Projection onto C=[-v,u], with
u>0, v=(b-1)u/B and initial point Au, has gradient u on the entire
prefix, lands at -Bv after the selected step, then has gradient -v
on the entire suffix and ends at -v. Its fixed legal function is

    F_C(x)=max_(z in C)(xz-z^2/2),  F_C'=P_C.

Every sample has f_i=x_i g_i-g_i^2/2. Expanding the squared-distance
telescope in (2) gives

    V_h=x_0^2-(x_n+Sg_n)^2
       =A^2u^2-D^2(b-1)^2u^2/B^2.

Hence primitive validity requires D(b-1)<=AB. For b<=1 its positive-
part version is automatic. This proves necessity of the tests in (3),
including all function values, independently of earlier findings.

## 2. All cuts in the two-copy ruler pass

Abbreviate c=c_sc, a=a_sc, s_j=ssc_j, b=bsc_j. For j>=17,

    s_j/b=[1-(2/c)^j]/(c-2)>=eta,  eta=13/8.          (5)

Indeed (2/c)^3<1/2 and (2/c)^2<4/5 imply (2/c)^17<1/40.
Every step b>1 has j>=18. A step b<=1 satisfies (3) strictly because
the right side is positive.

For a fixed level j<m, the first occurrence of b in Gsc_m is preceded
by exactly Hsc_j, and the last occurrence is followed by exactly Hsc_j.
The two-copy word is palindromic. Thus the prefix sum at any occurrence
lies between s_j and 2s_m-s_j-b. For fixed total step sum, the product
of the two cut masses is concave in the prefix sum, and the two endpoint
values agree. Its minimum is therefore

    (1+s_j)(1+2s_m-s_j-b).

Put s=s_j and L=2s_m. The margin over the cut left side is

    (1+s)(1+L-s-b)-(1+L)(b-1).

Its derivative in L is s+2-b>0 by (5). Since m>=j+1,
L>=2s_(j+1)=4s+2b. At this minimum L the margin is

    3s^2-3sb-2b^2+8s+2b+2.

The quadratic part is increasing for s>=eta b and is at least

    (3eta^2-3eta-2)b^2=(67/64)b^2>0.

Every margin is therefore strictly positive. This proves (a).

## 3. The exact quadratic energy and its chronological moment

Fix scalar curvature lambda in(0,1], initial point1, and
f(x)=lambda x^2/2. For ANY physical schedule h define

    P_i=product_(t<i)(1-lambda h_t),
    Q=|P_n|, tau=lambda sum h_i,
    R=lambda sum_(i<n) h_i P_i^2.

The quantity R includes every actual prefix product; order has not been
discarded. Direct substitution into (2), or the identity
1-Q^2=sum_i(2lambda h_i-lambda^2 h_i^2)P_i^2, gives

    V_h=1-[1+(1+lambda)tau+tau^2]Q^2-(1-lambda)R.     (6)

For the single word Hsc_j write Q_j,R_j,tau_j, and put
z_j=lambda bsc_j. The exact concatenation recurrences are

    Q_(j+1)=|1-z_j| Q_j^2,
    R_(j+1)=R_j+Q_j^2[(1-z_j)^2 R_j+z_j],
    tau_(j+1)=2tau_j+z_j.                             (7)

These formulas include the middle step and both copies in their actual
order. For two copies of Hsc_m the corresponding quantities are

    Q_double=Q_m^2,
    R_double=R_m(1+Q_m^2),
    tau_double=2tau_m.                                (8)

## 4. Any normalized-small-step word has nonnegative quadratic energy

Suppose every z_i=lambda h_i lies in[0,1]. During a chronological
prefix let tau,R,Q have their analogous partial meanings and set

    B_pot=R+(1+tau+tau^2)Q^2.

On adding a step z in[0,1], use R'=R+zQ^2, tau'=tau+z,
and (Q')^2=(1-z)^2Q^2. Exact expansion yields

    B_pot'-B_pot
      =-Q^2[tau^2 z(2-z)+tau z^2(3-2z)+z^3(1-z)]<=0.

Initially B_pot=1, so it remains at most1. Each partial product has
magnitude at least the final product, hence R>=tau Q^2. Equation (6)
can now be written

    V_h=1-B_pot+lambda(R-tau Q^2)>=0.                 (9)

This argument applies to any order and any physical h with lambda h<=1;
it does not require physical h<=1.

## 5. Controlling the moment before and at first activation

Let I be the first level for which t=z_I>1, and put J=I+1. Then
I>=18 and 1<t<=c. For all j>=17, (5) gives tau_j>=eta z_j.

First bound R_I. Put z=t/c in(1/c,1], so z is the central step of
Hsc_I. All normalized steps inside Hsc_(I-1) are at most z/c. If
q=Q_(I-1)^2, the squared-distance telescope there gives

    R_(I-1)<=(1-q)/(2-z/c).

Also q<=exp(-2tau_(I-1))<=exp(-2eta z), since those factors are in[0,1].
Set C=1/(2-z/c). Substituting into (7) and dropping a nonpositive term,

    R_I<=C+C z^2(1-1/c)q
        <=[c/(2c-1)] [1+(1-1/c)/(eta^2 exp(2))]
        <(13/21)[1+512/15379]<2/3.                   (10)

Here z^2 exp(-2eta z)<=1/(eta^2 exp(2)) follows by differentiating,
and exp(2)>7 follows from its power series. The final rational comparison
uses 13*512<15379.

The complete product on Hsc_I satisfies Q_I<=exp(-eta t).
Its first activated extension therefore has

    z_J Q_J<=c t(t-1)exp(-2eta t)
             <=3c/(16eta^3)=1248/10985<k_0:=1/8.     (11)

Use exp(2eta t)>(2eta t)^3/6 and (t-1)/t^2<=1/4 for this bound.
Meanwhile (7) and (10) give

    R_J<2/3+exp(-2eta t)[(2/3)(t-1)^2+t]<35/48.      (12)

To check the second inequality, put B(t)=(2/3)(t-1)^2+t. The polynomial
2B-B'=(4t^2-6t+5)/3 is positive, so B(t)exp(-2eta t) decreases
for t>=1, as 2eta>2. Its value at1 is exp(-13/4)<1/16.
The last bound follows from exp(3)>1+3+9/2+27/6+81/24>16.

## 6. Uniform moment control at every later level

For j>=J put w_j=z_j Q_j. Here z_j>=c>2. Equation (7) implies

    w_(j+1)=c(1-1/z_j)w_j^2<=c w_j^2.

With theta_0=c k_0=13/40, (11) therefore gives

    w_j<=k_0 theta_0^(j-J),
    sum_(j>=J) w_j^2<=k_0^2/(1-theta_0^2)=25/1431.  (13)

The moment recurrence also gives

    R_(j+1)-R_j<=w_j^2(R_j+1/z_j)
                         <=w_j^2(R_j+1/c).

Thus U_j=R_j+1/c obeys U_(j+1)<=(1+w_j^2)U_j. By (12)--(13),

    R_j+1/c
      <[35/48+5/13]/[1-25/1431]
      <3/4+5/13,

so R_j<3/4. We used product(1+w_j^2)<=exp(sum w_j^2)
<=1/[1-sum w_j^2]. The final exact comparison is
695*1431=994545<995448=59*12*1406.

Also tau_j<=z_j/(c-2)=5z_j/3 and Q_j^2<=k_0^2/z_j^2. Consequently

    [1+(1+lambda)tau_j+tau_j^2]Q_j^2
      <=(1/64)[1/c^2+10/(3c)+25/9]<1/8.             (14)

For the last simple inequality, the bracket is less than
1+4/3+3=16/3<8. This bound is uniform in lambda, its activation
phase t, and the horizon.

## 7. Every quadratic passes for the two-copy schedule

If m<=I, every normalized step in Gsc_m is at most1, so (9) applies.
If m>=J, (13)--(14) give Q_m^2<=1/(64c^2)<1/256 and R_m<3/4.
Using (8),

    R_double < (3/4)(1+1/256)=771/1024.

Further,

    [1+(1+lambda)tau_double+tau_double^2]Q_double^2
      <=4[1+(1+lambda)tau_m+tau_m^2]Q_m^4
      <(1/2)Q_m^2<1/512.

Equation (6) therefore yields the explicit positive margin

    V_(Gsc_m)>1-771/1024-1/512=251/1024>0             (15)

for a unit scalar initial point once m>=J. Curvature lambda=0 gives
energy0 and is harmless. Before activation (9) supplies nonnegativity.

For an arbitrary finite-dimensional convex quadratic with a minimizer,
translate that minimizer to zero, subtract the minimum value, and
orthogonally diagonalize its positive semidefinite Hessian. Smoothness
at most1 places every eigenvalue in[0,1]. The GD trajectory and (2)
separate across these eigendirections, with each scalar energy multiplied
by the squared initial coordinate. The proved scalar nonnegativity
therefore proves (b), including singular Hessians and arbitrary starts.

## 8. Capacity comparison and what remains open

From (1),

    Dsc_m ~ [2a_sc/(c_sc-2)] c_sc^m,
    Lsc_m+1=2^(m+1)-1.

Since c_sc=13/5>1+sqrt(2), dividing by
(Lsc_m+1)^(rho_sil) proves (4). Thus this family passes the ENTIRE
quadratic primitive-energy class and every one-cut projection test while
its capacity exceeds any fixed multiple of the proposed silver-power
bound for all sufficiently large m.

This is a concrete failure of that necessary-test closure, not a
counterexample to the primitive-capacity conjecture. No universal
primitive certificate for Gsc_m is supplied. If these schedules fail
primitivity, their failure must use geometry beyond all quadratics and
the displayed single-cut functions. The strict simplex norm game is an
appropriate remaining interface because it retains that full geometry;
an equivalent formulation alone does not settle its capacity bound.

author: max2
claim: Exact phase-resonance counterexample to automatic elliptic metric averaging: for every a>0 and c=13/5, there are arbitrarily small z=rho exp(i pi/3) with Re(z)>|z|² such that a tail product product_(j=J)^(m-1)|cos(arg R_j(z))| stays >9/10 for EVERY m>=J. evidence:
# Exact dyadic resonances prevent automatic metric isotropization

Status: complete unverified geometric counterexample. It does not assert
that the resulting smooth-convex prefixes are legal. All phase identities
and estimates used below are derived here; no earlier unverified finding
is a premise. This diagnoses a proposed step in the elliptic-prefix program.

## 1. Recursive phases and the failed proposed conclusion

Let c=13/5 and let a>0 be any fixed number. Put b_j=a c^j and
H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,b_j,H_j). For a nonreal z in the upper half plane set

    p_j(z)=product_(t=0)^(j-1)(1-b_t z)^(2^(j-t-1)),
    R_j(z)=p_j(z)(1-b_j z).

In an elliptic prefix the same2x2 metric M is rotated at each recursive
copy. Averaging a cycle over all copies of H_r inside H_m attenuates its
traceless metric component by

    Gamma_(r,m)(z)=product_(j=r)^(m-1)|cos(arg R_j(z))|.    (1)

The proposed generic repair was to assert Gamma_(r,m)(z)->0 for every fixed
nonreal z. We construct counterexamples with Re(z)/|z|=1/2 and
Re(z)-|z|^2>0, in the very wide-angle range where circular interpolation
is obstructed on the recursive family. For these parameters, there is a
finite J such that

    Gamma_(J,m)(z)>9/10       for EVERY m>=J.              (2)

Thus late copies can preserve almost all metric anisotropy forever. This
does not preclude a different argument using earlier cycles or complete
interpolation; it refutes the unconditional phase-decay step itself.

## 2. A uniquely defined sequence of small resonant parameters

Fix theta=pi/3. For rho>0 let z=rho exp(i theta) and define the continuous
principal factor arguments

    phi_j(rho)=arg(1-b_j rho exp(i theta)) in(-2pi/3,0),
    Phi(rho)=sum_(j=0)^infinity 2^(-j-1) phi_j(rho).

The series converges uniformly in rho because |phi_j|<=2pi/3 and the
weights sum to one. Each phi_j is strictly decreasing: direct
differentiation of its argument gives

    phi_j'(rho)=-b_j sin(theta)/|1-b_j rho exp(i theta)|^2<0.

Consequently Phi is continuous and strictly decreasing. For rho tending
to zero each fixed phi_j tends to zero; for rho tending to infinity each
tends to theta-pi=-2pi/3. In either limit, a finite-head/uniform-tail split
of the summable series justifies taking the limit. Hence Phi maps
(0,infinity) onto(-2pi/3,0).

For every integer k>=1 there is therefore a unique rho_k>0 such that

    Phi(rho_k)=-pi/2^k.                                  (3)

These radii decrease to zero. To see the last claim, for every epsilon>0
the fixed value Phi(epsilon)<0 is eventually smaller than -pi/2^k;
strict decrease of Phi then implies rho_k<epsilon.

Choose k sufficiently large that rho_k<1/2, and set z_k=rho_k exp(i pi/3).
This is a precise implicit definition with uniqueness, not a numerical
approximation. Its spectral parameters obey

    Re(z_k)/|z_k|=1/2,
    Re(z_k)-|z_k|^2=rho_k(1/2-rho_k)>0.                  (4)

Thus the counterexample is not obtained by leaving the usual circular
cocoercivity disk. No claim of full prefix legality follows from(4).

## 3. Exact phase formula at every recursive level

Fix one z=z_k and abbreviate phi_j=phi_j(rho_k), Phi=Phi(rho_k). Use an
unwrapped argument for p_j and R_j obtained by summing factor arguments.
From their exact multiplicities,

    arg_unwrapped(p_j)
       =sum_(t<j)2^(j-t-1)phi_t
       =2^j Phi-sum_(ell=0)^infinity2^(-ell-1)phi_(j+ell).

Therefore

    arg_unwrapped(R_j)=2^j Phi+epsilon_j,
    epsilon_j=phi_j-sum_(ell=0)^infinity2^(-ell-1)phi_(j+ell). (5)

As j increases, b_j increases and phi_j strictly decreases to
phi_infinity=-2pi/3. Thus

    0<epsilon_j<=phi_j-phi_infinity.

When b_j|z|>=2, write

    1-b_j z=(-b_j z)(1-1/(b_j z)).

The second factor has positive real part and positive imaginary part. Its
argument is phi_j-phi_infinity and is at most

    |1/(b_j z)|/[1-|1/(b_j z)|]<=2/(b_j|z|).

Here arg(1+w)<=|w|/(1-|w|) for |w|<1 follows directly by bounding the
tangent by |Im w|/(1-|w|) and using arctan(t)<=t. The argument sum has
no branch ambiguity because phi_j lies between phi_infinity and zero.
Hence

    0<epsilon_j<=2/(b_j|z|)      whenever b_j|z|>=2.       (6)

By(3), for every j>=k the term2^j Phi is an integer multiple of pi.
Equations(5),(6) give

    |cos(arg R_j)|=|cos(epsilon_j)|.

## 4. A uniform positive lower bound for all later averaging products

Choose a finite J>=k with b_J|z|>=8. Then for j>=J,

    0<epsilon_j<= (1/4)c^(-(j-J))<=1/4.

For0<=t<=1/4, integration of sin(s)<=s gives cos t>=1-t^2/2. Also
log(1-u)>=-2u for0<=u<=1/2, by integrating -1/(1-u)>=-2.
It follows that log(cos t)>=-t^2. Consequently, for every m>=J,

    log Gamma_(J,m)
       =sum_(j=J)^(m-1)log(cos epsilon_j)
       >=-sum_(j=J)^infinity epsilon_j^2
       >=-4/[b_J^2 |z|^2(1-c^(-2))]
       >=-169/2304.

Thus

    Gamma_(J,m)>=exp(-169/2304)
               >=1-169/2304=2135/2304>9/10,

proving(2). The finite products decrease, so they also have a strictly
positive infinite limit. This proof handles exact resonance; it does not
invoke equidistribution, generic parameter behavior, or numerical phases.

## 5. Why(1) is the actual metric attenuation factor

Every query position of H_m is a product of a subset of R_0,...,R_(m-1):
the right copy multiplies all positions of the left-copy pattern by its
bridge multiplier R_(m-1). Fix a cycle in H_J and average its transported
copies in H_m after dividing each inequality by the squared modulus of
its nonzero starting multiplier. All rotations commute, so this is the
successive average of identity conjugation and conjugation by the rotation
arg R_j for each j=J,...,m-1.

On a symmetric2x2 matrix, the scalar part tr(M)I/2 is unchanged. Identify
its traceless part [[u,v],[v,-u]] with the complex number u+i v. Rotation
conjugation multiplies that number by exp(+/-2i arg R_j), with the sign
depending only on the convention. Averaging multiplies its norm by
|(1+exp(2i arg R_j))/2|=|cos(arg R_j)|. This proves(1) directly and ties
the counterexample to the full common-metric cycle interface.

## 6. Honest remaining question

The radii in(3) are explicit by a uniquely solvable scalar monotone equation,
but no legality of all smooth-convex prefix inequalities has been proved
at them. A positive long-horizon construction must still choose one M>0,
check every cycle and value, and give an actual terminal payoff. An
obstruction must use additional geometry or quantitative finite-level
constraints; the copies alone do not force the metric to become circular.

Matlas retrieval returned unrelated statements in arXiv:2210.15480,
math/0701272 and1303.2019. None is imported. All estimates above are textual
and symbolic; there was no root-finding computation or numerical search.

claim: General re-selection cannot keep the supplied full PSD remainder fixed: for every n>=2, the unit-step schedule has an E_(1/n) certificate whose signed V certificate has invariant negative coefficient lambda_(0,n)=-1/n, even though its remainder is positive definite on all gradient differences. evidence:
# Signed terminal credit: two exact failures of direct repair

Status: complete candidate calculations, NOT verifier-accepted. No numerical
PEP or fact_submit call. These results do not decide equality of the signed
and ordinary primitive cones. In particular, preservation of the entire PSD
remainder is stronger than preservation of positive semidefiniteness.

## 1. Exact space of multiplier changes preserving the full remainder

Fix a nonnegative list h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), with n>=1, and formal independent
gradients g_0,...,g_n. Put s=sum h_i, x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t, and

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                               -s(s+1)||g_n||^2.

An intrinsic certificate is a multiplier array lambda on distinct finite
pairs such that V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij cancels the values and has a PSD
quadratic remainder on ALL independent formal gradients. A signed certificate
may have negative coefficients only on i->n. A certificate for
E_theta=V_h-theta sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,n) has an equivalent signed array with
lambda_(i,n)>=-theta h_i and all other coefficients nonnegative.

Define the (n+1)-by-(n+1) lower triangular matrix A by

 A_ii=1, A_it=h_t if t<i, A_it=0 if t>i.

Let e be the all-one vector and r=A^(-1)e. Direct forward substitution gives
r_0=1 and r_(i+1)=(1-h_i)r_i. For a change Delta lambda, with zero diagonal,
put L=diag(Delta lambda e)-Delta lambda. The following parameterization is
exact, without any sign assumption:

 Delta lambda preserves both value cancellation and the ENTIRE quadratic
 remainder if and only if

   L=B A^(-1), B^T=-B, B e=0, B r=0.                 (1)

To prove this, preserving value coefficients is exactly equality of incoming
and outgoing Delta flow at each node, equivalently e^T L=0. The row identity
L e=0 holds by definition. Write H=A-I. The position terms in sum Delta
lambda Q are g^T L H g. Because the flow is balanced, its squared-difference
terms are g^T L g. Thus the full quadratic change is g^T L A g, which is
identically zero exactly when B=L A is skew-symmetric. The two flow identities
become B r=0 and e^T B=0; skew-symmetry turns the latter into B e=0.
Conversely, these conditions imply both flow identities and a zero quadratic
change, and off-diagonal entries Delta lambda_ij=-L_ij recover the array.

If some step is positive, e and r are independent. The possible B are precisely
skew maps on the orthogonal complement of span{e,r}; hence the dimension of
the space in (1) is (n-1)(n-2)/2. This dimension is about algebraic changes
preserving a supplied remainder, not about sign-feasible certificates.

If h_0=1, then r=(1,0,...,0). Therefore B r=0 forces its first column and,
by skew-symmetry, first row to vanish. The first row of L also vanishes.
Consequently EVERY outgoing coefficient lambda_(0,j) is invariant under
every change preserving the complete remainder and value cancellation.
In particular, a negative lambda_(0,n) cannot be repaired in this way.

## 2. An arbitrarily long, strictly PSD example with a negative invariant

Take any integer n>=2, h_i=1 for all i<n, epsilon=theta=1/n, and
d_k=g_k-g_(k+1). Begin with the nonnegative adjacent array

 lambda^0_(k,k+1)=2(k+1)^2,
 lambda^0_(k+1,k)=2(k+1)(k+2), 0<=k<n,

all other entries zero. Direct expansion of the two adjacent Q terms at each
step, and summation of the value coefficients, gives

 V_h+sum lambda^0_ij Q_ij=sum_(k=0)^(n-1)(k+1)^2||d_k||^2.       (2)

Modify the four coefficients by adding

 Delta lambda_01=n epsilon,
 Delta lambda_10=(n-1)epsilon,
 Delta lambda_0n=-epsilon,
 Delta lambda_1n=epsilon.                             (3)

These are distinct ordered pairs for n>=2. When n=2, the 1n change is simply
added to the existing adjacent coefficient. The flow of (3) is zero at every
node. Its full quadratic is exactly

 epsilon[n Q_01+(n-1)Q_10-Q_0n+Q_1n]
   =-epsilon <d_0,sum_(k=1)^(n-1)(n-k)d_k>.           (4)

For a direct check, the value terms cancel. The quadratic left side divided
by epsilon is (g_0-g_1) dot [sum_(j=1)^n g_j-n g_1]. Writing
g_j-g_1=-sum_(k=1)^(j-1)d_k yields the right side.

The resulting signed remainder M is therefore the following sum of squares:

 M=sum_(k=1)^(n-1)(k+1)^2
       ||d_k-epsilon(n-k)d_0/[2(k+1)^2]||^2
   +[1-epsilon^2/4 sum_(k=1)^(n-1)(n-k)^2/(k+1)^2]||d_0||^2.   (5)

The last coefficient is strictly greater than 3/4. Indeed,
epsilon=1/n, (n-k)^2<n^2, and
sum_(j=2)^n 1/j^2 < sum_(j=2)^n 1/[j(j-1)] <1.
Thus M is positive definite in all the gradient differences and PSD on the
complete original formal gradient space, with exactly the constant-gradient
kernel. The only negative signed multiplier is lambda_0n=-1/n.

For the ACTUAL E_theta certificate, add theta h_i=1/n to every incoming
terminal multiplier. The 0n entry becomes zero, and every other entry is
nonnegative. These additions cancel the -theta J_h in E_theta, so the
remainder remains exactly (5). This is a full certificate, including the
actual function-value cancellation, for 0<theta<1.

Nevertheless no ordinary nonnegative certificate for V_h can have this SAME
remainder M: by Section 1 its 0n multiplier would still be -1/n. The ordinary
certificate (2) does exist and has a different PSD remainder. Thus this is
NOT a strict enlargement example. It disproves a general repair that keeps
the given matrix fixed, even for strictly positive difference matrices and
arbitrarily many positive steps. Any successful general repair must genuinely
change that matrix or use a different primal argument.

evidence:
# Applicability audit: the old normal-mixture proof does not transfer

Status: self-contained UNVERIFIED counterexample to a polynomial estimate,
not a counterexample to the target theorem and not a legal GD witness.
No verifier or numerical allocation is used.

Fix an integer m>1, lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m),
a=(1-1/m)/c, d_j=1+a c^j, and H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j).
All parameters remain fixed within this horizon. Write N=2^m-1,
p_m(z)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-d_j z)^(2^(m-j-1)), and let p_m^-(z)
be the polynomial of H_m with its ORIGINAL last step d_0 deleted.
Thus p_m=(1-d_0 z)p_m^- as a polynomial identity.

The old candidate22347ffeb25f8830 concerned fixed c=13/5, a=c^(-17),
steps a c^j (without the added1), the FULL H_m queried prefix, and an
APPENDED unit step. Its Section7 really did use a common cycle and allowed
joint repair of individually illegal modes. The issue is its hypotheses,
not separability of that proof.

## An explicit failure of the supposedly safe sector bound

Set z_m=1-5/m+2i/sqrt(m). For m>25 its parameters satisfy

    alpha=1-5/m, sigma=|z_m|^2=1-6/m+25/m^2,
    kappa=alpha-sigma=1/m-25/m^2>0.

Consequently z_m lies inside the cocoercivity disk sigma<alpha. Also
alpha/|z_m| tends to1 and is at least2/3 for all sufficiently large m.
Nevertheless

    log|p_m^-(z_m)| >= 2^m/(3m)                     (A)

for all sufficiently large m. In particular the old purely polynomial
estimate |z||p_m(z)|^2=O(c^(-m)) on this disk/sector is FALSE for the
new word, even with a constant allowed to depend on no other parameter.

Here is a full asymptotic proof with uniform remainder control. For the
parameters of each horizon extend d_j to all j>=0 and define

    A_j=d_j/(d_j-1)=1+1/(a c^j),
    L_m(z)=sum_(j>=0)2^(-j-1) log|1-d_j z|.

The series converges whenever the finitely many factors near1 are nonzero:
its terms grow at most linearly in j, whereas its weights decay geometrically.
For large m, a is bounded away from0 and all A_j<=4. At z=1,

    L_m(1)=log a+log c=log(1-1/m).

Put u_m=z_m-1. Since |u_m|=O(m^(-1/2)), |A_j u_m|<=1/2 for all j
and sufficiently large m. The power series of log(1+v) has remainder
after v-v^2/2 bounded in modulus by 2|v|^3 when |v|<=1/2: bound
sum_(k>=3)|v|^k/k by |v|^3/(1-|v|). This proves UNIFORMLY in j that

    log|1-d_j z_m|=log(a c^j)
              +Re(A_j u_m-A_j^2 u_m^2/2)+O(m^(-3/2)).

The weights sum to1. With D_m=sum 2^(-j-1)A_j and
J_m=sum 2^(-j-1)A_j^2, the exact geometric sums are

    D_m=1+1/[a(2-c^(-1))],
    J_m=1+2/[a(2-c^(-1))]+1/[a^2(2-c^(-2))].

As Re u_m=-5/m and Re u_m^2=-4/m+25/m^2, it follows that

    m L_m(z_m) -> -1-5D+2J=-4-D1+2D2,
    D1=lambda^2/(2lambda-1),
    D2=lambda^4/(2lambda^2-1), D=1+D1, J=1+2D1+D2.

This limit is strictly greater than3/5. Indeed 12/5<lambda<5/2;
t^2/(2t-1) increases for t>1, so D1<25/16<8/5. Likewise
t^4/(2t^2-1) increases for t>1, so
D2>20736/6575>31/10 (the last inequality is 207360>203825).
Therefore -4-D1+2D2>-4-8/5+62/10=3/5.
For sufficiently large m this gives L_m(z_m)>=1/(2m).

To pass to the ACTUAL finite product, note that |z_m| stays bounded and
c stays in a fixed compact interval in (2,infinity), while a is bounded
above and away from0. For j>=m and large m,

    log|1-d_j z_m| <= C0+j log c

with one absolute C0. Hence

    2^m sum_(j>=m)2^(-j-1)log|1-d_j z_m|
                                  <=C0+(m+1)log c.

It follows that log|p_m(z_m)|>=2^m/(2m)-O(m). The deleted factor
|1-d_0 z_m| tends to lambda^(-1)>0; its logarithm stays bounded.
Since m^2/2^m tends to0, (A) follows.

In particular kappa |p_m^-(z_m)|^2 also grows without bound. This is
ONLY a scalar polynomial statement. Neither this mode nor a mixture
containing it has been proved legal by this calculation.

## Other nontransferable interfaces

The old scale argument began at least seventeen small geometric levels
before reaching |z|h~1. Here d_0 tends to sqrt(2), so this assertion fails
for fixed nonzero spectral parameters. The old benchmark estimate used
c^3>16 to obtain a vanishing ratio; now c_m tends to lambda<2^(4/3),
and even a correctly proved O(c_m^(-m)) bound requires its leading
constant to be compared with the exact benchmark.

Finally the retained prefix has length N-1, ending BEFORE the original
last d_0 step. The original free displacement is x_(N-1)-d_0 g_(N-1),
not a unit step from the end of full H_m. Any new cycle and completion
estimate must use those actual indices. No whole-normal conclusion on
the new family is obtained from the old proof.

evidence:
# Source interface audit and an exact directed-certificate obstruction

Status: complete candidate counterexample to a specified coefficient move,
NOT verifier-accepted. It does not disprove reversal or certificate re-selection.
No numerical or verifier call.

## Source checked and exact applicability limit

Yoon--Grimmer, *A Theory of Composition and Duality of Extremal Optimal
Fixed-Point Algorithms*, arXiv:2605.02231v2, Sections2.1--2.4,3.1--3.2,
4.1--4.2.2, https://arxiv.org/html/2605.02231v2 . The complete HTML was
downloaded into this worker's downloads directory and extracted to text.
The definitions, inverse-matrix statement, and tree/path proof of Theorem4
were read. Matlas title/theorem search returned unrelated results, so no
Matlas grounding of this exact theorem is claimed.

The source's Theorem4 characterizes H-dual optimality for optimal VERTEX
algorithms for nonexpansive fixed-point residuals. Its arcs form a tree,
with one edge from each nonterminal vertex to a larger vertex. Its certificate
matrix is symmetric: a negative undirected Laplacian with one diagonal
anchor. The inverse transform takes order-reversed discrete differences;
noncrossing controls their signs. Those hypotheses do not identify an
arbitrary intrinsic GD multiplier array with the source's unique certificate.

## Own exact obstruction to diagonal symmetrization of a supplied array

For any n>=2, take the physical schedule h_i=1 for i=0,...,n-1. Define
Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 with the actual unit-step GD
substitution, and

 V=2sum_(i<n)(f_i-f_n)-n(n+1)||g_n||^2.

Every gradient g_0,...,g_n is a formal independent vector. Put d_k=g_k-g_(k+1).
The ordinary adjacent coefficients

 lambda^0_(k,k+1)=2(k+1)^2,
 lambda^0_(k+1,k)=2(k+1)(k+2)

give the exact full identity

                  V+sum lambda^0_ij Q_ij
                       =sum_(k<n)(k+1)^2||d_k||^2.       (1)

Here is a direct check. Their net forward flow across edge k is -2(k+1),
so the values cancel V. On a unit step, the forward Q has gradient part
-(1/2)||g_k||^2+(1/2)||g_(k+1)||^2-<g_k,g_(k+1)>, while the reverse Q
has part (1/2)||g_k||^2+(1/2)||g_(k+1)||^2. Their mixed coefficient is
-2(k+1)^2. The diagonal g_0 coefficient is1; at an interior index k it
is k^2+(k+1)^2; at n, after adding V, it is n^2. These are exactly (1).

Now modify just four ORIGINAL ordered coefficients:

 Delta lambda_01=-2,
 Delta lambda_10=-1,
 Delta lambda_02=1,
 Delta lambda_12=-1.                                    (2)

All actual coefficients remain nonnegative: the affected entries become
lambda_01=0, lambda_10=3, lambda_02=1 and lambda_12=7. The reverse edge
lambda_21 remains12, and all later adjacent entries retain their positive
values. Every other entry is zero. This is valid for every n>=2, including
arbitrarily many positive steps.

The added value flow is zero at nodes0,1,2 individually, and elsewhere no
coefficient changes. Direct expansion on the first two unit steps gives

          -2Q_01-Q_10+Q_02-Q_12=<d_0,d_1>.               (3)

For example the corresponding Q_02 gradient part is
-(1/2)||g_0||^2-<g_0,g_1>+(1/2)||g_2||^2-<g_0,g_2>,
which together with the adjacent formulas verifies every coefficient of
(3). Thus the FULL repaired ordinary certificate remainder is

 M=||d_0||^2+<d_0,d_1>+4||d_1||^2
                                  +sum_(k=2)^(n-1)(k+1)^2||d_k||^2
  =||d_0+d_1/2||^2+(15/4)||d_1||^2
                                  +sum_(k=2)^(n-1)(k+1)^2||d_k||^2.
                                                                  (4)

This is PSD on all original independent gradients and strictly positive
in the difference coordinates, with only the constant-gradient kernel.

Nevertheless no positive row/column diagonal rescaling of this ACTUAL
multiplier array can make it symmetric. Its support contains the directed
edge1->0 with weight3, but the reverse edge0->1 has weight0. Multiplication
on the left and right by strictly positive diagonal matrices preserves
that asymmetry of zeros, whereas any symmetric matrix must have symmetric
off-diagonal support. This also excludes diagonal similarity, positive
congruence, and destination weighting as ways to turn the given array
directly into an undirected nonnegative Laplacian.

In particular, the destination weights p_i=i+1 forced by the affine-kernel
identity produce mu_10=3 and mu_01=0. They do make a circulation, but do
not make the graph reversible or undirected. The distinction is substantive.

## What remains open

This is a failure of a SPECIFIED map on a supplied valid certificate.
The SAME schedule also has the adjacent certificate (1), whose destination-
weighted array is symmetric. Hence this example explicitly cannot disprove
existence of a different well-structured certificate, general reversal, or
the same-schedule credit repair conjecture. It shows why weighted circulation
alone cannot import the source's symmetric anchored-graph theorem.

An application of that theorem still needs a proved selection or nonlinear
transformation that matches the intrinsic V functional, preserves all actual
coefficient signs and the full PSD form, and supplies the source's optimal-
vertex/graph hypotheses. Merely noticing a graph in both settings supplies
none of these missing steps. The source is used only for this scope audit;
the construction (1)--(4) has a complete independent proof above.

gradient; we verify that fact against every normal now.

At the endpoint of the first ordinary block, multiply normal values by M.
The current value is (qR_0^2-x^2-s^2)/A^2.
The future values are x^2/(AB), -ws/A^2, and s/(At).
Equation(1) gives

    qR_0^2=(1+A/B)x^2+s^2+A s/t,

which dominates every one of these and zero.

At the endpoint of the next block, the current value is
(Qx^2-u^2)/B^2. Its future values are
(u^2/B-ws)/A and s/t.
Equation(1) implies BOTH required inequalities

 Qx^2>=(1+B/A)u^2-(B^2/A)ws,
 Qx^2>=u^2+B^2s/t.

The old p_0 normal is nonpositive.

At the endpoint of the third block, the current value is
(qu^2-Aws-w^2)/A^2. The final normal is (s+w/A)/t.
The first equation in(1) is exactly

    qu^2=Aws+w^2+(A^2/t)(s+w/A),

so this comparison holds with equality; zero and both old normals are
nonpositive or dominated. At the final phase t>=1 makes the p_3 normal
nonnegative; all older normals are nonpositive.

These endpoint tests cover EVERY actual query, not just the block ends.
During each block the current normal decreases affinely in the partial
ordinary mass. Every future normal that can be positive increases
affinely or stays constant. The only negative future normal, the p_2
normal in phase0, remains nonpositive throughout. Every old normal
stays nonpositive because its positive coordinate is exhausted and all
remaining proximal coordinates are nonnegative. Thus the block endpoint
is the worst of all actual partial times for each required comparison.

The simplex is triangular with positive diagonal. Its polar inequalities
force every coordinate of a minimizer to be nonpositive, so0 is the true
closest minimizer to R_0e_0, at squared distance R_0^2.
The original normalized terminal objective is exactly

    2F_C(x_end)/R_0^2=(2Mt-2M+1)/(M^2t^2 R_0^2)>0.       (2)

The exact total physical mass is
h_tot=4(M-1)+3+M(2q+Q).
The original primitive defect is also explicit:

 V/R_0^2=1-[(Mt-(M-1)+h_tot)/(Mt)]^2/R_0^2.               (3)

No claim that(2) attains the benchmark is made.

Finally, every adjacent correlation is strictly negative:

 <p_0,p_1>=-x^2/(M^2AB),
 <p_1,p_2>=-u^2/(M^2AB),
 <p_2,p_3>=-w/(M^2At).

But the remote correlation is strictly positive,

    <p_0,p_2>=sw/(M^2 A^2)>0.

At the HIGH phase1, the older sum contains only T_0p_0, so

 <T_0p_0,p_2>=sw/(MA)>0,
 <X_1,p_2>=-sw/(MA)<0.

Equivalently Delta_02=-sw<0. Thus the high-history sign is NOT automatic
for positive transfers, even with all adjacent correlations nonpositive
and all original queries belonging to the same fixed smooth convex function.

The remaining construction task is to make this genuine older-preload
credit survive at many scales with useful normalized payoff. This finite
control does not accomplish that amplification; its role is to prevent
the proved conditional obstruction from being mistaken for a closure of
all positive shared-coordinate flows.

author: max4
claim: At EVERY n>=4 there is an explicit actual ordinary unit-step intrinsic certificate, with full positive-square remainder and symmetric destination-weighted circulation, whose correctly grounded G,G source certificate fails the Shu-Wang inverse-difference coefficient-sign test. The source G,G performance and q>0 hypotheses are checked, the reduced matrix is invertible, and transformed row/column sums have the correct signs, but one actual off-diagonal is negative. This closes automatic inverse transformation of every supplied certificate; it does NOT disprove reversal or alternate-certificate re-selection.
evidence:
# An actual inverse-certificate sign obstruction at every length n>=4

Status: a complete candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. No solver or
fact_submit call. This disproves an automatic transformation of EVERY supplied
certificate; it does not disprove existence of a different certificate for a
reversed schedule. The schedules here have unit steps and no capacity advantage.

## 1. Actual intrinsic input, with a full square certificate

Fix n>=4, h_i=1 for 0<=i<n, D=n+1. Use normalized smoothness1,
x_(i+1)=x_i-g_i, and the project's ORIGINAL inequalities

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.

The intrinsic energy is

 V_h=2sum_(i<n)(f_i-f_n)-n(n+1)||g_n||^2.

Start with the adjacent multipliers

 lambda^0_(k,k+1)=2(k+1)^2,
 lambda^0_(k+1,k)=2(k+1)(k+2),   0<=k<n.

They give exactly

 V_h+sum lambda^0_ij Q_ij=sum_(k<n)(k+1)^2||g_k-g_(k+1)||^2. (1)

For a direct check, Q_(k,k+1) has gradient part
-||g_k||^2/2-<g_k,g_(k+1)>+||g_(k+1)||^2/2 and the reverse Q has
(||g_k||^2+||g_(k+1)||^2)/2. The flows are -2 at each i<n and
2n at n; substituting these two quadratic parts gives (1).

Make the following perturbation, with epsilon=1/10, leaving all other
entries unchanged:

 (i,j)       delta lambda_ij
 (0,1)       -2 epsilon/3
 (1,0)       -4 epsilon/3
 (1,2)       -11 epsilon/6
 (2,1)       -11 epsilon/4
 (2,3)       -3 epsilon/4
 (3,2)       -epsilon
 (0,2)       epsilon/3
 (2,0)       epsilon
 (1,3)       epsilon/4
 (3,1)       epsilon/2.

Every resulting multiplier is nonnegative. The changed entries are
lambda01=29/15,10=58/15,12=469/60,21=469/40,23=717/40,
32=239/10,02=1/30,20=1/10,13=1/40,31=1/20.
The perturbation has zero value flow at each node. Expanding the four
distance-two Q terms and the six adjacent ones gives the full identity

 V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij=M(g),                            (2)

 M(g)=(59/60)||g0-g1||^2+(1/60)||g0-g2||^2
      +(929/240)||g1-g2||^2+(1/80)||g1-g3||^2
      +(143/16)||g2-g3||^2
      +sum_(k=3)^(n-1)(k+1)^2||g_k-g_(k+1)||^2.

For example Q_(i,i+2) has gradient part
-||g_i||^2/2-<g_i,g_(i+1)>-<g_i,g_(i+2)>+||g_(i+2)||^2/2;
its reverse has (||g_i||^2+||g_(i+2)||^2)/2+<g_(i+2),g_(i+1)>.
These formulas verify every diagonal and cross coefficient in (2).
All weights in M are positive, so it is PSD on ALL n+1 independent
gradients, with kernel consisting of constant gradient lists.

There is even a reversible destination-weighted circulation. Put p_i=i+1
and mu_ij=lambda_ij p_j. Then mu_ij=mu_ji. Indeed the adjacent unperturbed
weights are 2(k+1)^2(k+2), while the changes in these symmetric weights are
-4epsilon/3,-11epsilon/2,-3epsilon on the first three adjacent pairs,
and +epsilon on each of the crossing pairs {0,2} and {1,3}.

## 2. A grounded matrix from an ACTUAL gradient-gradient certificate

Let e be the all-ones vector of dimension n+1 and e_n its last coordinate
vector. Write hbar=(1,...,1,0), and let L be the row Laplacian of lambda:
L_ij=-lambda_ij for i!=j, L_ii=sum_(j!=i)lambda_ij. Define

 K=L+diag(hbar)-hbar e_n^T+I.                           (3)

This is not an arbitrary matrix attached by analogy to the source. It is
the exact grounding of the following performance certificate. Prepend one
physical step D+1 to the unit schedule, index its initial query by a,
write u=g_a, and keep indices 0,...,n for the tail. Thus x0=xa-(D+1)u.
Define J=sum_(i<n)Q_(i,n) and G=sum_(i<n)Q_(i,a)+Q_(n,a).
Direct expansion using x_n=x0-sum_(i<n)g_i gives

 V_h-[G+D Q_(a,n)+J]=D^2(||u||^2-||g_n||^2).           (4)

One way to check (4) is to expand its values, and then use
2sum_(i<n)<g_i,sum_(j<i)g_j>=||sum_(i<n)g_i||^2-sum_(i<n)||g_i||^2;
all cross terms cancel. Substitution of (2) into (4) yields

 D^2(||u||^2-||g_n||^2)+sum Gamma_ij Q_ij=M(g).         (5)

Here every ACTUAL nonnegative multiplier is specified:
Gamma_(i,j)=lambda_ij+1_(i<n,j=n) inside the tail,
Gamma_(i,a)=1 for all i=0,...,n, and Gamma_(a,n)=D.
Coincident tail entries are added. There are no other edges.
Its row and column flows are equal: the extra incoming-terminal tail
flow is +1 at i<n and -n at n, the edges to a add +1 at every tail node,
and the edge a->n contributes -D at n and +D at a. Combining with
the intrinsic flow (-2,...,-2,2n) cancels every node.

Grounding the negative row Laplacian of Gamma by deleting a gives exactly
-K. Equivalently, for U=[-e^T;I], its complete balanced matrix is

                         U(-K)U^T.                    (6)

Here K e=e and K^T e=D e_n. Its off-diagonals are nonpositive and each
row is strictly diagonally dominant, with surplus1. In particular K is
invertible: if K v=0, choose a coordinate of maximal absolute value;
the row equation and strict diagonal dominance force that value to be0.

## 3. Precise match to the source matrix and performance setup

Primary source inspected locally, including the relevant proof:
Shu--Wang, A Unified Theory of H-Duality in First-Order Methods,
arXiv:2609.03281v1, Sections2.2--2.5,4.4,4.5, Theorem3/Corollary3.
https://arxiv.org/html/2609.03281v1

Their P is cumulative-sum times reversal, hence P^(-1)=Delta, where

 Delta_ij=1_(j=n-i)-1_(j=n-i-1), 0<=i,j<=n,            (7)

with out-of-range terms0. Their reduced G,G embedding in Theorem3 is
U=[-e^T;I]. (The prose just after the embedding definitions swaps two
labels; Theorem3, its proof, and Corollary3 explicitly use U for G,G.)
Their signed-matrix convention has nonnegative off-diagonal entries and
nonpositive row and column sums. The normalization of their slack is
one half of each squared performance term when their rate tau=1.

Consequently the reduced source input supplied by (5) is exactly

                      R=-K/(2D^2),                     (8)

with the full G,G coefficient matrix U R U^T. Its performance is the
gradient-norm bound for the physical schedule (D+1,1,...,1), with n+1
steps, at rate1. It has the required signs and full PSD slack M/(2D^2).

The source states its G,G/D,D congruence for strong-convexity parameter
q>0, so that hypothesis must also be checked. Let y_i denote the physical
query, s_i its physical gradient, X_i=y_i-s_i, and z_i=s_i-q X_i.
For q=0 the source slack equals M/(2D^2) by (5). For every q>=0 the
same matrix has slack

 M/(2D^2)+(q/(4D^2))sum_(i,j)Gamma_ij||X_i-X_j||^2>=0. (9)

This follows by substituting z=s-qX into tr(z^T U R U^T X) and using
the balanced flow of Gamma. It is a formal PSD identity, so it proves
the source hypothesis for every q>0 (equivalently mu=q/(1+q)>0), not
merely for a convex limit. The algorithm matrix has the physical steps
on its first subdiagonal, so its antitranspose reverses their order.

The source's exact inverse transformation applied to (8) is therefore

 Phi_source=(P R P)^(-1)=2D^2 Phi,
 Phi=-Delta K^(-1) Delta.                              (10)

No source theorem is invoked to claim automatic signs. The congruence
would preserve the full unsigned slack, but its separate sign test is
the issue tested next.

## 4. A negative off-diagonal entry, exactly and at ALL n>=4

Define the vector v of dimension n+1 by

 v0=-169089/673492, v1=1434/673492,
 v2=-3/673492, v_i=0 for every i>=3.                    (11)

Direct multiplication by (3) gives

                         K v=e1-e0.                   (12)

Here only the first four rows need checking; their nonzero columns
relevant to v are

 [119/30, -29/15, -1/30],
 [-58/15, 329/24, -469/60],
 [-1/10, -469/40, 127/4],
 [0, -1/20, -239/10].

For the numerators in (11), these four row products are respectively
-673492,673492,0,0 before division by673492. Every later row is0
because all its neighbors have index>=3. This works unchanged for every
n>=4; the terminal column added in (3) multiplies v_n=0.

Row n-3 of Delta is (e3-e2)^T and column n-1 is e1-e0. Equations
(10)--(12) therefore give the off-diagonal entry

             Phi_(n-3,n-1)=-(v3-v2)=-3/673492<0.        (13)

The actual source coefficient is -3D^2/336746<0. Invertibility and the
row/column sign conditions are NOT the problem. To see the latter
explicitly, destination-weighted symmetry and the value flow give
L p=diag(p)(-2,...,-2,2n)^T. Hence

 K p=-D e+2D^2 e_n,
 K^(-1)e_n=(p+D e)/(2D^2),  e_n^T K^(-1)=e^T/D.

Since Delta e=e_n and Delta p=e, it follows that

 Phi e=-(e+D e_n)/(2D^2)<=0,
 e^T Phi=-e_n^T/D<=0.                                 (14)

Thus precisely an actual off-diagonal interpolation coefficient fails.
The n=4 exact rational audit contains all5x5 matrices, but (11)--(14)
are a uniform symbolic proof and do not rely on that computation.

## 5. Scope

Even an actual intrinsic ordinary certificate with a full positive square
remainder and a symmetric destination-weighted circulation need not have
legal coefficients after the source's canonical inverse-difference map.
The example has crossing weighted edges {0,2},{1,3}; no optimal-vertex
fixed-point assumption is being imported from Yoon--Grimmer.

The same unit schedule also has the unperturbed certificate (1), and its
reversal is itself. Accordingly this does NOT disprove general reversal,
general variable-matrix re-selection, or the existence of a sign-good
certificate for the same algorithm. It closes only the proposal that
source inverse signs hold for every supplied full intrinsic certificate.
Any successful use of that route must select a better certificate or
prove additional sign structure. The unit capacities n+1 are below the
primitive benchmark and yield no improving objective family.

claim; its three returned papers were unrelated and used for no premise.
The primary source was already downloaded and its definitions and proof
were read directly. Exact Fraction arithmetic checked the displayed
n=4 matrices and solution in under0.1 second; this is not an SDP call.

evidence:
# Symmetric re-selection is impossible across a nontrivial saturated cut

Status: candidate proof, NOT verifier-accepted. This is an existential
obstruction for a precisely defined certificate class, unlike the earlier
example of one badly chosen array. No general reversal claim is refuted.

Let a,b be positive step lists, allowing a to be empty but requiring b to
have at least one step. Put A=1+sum a, D=1+sum b, and choose r>0 such that
rT=AD, where T=A+D+r. Let h=(a,1+r,b), L the bridge query, and z the
terminal query. The prefix query set P ends at L; the tail query set B
starts immediately after the bridge and ends at z. All Q and V are the
original normalized quantities

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<z)h_i(f_i-f_z)+sum_(i<z)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                            -(T-1)T||g_z||^2.

Suppose lambda is ANY intrinsic signed certificate: value cancellation is
exact; the FULL matrix of V_h+sum lambda Q is PSD; and lambda_ij>=0
except that incoming-terminal coefficients lambda_(i,z) may be arbitrary.
This includes every ordinary certificate and every actual E_theta
certificate after replacing its terminal coefficients by lambda=Lambda-theta h.

Then, with kappa=T^2/D^2, every nonterminal tail query j satisfies

              lambda_(L,j)=0,
              lambda_(j,L)=(kappa-1)b_j>0.              (1)

In particular NO choice of intrinsic certificate for this schedule can
have symmetric support. No positive diagonal row/column scaling can make
its multiplier matrix, row Laplacian, destination-weighted circulation,
or canonical grounded G,G matrix symmetric. This remains true for the
actual E_theta array Lambda, since neither entry in (1) targets z.

## Self-contained derivation of the forced entries

First, use a one-dimensional Huber function and start sufficiently far
along its positive affine ray that all gradients are1. All finite Q are0
and V_h=0, since
2sum_i h_i sum_(t>=i)h_t=(sum h_i)^2+sum h_i^2.
Thus the all-ones vector belongs to the kernel of the full PSD remainder.

For a second legal run put eta=r/D=A/T, use the fixed scalar derivative
f'(x)=min(1,max(x,-eta)), integrate it with f(0)=0, and start at x0=A.
This derivative is nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz. For prefix query i let
R_i^a be its remaining prefix step sum; for tail query j let R_j^b be
its remaining tail step sum. Its exact data are

 x_i=1+R_i^a, g_i=1, f_i=R_i^a+1/2            (i in P),
 x_j=-eta(1+R_j^b), g_j=-eta,
 f_j=eta^2(R_j^b+1/2)                         (j in B).

Indeed the bridge takes1 to-r, and the tail ends at-eta. Substitution
into Q gives ALL cross residuals

 Q_(i,j)=-(1+eta)eta R_j^b,
 Q_(j,i)=-(1+eta)R_i^a,                        (i in P,j in B). (2)

Same-group residuals are0, and ALL incoming-terminal residuals are0.
At every query f_i=<g_i,x_i>-||g_i||^2/2, so telescoping squared
positions shows V_h=A^2-T^2 eta^2=0. Since each nonterminal-directed
coefficient is nonnegative, the full PSD remainder lies between0 and0
on this run. Every strictly negative residual in (2) must have zero
coefficient, including lambda_(L,j)=0 for every j in B\{z}.

The only cross edges possibly left are nu_i=lambda_(i,z), i in P,
and mu_j=lambda_(j,L), j in B. The two equality gradient vectors are
e_P+e_B and e_P-eta e_B. PSD and eta>0 imply M e_P=M e_B=0.
Write p=g_L, q=g_z, H_b=sum_(j<z,j in B)b_j g_j.
The entire mixed part of the quadratic remainder is

       -sum_(i in P)nu_i<g_i,H_b+q>
                          +r sum_(j in B)mu_j<p,g_j>.  (3)

This follows directly from the position term of Q and its squared
gradient difference; within-group terms have no mixed contributions.
For i<L, row i of M e_B is -D nu_i/2, so nu_i=0. The tail rows of
M e_P now yield mu_j=(nu_L/r)b_j for j<z and mu_z=nu_L/r.

Value flow is out_i-in_i=-2h_i for each i<z. Summing through P gives
sum_(j in B)mu_j-nu_L=2(A+r). Consequently

 nu_L=2r(A+r)/(D-r)=r(kappa-1),
 mu_j=(kappa-1)b_j,    mu_z=kappa-1.                   (4)

The equality uses rT=AD and kappa=T^2/D^2; it also implies r<D and
kappa>1. This proves (1) with every sign and full-kernel condition retained.

For any positive diagonal matrices C,E, entries (C lambda E)_(L,j)
and (C lambda E)_(j,L) are respectively0 and positive, hence cannot be
equal. Adding a diagonal to form a Laplacian does not change this pair.
The canonical grounded matrix K=L_lambda+diag(hbar)-hbar e_z^T+diag(w)
also leaves this NONTERMINAL pair unchanged, up to the negative sign of
the row Laplacian. Thus the same obstruction holds there and in its full
balanced G,G embedding. A simultaneous relabeling cannot fix support
asymmetry. This argument concerns all intrinsic certificate choices,
including a changed full PSD remainder.

## Nonvacuity at unbounded lengths

Take a to be k unit steps, k>=1, and b=(1,1). Then A=k+1, D=3,
r=(-A-3+sqrt((A+3)^2+12A))/2 and n=k+3 can be arbitrarily large.
Every such schedule HAS an ordinary full certificate. Here are complete
coefficients and the identity, independent of any unverified result.

For a unit list of length m, use adjacent weights
sigma_(i,i+1)=2(i+1)^2 and sigma_(i+1,i)=2(i+1)(i+2).
Direct expansion gives V+sum sigma Q=sum_(i<m)(i+1)^2||g_i-g_(i+1)||^2.
Embed these arrays separately as sigma^a,sigma^b. Keep sigma^a on P;
on B use kappa sigma^b plus (kappa-1)b_j on each j->z;
add (kappa-1)b_j on j->L for j<z, (kappa-1) on z->L,
and r(kappa-1) on L->z. Every coefficient is nonnegative.

To check the full identity, define
C=sum b_j Q_(j,L)+Q_(z,L)+r Q_(L,z)+sum b_j Q_(j,z).
Using the physical bridge1+r, its value part is
2sum b_j f_j+(r-D)f_L+(2-D-r)f_z, and its gradient part is
sum b_j(1-b_j)||g_j||^2+[(D-r)/2-r^2]||g_L||^2
                                             +(D+r)||g_z||^2/2.
Cross terms cancel on expansion. Since
(kappa-1)(D-r)=2(A+r), kappa r^2=A^2, kappa D^2=T^2,
one obtains V_h=V_a+kappa V_b-(kappa-1)C.
Adding exactly the displayed coefficients leaves the full PSD remainder
M_a+kappa M_b. Thus the all-certificate asymmetry obstruction is nonvacuous
for this positive-step family at every n>=4.

At k=1 this is h=(1,2,1,1); the forced pairs include
lambda12=0,lambda21=3 and lambda13=0,lambda31=3 for EVERY intrinsic
certificate of the stated type. The ordinary full certificate previously
displayed for this h illustrates existence but is not needed as a premise.

## Exact scope of the closure

This excludes the proposal to re-select an intrinsic certificate and then
diagonally symmetrize it in order to apply a symmetric fixed-point arc
theorem. It does not exclude a nonsymmetric noncrossing theorem, another

claim: Stronger than fixed-remainder failure: for ANY schedule with h0=1, every value-cancelling intrinsic full matrix satisfies M00=1 and M0n=-lambda0n/2. Hence if the supplied lambda0n<0, EVERY ordinary repair has an INDEFINITE difference M_new-M, even if both endpoint matrices are PSD. evidence:
# Any ordinary repair in this family has an indefinite matrix change

Status: candidate, NOT verifier-accepted. Strengthens the fixed-remainder
obstruction4aaee6131a92da0e; it does not disprove general PSD-preserving repair.

## The boundary invariant

Fix ANY nonnegative schedule h of length n>=1 whose first step is h0=1.
Let lambda be any real intrinsic multiplier array cancelling all formal
function values, and let M be the FULL formal gradient matrix of

 V_h+sum lambda_ij Q_ij,
 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 x_i=x0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,
 V_h=2sum_(i<n)h_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2
                                        -s(s+1)||g_n||^2,
 s=sum h_i.

Write L for the row Laplacian of lambda and A for the lower triangular
matrix with diagonal1 and entries A_it=h_t for t<i. Direct expansion
of Q and the value flows gives

 M=diag(h_i(2-h_i),-s(s+2))+sym(L A).

Since h0=1, column0 of A is the all-ones vector, so column0 of L A
is zero. Consequently

                         M00=1,
                         M0n=-lambda_0n/2.             (1)

More generally, twice the off-diagonal portion of row0 of M equals
the corresponding portion of row0 of L A. Let M_new come from any other
value-cancelling intrinsic array on the SAME h. If M_new-M is positive
OR negative semidefinite, its00 entry is0 by (1), hence its entire
row0 is0. To see this without an external lemma, restrict its quadratic
form to e0+t e_j; a nonzero linear term in t contradicts either sign
near t=0. Invertibility of A then implies that row0 of L_new-L is0.
Thus EVERY outgoing coefficient lambda_(0,j) is unchanged by any
semidefinite-ordered matrix change.

In particular, if lambda_0n<0 and lambda_new is ordinary, then
lambda_new,0n>=0 implies (M_new-M)0n!=0 while (M_new-M)00=0.
The corresponding2x2 principal determinant is strictly negative.
Therefore M_new-M has both a positive and a negative eigenvalue.
This holds for EVERY ordinary repair, regardless of its other coefficients
and regardless of how far its full PSD matrix is allowed to move.

## An explicit credited input at every n>=2

For completeness the input family is rederived here, rather than using an
unverified finding as a premise. Take h=(1,...,1), epsilon=theta=1/n,
d_k=g_k-g_(k+1). The ordinary adjacent array

 lambda^0_(k,k+1)=2(k+1)^2,
 lambda^0_(k+1,k)=2(k+1)(k+2)

has remainder M0=sum_(k<n)(k+1)^2||d_k||^2 by expanding the adjacent Q.
Modify it by

 delta lambda01=n epsilon, delta lambda10=(n-1)epsilon,
 delta lambda0n=-epsilon, delta lambda1n=epsilon.

When n=2 the last change is added to its existing adjacent edge. The
changes have zero value flow. Their full quadratic sum is

 -epsilon<d0,sum_(k=1)^(n-1)(n-k)d_k>.

For a direct expansion, the left side before taking differences is
epsilon<g0-g1,sum_(j=1)^n g_j-n g1>. Thus the remainder is exactly

 M=sum_(k=1)^(n-1)(k+1)^2
       ||d_k-epsilon(n-k)d0/[2(k+1)^2]||^2
   +[1-epsilon^2/4 sum_(k=1)^(n-1)(n-k)^2/(k+1)^2]||d0||^2. (2)

The last coefficient is greater than3/4: use epsilon=1/n,
(n-k)^2<n^2, and
sum_(j=2)^n 1/j^2<sum_(j=2)^n 1/[j(j-1)]<1.
So the full matrix is PSD and is positive definite on gradient differences.
The sole negative intrinsic coefficient is lambda0n=-1/n.

For the ACTUAL E_theta=V_h-theta sum_(i<n)h_i Q_(i,n) certificate, use
Lambda_(i,n)=lambda_(i,n)+theta h_i and keep every other entry. All
actual coefficients are nonnegative, including Lambda0n=0; their added
terminal terms cancel the credit and leave (2). The ordinary certificate
lambda^0 already displayed proves that ordinary repair DOES exist.
Nevertheless its difference from this input, and the difference of EVERY
other ordinary repair from it, is indefinite by (1).

## Which routes this closes

A general repair cannot insist on keeping the matrix fixed, adding only
PSD remainders, subtracting only PSD remainders, or taking a sequence of
matrix changes all ordered in the same Loewner direction. The obstruction
already holds for arbitrarily long unit schedules and theta=1/n tending0.
It does NOT prohibit a path whose endpoint matrices are PSD and whose
individual differences are indefinite. Such a genuine matrix change is
exactly what a viable general repair must allow.

Its negative subspace has dimension2^(m-3)-1 with x0=x_n=g_n=g_(n-1)=0, so no initial-distance inflation, endpoint-only correction, final-step replacement using the same array, or PSD patch of smaller rank can repair it.
