evidence:
# Direct objective gluing on the actual critical words

Status: UNVERIFIED joint calculation and certificate-space obstruction.
No solver and no fact_submit. The negative formal vectors below are NOT legal
smooth-convex trajectories. They refute a specified full multiplier array and
its stated repairs, not the schedule or the original profile conjecture.

The only mathematical predecessor used is accepted fact
`1252b8823bb5a290` for interpolation, and `b98bb807d514e80d` for the
Huber/cut witnesses and the exact benchmark recursions. The recursive pattern
was suggested by Altschuler--Parrilo, arXiv:2309.16530, Theorem 3.4; all
identities needed here are derived below rather than imported from it.

## 1. Normalization and a fully specified multiplier array

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. For every sample let

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0,
    C_ij=-2 Q_ji
        =2(f_i-f_j)+2<g_j,x_j-x_i>-||g_i-g_j||^2 >=0.

Every position is substituted using the actual GD steps. In the full formal
quadratic, x_0,g_0,...,g_n are independent; they are not restricted to any
chosen primal family.

Fix positive numbers a,c, with c>2. Write

    d_j=a c^j,  H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+d_j,H_j),
    n_j=2^j-1, S_j=sum H_j, M_j=1+S_j.

Throughout this calculation require d_j<M_j at the levels being used.
Define the following exact scalar recurrence:

    Z_0=1, t_0=1,
    z_j=(M_j+d_j)/(M_j-d_j),
    r_j=1+2z_j=(3M_j+d_j)/(M_j-d_j),
    Z_(j+1)=r_j Z_j,
    t_(j+1)=(1+sqrt(4 Z_(j+1)-3))/2,
    delta_j=Z_j-r_j d_j^2.                              (1)

Thus Z_j=t_j^2-t_j+1. All r_j>1, so the square roots are real and
t_j>=1. This fixes every parameter; there is no numerical optimization.

Here is the actual nonnegative array lambda^(j) on C_ij. Its base has only
lambda^0_(star,0)=1. Suppose its block has length n=n_j, sum S=S_j,
and put p=n, q=2n+1, b=1+d_j, z=z_j, r=r_j, t=t_j, t'=t_(j+1).

1. Embed the old array on the left sample indices {0,...,p,star}.
2. Add r times the old array on {p+1,...,q,star}.
3. For each right queried index i=p+1,...,q-1, whose physical step is h_i,
   add z h_i to entries (p,i) and (q,i), and subtract 2z h_i from (star,i).
4. Add the following six sparse corrections:

    (p,q): z,                 (q,p): z d_j,
    (p,star): -S,             (q,star): 2S+b-rS,
    (star,p): b-t,            (star,q): t'-rt.           (2)

The corrections individually may be signed, but the FINAL array is
nonnegative. In fact its optimum entries are exactly

    lambda_(star,i)=h_i for i<q,
    lambda_(star,q)=t',
    lambda_(i,star)=0 for i<q,
    lambda_(q,star)=2S+b.                                (3)

To verify this inductively, left interior entries are unchanged, the old
left terminal entry t becomes b, right interior entries become
(r-2z)h_i=h_i, and the right terminal entry becomes t'. Incoming optimum
entries at the left terminal cancel, and the right terminal entry becomes
2S+b. Every other update either embeds a nonnegative old coefficient or
adds z h_i, z, or z d_j. This proves actual coefficient signs, including
all optimum edges, rather than just signs of an auxiliary matrix.

## 2. Complete identity and calibration

There is an exact gradient-only remainder E_j, defined on all the formal
gradients of the block, such that

    ||x_start||^2-||x_end-t_j g_end||^2-2t_j f_end
       =sum lambda^(j)_ik C_ik + E_j.                  (4)

Its recursion is

    E_0=0,
    E_(j+1)=E_j(left)+r_j E_j(right)
                         +delta_j ||g_p||^2.            (5)

Here each child is evaluated at its actual chronological sample indices.
In particular E_j contains no terminal-gradient term of its own: its
variables are only the midpoint gradients of all internal recursion nodes.

We verify (4)--(5) without omitting any function coefficient. Denote the
left endpoint and gradient by x,g and the right endpoint and gradient by
y,v. Their values are f,F. The weighted right displacement is

    w=sum_(p<i<q) h_i g_i=x-bg-y.

The rank-one correction in step 3 sums to

    2zS(f+F)-zS(||g||^2+||v||^2)
                         -2z<w,x+y-g-v>.               (6)

Combine the two child identities, the correction (6), and (2). The
coefficient of f is

    2[(z-1)S-b+z-zd_j]=0,

because z(S+2-b)=S+b. The coefficient of F is -2t', and every
interior value has already canceled within its child and (6). The
optimum value is zero under normalization; before normalization the
total value flow cancels it against the terminal coefficient.

The x^2, <x,g>, <x,v>, <y,g>, and <g,v> coefficients all cancel.
The remaining expression is

    ||x_start||^2-||y-t'v||^2-2t'F
       +(r d_j^2-Z_j)||g||^2
       +(Z_(j+1)-r Z_j)||v||^2
       -E_j(left)-r E_j(right).

The last gradient coefficient is zero by (1). This is exactly (4)--(5).
This calculation also follows by direct expansion of (6); the cancellations
use only z(S+2-b)=S+b and r=1+2z.

The calibration is exact. Set lambda=1+sqrt(2), a=1/lambda, c=lambda.
Then M_j=lambda^j, d_j=lambda^(j-1), z_j=lambda, r_j=lambda^2,
Z_j=M_j^2, and delta_j=0 at every level. Thus E_j=0 and (4) is a
valid full initial-distance certificate at the undeformed silver word.
It is the canonical endpoint-square guarantee, not a claim that this
particular certificate attains the sharper Huber constant.

For an arbitrary real q_cert, the SAME nonnegative array supplies the
following fully value-canceled candidate objective matrix:

    q_cert ||x_0||^2-2 f_n
       +sum_(i!=k) [2 lambda^(m)_ki/t_m] Q_ik
     =(q_cert-1/t_m)||x_0||^2
       +[||x_n-t_m g_n||^2+E_m]/t_m.                 (7)

This explicitly includes the true initial vector and the optimum index.
Its validity as an upper bound depends on FULL PSD of the right side.

## 3. An exact negative midpoint for the assigned parameters

Now set m>=128, epsilon=1/m, and use the assigned family

    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/c.

For these parameters 2<c<3 and 0<a<c-2<1. The exact mass formula is

    M_j=A c^j+(1-A)2^j,  A=a/(c-2),                 (8)

so 0<A<1 and M_j-d_j=A(3-c)c^j+(1-A)2^j>0.
Thus every coefficient in the proposed array is defined and nonnegative.

Nevertheless delta_2<0. Here is a finite exact proof with an explicit
parameter interval, not a limiting differential equation. Put s=sqrt(2).
For j=0,1,2, write r_j=N_j/D_j, where

    N_0=(2+s)+(4-s)epsilon,
    D_0=(2-s)+s epsilon,
    N_1=(4+3s)+(9-3s)epsilon-epsilon^2,
    D_1=s+(3-s)epsilon+epsilon^2,
    N_2=(10+7s)+(19-5s)epsilon-(4+s)epsilon^2
                                                 -(1+s)epsilon^3,
    D_2=(2+s)+(5-3s)epsilon+s epsilon^2
                                                 +(1+s)epsilon^3.

All denominator coefficients are positive. Since d_2=lambda(1-epsilon^2),

    delta_2=P(epsilon)/(D_0 D_1 D_2),
    P=N_0 N_1 D_2-lambda^2(1-epsilon^2)^2 N_2 D_0 D_1.

The coefficients of P, in increasing degree 0 through 10, are

    0,
    -112-96s,
    -96-84s,
    640+12s,
    528+368s,
    88+92s,
    -320-167s,
    -202-158s,
    -2-4s,
    42+30s,
    10+7s.                                           (9)

These coefficients follow by multiplying the displayed degree-at-most-three
polynomials. A tiny exact Q(sqrt(2)) polynomial multiplication independently
checked the list; the displayed identity is the mathematical evidence.
Using s<3/2, the sum of absolute upper bounds for coefficients of degree
at least two is 3311. Consequently, for 0<epsilon<=1/128,

    P(epsilon)/epsilon
       <=-112-96s+3311 epsilon
       <-112+3311/128<0.                             (10)

For comparison, the first derivative is

    delta_2=-(48+28sqrt(2))epsilon+O(epsilon^2).

The same negative coefficient occurs at the finite diagnostic m=3:

    P(1/3)=(-1059632-2141552sqrt(2))/59049<0.

The three relevant denominators are positive there as well. This agrees
with failure of the ARRAY even though max3's unrestricted numerical H_3
diagnostic reported a Huber match. That diagnostic is not used as a premise.

## 4. Negative FULL formal directions, and limits of repairs

Every occurrence of a level-two midpoint contributes

    omega_i delta_2 ||g_i||^2

to E_m, with omega_i>0, a product of right-child weights r_j from its
ancestors. There are K=2^(m-3) such indices. Their actual step is the same
number b_2=1+d_2. No other term of E_m uses any of those gradient
coordinates, by the diagonal recursion (5).

First choose one such index i, set x_0=0, g_i=v!=0, all other queried
gradients zero, and g_n=-(b_2/t_m)v. Then

    x_n=-b_2 v, x_n-t_m g_n=0, E_m=omega_i delta_2||v||^2<0.

Thus (7) is not PSD for ANY q_cert. Merely increasing the initial-distance
coefficient does not repair the proposed array.

There is a larger obstruction when m>=4. Work first with scalar formal
gradients, put x_0=g_n=0, allow arbitrary g_i at the K selected indices
subject to sum_i g_i=0, and set every other gradient to zero. This is a
subspace D of dimension K-1 on which

    x_n=0, g_(n-1)=0,
    E_m=delta_2 sum_i omega_i g_i^2<0

for every nonzero vector. The weights need not coincide. It follows that:

* Any added quadratic depending only on x_0,x_n,g_n,g_(n-1) vanishes on D.
* Replacing only the final physical step leaves every position unchanged
  on D, because g_(n-1)=0. With the same array, the negative evaluation
  persists for every prescribed final-step replacement and every q_cert.
* Any PSD matrix addition of rank less than K-1 has a nonzero kernel vector
  in D, by dimension counting, and therefore cannot repair the full matrix.

The last statement is about additions to this fixed matrix. Changing
relative interpolation multipliers may have an indefinite difference and
is NOT excluded. Likewise a correction of growing rank is not excluded.
The selected vectors deliberately do not satisfy the interpolation
constraints; no legal lower witness, no W upper bound, and no impossibility
theorem for H_m is inferred.

## 5. Fixed-constant deformations: the same ansatz always fails for tau>0

Consider the allowed neighboring family

    c=lambda(1+tau/m), a=(1-sigma/m)/c,                (11)

with fixed real tau,sigma, for all sufficiently large m. Positivity and
d_j<M_j hold uniformly over the word once 0<a<1 and 2<c<3: indeed

    M_j/d_j=1/(c-2)
               +[1/a-1/(c-2)](2/c)^j

lies between 1/a and 1/(c-2), both greater than one.

If tau>0, the specified multiplier recursion always develops a negative
coefficient at a FIXED level as m tends to infinity. If sigma+tau<0,
then d_0>1/lambda and delta_0=1-r_0 d_0^2<0, since
d maps to d^2(3+d)/(1-d) is strictly increasing for 0<d<1 and equals
one at d=1/lambda.

For sigma+tau>=0 the fixed level j=4 suffices. To show this, temporarily
regard epsilon as a real variable tending to zero and set

    u=2/lambda, D=sigma+(1+lambda^2)tau,
    T_j=lambda^2 tau-D u^j.

Differentiation at epsilon=0 of the explicit finite formulas gives

    M_j(0)=lambda^j,
    (d/depsilon)log M_j |0=j tau-D(1-u^j),
    (d/depsilon)(d_j/M_j)|0=(1/lambda)T_j.

For r(x)=(3+x)/(1-x), (d/dx)log r at x=1/lambda equals 2.
Using 1-u=1/lambda^2 and
2(1/lambda-1/lambda^2)/(1-u)=2sqrt(2), equation (1) therefore gives

    (d/depsilon)[delta_j/M_j^2]|0
       =2sqrt(2)[tau(j-lambda^2)-D(1-2u^j)].          (12)

One can also verify (12) by summing the finite geometric series for T_j.
At j=4, 4-lambda^2<0 and 1-2u^4>0. The latter follows from
u^4=272-192sqrt(2)<1/2; squaring 543<384sqrt(2) verifies it with
positive sides. Moreover D>=lambda^2 tau>0. Thus (12) is strictly
negative. The expression is an analytic finite rational function near
zero, so delta_4<0 for every sufficiently large m. This uses a derivative
at one fixed finite depth, not an unproved continuum recurrence.

The same full-vector argument as in Section 4 then excludes the array and
its stated endpoint or fixed-rank patches. This generalization does not
exclude a different full certificate for any of the deformed schedules.

## 6. Rechecking the exact comparison and an actual deformation filter

Set rho=log_2(lambda). From the accepted exact recursions, primitive shifted
mass C_n=S_circle(n)+1 has join

    Omega(A,B)=(A+B+sqrt((A+B)^2+4AB))/2,

and the benchmark B_n has join

    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

Here is a proof of C_n<=(n+1)^rho and B_n<=1+4n^rho, retained rather
than assuming the earlier draft comparison. Define F(t)=(1+t)^rho-1.
For t=exp(z), direct differentiation gives

    d^2/dz^2 log F(exp(z))
      =rho t(1+t)^(rho-2)
        [(1+t)^rho-1-rho t]/F(t)^2>0.

The numerator bracket is positive since rho>1 and its derivative is
rho[(1+t)^(rho-1)-1]>0. Convexity at z,-z gives
F(t)F(1/t)>=F(1)^2=(lambda-1)^2=2. With A=t^rho B and
E=(1+t)^rho B, this implies (E-A)(E-B)>=2AB, so

    Omega(A,B)<=(A^(1/rho)+B^(1/rho))^rho.

Induction in the primitive recursion gives its claimed bound. Also
G(A,D)<=4A+D. If k+l+1=n, the dominant induction now gives

    B_n<=1+4[(k+1)^rho+l^rho]<=1+4n^rho.

The last inequality follows from superadditivity of t^rho on nonnegative
arguments, which follows by integrating its increasing derivative.

For (11), the exact mass formula (8) gives

    M_m/lambda^m
      =(1+tau/m)^m [A+(1-A)(2/c)^m] -> exp(tau).       (13)

Thus the actual benchmark satisfies

    limsup B_(2^m-1)/(2M_m-1)<=2 exp(-tau).             (14)

In particular tau=1 recovers 2/e. This comparison alone is not an
objective upper bound; the failed matrix in Section 4 cannot supply one.

There is also a useful LOWER bound for the exact benchmark. Balanced
primitive joins give C_(2^j-1)>=lambda^j. Put b_0=1 and

    b_(j+1)=G(1,b_j)/lambda.

Balanced dominant joins imply B_(2^j-1)>=b_j lambda^j. The map in this
recursion is strictly increasing. Its fixed point above one is

    b_infty=sqrt(2)(1+lambda^(-1/2))>2.                (15)

To verify the fixed point, squaring the equation G(1,b)=lambda b
gives lambda(lambda-1)b^2-4lambda b+4=0; the positive root (15)
satisfies the original equation, whereas the smaller algebraic root does
not. Alternatively uniqueness above one follows because
G(1,b)/b=2/b+1/2+sqrt(1+8/b)/2 is strictly decreasing. Since
1<b_1=4/lambda<b_infty, monotonicity shows b_j increases to b_infty.

This yields an ACTUAL legal-witness filter even when the final step is
replaced arbitrarily. Let P_m=S_m-(1+d_0) be the sum of the queried prefix
before that final step, and prescribe any b_m>=0. For P_m>=1, the two
accepted Huber/cut witnesses give

    W_(n_m)(H_m with final step b_m)
       >=max{1/(2P_m+2b_m+1),
                    (b_m-1)_+^2/(P_m+1)^2}
       >=1/(2P_m+3+2sqrt(P_m)).                       (16)

For b_m<=1+sqrt(P_m), the first term proves (16). For larger b_m, the
second is at least P_m/(P_m+1)^2, which is at least its right side
because P_m^2+P_m+2P_m sqrt(P_m)-1>=0 for P_m>=1.
Equations (13), (15), and (16) prove the uniform statement

    liminf_m B_(n_m) W_(n_m)(modified word)
                     >=b_infty/(2 exp(tau)).           (17)

Consequently no fixed asymptotic separation below the benchmark is possible
within these fixed-constant deformations, even with an arbitrary final step,
when tau<=log(b_infty/2). This is a legal lower-bound conclusion for that
parameter region. It is distinct from the formal-matrix obstruction for
tau>0, and does not settle the assigned tau=1 family.

## 7. A richer exact join, with the unresolved full-matrix issue exposed

The following calculation records the next concrete repair interface. It
does not assert that a scalar local condition closes the target.

Replace the canonical child storage by

    I=||x_start||^2-||x_end-u0 g_end||^2-2v0 f_end
       =sum lambda C+E,
    Z=(u0-1)^2+v0,
    k=S+u0-v0>=0.

Assume its optimum entries are h_i on (star,i), u0 on the terminal
(star,end), zero on other (i,star), and k on (end,star); retain the
ENTIRE gradient remainder E. These properties hold for the calibrated
canonical family. They are assumptions of this interface, not all full
certificates.

Use two nonnegative correction weights A0,B0. Scale the right child by
r=1+A0+B0. For each right queried i add A0 h_i on (p,i), B0 h_i on
(q,i), and -(A0+B0)h_i on (star,i). Choose cross coefficients p0,q0>=0
with

    p0-q0=b+(1-A0)S.

Adjust optimum entries to physical h_i, terminal u1, and
k1=2S+b+u1-v1>=0 exactly as in (2), with child k in place of S.
Thus the actual final array is nonnegative provided the named scalar
coefficients and u1,k1 are nonnegative. Put

    d=b-1, M=S+1, t=A0-B0,
    H=M+d-B0(M-d)-t M,
    ell=p0-B0-t,
    Z1=(u1-1)^2+v1,
    V=x_p-x_q-g_p+g_q.

Full coefficient expansion, including all function values, gives

    E_new=E_left+r E_right
       +t||V||^2+2<V,(H-ell)g_p+ell g_q>
       +(Z-rd^2)||g_p||^2+(rZ-Z1)||g_q||^2.           (18)

For example the canonical construction sets A0=B0=z, p0=z,
q0=zd, H=ell=t=0 and Z1=rZ, recovering (5).
To check (18), first use D=x_p-x_q. The local coefficients of
D^2, D g_p, D g_q are t,-2(ell+t-H),2(ell+t).
Substituting D=V+g_p-g_q makes the g_p g_q coefficient zero and gives
exactly the displayed diagonal and cross terms. The value coefficient
at p is 2[(A0-1)S-b+p0-q0]=0 and the terminal coefficient is -2v1.

Demanding the isolated three-vector matrix in (18) be PSD is only a
SUFFICIENT restriction. It forces Z>=rd^2 and Z1<=rZ, and risks
repeating the already recorded scalar-deficit failure. The useful open
question is whether the FULL child remainders can pay for an indefinite
local term.

There is a finite exact way to retain that information for this array
class. Define the gradient moment z_block=sum h_i g_i+g_end. If a child
remainder is decomposed into nonnegative internal squares plus the sharp
two-variable form

    a0||z_block||^2+2b0<z_block,g_end>+c0||g_end||^2,

then the parent remainder before elimination is the explicit four-variable
form, in L=z_left, g=g_p, R=z_right, e=g_q,

    a0||L||^2+2b0<L,g>+c0||g||^2
      +r[a0||R||^2+2b0<R,e>+c0||e||^2]
      +t||d g+R||^2+2<d g+R,(H-ell)g+ell e>
      +(Z-rd^2)||g||^2+(rZ-Z1)||e||^2.                (19)

The parent moment is exactly z_parent=L+d g+R. Substituting
L=z_parent-dg-R and completing squares in g,R gives its next
two-variable form when the corresponding eliminated block is PSD and
the cross columns lie in its range. Negative eliminated directions are
full-matrix obstructions and must not be dropped. This is an explicit

no choice of its free parameters or uniform constant establishing the

evidence:
# C52: the two tail energies in the pending bipartite history branch

Status: unverified necessary-condition derivation and a counterexample to
one proposed simplification. No new solver or verifier call. This does not
close the bipartite class and does not assert that the relaxed example is
an interpolable full trajectory.

The C50 numerical batch is closed. C51 supplies its exact finite candidate.
The following is an analytic continuation of C48 with arbitrarily many
phases, rather than another fixed graph enumeration.

## 1. Real vectors and necessary terminal-normal constraints

There are K low/odd phase pairs, with indices 2j,2j+1 for 0<=j<K.
The last odd phase is terminal. Every ordinary block has total step mass
M-1, M>=1. Low phases have total phase length MA, A=1+q, q>0;
nonterminal odd phases have total length MB_j, B_j=1+Q_j, Q_j>0.
These total lengths include the following checkpoint. The last odd phase
has artificial gradient scale Mt with t>=1 and has no checkpoint.

Use orthonormal coordinate vectors e_i and nonnegative target coefficients
beta_l and gamma_l. Low sources have weights u_j>=0,
with u_0>0, and send u_j beta_l to every odd coordinate 2l+1 with l>=j.
Nonterminal odd sources have weights v_j>=0 and send v_j gamma_l to
every even coordinate 2l with l>j. Set

    U_j=sum_(i<j)u_i, U'_j=U_j+u_j,
    V_j=sum_(i<j)v_i,
    Y_j=sum_(l>=j)beta_l^2,
    X_j=sum_(l>=j)gamma_l^2,        j>=1,
    U_fin=U'_(K-1).

For j>=1 the mass at even coordinate 2j is V_j gamma_j. At odd
coordinate 2j+1 it is U'_j beta_j. The actual phase gradients are

    p_(2j)=[V_j gamma_j e_(2j)-u_j sum_(l>=j)beta_l e_(2l+1)]/(MA),
    p_(2j+1)=[U'_j beta_j e_(2j+1)-v_j sum_(l>j)gamma_l e_(2l)]/(MB_j).

At the root replace V_0 gamma_0 by the independent initial mass R0>0.
At the terminal phase use p_last=U_fin beta_last e_last/(Mt).
Subtracting each phase length times its gradient removes its current
coordinate and creates the stated inherited masses at the next phase.

If all the projection normals hold for these actual vectors, they are
gradients of the fixed function

    F_C(x)=max_(p in C)(<x,p>-||p||^2/2),
    C=conv(0,p_0,...,p_last).

Projection nonexpansiveness proves that this is a convex differentiable
1-smooth function with minimum at zero. All future normals, not just
those retained below, are required for this realization.

Assume beta_last>0 and put D_tail=U_fin beta_last^2/t>0. At the last
query of a low ordinary block, the comparison with the terminal vertex
gives

    q V_j^2 gamma_j^2
       >=u_j(AU_j+u_j)Y_j+A(AU_j+u_j)D_tail, j>=1.          (1)

At a nonterminal odd block, its corresponding comparison gives

    Q_j (U'_j)^2 beta_j^2
       >=v_j(B_j V_j+v_j)X_(j+1)+B_j^2 U'_j D_tail.         (2)

At the root it gives

               q R0^2>=u_0^2 Y_0+A u_0 D_tail.             (3)

For clarity these are direct normal calculations, not consequences of a
previous unverified claim. At a low endpoint, after multiplying the
normal height by M, the own height is
[q V_j^2 gamma_j^2-u_j(AU_j+u_j)Y_j]/A^2.
Its inner product with the terminal gradient, with the same scaling, is
(U_j+u_j/A)D_tail. This proves (1). At an odd endpoint the own height is
[Q_j(U'_j)^2 beta_j^2-v_j(B_jV_j+v_j)X_(j+1)]/B_j^2;
the terminal height is U'_j D_tail. This proves (2). The same root
calculation, with U_0=0 and initial mass R0, gives (3).

For a legal member with D_tail>0, (1) forces V_j gamma_j>0 for j>=1,
because U_j>=u_0>0. Likewise (2) forces every nonterminal odd mass
U'_j beta_j>0. All diagonal coordinate masses are therefore positive.
The polar inequalities <p_i,z><=0 imply z_i<=0 by backward induction,
starting with the terminal coordinate. Hence zero is the actual closest
minimizer to R0 e_0, with squared distance R0^2.

## 2. An explicit all-horizon positive transfer

For positive denominators set

    a_j=v_j(B_jV_j+v_j)/(Q_j(U'_j)^2),
    b_j=B_j^2/(Q_j U'_j),
    c_j=u_j(AU_j+u_j)/(q V_j^2),
    d_j=A(AU_j+u_j)/(q V_j^2).

Equations (1)--(2) imply the ordered backward inequalities

    Y_j>=Y_(j+1)+a_j X_(j+1)+b_j D_tail,
    X_j>=X_(j+1)+c_j Y_j+d_j D_tail.                       (4)

Thus the tail vector (X_j,Y_j) is bounded below by

    [[1+c_j a_j,c_j],[a_j,1]] (X_(j+1),Y_(j+1))
                       +(c_j b_j+d_j,b_j)D_tail.          (5)

All entries are nonnegative and the matrix determinant is one. The
terminal data are X_K=0, Y_(K-1)=beta_last^2=D_tail t/U_fin;
there is no odd transfer equation (2) at the terminal phase. Equation
(1) still applies to its preceding low phase. Apply the corresponding
low step first, then (4) for preceding pairs. Equations (3)--(5) give
a fully explicit lower bound on the actual initial squared norm for
every source-weight sequence and arbitrary number of phases.

If Yhat_0 is the lower bound on Y_0/D_tail produced by this ordered
affine recursion, the original prescribed-terminal objective obeys

  2F_C(x_end)/R0^2
    <=q(2Mt-2M+1)U_fin/[M^2 t(u_0^2 Yhat_0+A u_0)].        (6)

Indeed the terminal coordinate starts at U_fin beta_last, moves for
ordinary mass M-1 with gradient U_fin beta_last/(Mt), and hence its
objective is (2Mt-2M+1)(U_fin beta_last)^2/(2M^2t^2).
Divide by (3). This bound is only for the stated prescribed terminal;
no claim about all free terminal completions is made.

The full nonterminal normal inequalities have not been eliminated. A
small value of the right side of (6) is a valid exclusion for this class;
a large value supplies no actual hard function by itself.

## 3. Why source growth does not telescope through one tail alone

A tempting simplification was to make U'_j Y_j nondecreasing in the
backward direction at every odd phase with negative older history.
The following exact local example refutes that inference from (4).

Put s=sqrt(2), lambda_s=1+s,

    q=s-1, A=s, Q=lambda_s^3=7+5s, B=1+Q,
    U'_j=1, V_j=1, v_j=9, u_(j+1)=1,
    U'_(j+1)=2, V_(j+1)=10,
    D_tail=1, Y_(j+1)=1000, X_(j+2)=0.

Choose the next low coordinate and current odd coordinate at equality:

    x=gamma_(j+1)^2
      =[(lambda_s^2)/100]*1000+(4+3s)/100,
    X_(j+1)=x,
    Y_j=1000+[9(Q+10)/Q]x+(Q+1)^2/Q.                     (7)

These satisfy the two retained terminal-normal equations exactly.
The coefficient of 1000 in Y_j is

                 (37+108sqrt(2))/100 < 1339/700 < 2.       (8)

The additive term is less than 19: Q>14 gives
9(Q+10)/Q<108/7, (4+3s)/100<9/100, and
(Q+1)^2/Q=2+10s<17. Thus Y_j<2000 and

                  U'_j Y_j<U'_(j+1)Y_(j+1).              (9)

The older-history sign is nevertheless negative. Its numerator is

    V_j V_(j+1) gamma_(j+1)^2
                           -U'_j u_(j+1)Y_(j+1)=10x-1000<0,

because lambda_s^2<6 gives x<60+9/100. The parameters q and Q are
the critical low ratio and the level-four high ratio; the strict
inequalities persist in a neighborhood of them.

This is a counterexample to the proposed scalar monotonicity inside the
necessary-condition relaxation. It is not advertised as a full legal
projection transcript. For consistent terminal-anchor data one may set
t=2000, so D_tail=U_fin beta_last^2/t=1 when the next odd phase is
terminal with U_fin=2 and beta_last^2=1000. Other earlier-query normals
would still have to be checked for any global realization.

Consequently the C48 continuation must retain both tails in (5), or
exploit the still-retained future nonterminal normals. Negative-history
source growth by itself has not provided the uniform normalization
charge needed for an asymptotic witness-class bound. The full-target
upper and lower questions remain open.

## 1. The actual family and the scope of the claim

For integers m>=128 put lambda=1+sqrt(2), c_m=lambda(1+1/m),
a_m=(1-1/m)/c_m, d_j=1+a_m c_m^j, H_0=(), and

Choose ANY w_m in [0,1] and ANY real matrix T_add,m with two columns,
without an upper bound on its entries or number of rows. Set
R(v)=(Re v,-Im v)^T and define actual Euclidean vectors

      sqrt(1-w_m) Re P_i(z_2),sqrt(1-w_m) Im P_i(z_2),
      T_add,m R(P_i(z_1)-P_i(z_2))),
 g_i=(sqrt(w_m) Re[z_1 P_i(z_1)],sqrt(w_m) Im[z_1 P_i(z_1)],
      sqrt(1-w_m) Re[z_2 P_i(z_2)],sqrt(1-w_m) Im[z_2 P_i(z_2)],

Then ||x_0||=1 and x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i g_i exactly. The added coordinates

recovers the whole proposed modela0f6a1f128f59b70, with every rho>=0 and

## 2. A single shared two-anchor interpolation inequality

 F(x_q) <= <g_q,x_q>+<g_r-g_q,x_r>
                 -||g_r||^2/2-||g_q-g_r||^2/2.           (4)

function value at r cancels. Drop the two nonnegative squares.

before and after the unique largest bridge d_(m-1). Average (4)

 mu_r=sum_(j>=1)2^(j-1)(delta lambda^(-j))^r

This is a warning about extrapolation, not a proposed arbitrary-Gram
research program. For a positive schedule of length n>=1, select ANY
n+1 distinct positive real nodes theta_j, even inside an arbitrarily
small interval. Let P_i(z)=product_(t<i)(1-h_t z). The polynomials

                  1, zP_0(z), ..., zP_(n-1)(z)          (7)

have successive degrees0,1,...,n and nonzero leading coefficients.
They form a basis of polynomials of degree at most n. Their evaluations
at the n+1 distinct nodes are an invertible square matrix: a linear
combination vanishing at all nodes would be a polynomial of degree at
most n with n+1 roots, and hence zero; its basis coefficients must vanish.

proof of accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290.

The completed two-mode bound controls a fixed four-dimensional temporal

by the candidate proof. A new direction must change the temporal span or

evidence:
# A finite all-horizon obstruction to a root dispersion transfer

Status: **unverified candidate**, cumulative round 14. No solver or verifier
call. This is a class obstruction and a counterexample to the adequacy of two
primal tests, not a resolution of the unrestricted asymptotic problem.

The only accepted premises are the exact P/B recurrences and the explicit
single-cut lower bound in `b98bb807d514e80d`, and the actual canonical Huber
construction in `0be8b54e0a33381c`. All further algebra is proved here. The
source words coincide with arXiv:2410.12395v2 Definitions 4.1/4.3, but no
external closure theorem or earlier unverified finding is a proof premise.
Matlas was queried for related rotation results and returned unrelated hits.

## Statement

Put rho=1+sqrt(2), a=sqrt(2)-1. Let p^(n),d^(n) be the exact primitive and
dominant words selected by always choosing the SMALLEST maximizing split in
the accepted recurrences, and then using the actual bridges phi and psi.
In detail P_n=1+S_circle(n), B_n=1+2S_bullet(n), P_0=B_0=1,

    P_n=max_k Omega(P_k,P_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_k G(P_k,B_(n-k-1)),
    Omega(A,E)=(A+E+sqrt((A+E)^2+4AE))/2,
    G(A,D)=2A+D/2+sqrt(D^2+8AD)/2.

An empty word has mass 1. A primitive parent of masses A,E has word
(left,phi(A-1,E-1),right). A dominant parent of masses A,D has word
(primitive left,psi(A-1,(D-1)/2),dominant right). This is a finite exact
recursive algorithm, with all choices made before querying a function.

For EVERY n>=2, its dominant root has a nonempty primitive prefix. Write
that root as

    d^(n)=(p^(k),1+d,d^(l)),   k>=1, l=n-k-1,
    A=P_k, D=B_l, B_n=G(A,D).

Select the first occurrence of sqrt(2) in that prefix. There is at least
one. For any real t in (0,1], define the actual new word h^(n,t) by changing
only this selected entry and the root bridge:

    sqrt(2)  ->  1+a(1-t),
    1+d      ->  1+(1+t/2)d.                         (1)

Every new step is nonnegative, in fact at least one. Both the canonical
Huber payoff and the payoff of f(x)=x^2/2 decrease strictly below 1/B_n,
yet the actual worst-case value obeys

    B_n W_n(h^(n,t))
      >= (1+t/2)^2 [A/(A-a t)]^2
      >  (1+t/2)^2.                                (2)

In particular, the fixed deformation t=1/2 is defined at every horizon
n>=2 and satisfies

    B_n W_n(h^(n,1/2)) > 25/16.                    (3)

This is an exact obstruction with a uniform finite interval of allowed
deformations. It applies to ANY full multiplier/remainder array at the new
word, including new positive optimum-source coefficients, new interpolation
edges, and higher-rank remainders. It is a legal primal obstruction, not a
restriction of certificate support.

## 1. No empty maximizing dominant prefix for n>=2

For A>0,z>=0 define

    T_A(z)=(z+sqrt(z^2+8A))/2.

Then sqrt(G(A,D))=T_A(sqrt(D)), and T_A is increasing in A and z, as follows
directly from the formula. We prove the strict rotation inequality

    T_(Omega(1,A))(z) > T_1(T_A(z))   for A>=1,z>=1. (4)

Put C=Omega(1,A), u=T_A(z), v=T_1(u). The defining quadratics give

    C^2=(A+1)C+A,
    u^2=z u+2A,  u>=2,
    v(v-u)=2.

Consequently

    u^2(C+1)-2C^2
       =z u(C+1)-2C >=2(C+1)-2C=2>0.

Let r=v/u>1. Then r(r-1)=2/u^2, while
(1+1/C)(1/C)=(C+1)/C^2. Since r(r-1) is strictly increasing for r>=1,
the preceding strict inequality implies r<1+1/C. Therefore

    v(v-z)/2 = A v/u+1 < A(1+1/C)+1=C.

The positive root of w(w-z)/2=C is T_C(z); the polynomial is strictly
increasing for w>=z. Since v>z, the last inequality proves (4).

Suppose k=0 were a maximizing split for a horizon n>=2. Choose an actual
maximizing split j of its nonempty right child at horizon n-1, and let
A=P_j, D=B_(n-j-2). Its root value would be G(1,G(A,D)). But
P_(j+1)>=Omega(1,A), because that is one allowed primitive split. The
alternative root split j+1 at horizon n has value

    G(P_(j+1),D) >= G(Omega(1,A),D) > G(1,G(A,D)),

by (4). This contradicts maximality. Thus k>=1 for every maximizing tree,
independently of the specified tie rule. No eventually fixed or dyadic
maximizing pattern has been assumed.

Every nonempty finite primitive binary construction has an internal node
whose two children are empty: choose an internal node of largest depth.
Its bridge is phi(0,0)=sqrt(2), so the selected occurrence exists. Since
all other steps are nonnegative, A>=1+sqrt(2)=rho.

## 2. Exact product and root identities

For a primitive parent put C=Omega(A,E), d_P=phi(A-1,E-1)-1. Substitution
gives C=A+E+d_P and d_P C=AE. Inducting from the empty word yields

    product_(i in p^(n)) |1-h_i|=1/P_n.             (5)

At a dominant join let r=(1+sqrt(1+8A/D))/2. Direct substitution gives

    d=A/r,
    r^2-r=2A/D,
    G(A,D)=D r^2,
    2d^2+Dd=AD.                                    (6)

Inducting from its empty word, the dominant product is
d/(A sqrt(D))=1/sqrt(G(A,D)). Thus

    product_(i in d^(n)) (1-h_i)^2=1/B_n,
    d^2/(A^2 D)=1/B_n.                              (7)

All source steps exceed one. In particular the product contribution of the
selected prefix entry is a>0, and that of the root bridge is d>0.
We need the strict inequality d>2a. For the polynomial
F(z)=2z^2+Dz-AD, which is strictly increasing at z>=0 and vanishes at d,
use A>=rho, D>=1 to obtain

    F(2a)=8a^2-D(A-2a)
          <=8a^2-(rho-2a)=21-15sqrt(2)<0.

The last inequality follows from sqrt(2)>7/5, proved by squaring. Hence
d>2a, as required.

## 3. The two decreasing tests

The change (1) increases the physical step sum by

    Delta s=t(d/2-a)>0.                             (8)

The exact canonical Huber instance for the NEW word consequently has
normalized payoff

    1/[B_n+2t(d/2-a)] < 1/B_n.

The unit quadratic has x_0=1 and produces exactly the product of squared
step gaps. Using (7), its normalized payoff after (1) is

    [(1-t)(1+t/2)]^2/B_n < 1/B_n,                  (9)

because (1-t)(1+t/2)=1-t/2-t^2/2 belongs to [0,1) for t in (0,1].
These are actual, normalized legal instances. Their smaller values do not
give an upper bound on W_n of the changed word.

## 4. The legal cut that rules out every full-array continuation

Use the exact single-cut instance of accepted b98bb807d514e80d at the
ROOT bridge of the altered word. Its prefix mass is A-a t, the bridge
gap is (1+t/2)d, and its suffix mass remains D. That accepted construction
is valid for arbitrary nonnegative prefix and suffix steps, so it applies
to every chronological sample of (1). Its true initial distance is one,
its minimizer is zero, and its exact normalized objective payoff is

    ((1+t/2)d)^2 / [(A-a t)^2 D].                   (10)

For clarity, its derivative at smoothness one is
max(-c_minus,min(c_plus,x)), with

    c_plus=1/(A-a t),
    c_minus=c_plus(1+t/2)d/D,
    x_0=1.

The prefix has constant positive gradient c_plus, reaches x_p=c_plus,
and the bridge sends it to -D c_minus. All suffix gradients remain
-c_minus, so its final value is D c_minus^2/2. Thus (10) includes the
actual initial distance and does not reset at an intermediate point.

Multiplying (10) by B_n and using the second identity in (7) gives (2).
At t=1/2, (1+t/2)^2=25/16, proving (3). A valid full PSD upper
certificate q must satisfy q>=W_n, so no choice of its coefficients,
support, optimum incidences, or rank can yield q B_n<1 on this family.

## Scope and next interface

This eliminates a concrete gap-dispersion mechanism which escapes global
doubly stochastic averaging and the unchanged ConPD rule. Both source
children are genuine exact-benchmark words. The bridge and a primitive
leaf change, with a uniform relative bridge change at all horizons, and
the complete certificate may be reselected arbitrarily. The obstruction
uses one legal hard function and a fixed multiplicative gap.

It does not eliminate joint changes which also increase the root prefix
mass or sufficiently increase the suffix mass, nor arbitrary distributions
of changes across an unbounded set of scales. Such a candidate must pass
the root cut as well as the Huber/quadratic tests and must then establish
the full PSD continuation with a quantitatively useful radius. That
remaining uniform continuation is still OPEN.

# Actual Newton chronology: a birth chain and a joint covariance charge

Status: UNVERIFIED proof candidate and partial storage argument. The exact
coordinate identities and ordered-kernel result below are complete candidates.
The covariance domination in Section 5 is OPEN. In particular there is no
whole-interface error bound, no legal benchmark-scale construction, and no
resolution of the original exact-profile problem in this file. No optimization,
numerical experiment, installation, or fact submission was used in this round.

Accepted mathematical inputs: ordinary smooth interpolation and scaling in
fact 1252b8823bb5a290, and the benchmark definitions in b98bb807d514e80d.
The total-nonnegativity assertion also uses the explicitly identified and
audited published theorem in Section 3. No earlier unverified max2 result is
a premise: the identities needed for this argument are derived here.

## 1. The actual interface and notation

For an integer m>=128, put

 lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
 d_j=1+a c^j, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,d_j,H_j).

Set n=2^m-1 and q=n-1. The queried steps h_0,...,h_(q-1) are the word
H_m with its final d_0 deleted. The actual final step is b in [0,2]. Define

 s_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=s_q,
 p_ij=product_(t<i)(1-h_t/d_j),
 R_i=sum_(j<m)p_ij w_j, Z_i=sum_(j<m)d_j p_ij w_j,
 x_i=u-s_i v+Z_i, g_i=v+R_i, 0<=i<=q.

All these vectors use ONE arbitrary real PSD Gram matrix. The values f_i
form ONE array; the optimum jet is x_star=g_star=f_star=0; ||x_0||=1 is
the distance normalization relative to the chosen actual minimizer. Every
original queried inequality is retained:

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.       (1)

The first d_j occurs at step 2^j-1. Thus p_ij is positive before query
2^j and zero thereafter, and R_q=Z_q=0. The recursion gives

 Z_i-Z_(i+1)=h_i R_i, sum_i h_i p_ij=d_j.             (2)

Here and below unqualified time sums range over 0<=i<q.

For clarity about the original value budget, define

 C_min=f_q-<v,x_q>, eta=-C_min-||v||^2/2,
 delta_i=f_i-<v,x_i>-C_min-||R_i||^2/2.

On an actual legal function, tilting by -<v,x> makes x_q a minimizer;
the smooth optimum inequalities give delta_i>=0. Also eta>=0 follows
from Q_(q,star). Expanding Q_(0,star) gives the exact common budget

 eta>=delta_0+||R_0||^2+<v,R_0>-<R_0,x_0>.          (3)

No height is set to zero and neither eta nor the norm of x_0 is discarded.

## 2. A lossless stochastic change of coordinates

Define polynomials

 phi_k(z)=product_(r<k)(1-d_r z), 0<=k<=m.

Work modulo z phi_m(z), which has the m+1 distinct nodes
0,1/d_0,...,1/d_(m-1). The double zero in the position quotient leaves
exactly this simple-zero gradient quotient. Put

 V_k=v+sum_(j<m)phi_k(1/d_j) w_j, 0<=k<=m.

Then V_0=g_0 and V_m=v. This change from (w_0,...,w_(m-1),v) to
(V_0,...,V_m) is invertible: the evaluation matrix
phi_k(1/d_j), with columns ordered j=0,...,m-1, then the node0, is
upper triangular with strictly positive diagonal.

There are coefficients B_ik determined by B_00=1, B_0k=0 for k>0 and

 B_(i+1),0=(1-h_i/d_0)B_i0,
 B_(i+1),k=(1-h_i/d_k)B_ik+(h_i/d_(k-1))B_i,(k-1), 0<k<m,
 B_(i+1),m=B_im+(h_i/d_(m-1))B_i,(m-1).             (4)

Although an unused factor 1-h_i/d_k can be negative for a dead state,
it always multiplies zero. More precisely, if r_i distinct ruler levels
have occurred before query i, induction gives B_ik=0 for k<r_i.
The next step has level at most r_i, so h_i<=d_k on every occupied
state k<m. If it is the first d_(r_i), the mass at r_i moves entirely
to r_i+1. Consequently all B_ik are nonnegative, every row sums to one,
and after the first d_(m-1) the row is the point mass at state m.

The polynomial identity

 (1-hz)phi_k=(1-h/d_k)phi_k+(h/d_k)phi_(k+1)

for k<m, together with (1-hz)phi_m=phi_m modulo z phi_m, proves

 g_i=sum_(k=0)^m B_ik V_k.                           (5)

Thus B is exactly the marginal law of a time-inhomogeneous pure-birth
chain: from occupied state k<m it stays with probability 1-h_i/d_k
and advances one state with probability h_i/d_k; m is absorbing.
This probability space is auxiliary. No state vector V_k is assumed
to be a gradient at an additional sample of the legal function.

The positions are equally explicit. Let U_k=V_k-v and

 Y_k=sum_(r=k)^(m-1)d_r U_r, Y_m=0.

The conditional expected change of Y at step i is -h_i U_k when the
state is k. Hence sum_k B_ik Y_k changes by -h_i R_i. Initially

 Y_0=sum_k d_k U_k=sum_j d_j w_j=Z_0,

where the middle equality follows by telescoping
d_k phi_k(z)=(phi_k(z)-phi_(k+1)(z))/z at z=1/d_j.
Therefore

 Z_i=sum_k B_ik Y_k, x_i=u-s_i v+sum_k B_ik Y_k.      (6)

In particular the troublesome coupling remains, explicitly,

 <v,Z_0>=sum_(k<m)d_k<v,U_k>.                        (7)

Equations (5)-(6) preserve the original vectors, not just their norms.
Substitution in (1) gives EXACTLY

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j
   +<sum_k B_ik V_k, (s_i-s_j)v+sum_k(B_jk-B_ik)Y_k>
   +(1/2)||sum_k(B_ik-B_jk)V_k||^2.                  (8)

All earlier/earlier, suffix, and optimum conditions remain in this one
array. In particular (5) does not authorize independent state heights,
orthogonality of state vectors, or projected legality.

Two occupation identities retain quantitative physical costs:

 sum_i h_i B_ik=d_k,                                (9)
 sum_i s_(i+1)h_i B_ik=d_k sum_(r<=k)d_r, 0<=k<m.    (10)

To prove (9), sum the flow equation (4). State0 has initial mass1 and
final mass0, so its total outflow is1. Successive transient states have
equal total inflow and outflow, so their total outflows are also1.
For (10), write M_k=sum_i s_(i+1)h_i B_ik and M_(-1)=0.
Summation by parts gives

 sum_i s_(i+1)(B_(i+1),k-B_ik)=-sum_i h_i B_ik=-d_k.

Using (4), M_k/d_k-M_(k-1)/d_(k-1)=d_k, with the second term zero
at k=0. Induction proves (10). The terminal occupation is
sum_i h_i B_im=S-sum_(k<m)d_k; it is nonnegative and keeps the full
constant-gradient suffix in the budget.

## 3. Total nonnegativity for the ACTUAL chronological evaluations

This is a theorem about temporal coefficient matrices, not yet the
weighted energy matrix. It holds for arbitrary strictly increasing positive
levels d_0,...,d_(m-1) with the same ordered first-occurrence rule.

Let P be the matrix with chronological rows i=0,...,q and columns
p_i0,...,p_i,(m-1),1, in that order. Then P is totally nonnegative:
every square minor, with its inherited row and column order, is >=0.
The same is true of B, and of the jump matrix

 A_ij=(h_i/d_j)p_ij, 0<=i<q, 0<=j<m.                (11)

Every column of A sums to1 by (2).

External theorem used, with its local definitions made explicit:
David Galvin and Adrian Pacurar, *Total non-negativity of some combinatorial
matrices*, arXiv:1807.08658v3 (2019), Theorem1.2; published JCTA172 (2020),
105179. For a nondecreasing real sequence a_l, define C_ik by
product_(t<=i)(X-e_t)=sum_k C_ik product_(l<=k)(X-a_l).
Then C is totally nonnegative iff e is restricted growth relative to a:
the cap initially is a_1, an e_t below the cap leaves it unchanged,
an equality advances it to the next a_l, and exceeding it is forbidden.
The proof constructs a planar path matrix; zero pivots at cap hits move
all negative edge weights out of the network without changing its path
matrix. Disjoint-path determinant cancellation then proves the minor signs.

The exact PDF and extracted text were read, including Definition1.1,
Theorem1.2, the pivot lemmas3.7/3.9, and the complete proof of1.2.
Files: downloads/1807.08658v3.pdf and downloads/1807.08658.txt.
Matlas was queried repeatedly for this statement and title but did not
return the paper; the primary arXiv text, not a fabricated Matlas hit,
grounds this citation. No verifier acceptance is claimed for this application.

Here is the complete applicability check. Set

 a_1=-1/d_0<...<a_m=-1/d_(m-1)<a_(m+1)=0,

and continue the a sequence with zeros as far as necessary. Set
e_(i+1)=-1/h_i. A first occurrence of d_j is exactly a hit of the
current cap a_(j+1). Between first occurrences, every level is smaller
and hence its e is strictly below the next cap. After all levels have
appeared, every e is negative and the cap remains0. Thus the theorem's
restricted-growth condition is satisfied, with actual repetitions and
the actual deleted last d_0, not an ordered surrogate schedule.

Let N_k(X)=product_(r<k)(X+1/d_r), so
phi_k(z)=(product_(r<k)d_r)N_k(-z). The exact Newton expansion gives

 B_ik=(product_(t<i)h_t) C_ik/(product_(r<k)d_r),
 0<=k<=m.                                          (12)

The coefficients with k>m vanish upon evaluation at the m+1 nodes
-1/d_0,...,-1/d_(m-1),0. Positive row and column scaling and truncation
preserve all minor signs, proving that B is totally nonnegative.

For completeness the node-evaluation matrix V_kj=phi_k(1/d_j), with
the node0 last, is also totally nonnegative. After positive row scaling,
its transpose is L_jk=product_(r<k)(a_(j+1)-a_(r+1)). It is lower
triangular. In Neville elimination its pivot in row i,column k is

 product_(r=i-k)^(i-1)(a_(i+1)-a_(r+1))>0, i>=k.

Indeed the pivot is the ratio of determinants on consecutive rows
i-k,...,i and initial columns0,...,k, and on rows i-k,...,i-1 and
columns0,...,k-1. These determinants are Vandermonde determinants:
the monic Newton polynomials differ from monomials by a triangular
column change with diagonal1. Cancelling gives the displayed pivot.
All elimination multipliers are positive. Reversing the elimination
expresses L as a product of elementary lower bidiagonal matrices with
nonnegative off-diagonal entries and a positive diagonal matrix.
Each factor is totally nonnegative, as follows directly by expanding
its minors, and products preserve this property by Cauchy--Binet.
Thus V is totally nonnegative. Now P=BV, proving the assertion for P.
Finally A is a row and column positive scaling of P's residual submatrix,
so A has the asserted minor signs and stochastic column sums.

The chronological matrix has full column rank: the queries immediately
before first d_j, followed by any query after first d_(m-1), give a square
upper triangular evaluation submatrix with strictly positive diagonal.
Thus none of these representations has silently removed a modal direction.

## 4. Exact cancellation of ALL shared heights

Define the elapsed-time quadratic form

 J=sum_i [2s_(i+1)h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
          +s_(i+1)||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2].

The original interpolation inequalities have the algebraic identity

 ||x_0||^2-2S f_q+2sum_i h_i Q_(i,star)
       +2sum_i s_(i+1)Q_(i+1,i)=||x_q||^2+J.        (13)

To check it, GD gives
2sum_i h_i Q_(i,star)=2sum_i h_i f_i-||x_0||^2
 +||x_q||^2+sum_i h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2.
Also Q_(i+1,i)=f_(i+1)-f_i+h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
 +||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2/2. Summation by parts with s_0=0 and s_q=S
cancels the displayed common values and proves (13). All multipliers
are nonnegative. This is a sufficient certificate combination and does
not claim that its selected constraints are sufficient for legal data.

## 5. A Brownian-bridge covariance with the full diagonal cost

Put D_i=g_i-g_(i+1)=sum_j A_ij w_j, where A is (11). Define increasing
clock knots and nonnegative penalties

 beta_i=s_(i+1)(s_i+1), 0<=i<q,
 beta_q=S(S+1), beta_(-1)=0,
 c_i=(h_i-1)s_(i+1).

All h_i>1, so c_i>=0, and beta_0<...<beta_q. Expanding the squared
differences in J gives

 J=sum_(i=0)^q(beta_i-beta_(i-1))||g_i||^2
                          -sum_(i<q)c_i||D_i||^2. (14)

For example the coefficient of ||g_i||^2 at an interior node is
s_i(h_(i-1)+h_i)+h_i; that of ||g_q||^2 is S h_(q-1).
These are exactly the differences of beta in (14).

Since g_i=v+sum_(r>=i)D_r, changing the order of finite sums yields

 J=beta_q||v||^2+2<v,sum_i beta_i D_i>
        +sum_(i,l<q)beta_min(i,l)<D_i,D_l>
        -sum_i c_i||D_i||^2.

Define

 Kbr_(i,l)=beta_min(i,l)-beta_i beta_l/beta_q.

Completing the ONE constant-mode square proves the exact joint identity

 J=beta_q||v+(sum_i beta_i D_i)/beta_q||^2
       +sum_(i,l<q)Kbr_(i,l)<D_i,D_l>
       -sum_i c_i||D_i||^2.                         (15)

The kernel Kbr is a real covariance kernel. For a direct elementary
construction, take independent centered random variables xi_r of variances
beta_r-beta_(r-1), 0<=r<=q, let Z_i=sum_(r<=i)xi_r, and set
Zbr_i=Z_i-(beta_i/beta_q)Z_q. Direct expansion gives
E[Zbr_i Zbr_l]=Kbr_(i,l). Consequently Kbr is PSD. This use of
probability creates no randomness in the legal instance or its shared Gram.

The remaining sufficient claim is the EXPLICIT known-matrix domination

 A^T Kbr A >= A^T diag(c_i) A                        (16)

in the real PSD order, for the actual nearcritical ruler words. It is
equivalent to J>=0 on this temporal quotient, because the constant square
in (15) can be minimized by a freely chosen formal vector v. Every cost
is present, including all repeated small steps, the large-step penalties,
and the final constant-gradient suffix through beta_q.

Thus (16), IF PROVED, combines with (13) and ||x_0||=1 to give
2f_q<=1/S, and the ordinary smooth descent inequality then gives
2F(x_q-bv)<=1/S for every b in [0,2]. The previous draft's exact-B
comparison would have to be included in a complete eventual submission;
its conditional target constant is lambda/exp(1)<1. Neither (16) nor
that resulting whole-interface bound is asserted established here.

Equation (16) is a fixed, concrete covariance inequality on stochastic
Newton columns. It has no unknown interpolation multipliers or heights.
It remains a hard restricted weighted Hardy inequality, not a routine
check and not an equivalent restatement of the original all-h minimax goal.

## 6. Why total nonnegativity does NOT settle the energy sign

Here is an exact counterexample to that GENERIC implication. It is not a
counterexample to (16) for the actual m-dependent parameters.

Take levels t=3/2 and u_step=4 and the ruler word (t,u_step,t). On its first two
steps, choose the single residual column at rate1/u_step, namely

 g_0=1, g_1=5/8, g_2=0, v=0.

The post-annihilation third step contributes zero. The ordered Newton
matrix and birth matrix are totally nonnegative by the same construction
as above. Nevertheless the first step contributes

 2t^2(5/8)+t(3/8)^2+t(1-t)=291/128,

and the second contributes

 (t+u_step)(5/8)^2+u_step(1-u_step)(5/8)^2=-325/128.

Therefore J=-17/64<0. The hypotheses used to prove the temporal minor
signs all hold, but weighted-energy positivity fails. These scalar data
are a formal certificate test, not an asserted legal interpolation array.

Accordingly, a planar network for A cannot by itself be called a proof of
(16). A successful path argument must ALSO absorb the explicit costs c_i
using the actual relation between ruler levels and chronological mass.

### 6.1 Stronger test: keep the ACTUAL levels, step multiset and total mass

The insufficiency persists even when those scalar data are preserved.
Let t=d_0, u_step=d_1, d=d_2 be the ACTUAL parameters of Section1. The queried
word starts (t,u_step,t,d,...). Move that one intervening t just after d,
obtaining the permuted queried word

                 (t,u_step,d,t,...).

Every subsequent step is in its original order. The multiset, q, S, all
d_j, ordered first occurrences, and the final deleted d_0 are unchanged.
In particular the total-nonnegativity argument and occupation identities
(9)-(10) apply to this permuted word, too. It is deliberately NOT the
original chronological word in (16).

Use scalar modal vectors with v=0, w_j=0 for j>=3, and

 w_2=-1/[(1-t/d)(1-u_step/d)],
 w_1=[1-(1-t/d)w_2]/(1-t/u_step), w_0=-w_1-w_2.

All denominators are positive because t<u_step<d. On the permuted word the
gradients are exactly (0,1,-1,0,0,...). The common modal Gram is real PSD
of rank1. Direct substitution in J gives

 J=6t+6u_step-3u_step^2-2t u_step+2d-d^2.             (17)

Here the first step contributes t, the second contributes
4(t+u_step)-2u_step(t+u_step)+u_step(1-u_step), and the third contributes
t+u_step+2d-d^2; their sum is (17).

For a uniform exact sign, write epsilon=1/m and tau=sqrt(2). Then

 t=tau-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)]<=tau,
 u_step=2-epsilon, d=tau+2-lambda epsilon^2.

The expression (17) is increasing in t, since its t coefficient is
6-2u_step>0. Substituting tau for t, and comparing d with tau+2, gives

 J<=-2+(6+2tau)epsilon-3epsilon^2
                    +2lambda^2 epsilon^2-lambda^2 epsilon^4
   <-2+9epsilon+12epsilon^2<-19/10, m>=128.           (18)

The last strict inequality follows from
9/128+12/128^2=1164/16384<1/10. Thus actual levels, the original total
mass, stochastic column sums, total nonnegativity, and the exact first
occupation moments do NOT by themselves force the energy sign.

The example is explicitly illegal as interpolation data: g_0=0 and the
first GD step gives x_1=x_0, while g_1=1. Thus
Q_01+Q_10=||g_0-g_1||^2=1>0 for every choice of shared values. One may
set x_0=1 by choosing the free position offset u; that does not repair
the violation. No claim about W_n follows from this formal example.

As an algebraic illustration of the missing repeated-step storage, at
the limiting parameters t=tau, u_step=2, d=tau+2 the SAME modal vectors on
the original chronology have gradients

                 (0,1,-1,-(2-tau),0,...).

Their J is 2+4tau>0, whereas the permuted chronology gives J=-2.
Indeed the four original steps contribute respectively tau, -2,
4+3tau, and0. This comparison is only a fixed exact limiting identity;
it is not used as a proof at finite m or for arbitrary modal vectors.

## 7. Current proof state

Complete draft structure: lossless finite birth chain; invariant occupation

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0.       (1)

The first d_j occurs at step 2^j-1. Thus p_ij is positive before query
2^j and zero thereafter, and R_q=Z_q=0. The recursion gives

 Z_i-Z_(i+1)=h_i R_i, sum_i h_i p_ij=d_j.             (2)

Here and below unqualified time sums range over 0<=i<q.

For clarity about the original value budget, define

 C_min=f_q-<v,x_q>, eta=-C_min-||v||^2/2,
 delta_i=f_i-<v,x_i>-C_min-||R_i||^2/2.

On an actual legal function, tilting by -<v,x> makes x_q a minimizer;
the smooth optimum inequalities give delta_i>=0. Also eta>=0 follows
from Q_(q,star). Expanding Q_(0,star) gives the exact common budget

 eta>=delta_0+||R_0||^2+<v,R_0>-<R_0,x_0>.          (3)

No height is set to zero and neither eta nor the norm of x_0 is discarded.


Define the elapsed-time quadratic

 J=sum_(i<q)[2s_(i+1)h_i<g_(i+1),g_i>
       +s_(i+1)||g_(i+1)-g_i||^2+h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2].

It is the gradient form in the exact ordinary-Q identity

 ||x_0||^2-2S f_q+2sum_i h_i Q_(i,star)
       +2sum_i s_(i+1)Q_(i+1,i)=||x_q||^2+J.

This identity follows by expanding the GD norm difference and summing
s_(i+1)(f_(i+1)-f_i) by parts. No positivity of J is assumed here.

## 2. Exact adjacent-swap storage and its sign obstruction

There is a useful direct calculation identifying the chronology term that
an adjacent-step interchange spends. Consider two adjacent physical steps
alpha,beta>0 beginning at elapsed time t_clock. Let the current modal
coefficients be p_j, and define actual vectors

 g=v+sum_j p_j w_j,
 L_1=sum_j (p_j/d_j)w_j, L_2=sum_j(p_j/d_j^2)w_j.

These are DEFINITIONS through the modal coordinates. No linear operator on
the physical Euclidean space is presumed: a singular common Gram can identify
two modal vectors with different rates, so such an operator need not exist.

Let J_ab and J_ba be the energy J defined below for the two orders (alpha,beta) and
(beta,alpha), with the same formal modal data entering the pair and the
same earlier and later steps. Their endpoints, modal products, and elapsed
time after the pair agree. All other terms of J therefore cancel, and

 J_ab-J_ba=2alpha beta(beta-alpha)(t_clock+alpha+beta)
                                <L_2,g-L_1>.        (19)

Here is a polynomial verification. For rates z,w set U=z+w, V=zw and
D=z^2+w^2-zw(z+w). For a word W define P_W(z)=product_(h in W)(1-hz).
The unweighted and zero-clock weighted kernels of a single step h are

 K_[h](z,w)=h-(h^2/2)(U-V),
 T_[h](z,w)=h(h+1)-h^3(U-V).

Separating two consecutive blocks directly in the defining energy sums gives

 K_AB=K_A+P_A(z)P_A(w)K_B,
 T_AB=T_A+P_A(z)P_A(w)[T_B+2S_A K_B].

Substitution of P_[h](z)P_[h](w)=1-hU+h^2V yields

 K_ab-K_ba=-(alpha beta(alpha-beta)/2)D,
 T_ab-T_ba=-alpha beta(alpha-beta)(alpha+beta)D.

A nonzero starting clock adds 2t_clock(K_ab-K_ba). Finally D evaluated
on the entering common Gram is 2<L_2,g-L_1>, proving (19). This proof
uses only finite polynomial identities and applies to the original real
joint Gram, including its singular cases.

The sign in (19) is NOT fixed by the actual positive reciprocal rates.
Take a single live rate mu=1/d_j in (0,1), absorb its positive entering
factor into a nonzero vector W, and set all other residuals to zero.
Then L_1=mu W, L_2=mu^2 W, g=v+W, and

 <L_2,g-L_1>=mu^2[<W,v>+(1-mu)||W||^2].

It is positive when v=0 and negative when v=-(2-mu)W. Both assignments
have real PSD rank-one Grams and can be inserted before an actual adjacent
pair d_0,d_2, where the d_2 mode is still live. Thus neither swap order
universally dominates the other as an unconditional quadratic certificate
on this quotient. This does not assert legality of either assignment.
Indeed the negative one fails the first adjacent cocoercivity condition:

 <L_1,g-L_1>=-mu||W||^2<0.

In the ONE-live-rate case the two mixed terms differ by the positive factor
mu, so an actual adjacent Q cycle fixes the sign. With several live rates,
L_2 is not a scalar multiple of L_1. The next construction shows that even
all the original interpolation constraints do not make the sign positive.

## 3. Actual legal negative mixed curvature, on the original full word

This is a scoped counterexample to <L_2,g-L_1>>=0, not an adversary
matching the project's exact benchmark. It lies within a weak positive-scalar-
gradient class already considered in the project. Its purpose is to test the
new local swap step with FULL legality rather than only a formal PSD Gram.

Use the original word and m>=128. Choose the two actual levels

 d_f=d_4, d_s=d_5, r=d_s/d_f,
 v=1/[4(S+1)], epsilon_amp=v/(4r),
 w_4=-epsilon_amp, w_5=r epsilon_amp, w_j=0 otherwise.

All vectors are real scalars. Set x_0=1 and choose the free offset
u=1-Z_0, where Z_0=d_f w_4+d_s w_5. Define x_i,g_i by Section1.
Write p_f=p_i4 and p_s=p_i5 when a query i is understood. Then

 g_i=v+epsilon_amp(-p_f+r p_s),
 L_(1,i)=epsilon_amp(p_s-p_f)/d_f,
 L_(2,i)=epsilon_amp(-p_f+p_s/r)/d_f^2.              (20)

Before the first d_f both products are positive and every factor of p_s
is at least its corresponding factor in p_f. Afterwards p_f=0, and p_s
remains nonnegative until it also vanishes. Therefore 0<=p_f<=p_s<=1
for all queries. It follows that

 v<=g_i<=5v/4,
 0<=g_i-g_(i+1)=h_i L_(1,i)<=h_i epsilon_amp/d_f.    (21)

Every x_i strictly decreases, and

 x_q=1-sum_i h_i g_i>11/16.                         (22)

To build ONE actual function, define a continuous scalar derivative theta:

 theta(x)=x for x<=v;
 theta(x)=v for v<=x<=x_q;
 on [x_(i+1),x_i], theta is affine with endpoint values g_(i+1),g_i;
 theta(x)=g_0 for x>=1.

Overlaps at endpoints agree. Each interpolation interval has slope

 (g_i-g_(i+1))/(x_i-x_(i+1))=L_(1,i)/g_i
                      <=epsilon_amp/(d_f v)=1/(4r d_f)<1.

Hence theta is nondecreasing and globally1-Lipschitz. The function

                         F(x)=integral_0^x theta(t) dt

is everywhere finite, differentiable, convex and1-smooth, with F'(x_i)=g_i.
It is strictly decreasing on the negative half-line and strictly increasing
on the positive half-line. Thus its UNIQUE minimizer is0 and the true initial
distance is1. The GD recursion is the exact original chronological word.

The single common array of values can be written without integration:

 f_q=v x_q-v^2/2,
 f_i=f_(i+1)+(g_i+g_(i+1))(x_i-x_(i+1))/2.

These are exactly the values of F. Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies
necessity of EVERY ordered Q inequality for this one convex1-smooth function,
including all earlier/earlier pairs, every suffix comparison, and the optimum.
No Q inequality is dropped or checked only at neighboring points.

The heights are not all zero. Indeed C_min=-v^2/2 and eta=0 here by direct
calculation, while

 delta_i=integral_(x_q)^(x_i)(theta(x)-v)dx-(g_i-v)^2/2.

On [x_q,1] the slope of theta is at most kappa=1/(4r d_f)<1. If
R_i=g_i-v>0, its nonnegative increasing residual derivative must have area
at least R_i^2/(2kappa): on the interval of length R_i/kappa ending at x_i
it is at least max{0,R_i-kappa(x_i-x)}. This interval is inside [x_q,x_i]
because R_i<=kappa(x_i-x_q). Therefore

 delta_i>=(1/kappa-1)R_i^2/2>0 whenever R_i>0.        (23)

In particular delta_0>0. The zero value of eta is an explicit property of
THIS witness, not a normalization or reduction imposed on the full interface.

Now consider the ACTUAL query i=2, immediately before the consecutive
steps alpha=d_0 and beta=d_2. Set epsilon=1/m and tau=sqrt(2). Since

 d_f=1+lambda^3(1+2epsilon-2epsilon^3-epsilon^4)>15,
 12/5<c<5/2, r=c-(c-1)/d_f>23/10>2,
 d_0+d_1<7/2,

the two preceding factors give

 p_f=(1-d_0/d_f)(1-d_1/d_f)>1-7/(2d_f)>23/30>3/4,
 p_s/r<1/2.

Here lambda^3=7+5sqrt(2)>14 and epsilon<=1/128 justify the first bound;
the elementary bounds on c follow from its displayed definition. Thus

 L_(2,2)<-epsilon_amp/(4d_f^2),
 g_2-L_(1,2)>=v-epsilon_amp/d_f>3v/4,

and consequently

                  <L_(2,2),g_2-L_(1,2)>
                         <-3epsilon_amp v/(16d_f^2)<0.       (24)

At the same point the adjacent cocoercivity quantity is nonnegative:
L_(1,2)(g_2-L_(1,2))>=0, as required. Thus replacing L_1 by the
second modal curvature L_2 in that inference is false even on a fully legal
positive-height example at the original physical parameters.

For completeness, the unqueried final point stays in the same constant-
gradient interval for every b in [0,2]. Since S>1 gives v<1/8, (22) yields
x_q-bv>7/16>v. Its exact payoff is therefore

               2F(x_q-bv)=2v(x_q-bv)-v^2.

It lies between 3/[16(S+1)] and 1/[2(S+1)]. No comparison of this
weak constant with1/B_n is asserted as a matching lower bound. The example
does not refute the full elapsed-time storage candidate: a negative individual
swap term can be paid by other storage terms in the original chronology.

claim: C66 independent UNVERIFIED actual-word counterexample prevents overextending C65: quartic epigraph projection has increasing vertical and normal-coefficient states but DECREASING effective horizontal turning state. On every actual H_m,m>=128, exact start r0=1/2,v0=4 has gradient signs +,+,-,+: first turn level1, then LOWER level0. This is a new legal mechanism boundary, not a full-horizon profile witness.
evidence:
# C66: quartic epigraphs can reactivate lower turning levels

Status: COMPLETE UNVERIFIED construction and counterexample. This is an
independent follow-up after delivering C65, not a premise of that draft and
not a proposed solution of the original quantitative profile. No numerical
trajectory, optimization, installation, or verifier call was performed.

## 1. The exact claim tested

The parabolic construction has a nondecreasing effective horizontal normal
state, which prevents lower turning thresholds from becoming active again.
One must not generalize that property from a quadratic epigraph to every
convex epigraph merely because its vertical or projection-normal state grows.

For every m>=128, keep the actual enclosing-horizon parameters

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), c=lambda(1+1/m), a=(1-1/m)/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j).

The single quartic-epigraph function below, with the fixed initial state
(r_0,v_0)=(1/2,4), has actual horizontal gradient signs

    r_0>0, r_1>0, r_2<0, r_3>0

under the FIRST THREE steps of that same H_m. Its effective normal state
starts above d_1=ac, falls below d_0=a after the first step, and stays below
a at the next sample. Thus the first turn is at level1, and the next turn
is at the LOWER level0. All interpolation pairs come from one global
convex differentiable1-smooth function, with the true closest distance.

This refutes extending the parabolic normal monotonicity and permanent
deactivation of lower turning levels to general convex epigraphs. It does
not refute C65's stated parabolic result, and it supplies no lower bound
at the full terminal horizon2^m-1.

## 2. One global legal function and its exact state

Let phi_4(t)=t^4/4, and define

    K_4={(t,s):s>=phi_4(t)},
    F_4(X)=max_(g in K_4)(<X,g>-||g||^2/2).

The unique maximizer is the Euclidean projection onto the nonempty closed
convex set K_4, by completing the square. Projection existence follows
from coercivity and closedness; strict convexity gives uniqueness. The
two projection normal inequalities imply firm nonexpansiveness, hence a
1-Lipschitz projection map. Comparing the defining maxima bounds the
first-order remainder by ||Y-X||^2, so F_4 is differentiable with gradient
equal to that projection. It is globally convex as a supremum of affine
functions. These arguments establish global smoothness directly.

For r real and v>=0 define

    eta=v+r^4/4,
    u_4=eta*r^2=v*r^2+r^6/4,
    G_4(r)=(r,r^4/4),
    X_4(r,v)=(r+v*r^3+r^7/4,-v)=(r(1+u_4),-v).

The symbols eta and u_4 are DIFFERENT states: eta is the projection-normal
coefficient, whereas u_4 determines horizontal overshooting. For any
(t,s) in K_4,

    <X_4-G_4,(t,s)-G_4>
      <=eta[r^3(t-r)-(t^4-r^4)/4]
      =-(eta/4)(t-r)^2[(t+r)^2+2r^2]<=0.

Thus G_4(r) is the actual gradient at X_4(r,v). Substitution gives

    F_4(X_4(r,v))=r^2/2+3v*r^4/4+7r^8/32.                (1)

For every ordered pair of such states,

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<G_i,X_j-X_i>+||G_i-G_j||^2/2
        =<X_j-G_j,G_i-G_j>
        =-(eta_j/4)(r_i-r_j)^2[(r_i+r_j)^2+2r_j^2]<=0.   (2)

Hence all pairs are legal, for any number of actual steps. There is no
adjacent-pair relaxation.

The minimum value is0 and the minimizer set is exactly {(0,y):y<=0}.
Such points give a nonpositive inner product with every feasible gradient.
If the horizontal coordinate is nonzero, testing (t,t^4/4) for sufficiently
small t of the same sign gives positive value, since the linear term
dominates the quadratic and higher terms. If the vertical coordinate is
positive, testing a small vertical gradient gives positive value.
Thus the true closest minimizer to X_4(r_0,v_0) is(0,-v_0), and

    R_4^2=r_0^2(1+v_0*r_0^2+r_0^6/4)^2.                  (3)

For a step h>=0, the exact same-function GD recurrence is

    v_plus=v+h*r^4/4,
    r_plus+v_plus*r_plus^3+r_plus^7/4
      =r(1+v*r^2+r^6/4-h).                               (4)

For v_plus>=0, the polynomial on the left is strictly increasing and
surjective, because its derivative is1+3v_plus*r_plus^2+7r_plus^6/4>=1.
Consequently(4) specifies a unique real next state and exactly reproduces
X_plus=X-hG. The full normalized terminal payoff, if later studied, is

    [r_n^2+(3/2)v_n*r_n^4+(7/16)r_n^8]/R_4^2.             (5)

The projection-normal coefficient DOES increase at the physical steps:

    eta_plus-eta=(h-1)r^4/4+r_plus^4/4>=0  for h>=1.      (6)

The effective state is eta*r^2, however, so(6) does not imply that u_4
increases. A nonzero horizontal turn occurs exactly when u_4<h-1.

## 3. An exact actual-word counterexample, without solving any roots numerically

For m>=128 the elementary bounds

    2/5<a<5/12, 127/128<=b=ac<1

hold. For example sqrt(2)<99/70 gives c<73/30, hence
a>(127/128)(30/73)>2/5; also a<sqrt(2)-1<5/12.
The first three actual steps of H_m are (1+a,1+b,1+a).

Take r_0=1/2,v_0=4. Then

    u_(4,0)=257/256>1>b,
    X_0=(513/512,-4), R_4=513/512.

Here u_(4,i)=v_i*r_i^2+r_i^6/4 is the effective quartic state at sample i.
The first step has

    v_1=4+(1+a)/64<4+3/128,
    x_1=(1/2)(257/256-a),
    0<x_1<773/2560<5/16.

Write T_v(t)=t+v*t^3+t^7/4. It is increasing, T_(v_1)(0)=0, and
T_(v_1)(1/4)>1/4+4/64=5/16. The unique-root definition(4) therefore gives

    0<r_1<1/4,
    u_(4,1)<(4+3/128)/16+1/16384
             =4121/16384<2/5<a.                          (7)

Thus the effective normal state has strictly DECREASED from above the
level1 threshold to below the level0 threshold, although v and eta increased.

At the second step, with excess b, one has

    x_2=r_1(u_(4,1)-b)<0,
    |x_2|<b*r_1<1/4,
    v_2=v_1+(1+b)r_1^4/4<4+3/128+1/512=4+13/512.

Since T_(v_2) is odd and T_(v_2)(t)>=t for t>=0, its unique root satisfies
-1/4<r_2<0. Consequently

    u_(4,2)<(4+13/512)/16+1/16384
             =4123/16384<2/5<a.                          (8)

The third step has excess a and therefore x_3=r_2(u_(4,2)-a)>0. Its unique
root r_3 is positive. This establishes the displayed sign pattern and
the return from a level1 turn to a level0 turn using exact inequalities.

The higher-dimensional position and vertical state at every step are
inherited from(4). Nothing here replaces the actual H_m by H_2 with a
different physical parameter, or resets v after a turn.

## 4. Literature grounding and the remaining quantitative interface

The power-epigraph projection formula is consistent with Propositions3.2
and3.3 of Chierchia, Pustelnik, Pesquet and Pesquet-Popescu,
"Epigraphical splitting for solving constrained convex formulations of
inverse problems with proximal tools", arXiv:1210.5844v3. The downloaded
32-page PDF and its extracted text are in
downloads/c66_epigraph_projection_1210.5844.{pdf,txt}; the definitions and
both proofs in Section3.2 were read.

Their Hilbert product norm is Euclidean here; their epigraph generator is
proper, closed, convex and has domain all of R. Setting their power to4,
scale to1/4 and vertical query coordinate to-v yields the scalar equation
t+v*t^3+t^7/4=x. This is only projection background; their algorithmic
convergence statements do not supply a rate for the present prescribed GD
word. Sections2--3 derive all mathematical claims here independently.

The explicit change from quadratic to quartic epigraph keeps one legal
global function but separates the increasing normal coefficient eta from
the turning state eta*r^2. That extra curvature factor is the missing state
in an attempted extension of the parabolic argument.

The next quantitative task would be to control an entire same-v quartic
trajectory, possibly with horizon-dependent r_0,v_0 or an epigraph power
greater than2, and compare(5) to the exact B_n. The three-step return above
is not a useful full-horizon witness by itself. It remains possible that
this new proper family is also uniformly weak. No such assertion, and no
original-target success, is made.

# An explicit planar adversary for the five-step dense variation

Status: **joint unverified candidate**, cumulative round 16. No optimizer or
verifier is used in this proof. The full-model experiment suggested looking
at two consecutive equal gradients and a later two-gradient plateau. None
of its floating entries is used as a mathematical premise.

The accepted benchmark/interpolation conventions are b98bb807d514e80d and
1252b8823bb5a290. All additional construction and inequalities are proved
below. This is a finite path obstruction, not an unbounded-horizon result.

## 1. Concrete steps and statement

Put s=sqrt(2), A=3+2s, beta=sqrt(7+4s), B0=(beta+1)^2, and

 p=(16-11s)/3, q=(8s-10)/3, m=10s-14=q-2p.

For0<=t<=1/50 define

 a=s-p*t, b=2+q*t, c=beta-m*t/4,

This is the exact balanced weighted-mean proposal evaluated as
`n5_balanced_t002`. Indeed the primitive child's gaps are (s-1,1,s-1),
their arithmetic mean is (2s-1)/3, their harmonic mean is9-6s, and their
midpoint is(13-8s)/3. The child direction is(-p,q,-p), of total mass m;
the singleton right child has zero direction, and the root changes by-m/4.

For every t in this interval there is an explicit function F_t:R^2->R,
convex and differentiable with1-Lipschitz gradient and UNIQUE minimizer0,
whose GD trajectory for h(t), started at x0=(1,0), satisfies

 2F_t(x5) = (c-1)^2 J/[4(a+1)^2],                  (2)
 J=[(b-1)^2(2-a)+a(a^2-2)/2]/(a+2),
 B0*2F_t(x5)>=1+7t/10.                             (3)

The exact benchmark obeys B5>=B0. Consequently

 B5*W5(h(t))>=1+7t/10>1       for0<t<=1/50.        (4)

can improve the exact five-step benchmark on this path. This conclusion
comes from one legal original-model function, not a restricted dual array.

## 2. Four concrete gradient vectors

Write z=b-1, d=c-1, and define

 kappa= -[z^2+(a+1)/2]/[z(a+2)],
 u=(1/(a+1),0),
 v=(kappa,sqrt(1/2-kappa^2))/(a+1),
 w=-z*u-a*v,             k=-d*w/4.                 (5)

Let U=||u||^2=1/(a+1)^2. Then

 <u,v>=kappa*U, ||v||^2=U/2,
 ||w||^2=J*U,
 <u,w>/U=[a(a+1)/2-2z^2]/[z(a+2)]=:r_u,
 <v,w>/U=[z^2+(1-a-a^2)/2]/(a+2)=:r_v.            (6)

Expanding (5) proves (6). The defining choice of kappa gives the exact
orthogonality identity

 <w-v,-z*u-v>=0.                                   (7)

All radicals in (5) are real. Here are rational bounds proving that claim
and all the normal inequalities used below. Squaring the rational endpoints
gives1.4142<s<1.4143 and3.557<beta<3.558. Hence

 .147<p<.149, .437<q<.439, .140<m<.145,
 1.411<=a<=1.415, 1<=z<=1.01, 2.55<=d<=2.57.        (8)

Every terminating decimal in this proof denotes the corresponding exact
rational. From (8),

 -.654<kappa<-.639, .169<J<.177,
 -.1<r_u<0,               -.062<r_v<0.             (9)

For explicit checks: the numerator in -kappa lies between2.2055 and2.2276,
its denominator between3.411 and3.44915, giving the first bound. Set
N=z^2(2-a)+a(a^2-2)/2. The polynomial a(a^2-2)/2 is increasing throughout
(8), so direct endpoint substitution gives .578<N<.603. Dividing by
a+2 gives the asserted J bounds (using the slightly sharper lower
endpoint .585+1.411*(1.411^2-2)/2>.5785 when desired).
The numerator of r_u is at least
1.411*2.411/2-2*1.01^2=-.3392395 and is negative; its denominator is at
least3.411, giving -.1<r_u<0. The numerator of r_v is at least
1+(1-1.415-1.415^2)/2=-.2086125 and is negative; division by at least3.411
gives -.062<r_v<0. Thus1/2-kappa^2>1/2-.654^2>0.

## 3. One compact convex set and EVERY original normal inequality

Let K=conv{0,u,v,w,k}. The vectors u,v are independent and
z*u+a*v+w=0 with all three coefficients positive. Therefore0 lies in the
interior of the triangle conv{u,v,w}, and hence in the interior of K.

Use the proposed full trajectory

 x0=(a+1)u, g0=u;
 x1=u,     g1=u;
 x2=-z*u,  g2=v;
 x3=w,     g3=w;
 x4=-d*w=4k, g4=k;
 x5=(5/2)k,  g5=k.                                 (10)

Every equation x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i follows immediately from (1) and (5).
To prove g_i=Proj_K(x_i), it suffices to check
<r-g_i,x_i-g_i><=0 for all vertices r of K. Linear interpolation then
gives it for every r in K. These checks cover every ordered original pair,
including optimum and terminal pairs, with one common K.

At samples1 and3 the residual x_i-g_i is zero. At sample0 it is a*u.
We have <v,u>/U=kappa<0, <w,u>/U=r_u<0 and
<k,u>/U=-(d/4)r_u<(2.57/4)*.1<1; the vertices0 andu also satisfy the
normal inequality. This checks sample0.

At sample2 its residual is y2=-z*u-v. In units of U, the inequalities
for vertices0 andu are respectively

 <-v,y2>/U=z*kappa+1/2<0,
 <u-v,y2>/U=-z+(z-1)kappa+1/2<=-1/2.

The vertex w has equality by (7), and the vertex v has equality trivially.
Write T=<v,y2>=(-z*kappa-1/2)U>0. By (7), <w,y2>=T. Thus
<k-v,y2>=-(1+d/4)T<0, which checks the last vertex.

At samples4 and5 the residuals are3k and(3/2)k. It is enough to check
<r-k,k><=0. The vertices0,w,k satisfy this directly since k=-d*w/4.
For the other two vertices this condition is

 r_u >= -d*J/4,       r_v >= -d*J/4.

It follows from (9), since d*J/4>2.55*.169/4>.1. Every original
normal inequality has now been checked without dropping remote pairs.

## 4. A global smooth function with the correct initial distance

Define

 F_t(x)=max_(r in K){<x,r>-||r||^2/2}.              (11)

The maximizer is unique and equals Proj_K(x), by completing the square.
If P and P' are the projections of x and x', their normal inequalities
give ||P-P'||^2<=<x-x',P-P'>, so the projection is1-Lipschitz. Evaluating
the maxima in (11) at each other's maximizers yields

 0<=F_t(x')-F_t(x)-<P,x'-x>
      <=<P'-P,x'-x><=||x'-x||^2.

This proves differentiability with gradient P and1-Lipschitz gradient.
It is finite and convex because K is compact and (11) is a maximum of
affine functions of x. Since0 is interior to K, for every x!=0 a sufficiently
small positive multiple r=epsilon*x belongs to K and makes
<x,r>-||r||^2/2 positive. Therefore F_t(0)=0 and0 is its UNIQUE minimizer.
The initial point in (10) is(1,0), so its true initial distance is exactly1.

Section3 now proves that (10) is the actual GD trajectory of this single
global function. At x5=(5/2)k, (11) gives F_t(x5)=2||k||^2. Thus
2F_t(x5)=4||k||^2=d^2||w||^2/4, proving (2). Replacing F_t by L*F_t
for any L>0 preserves the project's normalized performance under h_i/L.

## 5. Exact payoff comparison over the entire interval

For t=0, a=s,z=1 and J=(2-s)/(2+s)=1/A. Since(a+1)^2=A and
2A=(beta-1)(beta+1), (2) is exactly1/B0.

Set R(t)=B0*d^2*N/[4(a+1)^2(a+2)], with N as in section2. The preceding
bounds give N>0, and differentiation gives

 (log R)'=-m/(2d)+2p/(a+1)+N'/N+p/(a+2),
 N'=2z(2-a)q-p[-z^2+(3a^2-2)/2].                  (12)

Using (8), 2z(2-a)>=1.17 and the square bracket is<1.004. Hence
N'>1.17*.437-1.004*.149>.361. Since N<.603, (12) gives

 (log R)'>-29/1020+98/805+361/603+147/3415>7/10.

The last comparison is a rational inequality, obtained by multiplication
by the positive product of the displayed denominators. Integrating from0
to t and using exp(u)>=1+u proves R(t)>=1+7t/10, namely (3).

Finally the exact benchmark recurrence in b98bb807d514e80d allows the
primitive three-step construction(s,2,s), of mass A=1+sum h, and a
dominant one-step suffix(3/2), of mass4. Its mass join is

 G(A,4)=2A+2+2sqrt(1+2A)=(beta+1)^2=B0.

The optimal primitive mass is at least A and G is increasing in that mass,
so B5>=B0. This argument needs NO decimal comparison of candidate splits.
Multiply the legal payoff by B5 to obtain (4).

## 6. What this explains and does not explain

The constructed path increases total step mass, and its tested finite case
passes the earlier necessary scalar screens. A planar convex body now gives
a direct, exact obstruction on the whole interval0<t<=1/50, even when the
entire upper certificate is reselected. The construction uses a true common
projection body and all original pairs; it is not a formal Gram test alone.

It does not claim to attain the full SDP optimum or to require dimension2
in every worst case. No automatic recursive lift to n15,n31 or unbounded n
is established here. The separate common-offset mass argument covers the
asymptotic limitation of that particular dense family; arbitrary coordinated
redistribution and the original minimax conjecture remain open.

claim: Round17 exact active-face counterexample candidate: at the five-step source word, v=(1,1/2,-1,-1/20,-3/10) decreases Huber, unit quadratic, root-cut and EVERY member of the exact planar continuum with x1=g1,x3=g3; a distinct legal two-dimensional projection face with x1!=g1 has normalized logarithmic slope >1/4 and defeats that direction.
