 p_s(x)=b_s*exp(<v_s,x>/tau)/sum_t b_t*exp(<v_t,x>/tau),
 mu(x)=sum_s p_s(x)*v_s.

Differentiation of a finite sum gives, on the whole Euclidean space,

 grad Phi_tau=mu,
 Hess Phi_tau=(1/tau)[sum_s p_s v_s v_s^T-mu mu^T].  (8)

The quadratic form is a variance, so Phi_tau is convex. If the feature
diameter is Dfeat, its variance in any unit direction is at most
Dfeat^2/4. To prove this, for a random scalar T in [b,d], the nonnegative
quantity (T-b)(d-T) gives
Var(T)<=(d-E T)(E T-b)<=(d-b)^2/4.
Consequently Lbase=Dfeat^2/(4tau) is valid globally. One may also use
an explicitly proved sharper covariance bound in a particular geometry.

The EXACT probability update at the physical step is

 p_(i+1),s = p_i,s * exp[-h_i <v_s,mu_i>/(Lbase*tau)]
             / sum_t p_i,t*exp[-h_i <v_t,mu_i>/(Lbase*tau)]. (9)

This equation follows from the actual vector update; no label is chosen
after a step. Every weight remains strictly positive at every finite
query. All functions and recurrences in this manuscript are finite even
when their feature counts are large; none is evaluated by a host job.

Attainment must be checked separately. In the centered uniform examples
below, sum_s v_s=0 and the features span their stated ambient space.
Jensen's inequality gives Phi_1(x)>=0=Phi_1(0). Equality requires all
<v_s,x> equal; their mean is zero, so they all vanish and span implies
x=0. This proves the actual unique minimum, not an infimum at infinity.
The chain's attained minimum is computed explicitly in Section4.

Temperature is not a free normalization improvement. Choose x_star to
be a closest attained minimizer to the chosen initial point, and let
pi_s=p_s(x_star), z=(x-x_star)/tau and
Lbase=Ccov/tau, for a fixed proved covariance bound Ccov. Then

 Phi_tau(x)-Phi_tau(x_star)=tau*log sum_s pi_s exp(<v_s,z>),
 z_(i+1)=z_i-(h_i/Ccov)sum_s p_i,s v_s,
 V=2 log(sum_s pi_s exp(<v_s,z_n>))/(Ccov*||z_0||^2). (10)

Here sum_s pi_s v_s=0. The temperature cancels simultaneously from the
physical recurrence and the paid score at a fixed scaled initial state.
Changing that state, the features, weights, or dimension can still matter;
(10) does not exclude those choices or holding x_0 fixed while changing tau.

All original directed and optimum interpolation inequalities follow
from the actual function and its stated smoothness, as follows. For any
convex differentiable Lbase-smooth Phi and any x, define
k(u)=Phi(u)-<grad Phi(x),u>. It is minimized at x. Integrating its
Lipschitz gradient gives
k(y-grad k(y)/Lbase)<=k(y)-||grad k(y)||^2/(2Lbase).
Comparison with k(x) proves

 Phi(y)>=Phi(x)+<grad Phi(x),y-x>
                  +||grad Phi(y)-grad Phi(x)||^2/(2Lbase). (11)

With F_i=(Phi(x_i)-Phi_star)/Lbase and g_i=grad Phi(x_i)/Lbase,
(11) is exactly

 Q_ij=F_i-F_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=0

for EVERY ordered pair of distinct physical queries, including BOTH
terminal orientations and EVERY optimum pair. This agrees with accepted
1252b8823bb5a290. No local-to-global inference about prescribed jets is
being used. Zero steps simply repeat an actual query.

## 5. Candidate three: an explicit weighted tree simplex

Keep the original enclosing m and c of Section1. To avoid collision with
the accepted denominator-ray symbols Z_b, define

 r_tree=2/c in(0,1),
 Zgeom=sum_(j=0)^(m-1)r_tree^j=(1-r_tree^m)/(1-r_tree),
 w_j=r_tree^j/Zgeom, 0<=j<m.                        (26)

There is one orthonormal coordinate e_v for EVERY binary word v of
length j<m, including the empty root. The dimension is N-1. For a leaf
s=(s_1,...,s_m) in {0,1}^m define the explicit feature

 a_s=sum_(j=0)^(m-1) sqrt(w_j)*(-1)^(s_(j+1))*e_(s_1...s_j),
 Phi_T(x)=log[N^(-1)sum_s exp(<a_s,x>)].             (27)

The library has N features and all weights are 1/N. It may know m and
the entire original word. No online or dimension restriction is imposed
on competing adversaries. The tree is a choice of geometry, not a
lossless representation theorem for all smooth convex functions.

The features sum to zero and each has squared norm1. Their coordinate
rows are orthogonal: a row at depth j has N/2^j nonzero entries of
magnitude sqrt(w_j); a proper descendant row cancels separately inside
its support, and disjoint rows have zero product. Thus the feature
matrix has full row rank N-1. The centered Jensen argument from Section2
gives the unique attained minimum

                x_star=0, Phi_T,star=0.             (28)

The SAME argument also proves affine independence of the N vertices.
The only linear dependence among their columns is the all-ones vector;
a dependence with coefficients summing to zero must consequently vanish.
Equivalently, the map x -> (<a_s,x>)_s is onto the zero-mean logit space.

If two leaves first diverge at depth j, their squared feature distance is

             4w_j+2sum_(ell>j)w_ell.               (29)

Their common prefix cancels, the divergent coordinate contributes4w_j,
and their later paths use orthogonal coordinates. The quarter-distances
w_j+(1/2)sum_(ell>j)w_ell strictly decrease with j, since the difference
between consecutive ones is w_j-w_(j+1)/2>0. Therefore (8) gives the
globally valid constant

 Ltree=(1+w_0)/2.                                  (30)

It is SHARP. Choose a pair diverging at the root and prescribe equal
logits for that pair and logits smaller by T for all other leaves,
then subtract the common mean. The onto map just proved supplies an
actual point for every finite T. As T tends to infinity, its Gibbs
distribution tends to half mass on each chosen vertex. Covariance in
the difference direction tends to their squared distance divided by4,
which equals (30). This is a proof of the global supremum, not a
numeric eigenvalue calculation or an implicit feature-fitting step.

The full, actual, persistent vector and probability updates are

 x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/Ltree)sum_s p_i,s*a_s,
 p_(i+1),s=p_i,s exp[-(h_i/Ltree)sum_t K_st*p_i,t]
          /sum_u p_i,u exp[-(h_i/Ltree)sum_t K_ut*p_i,t],
 K_st=<a_s,a_t>.                                    (31)

All entries of K are fixed by the explicit coordinates (27); K is not
an unknown Gram matrix. If s,t diverge at j, then
K_st=sum_(ell<j)w_ell-w_j; K_ss=1. Formula (31) defines every physical
query, not just level checkpoints. Values are Phi_T(x_i), and (11)
proves all original rows and optimum rows without separately fitting them.

## 6. A specified initial state, exact radius, and actual nonlinear reduction

Let t0=log2. Specify the complete initial point by

 x_0,(0^j)=t0/sqrt(w_j) for 0<=j<m,
 x_0,v=0 for every other internal node v.           (32)

Here 0^j is the all-left prefix of length j, including the root at j=0.
The full unique minimum is still (28), hence the TRUE squared radius is

 R_T^2=t0^2 sum_(j=0)^(m-1)1/w_j
      =t0^2*r_tree^(1-m)*Zgeom^2.                  (33)

The second equality follows from the two finite geometric sums in (26).
There is no discarded orthogonal component or convenient surrogate minimum.

Leaves can be grouped by the depth k of their first right turn,
0<=k<m, and by the all-left leaf k=m. Their uniform reference masses are

 q_k=2^(-(k+1)) for k<m, q_m=2^(-m).

All coordinates outside the leftmost spine remain ZERO at every physical
query. Indeed, if they are zero, logits are constant on each first-exit
group. Every non-spine node lies inside one such group, and its two
halves have equal counts and logits, so its mean feature coordinate is
zero. The next update preserves zero, completing induction.

Define the ACTUAL spine fields y_i,j=sqrt(w_j)*x_i,(0^j), exit logits

 ell_i,k=sum_(j<k)y_i,j-y_i,k for k<m,
 ell_i,m=sum_(j<m)y_i,j,
 P_i,k=q_k exp(ell_i,k)/sum_(u=0)^m q_u exp(ell_i,u).

The exact reduction of (31) is

 y_(i+1),j=y_i,j-(h_i*w_j/Ltree)
                    [sum_(k>j)P_i,k-P_i,j],
 y_0,j=t0.                                         (34)

These m equations are NONLINEAR and COUPLED through the same probabilities.
They are not independent scalar quadratics or a prescribed label policy.
For example, at the initial state the Hessian covariance between the root
and any deeper spine coordinate j is

 Cov(a_root,a_(0^j))
   =2sqrt(w_0)*P_0,0*E[a_(0^j)]>0.                 (35)

The equality holds because the root feature is +sqrt(w_0) wherever
the deeper coordinate is nonzero. Positivity follows from the explicit
initial means computed next. The changing distribution in (34), rather
than a fixed Hessian, determines later interactions.

Initially ell_0,k=(k-1)t0 for k<m and ell_0,m=m*t0. Thus

 P_0,k=1/(m+4) for k<m, P_0,m=4/(m+4),
 Phi_T(x_0)=log[(m+4)/4],
 E[a_(0^j)]=sqrt(w_j)*(m+2-j)/(m+4).                (36)

The weights and the starting point are fully specified before the
trajectory. Formula (34) is an exact analytic recurrence, not evidence
that its final value has a desired size.

Since sum_k q_k ell_i,k=0, there is an exact objective identity

 D_i:=Phi_T(x_i)=sum_(k=0)^m q_k log(q_k/P_i,k),
 V_T=2D_n/(Ltree*R_T^2).                            (37)

Thus D_i is relative entropy with the stated orientation: the uniform
leaf reference is the FIRST argument, not the current Gibbs law.
All probabilities are positive. Its nonnegativity also follows directly
from Jensen. This entropy is the actual value, not an added potential.

## 7. The priced missing estimate and exact same-word comparison interface

Equations (26), (30), (33), (34), and (37) specify a globally legal family
on every original H_m. They do NOT yet provide a useful terminal payoff.
The diagnostic target B_n V_T>=1 is EXACTLY

 D_n>=eta_m,
 eta_m=Ltree*t0^2*r_tree^(1-m)*Zgeom^2/(2B_n).       (38)

It is a concrete inequality for the entirely specified recurrence (34),
not an unknown initial state, unknown feature library, or Gram oracle.
Let r_inf=2/lambda, Zgeom_inf=1/(1-r_inf), and
Ltree_inf=(2-r_inf)/2. From (1) and (7),

 N*eta_m -> eta_inf
   =exp(1)*Ltree_inf*t0^2*r_inf/
                     [2 Z_1 (1-r_inf)^2] in(0,infinity).  (39)

Indeed N*r_tree^(-m)=c^m. Thus the needed entropy has order1/N after
the exact radius has been paid. The assertion D_n>=eta_m is UNPROVED.
No claim of even a uniform constant fraction of (38) is made.

One rigorous terminal diagnostic follows by conditioning the relative
entropy (37) on the last two leaves. They have reference masses1/N each,
and their current log probability ratio is2y_n,m-1. Splitting the
relative-entropy sum into this pair and its complement gives a binary
group divergence plus two nonnegative conditional divergences. Therefore

 D_n >= (2/N) log cosh(y_n,m-1).                    (40)

For detail, the conditional pair law has probabilities proportional to
exp(y_n,m-1),exp(-y_n,m-1). Its divergence from the equal pair law is
log cosh(y_n,m-1). The pair's reference weight is2/N. Nonnegativity
of the other divergences is Jensen applied to log. This is a LOWER
bound and need not capture the whole final entropy.

A SUFFICIENT deep-coordinate condition for (38) is consequently

 log cosh(y_n,m-1) >= N*eta_m/2.                    (41)

The exact accumulated coordinate update is

 y_n,m-1=t0-(w_(m-1)/Ltree)
                  sum_(i=0)^(n-1)h_i*(P_i,m-P_i,m-1).   (42)

Neither (41) nor a useful bound on the signed sum in (42) has been proved.
The trivial bound by S gives a coordinate uncertainty of order N and
does not supply a terminal lower bound. It also permits exact cancellation.

For clarity, the complete SAME-word comparisons remain the following
explicit, unresolved scalar thresholds, with NO replacement of a full
reference by a selected path or a lens:

 V_T>=K_n(h)       iff D_n>=Ltree*R_T^2*K_n(h)/2,
 V_T>=F_ray_n(h)   iff D_n>=Ltree*R_T^2*F_ray_n(h)/2,
 V_T>=Cfull(h)     iff D_n>=Ltree*R_T^2*Cfull(h)/2,
 B_n V_T>=1       iff D_n>=eta_m.                   (43)

The equality (37) is a complete payoff formula, but (43) is NOT a
completed performance comparison. All four terminal comparisons for
this third candidate are BLOCKED. In particular, legality alone and a
large initial entropy do not prove a useful hard instance.

## 8. Two direct attempts, their exact failures, and counterexample checks

Attempt A: propagate the equal initial spine fields or compare all leaf
masses to a constant multiple of uniform. Both proposed shortcuts fail
already in the explicit initial/first-step data. Equation (34) gives

 y_1,j=t0-[h_0*w_j/Ltree]*(m+2-j)/(m+4).

Thus

 y_1,0-y_1,1
 =-h_0*[w_0*(m+2)-w_1*(m+1)]/[Ltree*(m+4)]<0.      (44)

The equal-field ansatz is not invariant. Also P_0,m=4/(m+4), so
P_0,m/q_m=4N/(m+4) is unbounded. A proposed absolute, all-time
near-uniform probability cap is false for this very initial condition.
These observations do not exclude a later mixing statement with a paid
transient. No such statement is assumed in (38).

Attempt B: use the repeated original word H_j as an independent child
evolution. Split the feature tree at the root and write

 Phi_T=log[(exp(y_root)*exp(Phi_left)
                  +exp(-y_root)*exp(Phi_right))/2].

Each child Phi is the log-partition function of its explicitly inherited
descendant features on its own Euclidean coordinates. If P_left is the
current subtree mass, then

 grad_left Phi_T=P_left*grad Phi_left,
 x_left' =x_left-(h/Ltree)*P_left*grad Phi_left.       (45)

Thus, with the child's own sharp constant

 L_left=w_1+(1/2)sum_(j>1)w_j < Ltree,

its actual normalized step is

               h_eff=h*P_left*L_left/Ltree.         (46)

This is a state-dependent number, not the original physical h. Initially
P_left=(m+3)/(m+4), and it strictly decreases after the FIRST actual step.
To prove the strict change, the right child starts at0 and has zero
gradient, so stays at0. The root field strictly decreases because
P_left>1/2. The left child makes a positive step of size
h_0 P_left/Ltree <2/L_left, since h_0<2 and L_left<Ltree.
The smooth descent inequality shows its value strictly decreases, as
its gradient is nonzero by (36). Its odds
P_left/(1-P_left)=exp(2y_root+Phi_left-Phi_right)
therefore strictly decrease. This proves that even the first two
effective clock factors in (46) differ.

Consequently a recursion that inserts fresh copies of the ORIGINAL
child schedule silently changes the physical steps. An adaptive clock
bound might still be useful, but it must account for the full history
of subtree masses, coupling to ancestors, all returns and the exact
radius (33). No such bound has been proved in this round.

An additional counterexample check rules out a global entropy-monotonicity
shortcut for (34)'s function. In this SAME Phi_T, put only the root field
equal to s and all descendants zero. The function is log cosh(s), and a
step h gives s'=s-h*(w_0/Ltree)*tanh(s). Whenever
h*w_0/Ltree>2, sufficiently small positive s has s'<-s and therefore
Phi_T(x')>Phi_T(x). Such a level occurs in H_m for all sufficiently
large m, since its maximum h grows without bound whereas w_0/Ltree
tends to a positive constant. This point is a test state of the same
function, not a claim that the trajectory (32) visits it. It refutes
global monotonicity at those steps, not a trajectory-specific inequality.
This scalar slice is ONLY a counterexample test; it is not substituted
for the actual coupled construction (32)--(37).

After these two genuine attempts and the counterexample checks, the
unresolved estimate is (38), or an alternative actual terminal bound
strong enough to decide (43). Its scope is the specified growing tree
Gibbs family and original enclosing-m word. Mark it BLOCKED, not a
routine missing lemma, and not a theorem-level impossibility claim.

              Ltree=(1+w_0)/2=(Zgeom+1)/(2Zgeom)            (3.3)

             x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/Ltree)g(x_i).                (3.4)

Neither injectivity nor norm contractivity of a long step is available,
even on a simple slice of this SAME function. At root-only points

           y -> map_root(y)=y-alpha_root tanh y,
              alpha_root=hmax/(Ltree Zgeom).

contractivity. It is not a counterexample to existence of a better
selected branch, and terminal0 is not used as a payoff witness.

The first attempt was to propagate a fixed exposed face, or treat a

Its unique full-leaf barycentric coefficients are

The strict inequality follows from a>2/5 and N>=4. Consequently
P_K_ctr(x_1)!=x_1. An initial core visit already fails to persist through
the next original step. No remote interpolation defect occurs: (2.4)
holds, and the true projection supplies the required repair automatically.

The second attempt was to simplify the full simplex projection by
thresholding its unconstrained leaf masses with the ordinary Euclidean
probability-simplex formula. This is false for the selected Haar metric.
Applying that threshold formula to (7.1) would give mass1/(N-1) on all
non-left leaves, mass0 on the left leaf, and hence

All those non-left leaves would have positive weights, so their normal

projection. The values for leaves first diverging at depths0 and1 differ
by

 (-a+1/(N-1))*(2w_0-w_1),                          (7.2)

which is nonzero. This directly violates the within-face stationarity
condition. The inverse feature map changes the Euclidean metric; ordinary
thresholding is not invariant under that change of coordinates.

These are concrete failures of two attempted reductions, not a proof
that a competitive centered-tree trajectory is impossible. In particular
there is no proof that the support remains a prefix of exit groups after
query2, and no failure of such a later-only prefix conjecture is asserted.
The full state rule retains arbitrary later supports.

  -||y_n||^2.                                     (8.1)

the squared-residual contribution can be positive, and its size must
be controlled jointly with the negative terms and the terminal residual.
For this candidate the exact benchmark-matching requirement is

  {h_i(2-h_i)||y_i||^2-2h_i(h_i-1)cex_i}/Pi_(i+1)^2]

## 9. Literature and resource record

Search stage: active_program. Program: actual growing tree-simplex
projection dynamics. Missing mechanism: an analytic all-query active-set

"Projection onto the probability simplex: An efficient algorithm with a
simple proof, and an application", arXiv:1309.1541, 2013, Sections1-3

sum p=1 in the STANDARD Euclidean probability coordinates. It characterizes

an explicit sorted-support test. The relevant proof idea is equality of
normal derivatives on the positive support, used directly in(3.5),(3.6)

## 6. What these two obstructions leave open

The first construction genuinely crosses from chi=0 into chi>0, while
increasing physical capacity above lambda^3. The second starts with the
explicit full-rank original certificate(20), permits a subunit physical
step, is asymmetric, and reaches capacity301/20. In both cases the complete
static witnesses prohibit every possible original nonnegative coefficient
array, including all homogeneous skew repairs and full nonzero PSD
remainders. No prescribed rank-one rate mechanism was reused.

These are restrictions on TWO declared physical families only. They do not
prove full seven-step impossibility, a maximum-capacity theorem, or the
original all-h/all-n asymptotic profile. A subthreshold starting certificate
and the conditional lift(4) are not substitutes for the missing seed.

A specific direction outside the exclusions remains: vary the two ordered

evidence:
UNVERIFIED joint derivation, part of 9be1a10ee154498a. No formal gate is authorized.

## 1. Original coordinates, counts, and the fixed child

Normalize smoothness to1. For any word w=(w_0,...,w_(n-1)), write
S_w=sum w_i, A_w=1+S_w, and retain all n+1 formal gradients g_i and values

 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 V_w=2sum_(i<n)w_i(f_i-f_n)+sum_(i<n)w_i(1-w_i)||g_i||^2
                                      -S_w(S_w+1)||g_n||^2.

Let e be the all-ones column, T_ii=1, T_it=w_t for t<i, T_it=0 for t>i,
omega=(-2w_0,...,-2w_(n-1),2S_w)^T, and

 D=diag(w_0(2-w_0),...,w_(n-1)(2-w_(n-1)),-S_w(S_w+2)).

A full certificate consists of Lambda_ii=0, Lambda_ij>=0 for every
ordered i!=j, L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda, L^T e=omega, and

 M=D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2 positive semidefinite.                    (1)

Here sym(B)=(B+B^T)/2; Gram is the matrix of pairwise gradient inner
products, and the matrix pairing in (2) is trace(M^T Gram).

The accepted original-coordinate identity is

 V_w+sum_(i!=j)Lambda_ij Q_ij=<M,Gram(g_0,...,g_n)>.          (2)

It holds as a polynomial in every formal gradient and value, without
identifying coordinates. The signs Q_ij<=0 hold on an actual trajectory
of a single convex differentiable1-smooth function. Consequently (1)
is a sufficient primitive certificate on all such trajectories.

In this manuscript only, set a=sqrt(2), C=1+a, d=a-1=1/C. The fixed child
is q=(a). Its two-node certificate is

 Lambda^q=[[0,2],[2C,0]], M^q=0.                             (3)

a(2-a)+2(1-a)=2-a^2=0 and -a(a+2)+2C=0. Twice the off-diagonal is

The arbitrary input h has length r>=1, h_i>=1, capacity A=1+sum h_i,

## 2. A nonbasic legal input, with its complete certificate

Take h=(3/2,3/2), A=4, and

 Lambda^h=[[0,1,1/2],[7/2,0,17/2],[1,14,0]].                (6)

Its six ordered entries are positive and its flow is (-3,-3,6).

## 3. Mechanism1: every cross-block ordered pair is retained

For arbitrary input h choose t_i in[0,1], i=0,...,r, and let the two

evidence:
# A killed coefficient chain and the unpaid interval reward

Status: COMPLETE JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT, UNVERIFIED. The full zero-remainder
hereditary interval implication is neither proved nor refuted. One specific
killed-chain/Doob-transform mechanism has been carried through and tested on
two actual full arrays. Its first quantitative maximum-principle bound is
insufficient, and conditioning on return discards a strictly positive,
explicitly calculated term. These are obstructions to this proof mechanism,
not counterexamples to interval heredity.

This is max2's ONE allocated analytical round after completed48, under
TASK.md and master_guidance b5768bac207b0736. Completed ceiling49 and attempted
ceiling50 are unchanged. Latest guidance 6f0edac954b884a8 leaves this allocation
unchanged. No numerical evaluation, solver, symbolic program, parameter scan,
benchmark replay, formal verifier, fact_submit, installation, consult, or
subagent was used. There is no renewal or claim of observing the outer loop's
post-return counter or termination. The original Goal remains OPEN.

Accepted inputs: fact04219554e41d9750, proof Sections10--11, for the original
full polynomial identity and primitive composition; fact1252b8823bb5a290 for
the interpolation orientation. Findings821f43aa871af2a2,779f76962263fabc,
c1d41aaebcae37de,ac0c1e866da0d926 are awareness only. Every auxiliary assertion
used here is derived jointly below. In particular no hereditary or scalar
capacity theorem from those drafts is a premise.

The immutable input821f43aa871af2a2 was read and its SHA256 matched
2b96fb4095e0fc931b8ad619667feacf6a636294ed25cea3e7fb6389bb6778a3.
The mechanism is a random walk of CERTIFICATE coefficients. It imposes no
random, orthogonal, or Markov law on gradient trajectories.

## 1. Original space and algebraic zero-step isolation

Fix a physical length r>=1, h_i>=0 for 0<=i<r, s=sum_(i<r)h_i, and A=1+s.
All r+1 formal gradients remain independent. Define

 T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, T_it=0 for t>i,
 e=(1,...,1)^T,
 L=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,
 omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(r-1),2s)^T,
 D=diag(h_i(2-h_i) for i<r,-s(s+2)).

The complete hypotheses are

 Lambda_ii=0, Lambda_ij>=0 for i!=j,
 L^T e=omega,                 D+(LT+T^T L^T)/2=0.       (1)

There is no support, rank, factorization, or symmetry restriction. Put

 x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,
 Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
 Qbar_ij=-2Q_ji,
 mu_ij=Lambda_ji/2,
 V_h=2sum_(i<r)h_i(f_i-f_r)
       +sum_(i<r)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-sA||g_r||^2.

Fact04219554e41d9750 gives the full polynomial identity

              V_h=sum_(i!=j)mu_ij Qbar_ij.              (2)

It holds for arbitrary formal values and gradients, not only interpolable
data. Fact1252b8823bb5a290 fixes Q_ij<=0 on actual normalized smooth convex
samples; no actual interpolation assertion is needed for the formal tests
below.

For i<r let t_i=h_i-1, I_i=sum_(j<i)mu_ji, J_i=sum_(j>i)mu_ji. Matching the
f_i coefficient in (2) gives out_mu(i)-in_mu(i)=h_i. Matching ||g_i||^2 gives

                  t_i J_i-I_i=(1-t_i^2)/2.              (3)

Indeed the squared differences contribute -h_i-2I_i-2J_i, and precisely
the terms Qbar_(j,i) with j>i contribute the additional diagonal 2h_i J_i.
For 0<h_i<=1 the left side of (3) is nonpositive and the right side is
positive. Thus every positive step exceeds1. If h_i=0, (3) makes I_i+J_i=0;
all incoming mu entries vanish, and zero net flow makes every outgoing
entry vanish. The entire original Lambda row and column at i are zero.

List the positive-step indices increasingly and retain the original terminal
r. Restriction to those indices preserves (1): zero steps contribute no
trajectory displacement, and every removed multiplier row and column was
already zero. Conversely every removed T column is its coordinate vector,
and the corresponding L row and column are zero, so the full remainder
extends by zero on those independent coordinates. This is algebraic
relabeling only; no physical iteration is removed from a horizon comparison.

If all steps vanish, Lambda=0 and there is no nonempty positive interval.
Henceforth r denotes the relabeled positive length, so h_i>1 and s>0.
Substitution of the unit quadratic with g_0=1, g_(i+1)=-t_i g_i gives
V_h=1-A^2 g_r^2 and all Qbar_ij=0. Thus A product_(i<r)t_i=1. This global
restriction will not be substituted for the unproved interval restriction.

## 2. The normalization is forced by the full matrix identity

Let S_i=sum_(t<i)h_t and a_i=1+S_i, including S_r=s and a_r=A. Let

 o_i=sum_j Lambda_ij,                  c_i=sum_j Lambda_ji.

For i<r, flow gives c_i=o_i+2h_i>0. The terminal matrix entry in (1) is
-s(s+2)+o_r=0, since the terminal column of T is its coordinate vector.
Consequently

                  o_r=s(s+2),          c_r=s^2.         (4)

Write R0=s(s+2). In particular the terminal normalizers below are positive.

The full matrix equation, applied to e, gives

                   L a=-2D e-T^T omega.

For i<r, (T^T omega)_i=2h_i(S_i+h_i-1), while the terminal entry is2s.
Therefore

 (L a)_i=-2h_i a_i (i<r),          (L a)_r=2sA,
                 sum_j Lambda_ij a_j=c_i a_i.          (5)

This calculation uses the full matrix equation and exact flow, rather than
assuming a subword certificate. Since a_i>0, (5) also implies o_i>0 at every
retained index. Zero row degree was resolved before any row normalization;
no irreducibility assumption is used.

## 3. A killed chain with all source and sink masses accounted for

Add a cemetery state dagger. From a nonterminal i<r use transitions

 P_ij=Lambda_ij/c_i for 0<=j<=r,
 P_i,dagger=2h_i/c_i.                                  (6)

Both r and dagger are absorbing. The row sum is1 by flow. Every retained
nonterminal killing probability is positive. With epsilon the minimum of
these finitely many probabilities, the probability of surviving n more
nonterminal transitions is at most (1-epsilon)^n. Thus absorption occurs
almost surely with finite mean, even if the original array is reducible or
has missing edges. The transient submatrix P_U, indexed by U={0,...,r-1},
satisfies

 G=sum_(n>=0)P_U^n=(Id-P_U)^(-1)>=0.                    (7)

This follows directly from the geometric row-sum bound; no inverse is
asserted for the singular full Laplacian.

Set a_dagger=0. Equation(5) says that a is harmonic at all nonterminal
states for (6). With boundary values a_r=A,a_dagger=0, uniqueness follows
from the same row-sum bound: two solutions differ by P_U^n times their
bounded difference, which tends to zero. Conditioning on the first
transition gives a harmonic hitting-probability vector, so

             Prob_i(hit r before dagger)=a_i/A.        (8)

Start an excursion by making one INITIAL jump from r to i<r with law

                    beta_i=Lambda_ri/R0,               (9)

then run (6) until its first absorption. This initial jump is part of every
edge reward and may not be discarded. Let N_ij be its total number of
traversals of the original ordered edge i->j, including the initial jump.
The expected visits to i<r are c_i/R0. To verify this, the occupation row
u obeys u=beta+u P_U, whose unique solution is beta G. The candidate
c_i/R0 obeys that equation because c_i=Lambda_ri+sum_(j<r)Lambda_ji.
Therefore

                R0 E N_ij=Lambda_ij                    (10)

for every original edge, including edges into r and the initial edges out
of r. The chance of killing at i is 2h_i/R0. It follows that

 Prob(return)=s/(s+2),       Prob(killed)=2/(s+2),
 Prob(killing vertex=i | killed)=h_i/s.                (11)

These formulas also follow from (8): sum_i Lambda_ri a_i=c_r A=s^2 A.
Thus every source, return, and killing weight has been paid.

For later use put b_i=A-a_i=s-S_i on the original states; b_r=0, and set
b_dagger=A. Both a and b are harmonic for (6), and b_i>0 for i<r.
The two conditional laws are explicit. Conditional on return, the initial
law and subsequent transitions are

 beta_i^+=Lambda_ri a_i/(s^2 A),
 P_ij^+=Lambda_ij a_j/(c_i a_i),    P_i,dagger^+=0.     (12)

Conditional on killing, they are

 beta_i^-=Lambda_ri b_i/(2sA),
 P_ij^-=Lambda_ij b_j/(c_i b_i),
 P_i,dagger^-=2h_i A/(c_i b_i).                        (13)

These formulas are obtained by multiplying a transition probability by
the ratio of its successor's and current state's absorption probabilities.
Their row sums and initial sums are1 by (5) and its b counterpart. Finite
mean absorption persists because a conditional survival probability is
at most the original survival probability divided by the positive event
probability. This proves the needed stopping and summability properties
without assuming reversibility or irreducibility.

## 4. Both interval boundaries become a signed edge reward

Fix I=[l,k), 0<=l<k<=r. Define

 Pfx=S_l, H=S_k-S_l,
 v_l=1, v_(i+1)=-t_i v_i for l<=i<k,
 p=v_k, q=|p|=product_(i in I)t_i,
 psi_i=1 for i<l, psi_i=v_i for l<=i<k, psi_i=p for i>=k.

The desired conclusion is (1+H)q>=1, equivalently

                    Delta_I=(1+H)^2 p^2-1>=0.          (14)

Use formal gradients psi_i and choose x_l=1. Define formal positions and
values by

 x_i=1+Pfx-S_i, f_i=1/2+Pfx-S_i                       (i<l),
 x_i=v_i,      f_i=v_i^2/2                           (l<=i<k),
 x_i=p(1-(S_i-S_k)), f_i=p^2/2-p^2(S_i-S_k)           (i>=k).

The original GD displacements hold, including both exterior regions.
The only potentially nonzero Qbar residuals are

 Qbar_ij=2(S_l-S_i)(1-psi_j)        (i<l,j>=l),
 Qbar_ji=2(S_j-S_k)p(psi_i-p)       (j>=k,i<k).         (15)

For a left/middle pair, put d0=S_l-S_i. The first residual expands to
1+2d0-v_j^2-2v_j(1+d0-v_j)-(1-v_j)^2=2d0(1-v_j);
the reverse residual is zero. For a middle/right pair with e0=S_j-S_k,
substitution gives Qbar_ij=0 and Qbar_ji=2e0 p(v_i-p).
For a left/right pair the two orientations give 2d0(1-p) and
2e0 p(1-p), respectively. Within each of the three regions they vanish.
Thus all crossings are retained and neither orientation is double-counted.

Define the original boundary sums

 C_L=sum_(i<l,j>=l)mu_ij(S_l-S_i)(1-psi_j),
 C_R=sum_(j>=k,i<k)mu_ji(S_j-S_k)p(psi_i-p).            (16)

The value of the left side of(2) is

                 (Pfx+1)^2-(Pfx+H+1)^2 p^2.

Here the prefix contribution to 2sum h_i f_i+sum h_i(1-h_i)psi_i^2 is
Pfx^2+2Pfx; the interval contribution telescopes to1-p^2; with suffix
mass Rtail=s-Pfx-H the suffix contribution is p^2(2Rtail-Rtail^2).
The terminal terms are -s(s+2)p^2+2sRtail p^2. Adding them proves the
displayed value. Consequently

 Delta_I=B_I-2(C_L+C_R),
 B_I=Pfx[Pfx+2-(Pfx+2H+2)p^2].                        (17)

These are formal polynomial tests, not asserted convex interpolation data.

For an ORIGINAL Lambda edge u->w assign reward

 R_I(u,w)=1_(u>=l,w<l)(S_l-S_w)(1-psi_u)
          +1_(u<k,w>=k)(S_w-S_k)p(psi_u-p).            (18)

The indicators select disjoint kinds of edges. Rewards of killing edges
are zero. In particular an initial edge r->w with w<l has reward
(S_l-S_w)(1-p), and must be retained. The reversal Lambda=2mu^T gives

        sum_(u,w)Lambda_uw R_I(u,w)=2(C_L+C_R).         (19)

Let Gamma_I be the sum of(18) over the entire killed excursion, including
its initial terminal jump. The finite mean duration and bounded rewards
justify summing expectations. Equation(10) yields

                   2(C_L+C_R)=R0 E Gamma_I.            (20)

The exact missing estimate is therefore

                         R0 E Gamma_I<=B_I.           (21)

Equation(20) alone is not offered as progress closing(21).

## 5. What the maximum principle actually supplies

For i<r put n_i=sum_j Lambda_ij R_I(i,j), z_i=E_i(sum of rewards before
absorption), and J_I=sum_i Lambda_ri R_I(r,i). Let z_r=z_dagger=0. Then

 z=G(n_i/c_i)_(i<r),
 R0 E Gamma_I=J_I+sum_i Lambda_ri z_i.                 (22)

Because b_dagger=A but the zero-boundary vector b_U has both terminal
boundary coordinates set to0 in the transient equation,

             (Id-P_U)b_U=(2A h_i/c_i)_(i<r).           (23)

Define the concrete scalar barrier

                 theta_I=max_(i<r) n_i/(2A h_i).

Positivity of G and(23) prove the valid bound

             z<=theta_I b_U,
 R0 E Gamma_I<=J_I+2sA theta_I.                        (24)

No sign of theta_I is presumed. The last equality uses
sum_i Lambda_ri b_i=2sA. This is an actual maximum-principle estimate for
the actual chain. Section7.2 shows that it does NOT imply(21), even for a
legal prefix with B_I=0: its right side is strictly positive there.

The exact discarded term can be displayed without a qualitative appeal to
positive or negative edges. Set delta_i=2A h_i theta_I-n_i>=0. Then

 R0 E Gamma_I=J_I+2sA theta_I
       -sum_i Lambda_ri [G(delta_j/c_j)_j]_i.          (25)

Hence repairing this barrier requires the quantitative bound

 sum_i Lambda_ri [G(delta_j/c_j)_j]_i
                         >=J_I+2sA theta_I-B_I.       (26)

The occupation relation Lambda_(r,U)G=(c_i)_i makes the left side equal
to sum_i delta_i. Thus using source conservation alone cancels the barrier
and gives back J_I+sum_i n_i<=B_I. It supplies no new signed inequality.
This is the precise first failed quantitative estimate, rather than an
assumption that every crossing edge has a favorable sign.

## 6. Conditioning has a real, generally positive cost

Let E_+ and E_- denote expectations for(12) and(13), respectively. Equation
(11) gives the exact decomposition

         2(C_L+C_R)=s^2 E_+ Gamma_I+2s E_- Gamma_I.     (27)

For any original edge u->w, expected traversals multiplied by the indicator
of eventual return equal the unconditioned expected traversals multiplied
by a_w/A. This is first-step conditioning after the traversal; absolute
summability permits summing it over all visits. The initial edge obeys the
same statement. Thus the omitted killing contribution has the exact form

 K_I:=2s E_- Gamma_I
       =(1/A)sum_(u,w)Lambda_uw b_w R_I(u,w),          (28)

and the return contribution has a_w in place of b_w. The weighted bound
still required after the Doob transform is

                    s^2 E_+ Gamma_I<=B_I-K_I.          (29)

There is no theorem here making K_I nonpositive or determined by the
killing vertex. Section7.3 proves K_I>B_I>0 in an actual interior-interval
example. Section8 proves K_I=8 at a tight interval in a balanced basic
array, and gives two killed paths with the same killing vertex but
different rewards. Replacing(29) by a free conditioning argument would
lose these terms.

## 7. Exact test on the legal array with opposite crossing signs

### 7.1 Full original array and its certification

Let d be the positive root of d^2+5d-4=0 and put

 A=5+d, kappa=A^2/16, K=kappa-1,
 h=(1+d,3/2,3/2), s=4+d.

The polynomial is strictly increasing on [0,infinity), negative at0 and
positive at1. Hence 0<d<1, dA=4, K>0, and

                       K(4-d)=2(1+d).                 (30)

To check(30), multiplying it by16 gives
(A^2-16)(4-d)-32(1+d)=-(1+d)(d^2+5d-4)=0.
Define the entire original array in indices0,1,2,3 by

 Lambda=
 [0,      0,          0,             Kd              ]
 [3K/2,   0,          kappa,         kappa/2+3K/2     ]
 [3K/2,   7kappa/2,   0,             17kappa/2+3K/2   ]
 [K,      kappa,      14kappa,       0               ]. (31)

Every entry has the required sign. Row-minus-column sums are

## 8. Exact test on the balanced basic array with two factor channels

Let w=sqrt(2), lambda=1+w, kappa=lambda^2, and h=(w,2,w). Then
s=2lambda, A=kappa. Consider the full original array

 Lambda=
 [0,       2,                 0,                 0]

Its entries are nonnegative. For completeness a single step w obeys
V_(w)=-2Q_01-2lambda Q_10, by expanding the two residuals and using
(w-1)lambda=1. Join two such children with bridge2. Their capacities are
lambda, and d=1 solves d(2lambda+d)=lambda^2. The accepted join gives

         -(kappa-1)[w Q_21+Q_31+Q_13+w Q_23].          (40)

such as Lambda_30 are retained; no one-factor substitution is made.

Take the suffix I=[2,3). Then Pfx=w+2, H=w, p=-(w-1), and Delta_I=0.
Here B_I=4(w+2)=4lambda w: indeed
(3w+4)(w-1)^2=w, so the bracket in(17) equals4.

                  R_I(3,1)=2(1+w-1)=2w.

       R0 E Gamma_I=4lambda w=B_I.                    (41)

Their sum is4w+8=4lambda w, as required. Ignoring killed excursions would

The killing-vertex marginal h_i/s cannot determine this reward. The two

each specified original edge is positive in(39), and killing at0 has
positive probability. Both are killed at0. The first has total reward2w,
and the second has total reward0. Thus the relevant cost depends on the

The three singleton interval products of this word are1,3,1; both
length-two products are2w-1>1, and the full product is1. Thus it is also

## 9. Remaining interface and bounded-round conclusion

The killed process is well defined for every original array satisfying(1),
after the proved isolation of zero coordinates. It retains the original
terminal source, every crossing entry, both exterior boundaries, all
alternating weights, and every absorption cost. It requires no irreducible,
reversible, positive-support, factorized, or inherited-subword assumption.

The attempted direct estimates have the following precise status:

1. Normalization, harmonic hitting probabilities, finite occupation measure,
   conditional laws, and full coefficient recovery are derived jointly.
2. The complete interval crossing expression is the signed excursion reward
   in(18)--(21), not an interpolable gradient process.
3. The concrete death-potential maximum principle(24) is valid but too weak:
   (33) is positive where the required prefix budget is zero. Its exact
   missing compensation is(26); source conservation by itself is circular.
4. Conditioning on return leaves the history-dependent term(28). It is
   larger than the entire interior budget in(37)--(38), and equals8 at the
   tight basic interval(42). This term cannot be dropped or replaced by the
   marginal distribution of the killing vertex.

Accordingly the first unproved implication for this mechanism remains

 s^2 E_+ Gamma_I
 <=Pfx[Pfx+2-(Pfx+2H+2)p^2]
      -(1/A)sum_(u,w)Lambda_uw(s-S_w)R_I(u,w),          (43)

for every interval and every full original M=0 array. Equivalently one
must establish(26) from more than the unsigned flow/harmonic accounting.
No such signed comparison is proved here, and no full-array violation of
the interval theorem is produced. The explicit arrays satisfy heredity.

This report does not infer a capacity ceiling, a theorem for arbitrary
M>=0, a neighborhood theorem at seven steps, or a conclusion about the
original unrestricted exact-profile Goal. The earlier scalar extremal
draft cannot be used downstream because its full-M0 interval hypothesis
has not been established. All new claims remain UNVERIFIED, with no
fact_submit and no new accepted fact. This completes the one assigned
mechanism/round; no additional allocation is inferred.

## 10. Retrieval, verification status, and glossary

The query-memory, search-math-results, direct-proving, and
construct-counterexamples procedures were used. Matlas returned two
inapplicable results and the finite harmonic-extension Proposition12 of
Yang Chu and Robert Hough, *Solution of the 15 puzzle problem*,
arXiv:1908.07106v1 (2019), https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.07106.
The exact source was downloaded and read around the Markov-chain
definitions, Proposition12, and the return-probability proof in Section5.
That proposition assumes irreducibility and cites its proof elsewhere;
the surrounding application uses a reversible torus walk. Those hypotheses
are not imported. The finite absorption and harmonic uniqueness arguments
needed here were instead proved explicitly by(6)--(8). The reference
provides a proof-pattern comparison, not an external mathematical premise.

Operational retrieval errors were exposed rather than treated as success:
project-name memory calls failed with DANUS_AGENTS_ROOT unset; the worker-
pinned calls succeeded. A lecture-note PDF download failed SSL certificate
validation and web retrieval timed out. The arXiv PDF downloaded, but
pdftotext was unavailable; its source was then retrieved. Treating the
source as tar returned invalid header; inspection identified a single
gzip-compressed TeX file, which was decompressed successfully and read.
No package was installed and no mathematical program was evaluated.

# Finite equal-angle obstruction to polynomial activation allowances
Status: UNVERIFIED companion to the joint spiral checkpoint candidate cdd7f057606aeb18.
No fact_submit or mathematical computation was used.

Targeted claim: for the specified spiral support geometry with a required zero
minimum at the old reset point, an inverse scale c_sp S+A(kappa), or
c_sp S+kappa b+A(kappa), can work for every ordinary word with a fixed
polynomially bounded nonnegative A(kappa) as kappa tends to0.
This claim is refuted by the following exact finite family, at draft level.

Fix 0<kappa<=1/2 and set epsilon=kappa,
Theta=arctan(1/kappa), c_sp=sqrt(1+kappa^2)exp(kappa Theta),
d_sp=1-kappa^2, T_sp=[exp(d_sp Theta/kappa)-1]/d_sp.
Put e(theta)=(cos theta,-sin theta),
e_t(theta)=(-sin theta,-cos theta), R_sp(theta)=c_sp exp(-kappa theta),
v(theta)=R_sp(theta)e(theta), and K=conv({0} union {v(theta):0<=theta<=Theta}).
The vector n_sp(theta)=e(theta)+kappa e_t(theta) supports K at v(theta):
its inner product with v(phi), divided by R_sp(theta), is
exp(-kappa Delta)(cos Delta+kappa sin Delta), Delta=phi-theta.
Its derivative is -(1+kappa^2)exp(-kappa Delta)sin Delta, so its maximum
on [-Theta,Theta] is1, at0. It is also strictly larger at v(theta) than at0.

For any integer M>=1 set Delta=Theta/M, theta_l=Theta-l Delta, and
A_D=exp(-kappa Delta)(cos Delta+sin Delta/kappa),
B_D=exp(-kappa Delta)sin Delta/kappa,
t_0=0, t_l=B_D+A_D t_(l-1),
r_l=R_sp(theta_l)[(1+t_l)e(theta_l)+kappa t_l e_t(theta_l)],
alpha_l=1-exp(-kappa Delta)cos Delta+B_D+(1+kappa^2)B_D t_(l-1).

All t_l>=0 and alpha_l>=0. Resolving radial and tangential components
gives r_l-r_(l-1)=alpha_l v(theta_l). The supporting-normal calculation
gives Pi_K(r_l)=v(theta_l). Hence the ACTUAL finite chronological
ordinary word (alpha_M,...,alpha_1) follows these projection gradients
from r_M to r_0=(kappa,-1). Every step is finite; this family is defined
analytically, without executing any sweep.

Let S_M=sum alpha_l, P_M=(r_M)_1-kappa, Q_M=-(r_M)_2-1.
Then P_M=c_sp(1+t_M)-kappa and 1+Q_M=c_sp kappa t_M.
For sufficiently large M, A_D>1. Exact summation gives
t_M=B_D(A_D^M-1)/(A_D-1),
S_M=M a_D+(1+kappa^2)B_D(t_M-M B_D)/(A_D-1),
where a_D=1-exp(-kappa Delta)cos Delta+B_D.
The derivatives at Delta0 imply
t_M -> T_sp,
S_M -> (1+kappa^2)T_sp/d_sp-kappa(1+kappa^2)Theta/d_sp.

Now center and scale the finite support envelope to start at (1,0):
z_circ=(1,0)-sigma(kappa+P_M,-1-Q_M),
phi(z)=sigma max_(v in V_fin)<v,z-z_circ>,
where V_fin contains0, both endpoint vectors and every gradient just constructed.
The terminal local jet is
x_end=z_circ+sigma(kappa,-1),
g_end=sigma(kappa,-1),
f_end=sigma^2(1+kappa^2)/2.
It is an actual envelope jet, because (kappa,-1) belongs to K.

If the old reset point0 is to remain a minimizer with f_star=0,g_star=0,
the ORIGINAL directed interpolation row must satisfy
Q_(end,star)=f_end-<g_end,x_end>+||g_end||^2/2
 =sigma[-kappa+sigma(kappa(kappa+P_M)+1+Q_M)]<=0.
This is exactly the endpoint-plane condition phi(0)=0. It forces

    sigma^(-1)>=kappa+P_M+(1+Q_M)/kappa.

Thus the excess after paying the FULL available horizontal budget is
E_M=kappa+P_M+(1+Q_M)/kappa-c_sp S_M, and its exact limit is

    E_sp=c_sp[1+(1-3kappa^2)T_sp/d_sp
                       +kappa(1+kappa^2)Theta/d_sp]>0,
    lim_(kappa->0) kappa log E_sp=pi/2.

Therefore a universal inverse scale c_sp S+A(kappa) requires A(kappa)>=E_sp.
For the form c_sp S+kappa b+A(kappa), take the legal fixed local
checkpoint b=1+kappa^(-2); it requires A(kappa)>=E_sp-kappa b.
If A(kappa)<=C kappa^(-p) for any fixed finite C,p, choose kappa small
enough to violate this strict limiting inequality, then choose a finite
M large enough. The displayed ORIGINAL row Q_(end,star) is strictly positive.
The failed conclusion is the promised preserved minimum/interpolation
condition, not smoothness of the support envelope at a different minimum.

This obstruction keeps the actual finite chronological states and pays
c_sp S_M-P_M before declaring a deficit. It is stronger than merely
observing Q_M is large. It applies only to this support curve and the
specified zero-height reset architecture. Positive-height gluings,
other endpoints/curves, and unrestricted W_n remain open.

          +sum_i nu_i[sum_(t<i)h_t<g_i,g_t>+||g_i||^2/2]
          +sum_i xi_i||g_i||^2/2
          +sum_(i!=j finite)K_ij[<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2]. (2)

Its original matrix is [[q,-nu^T/2],[-nu/2,C]]. Every entry is

    C_ii=out_i-1_(i=n)-h_i sum_(j>i)K_ij,
    2C_ij=-(K_ij+K_ji)-h_j sum_(v>j)K_iv
                             +h_i[nu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j, (3)
    out_i=nu_i+sum_j K_ij.

To check (2)--(3), each optimum-incoming row contributes its displayed
initial-point mixed term and its gradient position term. Optimum-outgoing
rows have no position term. Half the total incident mass at i, by (1), is
out_i-1_(i=n), including both optimum directions. A forward position row out
of i subtracts h_i K_ij from its diagonal. Difference squares and the two
possible position-row source indices give exactly the off-diagonal in (3).
No original coordinate or interpolation pair is removed.

When q>0, square completion gives

    M(q)=q||x_0-sum_i nu_i g_i/(2q)||^2
                       +sum_(i,j)[C_ij-nu_i nu_j/(4q)]<g_i,g_j>. (4)

Full PSD of (2), not just a compression of (4), would imply W_n(h)<=q.

For orientation, the actual Huber function Hub(x)=x^2/2 on |x|<=1 and
|x|-1/2 otherwise, started at x_0=D, has g_i=1 and
f_i=D-P_i-1/2 at every finite query. All finite Q_ij and Q_(i,star) are
zero; Q_(star,i)=-(2S-P_i). Consequently a necessary paid-row budget at
q=(1+eta)/D is

    sum_i xi_i(2S-P_i)<=D eta.                            (5)

At eta=0 this forces every xi_i=0. A tight PSD quadratic must then annihilate
(D,1,...,1). Direct differentiation of (2), using (1), gives the finite
coordinate contact equations

    (2S-P_i)nu_i=2h_i+sum_j K_ij(P_i-P_j).                (6)

For a derivation, twice the i-th gradient row sum of C is
2h_i+(1+P_i)nu_i+sum_j K_ij(P_i-P_j): the summed GD displacements use
the full flow, and the gradient-difference rows contribute nu_i. The equation
2Ce=D nu is therefore exactly (6). Equations (1),(6) are algebraic contact
conditions, not a positivity assertion.

## 2. Exact common-gradient compression with arbitrary finite redistribution

Consider ANY last join (H_j,d,H_j), with k=2^j-1 and physical bridge
d=1+a*c^j. In THIS section and Sections3,5,6,

    A=sum H_j, t=A+d, S=2A+d, D=1+2S, D_c=1+2A,
    p_l=sum of child steps before l, 0<=l<=k.

L_l=l include the bridge query L_k. Right labels R_i=k+1+i include the
original terminal R_k=n. On the exact original-coordinate subspace

    g_(L_l)=u for EVERY left label,
    g_(R_i)=v for EVERY right label, x_0=x,

positions are x_(L_l)=x-p_l u and x_(R_i)=x-t u-p_i v. This is a
quadratic-form test subspace, not a constraint on the original model.

Define nonnegative cross arrays and their moments

    B_il=K_(R_i,L_l), F_li=K_(L_l,R_i),
    B=sum_(i,l) B_il, F=sum_(l,i) F_li,
    pi_B=sum_(i,l)p_l B_il,
    pi_F=sum_(l,i)p_i F_li,
    nu_L=sum_l nu_(L_l), nu_R=sum_i nu_(R_i),
    xi_L=sum_l xi_(L_l), xi_R=sum_i xi_(R_i).

Here B is a cross-row total, distinct from the benchmark B_n. Then the FULL
polynomial restricts EXACTLY to

    M(q)=q||x||^2-nu_L<x,u>-nu_R<x,v>
                      +Gamma_L||u||^2+Gamma_R||v||^2+J<u,v>, (7)
    Gamma_L=B+pi_B-tF+sum_l(1+p_l)xi_(L_l),
    Gamma_R=D_c+F+pi_F+sum_i(1+p_i)xi_(R_i),
    J=t nu_R+(t-1)B-pi_B-F-pi_F.                         (8)

Thus its three-coordinate matrix is

    [[q,-nu_L/2,-nu_R/2],
     [-nu_L/2,Gamma_L,J/2],
     [-nu_R/2,J/2,Gamma_R]].                             (9)

Derivation retaining every within-block row: internal left finite positions
sum to sum_l p_l[xi_(L_l)-nu_(L_l)+sum_i B_il-sum_i F_li]||u||^2
by left flow. Right positions sum to
[2A+sum_i p_i(xi_(R_i)-nu_(R_i)-sum_l B_il+sum_l F_li)]||v||^2
by right flow.
An individual backward row has quadratic coefficients

    ||u||^2/2+(p_i+1/2)||v||^2+(t-p_l-1)<u,v>,

and an individual forward row has

    (p_l-t+1/2)||u||^2+||v||^2/2-(p_i+1)<u,v>.

The optimum-incoming rows supply nu_l(p_l+1/2)||u||^2 on the left and
nu_i[(p_i+1/2)||v||^2+t<u,v>] on the right, together with their x mixed
terms. The outgoing optimum rows supply xi_i||g_i||^2/2. Insert these into
(2). The p_l nu_l,p_i nu_i and the other internal-source moments cancel.
Aggregate flow nu_L-xi_L=B-F and nu_R-xi_R+B-F=2 reduces the remaining
diagonals to (8). This proves (7)--(9) for arbitrary final finite arrays,
including signed changes to their predecessors.

For xi=0, q=1/D, full PSD would force (D,1,1) into the kernel of (9).
It follows that

    pi_B-tF-pi_F=2S nu_L-2t.                             (10)

The Schur remainder in (9) is then necessarily
kappa_2*[[1,-1],[-1,1]], where

    kappa_2=Gamma_L-D nu_L^2/4=Gamma_R-D nu_R^2/4>=0.    (11)

Indeed the two row sums of that Schur remainder vanish. Since B-F=nu_L,

# Explicit alternative-state tests for the three terminal screens

Status: JOINT UNVERIFIED. These tests refute weaker universal claims only.
They do not assert that any tested state is reached from e_1.
The frozen static function, backward definitions, physical word and true
radius are exactly those of joint_analysis.md, shared finding8dfaa8cef518215c.
No new function, step, computation or formal submission is introduced.

Use its C=beta+sqrt(1+2beta), kappa=1+beta^2, sigma_i, ell_i, A_i,D_i.
A component vanishes exactly when x_j<=A_j and
x_(j+1)>=beta*(x_j-ell_j).

## A. Cross-time pairing need not be nonnegative

Choose 2<=i<=k-2 and a physical suffix step h=b_(m-2) satisfying

    h>2kappa+2ell_(i+2)/(beta*sigma_i)
                                 +2C*sigma_(i+1)/sigma_i.
    alpha=h/2.

Set x_i=A_i, x_(i+1)=ell_(i+1)-kappa*sigma_i,
x_(i+2)=ell_(i+2), and x_j=0 for i+3<=j<=k.
Set x_(k+1)=ell_(k+1)+D_(k+1).

Here is an explicit choice of every earlier coordinate, removing any
implicit "sufficiently negative" selection. The known proposed update
of coordinate i is x_i^+=A_i-alpha*beta*sigma_i. Set

    x_(i-1)=min(A_(i-1),
              ell_(i-1)+min(x_i,x_i^+)/beta)-sigma_(i-1),

and successively for j=i-2,...,1 set

    x_j=min(A_j,ell_j+x_(j+1)/beta)-sigma_j.

Finally replace x_1 by min(x_1,A_1-beta*D_2).
Lowering x_1 cannot spoil its zero-cone inequality. At both the initial
and proposed next samples every component j<i has nonpositive input and
edge residuals. Hence its projection is zero, and (6) leaves all these earlier
coordinates unchanged, verifying the proposed update consistently.

Initially r_i=0,z_i=kappa*sigma_i, so

    (P_i,Q_i)=(beta*sigma_i,sigma_i).

The next component has input <ell_(i+1) and output ell_(i+2), so it is
zero. At j=i+2 the input is ell_(i+2) with nonnegative output, hence zero;
all later retired components are also zero. Therefore the retired
combined-gradient vector before the step is exactly
(beta*sigma_i,-sigma_i) on coordinates i,i+1.

After the step,

    r_i^+=-alpha*beta*sigma_i,
    z_i^+=kappa*sigma_i*(1-alpha)<0,
    r_(i+1)^+=(alpha-kappa)*sigma_i-ell_(i+2)/beta
                                               >C*sigma_(i+1).

Thus component i vanishes, while i+1 is in its horizontal cap since
its output remains ell_(i+2). All earlier components are zero by the
explicit selection; later retired components stay zero. The terminal
scalar remains isolated: its excess after the step is
D_(k+1)*(1-h/[2(1+S_(m-1))])>0, because
S_(m-1)>=b_(m-2)=h. Thus no omitted last gradient enters the retired vector.

The retired combined-gradient vector after the step is exactly
(0,C*sigma_(i+1)) on these coordinates. Consequently

    <d_after,d_before>=-C*sigma_i*sigma_(i+1)<0.

This uses the full static function and its physical available h.
It refutes universal nonnegativity of cross-time retired gradient
pairings. It does not refute an integrated inequality on the actual
initialized trajectory.

## B. Own-checkpoint margins are not sufficient for retirement invariance

Choose 2<=i<=k-1 and h=b_(J+i-2), alpha=h/2. This step occurs in the
complete H_(J+i-1) after checkpoint i. Assume the explicit finite conditions

    beta*D_(i+1)-beta^2*D_i-ell_(i+1)/beta
                                             >=kappa*sigma_(i-1),
    beta*T_i/M_i<1, h*C<2M_(i+1),
    u_(i+1)>=C+sqrt(1+2beta)*y_(i+1)/beta.                 (B1)

Set

    x_(i-1)=A_(i-1)-beta*D_i,
    x_i=A_i-beta*D_(i+1),
    x_(i+1)=ell_(i+1)+D_(i+1),
    x_j=0 for j>=i+2.

If i>=3, choose the earlier coordinates by the same zero-cone recipe
as in A, using boundary coordinate x_(i-1) and its proposed next value

    x_(i-1)^+=x_(i-1)-alpha*beta*sigma_(i-1).

That makes every component j<i-1 zero before and after. Enforce also
x_1<=A_1-beta*D_2 as in A. For i=2 no additional earlier coordinate
is needed: x_1=A_1-beta*D_2 already has the permanent first margin.

Now r_(i-1)=-beta*D_i<0 and

    z_(i-1)=beta*D_(i+1)-beta^2*D_i-ell_(i+1)/beta.

Condition(B1) and the exact edge formula give

    P_(i-1)=beta*sigma_(i-1),
    Q_(i-1)=sigma_(i-1)>0.

The own component i has its exact negative checkpoint margins

    r_i=-beta*D_(i+1), z_i=-kappa*D_(i+1),

so P_i=Q_i=0. The next component is precisely at its local block's
starting pair (ell_(i+1)+D_(i+1),0). The last condition in (B1)
therefore gives P_(i+1)=C*sigma_(i+1), Q_(i+1)=0.
Every old and future derivative is evaluated from the same function;
none is removed in this update.

Using D_i=sigma_(i-1)*(h/2-1),

    r_i^+=-beta*D_(i+1)+alpha*sigma_(i-1)
          =-beta*D_(i+1)+D_i+sigma_(i-1)>0,
    x_(i+1)^+=ell_(i+1)
                         +D_(i+1)*(1-h*C/[2M_(i+1)])
                                                >ell_(i+1).

Its new actual envelope value is consequently the positive horizontal
Huber Hub_(C*sigma_i)(r_i^+). The earlier zero-cone recipe verifies
the proposed previous-coordinate update; for i=2 it follows from Q_0=0.

The conditions in (B1) hold eventually in the joint scale derivation:
the amplitude ratios are uniformly positive, beta=1/k, the sigma and
translation terms are exponentially smaller than beta*D_i, and
h*C/(2M_(i+1)) tends to (lambda-2)/lambda<1.
No numerical threshold or finite-depth m>=1536 claim is inferred.

This refutes invariance based only on own-checkpoint margins and earlier
negative margins. It retains a saturated incoming Q_(i-1) and a legal
later step. The simultaneous tested point is an alternative state; the
true later state must instead be derived from the complete ordered history
in equations(32),(33),(33a). Initialized retirement is neither disproved
nor established.

### B3. An exact scoped failure of a source-free horizontal-exit reset

The claim that every horizontal exit automatically has z_i=O(sigma_i)
is false for the SAME frozen function, even with no incoming gradient
and no downstream horizontal gradient. The following is an ALTERNATIVE
state test, not an initialized trajectory or a lower witness.

Choose2<=i<=k-2 and a physical available h=b_(m-2), alpha=h/2, with
alpha>1 and alpha beta>C/2. Choose q in(0,1) close to1 and write p=p(q).
Set

    t=[(alpha-1)sigma_i p+L_i/2]/(p-beta)>0,
    r_i= sigma_i p+t(p-beta)=alpha sigma_i p+L_i/2,
    v_i= sigma_i q+t(q+beta),
    x_i=A_i+r_i, x_(i+1)=ell_(i+1)-v_i,
    x_(i+2)=ell_(i+2).

The vector (r_i,-v_i)-(sigma_i p,-sigma_i q)
is t(p-beta,-q-beta), an outward circle normal. Thus its ACTUAL
projection is(P_i,-Q_i)=(sigma_i p,-sigma_i q).

All earlier components can be made zero at both samples by the explicit
recursive choice x_j=min(A_j,ell_j+x_(j+1)/beta)-sigma_j for j=i-1,...,1,
using the smaller of the initial and proposed next boundary coordinate
at j=i-1; also enforce x_1<=A_1-beta D_2. Earlier coordinates then have
zero gradients and do not move. All later coordinates after i+2 are0,
except the isolated scalar x_(k+1)=ell_(k+1)+D_(k+1).
The next component has input below ell_(i+1) and output ell_(i+2),
so P_(i+1)=Q_(i+1)=0; all other retired components also vanish.

The actual step therefore has

    r_i^+=L_i/2,
    v_i^+=v_i-alpha sigma_i q
        =(alpha-1)sigma_i beta(p+q)/(p-beta)
                                  +(L_i/2)(q+beta)/(p-beta)>0,
    z_i^+=beta L_i/2+v_i^+.                                 (23)

As q approaches1, p-beta approaches0 while beta>0. For any proposed
constant cap-scale reset, (23) exceeds it. The new input is below L_i,
while the new actual edge residual is arbitrarily large. The next
component remains zero since its input is still below its translation;
all earlier zero-cone choices remain valid since x_i^+>A_i>=ell_i.
The isolated tail excess stays positive for this legal suffix step.

Thus terminal/exit input information alone does not supply a bounded
edge state. The tested normal parameter and huge initial downstream
deficit are not asserted reachable from e_1. The actual initialized
exit debt(21),(22) remains OPEN, not refuted. This is a new exit-reset
failure, distinct from the previously screened cross-time and
simultaneous-checkpoint-margin claims.


### C2. Pay the source inside the signed terminal-gradient identity

Fix the ACTUAL terminal local projection p_N=P_i(n), q_N=Q_i(n).
The full own-checkpoint identity from the maximizing formula is

    Phi_i(x_n)=-beta D_(i+1)p_N-D_(i+1)q_N
         -(p_N^2+q_N^2)/2
         -sum_(u=t_i)^(n-1)(h_u/2)
              [p_N(P_i-Q_(i-1))-q_N(P_(i+1)-Q_i)](u).       (28)

This is algebra for the ACTUAL terminal support, not a generic
cross-time sign claim. Its full Q_k before the final root is retained.
Split exactly at t_(i+1). By Q_i=0 and(24), the large initialized
-D_(i+1)q_N is paid by the completely known successor P integral.
The resulting equality is

    Phi_i(x_n)=-beta D_(i+1)p_N
              +[beta D_(i+2)-ell_(i+2)/beta]q_N
              +p_N J_i^in-(p_N^2+q_N^2)/2
         -sum_(u=t_(i+1))^(n-1)(h_u/2)
              [p_N(P_i-Q_(i-1))-q_N(P_(i+1)-Q_i)](u).       (29)

All old/future gradients and all later dissipation remain. The
remaining word starts H_(l_i+1),b_(l_i+2),H_(l_i+2),...,
b_(m-1),H_(m-1); for i=k-1 it is exactly the final H_(m-1).
The decomposition is staggered by each actual own checkpoint, not a
simultaneous array of checkpoint margins.

First direct attempt: use the explicit negative mixed margin(27) to
dominate the terminal support in(29). This requires control of the
actual J_i^in AND the later signed integral. A small bound on v_i at
t_(i+1) alone is insufficient: r_i contains the full J_i^in.
The terminal-gradient coefficients p_N,q_N depend on the true reached
state and cannot be freely optimized independently of those histories.

Second direct attempt: telescope the static successor terms across
middle components. If p_i=P_i(n), q_i=Q_i(n), the two neighboring
static D terms in the sum are beta D_(i+2)[q_i-p_(i+1)].
This is -beta D_(i+2) times the ACTUAL combined terminal derivative
at i+1. That derivative is not nonnegative: on a feasible edge-only
terminal support q_i>0 forces U_(i+1)=0 and may have p_(i+1)=0.
Thus the static sum is not a nonpositive boundary term. All staggered
J_i^in terms and all later signed pairings must remain to pay it.
No already-refuted universal cross-time positivity is proposed.

A precise coefficient screen illustrates this failure without making
an initialized counterexample. A feasible pure-edge terminal projection
for component i has p_N=beta q_N, q_N=sigma_i; other retired projections
can be zero. To specify all coordinates, take x_i=A_i,
x_(i+1)=ell_(i+1)-kappa sigma_i, x_(i+2)=ell_(i+2),

    sigma_i[beta D_(i+2)-beta^2 D_(i+1)-ell_(i+2)/beta]>0     (30)

eventually by the joint amplitude/translation limits. Its negative

## 2. Geometry, true radius, and every neighboring gradient

Completing the square in E_B identifies its unique maximizer as Pi_B(w),
the Euclidean projection. The maximizing inequalities at w and w' imply

    ||Pi_B(w)-Pi_B(w')||^2
                <=<Pi_B(w)-Pi_B(w'),w-w'>.

The maximizing formula and this inequality give differentiability with
gradient Pi_B and a 1-Lipschitz gradient. Thus E_B is convex, nonnegative
and1-smooth. Its zero set is the polar cone of B: if some support pairing
is positive, taking a sufficiently small positive multiple of that
support vector gives a positive envelope value.

The cone of K has extreme rays (C,0),(beta,-1). Consequently

    Phi_i=0 iff x_i<=A_i and
                      x_(i+1)>=beta*(x_i-ell_i).            (4)

The disk with center(beta,beta), radius1+beta supports the whole arc.

    Pi_K(u_j,-y_j)=(p(q_j),-q_j),

evidence:
# Coupled finite rows and depth retention: three complete analytical screens

JOINT ANALYTICAL DRAFT — UNVERIFIED. Worker max, invocation73 after assigned
completed baseline72; assigned attempted ceiling74. This is research evidence,
not a fact. There is no verifier submission, computational evaluation, actual
full-class upper bound, or resolution of the original exact-profile problem.

The three specified laws are: a pair of paid contact-neutral circulations;
a smooth depth ramp toward sustained inherited curvature; and immediate
mass-normalized retention after H4. Their complete arrays and entire-space
identities are below. The first law has two independent source restrictions
on the actual negative plane but pays one of them with the wrong sign. The
second starts positively on the entire plane, retains a uniformly positive
fraction of late inherited curvature, yet has already made the entire plane
negative by H9. The third starts positively on that plane at H5 but fails an
original initial-point mixed direction, including its Silver calibration.

## 1. Original target, fixed physical word, and authority

For every nonnegative physical word h of length n, W_n(h) is the supremum of
2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2), over every finite-dimensional real
Euclidean space, every convex differentiable L-smooth f with a minimizer
x_star, every L>0 and x_0!=x_star, with the actual updates
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R. The original all-split benchmark is

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=k<n)Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=k<n)G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

Every split is an original integer split. The affirmative goal requires a
uniform all-word, all-large-horizon lower comparison. The negative route
requires an actual unrestricted W upper with fixed relative improvement on
unbounded actual horizons. No failed dual is a primal lower witness.

Fix ONE enclosing integer m>=1536 and set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c,
    Hword_0=(), Hword_(j+1)=(Hword_j,1+a*c^j,Hword_j),
    A_j=1+sum Hword_j, d_j=a*c^j, D_j=2A_j-1.

The actual word is Hword_m=H_(m,1/4) of length n_m=2^m-1. Every child
inherits the SAME m and epsilon. Hword_j is used here to distinguish the
physical word from the conjugate quadratic H_j of fact1252b8823bb5a290.
The diagnostic epsilon=0 is the original Silver word; it is never substituted
for the assigned positive epsilon. All displayed recurrences are finite
mathematical definitions or symbolic identities, never executed programs.

Accepted inputs are fact1252b8823bb5a290 (original interpolation and formal
space), fact04219554e41d9750 Sections10--11 (primitive/history and full-space
composition conventions), and fact5fd396eba75651e7 Section10 (ONLY the
unconditional scalar benchmark comparison). Full findings9864512779c0d768,
23ca982e95eefa1f and70884c07cdfd260a and main elaboration0d9770af2df0344c were
read as awareness, not predecessors. All unverified formulas needed here are
derived together in this draft. None is promoted or reused as verified truth.

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Retain independent original formal
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n, including every actual bridge and the unqueried
terminal, and every ordered finite and optimum row. Put

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,
    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
    Ppos_i=sum_(t<i)h_t, S=sum h, D=1+2S, h_n=0.

Actual interpolation gives Q_ij<=0 by fact1252. Write K_ij for finite
multipliers, nu_i for i->star, xi_i for star->i, with K_ii=0. Every law
below has xi_i=0. All FINAL multipliers must be nonnegative. The exact value
flow and complete objective matrix are

    sum_j K_ij-sum_j K_ji+nu_i=2*1_(i=n),                    (1)
    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)K_ij Q_ij
                              +sum_i nu_i Q_(i,star)
        =q||x_0||^2-sum_i nu_i<x_0,g_i>+C(g),               (2)
    C_ii=out_i-1_(i=n)-h_i*sum_(j>i)K_ij,
    2C_ij=-(K_ij+K_ji)-h_j*sum_(v>j)K_iv
                         +h_i[nu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j,
    out_i=nu_i+sum_j K_ij.                                 (3)

Here C(g)=sum_(i,j)C_ij<g_i,g_j>. The full matrix is
[[q,-nu^T/2],[-nu/2,C]]. To derive (3), half the incident mass is
out_i-1_(i=n) by (1); forward position rows subtract h_i K_ij from the
source diagonal. Difference squares and the two prefix position terms give
the three displayed off-diagonal contributions. Thus (1)--(3) retain ALL
initial-point and gradient directions. Full PSD would imply W<=q, with no
quotient or child-feasibility assumption.

The original Huber assignment x_0=D,g_i=1,f_i=D-Ppos_i-1/2 makes M(1/D)=0.
Its contact equations, including the mixed derivatives, are

    (2S-Ppos_i)nu_i=2h_i+sum_j K_ij(Ppos_i-Ppos_j).          (4)

Indeed twice row i's sum in C is
2h_i+(1+Ppos_i)nu_i+sum_j K_ij(Ppos_i-Ppos_j). All arrays below obey (4).
Raising q adds only (q-1/D)||x_0||^2; it cannot fix a test with x_0=0.

## 2. Complete source array and its actual two-dimensional negative plane

Let z be a child terminal and define the full primitive history

    V_j=2sum_(i<z)h_i(f_i-f_z)
       +sum_(i<z)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-A_j(A_j-1)||g_z||^2.

Starting from Lambda^0=0, at the actual join from Hword_j to Hword_(j+1)
embed Lambda^j on the left with weight1 and on the right with weight k_j.
With bridge p and terminal z, add exactly

    u_j sum_(i right,i<z)h_i Q_(i,p)
     +v_j sum_(i right,i<z)h_i Q_(i,z)
     +w_j Q_(z,p)+z_j Q_(p,z),
    u_j=2lambda,
    v_j=[u_j d_j+2(A_j+d_j)]/A_j,
    k_j=1+(u_j+v_j)/2,
    z_j=2A_j,
    w_j=4A_j+2d_j-u_j(A_j-1)
                           =2lambda+2(d_j-A_j/lambda).    (5)

Aggregate repeated actual rows. The identities u_j+v_j=2(k_j-1) and
u_j(A_j-1)+w_j-z_j=2(A_j+d_j) give divergence -2h_i at nonterminals and

    V_j+sum_(i!=v)Lambda^j_iv Q_iv=Psrc_j(g).                (6)

For a complete audit, the four unweighted gradient polynomials of the new
rows in (5) are

    d_j<r,g_p>+||r||^2/2
       +sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2/2+(A_j-1)||g_p||^2/2;
    -||r||^2/2+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2/2
       +(A_j-1)||g_z||^2/2-<r,g_z>;
    d_j<g_z,g_p>+<g_z,r>+(||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2)/2;
    -(d_j+1/2)||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2/2-<g_p,r>-<g_p,g_z>.

The ||r||^2,r*g_p,r*g_z coefficients are (u_j-v_j)/2,

    A_j(A_j-1)-d_j-d_j^2+[u_j(A_j-1)+w_j]/2-(d_j+1/2)z_j,
    -A_(j+1)(A_(j+1)-1)+k_j A_j(A_j-1)
                                     +v_j(A_j-1)/2+(w_j+z_j)/2.

Substitution yields (7) on the whole original gradient space. Its bracket

Put v_h=a/(c-2). Direct summation of the mathematical word gives

## 6. Gadget C: two exact blocks and two arbitrary upper coefficients

Consider the ENTIRE following physical layout, not just one fixed probe:

 a_m>=0, b_m>=0 chosen before the function,

### 6.2 A strict finite all-split benchmark comparison, done textually

Define eta=29/21000. We now derive, jointly, the useful strict lower
benchmark comparison

 B_(N_C)/C > gamma+eta,  m>=2.                             (25)

This does not evaluate the benchmark recurrence. It displays legal
splits and exact elementary inequalities. In (3), C_1=lambda,
C_2=Omega(1,lambda)>4, and the split (1,2) gives
C_4>=Omega(lambda,C_2)>Omega(lambda,4)>23/3. For the last inequality,
the primitive root polynomial at 23/3 is

### 6.3 Uniform exclusion of EVERY word-dependent member of layout C

The following argument is not limited to fixed a,b, to bounded guesses,
or to sublinear assumed tails. Set

 r=gamma+eta/2,
 C_cut=(16/eta)^2,
 M_C=max(2,ceil(log C_cut/log lambda)).                      (28)

For EVERY m>=M_C and EVERY a_m,b_m>=0, the candidate joint conclusion is

 W_(N_C)(H_C)>1/(r C),
 W_(N_C)(H_C)/U_(N_C)^ZJ>1+eta/12=1+29/252000.              (29)

Proof using the COMPLETE necessary system (23): suppose instead that
W<=1/(r C). The first two terms in (23) imply

 r<=4+2a+(2b-1)/C,
 r a^2<=2+(2b-1)/C.                                       (30)

The last term implies (b-1)_+<=(2+a)sqrt(C/r), so also
b<=1+(2+a)sqrt(C/r), with no division by a and no omission when b<=1.
Consequently, putting

 e_C=1/C+2(2+a)/sqrt(r C),

we have (2b-1)/C<=e_C. Since C>=C_cut>=16 and r>gamma>5,

 r a^2<=2+e_C<41/16+a/4.

If a>=1 the right side is at most (45/16)a^2<5a^2<r a^2,
a contradiction. Thus a<1. It follows that

 0<e_C<1/C+6/sqrt(r C)<=4/sqrt C<=eta/4.                    (31)

From the second line of (30),

 a<=sqrt((2+e_C)/r)
   <=sqrt((2+e_C)/gamma)
   =a_g sqrt(1+e_C/2)<=a_g(1+e_C/4).

Here sqrt(1+t)<=1+t/2 for t>=0 follows by squaring, and
a_g^2 gamma=2 was checked in Section 6. Combining with the first
line of (30) gives

 r<=4+2a+e_C
   <=gamma+(1+a_g/2)e_C
   <gamma+3eta/8<gamma+eta/2=r,

again a contradiction. This proves the first assertion in (29).
Multiplying by the correct original B_(N_C), using (25), gives
W/U>(gamma+eta)/(gamma+eta/2)>1+eta/12 since r<6.
This proves the second assertion in (29). All constants and the one
cutoff are independent of the selected a_m,b_m. The argument retains
arbitrarily large coefficients rather than assuming them bounded:
their attempted small objective error forces a<1 and the tail bound.

The proof also identifies an actual violating function constructively:
at least one of the three terms in (23) exceeds 1/(r C). Choose its
global Huber or exact cut instance from Section 3 after the word is
selected. That function realizes the failure on the whole physical
run. This is not an interpolation-feasibility conjecture or a missing
theorem-level lemma.

## 7. Full scope, missing lift, and the next permitted interface

All three screened layouts are rejected as candidates for an ORIGINAL
negative resolution. Gadget A loses a constant objective amount on a
legal asymmetric Huber function. Gadget B has TWO explicit uniformly
failed full sign/flow array lifts, and, more decisively, its actual
Huber mass is already below an available original benchmark tree.
Gadget C, including arbitrary word-dependent nonnegative coefficients
in its displayed scope, has a quantified uniform ORIGINAL relative
loss proved using the accepted global and two cut witnesses.

No arbitrary-template inflation theorem follows. For other templates,
the exact unpaid term in an endpoint lift is still the full mixed
block-displacement debt in (12)--(14). A valid useful upper gadget
needs an explicit nonnegative physical-row payment and a full PSD
remainder for that debt, on every original gradient and free initial
coordinate uniformly as exact block sizes grow. The two formulas in
Section 5 do not give such a payment, and formal negative directions
in those formulas do not prove failure of every core certificate.

For a broader subsequent physical layout, this round specifically does
NOT exclude unequal lower blocks, a different ordering of primitive
and already exact basic objective blocks, more than two equal lower
blocks with other coefficients, first upper coefficients below 1,
or a coupled multi-source objective gadget retaining enough suffix
mass. Those are scope boundaries, not allocations or claims of promise.
No fourth layout is screened in this invocation.

The original target is OPEN. The frozen circle policy is OPEN and was
not used as a premise. There is no fact_submit call, new accepted fact,
successful improving schedule, original-Goal completion, finalization,
publication, revocation, shutdown, resource renewal, or automatic next
planning round. Further strategic work needs a new dispatch from main.

chosen zero in these three laws, while all outgoing ones remain unchanged

## 4. Two explicit GLOBAL laws and their entire polynomial

At the final depth m abbreviate mu=mubase^m. In the following formulas
the coefficients eta,chi are arbitrary nonnegative scalars. Define

    K_ij=Kbase_ij+eta*mu_i*mu_j, i!=j; K_ii=0,
    nu_i=(1+chi)mu_i,
    xiCert_i=chi*mu_i,                         0<=i,j<=n. (21)

The two concrete laws are

    Law A: eta=64epsilon, chi=0;
    Law B: eta=0, chi=128epsilon.                     (22)

For a calibration child r<5 use eta=chi=0; for r>=5 use(22) with
the SAME enclosing epsilon. At epsilon=0 both laws use eta=chi=0 at
every depth. The scope extension to arbitrary eta,chi in(21) is an
exclusion of the whole fixed two-parameter family, not another law
or a parameter search. No retuning is performed after the obstruction.

Every final coefficient is a finite formula supplied by(15),(18),(21).
There are no decrements, so no zero coefficient is subtracted from.
All finite pairs, including pairs INTO and OUT OF the actual terminal,
are retained. Law A adds equal mass to each pair i->j and j->i;
Law B adds equal mass to i->star and star->i. Thus every original
value equation(5) stays exact. These are global balanced circulations,
not source-dependent terminal paths or changes of physical GD steps.

Their total additions over the ONE word are

    finite addition = eta*(4-sum_i mu_i^2) <=4eta,
    outgoing optimum addition = 2chi,
    incoming optimum addition = 2chi.                (23)

In A the finite addition is at most256epsilon=64/m<=1/24.
In B each optimum addition is256epsilon=64/m<=1/24 and their
combined addition is at most1/12. There is no per-node allowance.

For the entire original vector family define

    Tmu=sum_i mu_i g_i,
    Xmu=sum_i mu_i x_i,
    Vmu=sum_i mu_i[||g_i||^2-<g_i,x_i>].              (24)

Value cancellation and Q_(i,star)+Q_(star,i)=||g_i||^2-<g_i,x_i>
give the exact polynomial

           +eta*[2Vmu-||Tmu||^2+<Tmu,Xmu>]+chi*Vmu. (25)

For the finite term, sum over unordered pairs mu_i mu_j(Q_ij+Q_ji).
The difference-square part is 2sum mu_i||g_i||^2-||Tmu||^2 because
sum mu=2. The position part is <Tmu,Xmu>-2sum mu_i<g_i,x_i>.
This proves(25) with every coordinate, including x_0 and g_n, present.
In the eta term the x_0 contributions cancel; the chi term contributes
-chi<Tmu,x_0>. The full initial mixed column is therefore
-(1+chi)mu/2 as required by(21), and its Schur expenditure is
(1+chi)^2 mu mu^T/(4q). The terminal diagonal and every incoming
terminal row are retained by(7),(21); a unit terminal-square coefficient
from an incoming-free theorem is NOT assumed for this new array.

Here is the exact terminal completion for the ACTUAL altered array.
The base terminal has total outgoing mass2 and no incoming rows, so
Cbase_nn=1. The final original terminal entries are

    K_(i,n)=eta*mu_i*mu_n for i<n,
    K_(n,i)=Kbase_(n,i)+eta*mu_n*mu_i for i<n,
    nu_n=(1+chi)mu_n, xiCert_n=chi*mu_n,
    gammaTerm=C_nn=1+eta*mu_n*(2-mu_n)+chi*mu_n>0.

With C from(7), put

              +sum_(i,j<n)C_ij<g_i,g_j>-||vterm||^2/gammaTerm.

Then the COMPLETE original polynomial, without a re-selection, is

Every coefficient in this identity is fixed by the finite formulas
above. Thus the actual terminal expenditure ||vterm||^2/gammaTerm

Set Pbar=sum_i mu_i P_i and Utail_i=sum_(j>i)mu_j. From(21),

Equations(11),(21),(26),(31) give the EXACT remaining transverse

No bound paying this transverse expenditure is claimed.

                  +(dfin^T v)^2/[D(zeta-1)].        (32)

At zeta=1 the singular common block instead requires dfin=0.
As mu has positive weights at different physical prefixes, A at

At zeta=21/20 the cost in(32) is finite but remains a real full-space
