## 6. General balanced-circulation contact obstruction

This calculation is not limited to the rank-product law. Let J_ij>=0
be ANY zero-diagonal finite-node array with equal row and column sums
at every node. On ANY finite nonnegative word define

    R_J(g)=sum_(i!=j)J_ij[<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2].

Its value terms cancel by balance and its x_0 terms cancel in position
differences. Let C_J be its full symmetric gradient matrix. At common
gradients, R_J(e)=0. Its row-sum vector satisfies

    (C_J e)_i=(1/2)sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j),
    P^T C_J e=(1/4)sum_(i,j)J_ij(P_i-P_j)^2.         (33)

For the first equality, the derivative of the source gradient gives
sum_j J_ij(P_i-P_j). The derivatives of the positions cancel because
row and column masses agree. The difference-square derivative vanishes
at e. Divide the derivative by2. For the second equality, expand the
sum of squared differences and use balance to equate the P_i^2 and
P_j^2 sums. This proves both equalities directly without invoking a
graph theorem.

It follows that C_J e=0 if and only if every positive J_ij joins
equal P_i and P_j. Necessity follows from the nonnegative sum in(33);
sufficiency follows from its first equality. With nonnegative h,
P_i=P_j means all intervening steps are zero, hence x_i=x_j as a
FORMAL identity even with independent gradients. In this case

    R_J(g)=(1/2)sum J_ij||g_i-g_j||^2 >=0.           (34)

Conversely, if some positive edge has unequal physical prefixes,
C_J e!=0 while e^T C_J e=0. Taking v=C_J e and expanding
R_J(e+t v)=2t||C_J e||^2+t^2 v^T C_J v shows a negative value
for sufficiently small negative t. Thus C_J is not PSD. In particular,
on a strictly positive word EVERY nonzero nonnegative balanced finite
circulation is an indefinite correction, despite exact value balance.

Moreover no collection of such additions can cancel its physical-
prefix contact work: the right side of(33) is additive and nonnegative.
At an exactly contacting base with zero incoming optimum rows and
q=1/D, the common kernel condition forces C_J e=0. Hence no nonzero
nonnegative finite circulation preserves full PSD at that exact level
on a positive word. This is NOT a statement at q>1/D, about signed
changes with paid decrements, about changed optimum profiles, or about
arbitrary full certificates. The explicit paid test in the next
section is needed to exclude our concrete laws at larger q.

## 7. Entire zero-displacement restriction of BOTH global corrections

Consider any original gradient assignment supported strictly within

    sum_(i in support)h_i g_i=0.                     (35)

All later formal positions are zero. On the supported indices(18)
gives mu_i=2h_i/D. Therefore Tmu=0 exactly. By(24),(25),

Here is a direct verification retaining all prefix positions. Since
x_i=-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t,

      =-(1/2)||sum_i h_i g_i||^2+(1/2)sum_i h_i^2||g_i||^2
      =(1/2)sum_i h_i^2||g_i||^2.

Multiplying Vmu by D consequently gives exactly the diagonal sum
in(36). Every unsupported term in Vmu has gradient zero, and Tmu=0

## 9. All nonnegative mixtures fail: no parameter retuning can repair them

On(43), the full diagonal sum in(36) is

Combining the complete identities(36),(44) with(45),(46) proves,
jointly within this unverified draft, that

    M_(eta,chi)(q;43)<-epsilon*A_j^2/(20D)<0          (47)

for EVERY m>=1536, EVERY62<=j<=m-3, EVERY eta,chi>=0,
and EVERY real q. This includes eta=chi=0 and arbitrary unbounded

worse. Thus no nonnegative tuning of the two specified global
generators can produce a full PSD certificate on this base. Laws A
and B are stopped at this declared-domain obstruction; no third law
or tuned variant is proposed.

This is broader than failure of the three previous conditional paths:
it permits every finite-node pair of the rank-product generator,
includes the independent incoming terminal rows, includes both
optimum directions with nonzero whole-word expenditure, and excludes
the complete nonnegative cone of the two global generators. It still
does NOT exclude other circulations, non-product weights, signed
reallocations with paid decrements, different optimum profiles,
different bases or arbitrary certificates.

In particular(43) is NOT a primal hard function. It has x_0=0 and
a later x_i=0 but different assigned gradients. A differentiable
static function cannot have those two gradients at the same point;
also an actual start at the normalized optimum0 cannot have nonzero

## 1. Result and precise scope

Fix the SAME enclosing integer m>=1536 and tau=1/4. Put

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), beta=1-1/(4m),

    S_l=sum H_l, X_l=1+S_l, n=2^m-1, h=H_m.

Every child uses this one pair (m,tau). Let j_L,j_O,j_R be the roots
of the left immediate child, the whole word, and the right immediate

Consider EVERY finite-dimensional static globally convex C1 function

## 3. Exact finite original-space lift of arbitrary three-sector data

This section applies to any original nonnegative finite word written

    h=(block_0,b,block_1,c_step,block_2),
    P=sum block_0, M=sum block_1, T=sum block_2.

The blocks are their actual complete chronological lists; no entry is
replaced or executed by a different algorithm. Define their actual
starting points from any real x_0,p,q,r by

    Z_p=x_0,
    Z_q=x_0-(P+b)p,
    Z_r=x_0-(P+b)p-(M+c_step)q.                          (3.1)

Choose real starting values F_p,F_q,F_r. The proposed data at a query
with already executed sector mass s are

    (Z_p-s p,p,F_p-s||p||^2), 0<=s<=P,
    (Z_q-s q,q,F_q-s||q||^2), 0<=s<=M,
    (Z_r-s r,r,F_r-s||r||^2), 0<=s<=T.                  (3.2)

Only actual partial sums need to be queried. The final points s=P,M
are the first and second checkpoint queries; s=T is the actual

ordered residuals Q_ij<=0 between these endpoints and the optimum.
This is an exact characterization of legal data of this form, not a
PSD-Gram-only relaxation.

Necessity of the displayed values for any real function follows by
using both convexity inequalities between two equal-gradient samples:
their value difference is exactly the inner product with that gradient.
In particular each physical step within a sector pays its own
h_i||g_i||^2 decrease, even when h_i is huge, unordered, or zero.

## 4. A mass-selected certificate without height restrictions

Write d=b-1 and e=c_step-1. For this section the following algebra

for a specified real charge t. For Family E, z=f(x_n), t=T, and

## 7. All legal prefix completions and the actual last leaf

Now require only the queried gradients (1.1), allowing an arbitrary
terminal gradient and any static function consistent with the complete
prefix. No completion is being proposed as a new lower construction;
we prove an upper bound for EVERY such completion using its actual
last jet. It is unnecessary to select a conjugate active face or to
solve for an unspecified terminal Gram.

The last physical step is d0=1+a. The suffix has at least one query,
and its last query is at Z_r-(T-d0)r with value

    f(x_(n-1))=F_r-(T-d0)||r||^2.

This equality follows from all original equal-gradient samples. The
actual next point is x_n=x_(n-1)-d0*r=Z_r-T*r. Smoothness along precisely

             =F_r-(T-d0^2/2)||r||^2.                    (7.1)

All earlier positions, queried values, and every minimum remain those
of the one actual function being bounded. The proof in Section6
applies with delta=(1+d0^2)/(2X), and now

    2D=1+2S_m-d0^2>0.

It proves the upper bound in (1.3). Because the argument began at ANY
chosen actual minimizer, moving to the actual closest one does not
evade it. Completing an old prefix can change the complete minimum
set, but applying these inequalities to that very completed function
and its new closest minimizer already pays that change. There is no
assumption that a radius from a different function is inherited.

All original remote/interior/optimum rows remain valid for each
function in this quantification. They are not deleted from a primal
optimization to assert existence. The proof uses a necessary subset
to obtain a bound on the larger family, then pays the original last
leaf by (7.1). This also covers arbitrary affine conjugate offsets
and all genuine3D nonparallel terminal choices compatible with the

## 8. Explicit sharp member and exact original-B comparison

Let S=S_m, kappa=1/(1+2S), and define the scalar function

    f_H(x)=x^2/2                         if |x|<=kappa,
           kappa*|x|-kappa^2/2           if |x|>=kappa.

Start at x_0=1. Its unique minimizer is0, its derivative is continuous,
nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz, and it is one fixed global function.
At actual cumulative mass s<=S,

    x=1-kappa*s >=1-kappa*S>kappa,
    grad f_H(x)=kappa,
    f_H(x)=kappa*(1-kappa*s)-kappa^2/2.

Thus every actual physical entry, including the actual last leaf, is
executed with the same gradient. This is a member of all three pair
families with p=q=r=kappa. Its queried proximal heights are

    delta(s)=f_H(x)-kappa^2/2=kappa-kappa^2*(s+1)>0,

since S>0 and s<=S<2S. Its OWN closest radius is exactly1 and

    2f_H(x_n)=2kappa-(2S+1)kappa^2=1/(1+2S).

gradients cannot attain equality in Family E by positive definiteness,
although we do not need to decide their restricted supremum.

The exact original benchmark is retained throughout:

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt((x+y)^2+4xy))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n)Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n)G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

No dyadic-only recurrence is substituted for these all-integer-split
maxima. Fact5fd396eba75651e7 gives exactly

    B_(2^m-1)/(1+2S_m)<237/250,

at our SAME tau=1/4 and m>=1536. That proves the first inequality in
(1.4). Put Z=1+2S_m. Equations(5.2),(5.4), with the Family E charge,
give Z>(23/2)X>=23552. Since d0^2<9/4, we have
d0^2/Z<1/1000. Hence, for Family Q,

    B_n V <= B_n/(Z-d0^2)
           < (237/250)*(1000/999)=316/333<19/20.

This is a finite, uniform, quantitatively separated statement at every
declared m, at the ACTUAL horizon n=2^m-1. It is a witness-family
obstruction. It is neither a certificate for unrestricted W_n(h) nor
a negative resolution of the original minimax problem.

## 9. What the original-space lift does and does not buy

The seven-endpoint lift shows that one can safely reason in finitely
many real vectors and paid scalar heights for this three-sector model.
It retains all intermediate samples and gives a genuine global smooth
convex interpolant, attained minimum, exact terminal and complete
minimum hull. A3x3 PSD gradient Gram alone cannot replace its endpoint
interpolation tests or the x_0 inner products.

The certificate then proves a bound over the WHOLE declared geometry,
not just over one explicit feasible parameter law. This is why no
new numerical or symbolic optimizer is needed. In particular, adding
a third coordinate, freeing the angle of r relative to q, introducing
independent affine offsets, or choosing x_0 nonradially cannot repair
the canonical top-two choice while the actual gradients remain in
the three sectors (1.1). The same applies to the other two pairs
printed in Section5 and to arbitrary completions of their entire
queried prefixes, even after paying their new closest minima.

Nothing here declares all real three-gradient geometry exhausted on
ALL possible checkpoint pairs. It is also not an obstruction to a
projection hull whose actual gradients move along an edge inside one
of the displayed blocks: such a trajectory violates (1.1).

## 10. Concrete failure of the certificate on another actual pair

To test a fragile all-pair extrapolation, choose the whole-word root
as the first checkpoint and the immediately following physical leaf
as the second. These are actual positions j=2^(m-1)-1 and k=j+1.
This pair is outside Pairs_top for m>=3. Write U=X_(m-1) and
Droot=a*c^(m-1). Its full masses are

    u=U, v=1, d=Droot, e=a,
    T=U-2-a, w=U-3/2-a,
    D=2U+Droot-1/2.                                    (10.1)

Here the middle block is empty, and the suffix is the full right child
after its ACTUAL first leaf. Formula(10.1) keeps all of that suffix.
As m tends to infinity in the SAME-enclosing-m tau1/4 family,

    Droot/U -> lambda-2=:t0, U->infinity,
    (u,v,d,e,w,D)/U -> (1,0,t0,0,1,lambda).

This follows from the exact mass formula in Section5: c->lambda,
a->lambda-2, v_h->1 and (2/c)^(m-1)->0, since c>lambda>2.
All denominators in (4.4) have positive limits. The weights tend to

    alpha -> (lambda-1)/(2lambda-1),
    eta -> (lambda-1)/(lambda+1)=lambda-2=t0.

Substitute these limits in (4.5), using lambda^2=2lambda+1.
The normalized limiting matrix entries are

    J11/U -> (lambda-1)*t0/(2lambda-1)^2,
    J22/U -> t0^2,
    J12/U -> t0/(2lambda-1).

Its determinant is exactly

    lim det(J)/U^2 = -t0^3/(2lambda-1)^2 <0.              (10.2)

For example, the last simplification uses
(lambda-1)t0=3-lambda. Thus the matrix is indefinite for all sufficiently
large m in this very physical hierarchy. This is a rigorous failure
of THIS PARTICULAR five-row certificate, not a construction of legal
data violating Huber and not a claim about the optimum at that pair.
Additional remote rows may repair the proof. A claimed all-pair
extension of Section6 without such work would be false.

This test was textual and symbolic; no determinant evaluation or
trajectory replay was executed. It pinpoints the remaining degree
of freedom: a materially different checkpoint selection, potentially
with essential remote-row information, remains open even within the
three-gradient program. More gradient sectors or a nonconstant
gradient inside a block are also outside the present obstruction.

## 11. Retrieval, resources and remaining theorem-level gap

Applied skills: query-memory for prior state and exact scope;
obtain-immediate-conclusions for block-value equalities and mass
normalization; direct-proving for the explicit weighted certificate;
search-math-results for interpolation/conjugacy background; and
construct-counterexamples for the failed all-pair extension in Section10.

Matlas was queried for smooth convex interpolation and constructive
strongly convex conjugate envelopes. Its returned two lemmas did not

definitions/proof context. This reference is background only; every

No new external theorem is imported as a correctness premise.

All new conclusions above are asserted jointly and remain UNVERIFIED.
No intermediate draft was promoted or treated as a fact. The original
all-word/all-horizon comparison against the exact B_n remains a
theorem-level gap. The current result supplies no legal new witness

The authorized deliverable is the complete exact obstruction (1.2)
and uniform full-prefix bound (1.3) on the precisely declared broader

    -||r_R||^2/2+sum h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2/2
                        +(A_j-1)||g_z||^2/2-<r_R,g_z>;
    d_j<g_z,g_p>+<g_z,r_R>+(||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2)/2;
    -(d_j+1/2)||g_p||^2+||g_z||^2/2-<g_p,r_R>-<g_p,g_z>.

For example the sum of forward within-right displacement terms is
-||r_R||^2/2+sum h_i^2||g_i||^2/2; this fixes its diagonal correction.
Multiply the displays by u_j,v_j,w_j,z_j and add V and the child terms.
Using lambda^2=2lambda+1 gives the complete identity

    Psrc_(j+1)=Psrc_j^left+k_j Psrc_j^right
      +(tstar-t_j)[(lambda+1)||Y||^2-2lambda A_j<Y,Z>
                         +A_j^2(2+tstar+t_j)||Z||^2].    (6)

This is an identity on all original gradients. In particular it makes no
positive-epsilon primitive PSD assertion.

Let Cbase^j be the entire gradient matrix of the objective polynomial after
(5). Put T_R=sum_i mu^j_i g_(R_i), x_p=x_0-sum_(l<n_j)h_l g_l and

    Rchild=Cbase^j(g_R)-Dc||T_R||^2/4,
    kappa_j=Dc-Dp theta_j^2.

Expansion of all (4) rows gives

    Mbase_(j+1)(1/Dp)=Psrc_j(g_left)/Dp+Rchild
     +||x_p+(S_j-Dp s_j)g_p-(Dp theta_j/2)T_R||^2/Dp
     +(kappa_j/4)||T_R-2g_p||^2.                       (7)

For a coefficient check, after subtracting the first two terms the remaining
polynomial is exactly

    ||x_p||^2/Dp+2(S_j/Dp-s_j)<x_p,g_p>
    +(S_j^2/Dp+2s_j)||g_p||^2-theta_j<x_p,T_R>
    +(1+d_j-s_j)<g_p,T_R>+Dc||T_R||^2/4.

Expanding the two squares agrees because
s_j(3S_j+2(1+d_j))=S_j+1+d_j. Neither Rchild nor kappa_j is assumed
nonnegative for the deformed hierarchy.

At the full Huber contact tuple x_0=D_j, g_i=1, every square argument
and each Y,Z in (6) is zero. Induction from Mbase_0=||x_0-g_0||^2
also makes the derivative of Rchild zero at its common-gradient vector.
Thus, writing e=(1,...,1),

    Cbase e=D mu/2, e^T Cbase e=D.                     (8)

For the actual m>=1536 (indeed m>=2), one useful original entry is
Cbase_00=2/D, with mu_0=2b/D: only the
first primitive depth1 term (2-b^2)||g_0-g_1||^2 contributes to the first
gradient diagonal in the left source, and the x_p square contributes b^2/D.
These statements are jointly derived here, not imported from the last report.

## 5. The two explicit additions and every final sign

The physical non-leaf checkpoints are the odd indices p<n. If level(p)=l,
then 1<=l<=m-1 and p=o+2^l-1 for a unique cell offset
o=k*2^(l+1), 0<=k<2^(m-l-1). Define the complete cell of original
gradient indices as o,...,o+2^(l+1)-1, and its short-leaf set

    E_(l,o)={o,o+2,...,o+2^(l+1)-2}.

These are actual even queried indices; every one has h_i=b. No terminal
gradient is a member of a leaf set or checkpoint set.

LAW A, preceding leaf. For each non-leaf p of level l put

    omega_p=epsilon*A_l^2/D,
    J^A_(p-1,p)=J^A_(p,p-1)=omega_p.                  (9)

LAW B, whole-cell fan. For each (l,o) and p=o+2^l-1 put

    gamma_(l,o)=epsilon*A_l^2/(D*2^l),
    J^B_(i,p) += gamma_(l,o), J^B_(p,i) += gamma_(l,o)
                         for every i in E_(l,o).      (10)

All other entries of J are zero and all stated contributions are summed.
The two laws are different supports, not two fits of the old optimum-row
transport. The factor 2^l makes their total added mass identical at every
scale, allowing a direct comparison without silently increasing a budget.
For either law the FINAL original coefficients are

    K_ij=Kbase_ij+J_ij (i!=j), K_ii=0,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i, lambda_(star,i)=0,
    q=21/(20D).                                      (11)

All final multipliers are nonnegative. Symmetry J_ij=J_ji preserves every
value-flow equation (5). The optimum profile is fixed as a deliberate
restriction of these two laws; no claim is made that a general slack-spending
construction may be reduced to this restriction. No decrement is hidden.

Each law has the ONE entire-word multiplier-mass account

    T79=(epsilon/D)sum_(l=1)^(m-1)2^(m-l-1)A_l^2,
    sum_(i!=j)J_ij=2T79.                             (12)

This is not a sufficient PSD budget. The actual global objective/contact
budget, including all cross terms between cells, is given next.

## 6. Every full entry, the changed contact, and its ONE Schur budget

For ANY array of the form (11) define out_i=mu_i+sum_v K_iv. The entire
matrix C in

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-sum_i mu_i<x_0,g_i>
                       +sum_(i,j)C_ij<g_i,g_j>

has entries

    C_ii=out_i-1_(i=n)-h_i sum_(v>i)K_iv,
    2C_ij=-(K_ij+K_ji)-h_j sum_(v>j)K_iv
                         +h_i[mu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j. (13)

The complete original matrix therefore has initial entry q and initial
mixed entries -mu_i/2. To derive (13), flow says half the incident row mass
equals out_i-1_(i=n). A forward row sourced at i contributes -h_i K_iv
to its diagonal. For i<j the difference squares give -(K_ij+K_ji),
rows out of i ending after j give the second term, and rows out of j ending
at/before i or at the optimum give the last term. This also accounts for
every physical intermediate gradient in a nonlocal pair.

For an unordered pair represented by u<v let L_uv(g)=sum_(t=u)^(v-1)h_t g_t
and ell_uv=Ppos_v-Ppos_u. The exact added polynomial per unit weight is

    Q_uv+Q_vu=||g_u-g_v||^2-<g_u-g_v,L_uv(g)>
             =<g_u-g_v,y_v-y_u>.                     (14)

For v=u+1 across b this is
(1-b)||g_u||^2+(b-2)<g_u,g_v>+||g_v||^2. Its determinant is -b^2/4,
so it is indefinite whenever b>0. It is not a free PSD correction.

At g=e the value of (14) is zero, but its gradient is
ell_uv(e_v-e_u). Consequently define the entire contact-defect column

    d79=(1/2)sum_(unordered {u,v},u<v)J_uv*ell_uv*(e_v-e_u).

Here e_i denotes the standard coordinate column, distinct from e. Then

    Ce=D mu/2+d79, e^T d79=0, e^T C e=D.              (15)

For A the formula is d79=(b/2)sum_p omega_p(e_p-e_(p-1)). For B it is
(1/2)sum_(l,o)gamma_(l,o)sum_(i in E_(l,o))(Ppos_p-Ppos_i)(e_p-e_i),
with signed Ppos_p-Ppos_i valid on both sides of the checkpoint. Each is one
finite original-index vector, not separate contact credits. Both are nonzero:

    Ppos^T d79=(1/2)sum_(u<v)J_uv(Ppos_v-Ppos_u)^2>0.           (16)

All physical steps are positive and each law has a positive added edge.
Thus Ce=D mu/2 is NOT assumed; it is false for both candidates.

At x_0=D,g=e the complete value is (qD-1)D=D/20. Its initial/common
two-by-two block is

    Bcommon=[[q,-1],[-1,D]], det Bcommon=qD-1=1/20.

This is the ONE scalar allowance for the whole word. Write arbitrary
gradients as g=t e+v with e^T v=0, first in one real coordinate and then
coordinatewise in a Euclidean space. Set u=mu^T v and z=d79^T v. Their
mixed column with (x_0,t) is (-u/2,Du/2+z). Exact inversion gives

    (-u/2,Du/2+z) Bcommon^(-1) (-u/2,Du/2+z)^T
       =D u^2/4+u z+[q/(qD-1)]z^2
       =D u^2/4+u z+21z^2/D.                        (17)

For clarity the numerator before dividing by qD-1 is
D(qD-1)u^2/4+(qD-1)uz+qz^2. Thus all contact, common-gradient and
initial costs have been charged exactly once. In particular the last term
is the square of the WHOLE sum d79^T v and includes all cross-cell terms.
It cannot be paid anew from 1/20 at every node.

Equivalently, the entire remaining gradient matrix is

    R79=C-D mu mu^T/4-(mu d79^T+d79 mu^T)/2
                                      -(21/D)d79 d79^T,
    R79 e=0.                                        (18)

Full PSD at q=21/(20D) is equivalent to R79 being PSD on the entire
e-perpendicular space, or equivalently on all gradient coordinates since
R79 e=0. Equations (17)--(18) are a necessary-and-sufficient expenditure
identity, NOT a claim that either law pays it successfully. The direct
negative full-polynomial test below disproves that claim.

## 7. Actual terminal-square expenditure

Neither added support touches n. The final incoming-terminal coefficients
remain zero by the explicit formulas, not by deleting rows from a supplied
certificate. Full terminal flow is therefore sum_j lambda_(n,j)=2 and
C_nn=1. More explicitly the receivers are star and the right-spine bridges

    p_l=2^m-2^l-1, 0<=l<m,
    alpha_star=product_(v=0)^(m-1)theta_v,
    alpha_(p_l)=s_l product_(v=0)^(l-1)theta_v.        (19)

An empty product is1. All other alpha_i are zero. The finite telescoping
identity sum_l s_l product_(v<l)theta_v=1-product_(v<m)theta_v shows these
are probabilities. They are exactly lambda_(n,j)/2 from (4), including
the adjacent final bridge p_0=n-1. No unqueried gradient is discarded.

The exact vector in the terminal square is

    Vterm=alpha_star x_0
         -sum_(t<n)[h_t w_t-(w_t-w_(t-1))]g_t,
    w_(-1)=alpha_star, w_t=alpha_star+sum_(i=0)^t alpha_i.

The complete remainder is

    M(q)=||g_n-Vterm||^2+Rprefix,
    Rprefix=q||x_0||^2-2sum_(j in {star,0,...,n-1})alpha_j
                    (f_j-||g_j||^2/2)-||Vterm||^2
                  +sum_(i!=j in {star,0,...,n-1})lambda_ij Q_ij. (20)

The prefix flow cancels every f_j. Formula (20) follows by expanding the
terminal rows, as in
fact1252b8823bb5a290(c), and retains the actual negative square cost.
Equivalently put vterm=(mu_n/2)x_0-sum_(i<n)C_in g_i; then Vterm=vterm
and Rprefix=q||x_0||^2-sum_(i<n)mu_i<x_0,g_i>
+sum_(i,j<n)C_ij<g_i,g_j>-||vterm||^2.
Since the added rows contain no terminal gradients, they do not alter
C_in or vterm. They add their FULL (14) expressions to Rprefix.

## 8. Original-space block direction and its complete base action

Put

    W79=A_2+d_2, Bfirst=b+1+d_1,
    Edef=(t_2-tstar)A_2^2(lambda+t_2)>0,
    delta3=t_3-tstar>0.

W79 is the physical mass of steps0,...,3 and of steps8,...,11.
The notation is local and does not replace W_n(h). In the ENTIRE original
formal space assign scalar values

    x_0=0,
    g_i=1 for i=0,1,2,3;
    g_i=-1 for i=8,9,10,11;
    g_i=0 for every other i=0,...,n.                 (21)

The two active four-step blocks have identical physical words. Hence the
total displacement is W79-W79=0. All positions from index12 onward are0;
g_7=g_15=g_n=0. These are chosen test values, not equality constraints
on formal coordinates and not a legal primal trajectory.

In the first H3, its left H2 gradients are all1, its right H2 all0,
so both child Psrc terms vanish by (6), and Y=0,Z=1 gives -Edef.
The H3 beginning at8 gives the same -Edef. At their H4 join,
Y=-W79,Z=0. Thus the COMPLETE source polynomial is

    Psrc_4=-(1+k_3)Edef-delta3(lambda+1)W79^2<0.     (22)

For every containing source ancestor all its right gradients, bridge and
terminal are zero, so Y=Z=0 and (6) propagates exactly (22), with left
factor1. At the top objective join the left displacement, x_p, g_p and
T_R are allzero; Rchild on its zero right gradients is zero. Equation (7)
therefore gives for every m>=5, in particular all m>=1536,

    Mbase(q;21)=Psrc_4/D<0 for EVERY real q.           (23)

No positive-epsilon primitive child or quotient feasibility has been used.
The parameter signs came from the exact SAME-m (2).

## 9. Law A: every preceding-leaf symmetric pair vanishes

Every edge in (9) connects an even index to the next odd index. Assignment
(21) is constant on every such pair, including pairs outside its support.
Thus g_(p-1)-g_p=0 and its ENTIRE (14) polynomial is zero. All preceding
gradient costs and cross terms cancel exactly; no diagonal-only inference
is involved. Summing every added pair gives

    M_A(q;21)=Mbase(q;21)=Psrc_4/D<0.                 (24)

This proves a stronger, precise scope: for the fixed inherited base, ANY
nonnegative weights omega_p on this support fail for every q. Allowing
different scale laws, horizon dependence, arbitrary magnitudes or zero
weights cannot change (24). The new support is not a repair of the earlier
H4 defect. This is a formal PSD obstruction, not an interpolable witness.

## 10. Law B: every full-cell fan has nonpositive action

For a cell define its UNWEIGHTED full polynomial

    F_(l,o)=sum_(i in E_(l,o))<g_i-g_p,y_p-y_i>, p=o+2^l-1.

Then M_B-Mbase=sum_(l,o)gamma_(l,o)F_(l,o), with no omitted rows.
We evaluate every nonzero cell on (21), including cells whose checkpoint
is zero but whose source leaves are nonzero.

At l=1 each cell comprises four consecutive gradient indices; (21) is
constant on that cell. Its fan is zero. At l=2 only the cells o=0 and
o=8 can contribute. For o=0, p=3 has gradient1. The left leaves0,2 have
the same gradient and contribute zero. The right leaves4,6 have gradient0,
position -W79 and y=-W79, whereas y_3=-A_2. Each contributes
(-1)(W79-A_2)=-d_2. At o=8 the entire geometry through15 is the negative
of the first cell, apart from a common positional translation. A common
translation cancels in y_p-y_i, and negating both factors preserves their
product. Its two nonzero terms likewise equal -d_2. Therefore

    F_(2,0)=F_(2,8)=-2d_2<0.                        (25)

At l=3 only the first cell is active, with p=7, g_p=0 and y_p=-W79.
Its nonzero source leaves are0,2,8,10. Their original proximal positions
are respectively -1,-Bfirst-1,-W79+1,-W79+Bfirst+1.
The four complete terms, in this order, are

    1-W79, 1-W79+Bfirst, 1, 1+Bfirst.

Their sum is 4-2W79+2Bfirst. Since
W79=2b+2+d_1+d_2 and Bfirst=b+1+d_1, this is

    F_(3,0)=-2(b+d_2-1)<0.                          (26)

The positive terms1 and1+Bfirst have been explicitly paid by the negative
terms; they are not omitted. At EVERY l>=4 only the first cell can have
nonzero endpoint gradients, and its checkpoint has y_p=g_p=0. The same
four source leaves now contribute

    1, 1+Bfirst, 1-W79, 1-W79+Bfirst,

whose sum is again -2(b+d_2-1). Every other source and checkpoint has
zero gradient, so its factor g_i-g_p is zero, even if a position is nonzero.
All cells not listed are either disjoint from the support or were covered
by the constant-cell calculation. Hence the ENTIRE added value is

    M_B(q;21)-Mbase(q;21)
      =-2d_2[gamma_(2,0)+gamma_(2,8)]
       -2(b+d_2-1)sum_(l=3)^(m-1)gamma_(l,0)<0.      (27)

This proves M_B(q;21)<0 at every real q. More generally (27) is nonpositive
for arbitrary nonnegative weights gamma_(l,o), provided each individual
cell uses the SAME weight for all of its even source leaves. Thus every
nonnegative combination of these uniform full-cell fans, and also every
addition of the adjacent pairs from Section9, fails on the fixed base.
This is a consequence of the same two support calculations, not a third
law or extra search. Arbitrary unequal within-cell weights are NOT covered.

## 11. Boundary calibrations and scope audit

For n=0, the empty base uses mu_0=2 and M(q)=||x_0-g_0||^2+(q-1)||x_0||^2.
There are no additions in (9)--(10). For an arbitrary all-zero word, the
separate accepted calibration is lambda_(n,star)=2 with all other rowszero,
giving M(1)=||x_0-g_n||^2 on every original independent vector, including
duplicate-position gradients. It is not obtained by substituting a fictitious
positive hierarchy into the zero word. The general zero-step embedding is
exactly that of fact1252b8823bb5a290; neither new law asserts an arbitrary-word
extension or removes any formal coordinate at a zero step.

For a one-step hierarchy there is no non-leaf checkpoint. Direct expansion
of (3)--(7) gives

    Psrc_1=(2-b^2)||g_0-g_1||^2,
    Mbase_1(1/D_1)=||x_0-D_1(g_0+g_1)/2||^2/D_1
                              +(3-2b)||g_0-g_1||^2/4.

This is full PSD because b<sqrt(2)<3/2. It does not prove later PSD.

For the epsilon=0 Silver calibration, retain the same definitions with
epsilon=0, so A_j=lambda^j,d_j=A_j/lambda and t_j=tstar. Both additions
vanish identically; (6) gives Psrc_j=0 at all depths. Write A=S_j and
Bjoin=1+tstar(A+1). Direct expansion of kappa_j in (7) gives

    (3A+2Bjoin)^2 kappa_j
      =2(1-tstar)A^3+(6-8tstar)A^2
        +(1+tstar)(8tstar-2)A+(1+tstar)^2(1-2tstar)>0.

All coefficients are positive since 1/4<tstar<1/2. Starting at the empty
square, the Schur remainder Rchild of a PSD child with positive initial
coefficient is PSD, and (7) proves full Silver PSD inductively. This invokes
child PSD ONLY at epsilon=0, where it has just been established. The original
q=21/(20D) merely adds ||x_0||^2/(20D). It does not change the failures for
positive epsilon. No Silver calibration is imported to a deformed child.

The vector (21) is NOT an interpolable primal witness: x_0=0 would be an

## 12. Remaining interface, retrieval, and handoff

The at-most-two-law allocation is exhausted. An eventual repair of this
inherited base must have strictly positive total action on (21), exceeding
-Psrc_4/D, after all signed changes and costs. Adjacent pairs cannot supply
any; the uniform fans make its value worse. To escape this calculation one
must change a substantive ingredient, such as the base or within-cell source
distribution, or use paid signed finite/optimum reallocation. This is a
necessary directional screen, not a sufficient construction, a claim that
any such repair exists, or authorization for another law.

# Two new original-row bases and a reset-threshold obstruction

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical report, worker max80. Original target OPEN.
This is the single invocation allocated by TASK.md, after baseline79, with
at most two storage mechanisms. No fact_submit, mathematical program,
numerical or arithmetic replay, solver, executed recurrence, subagent,
installation, or consult was used. Every new calculation below belongs to
this ONE proof attempt. None is an accepted intermediate result.

The proposed replacement bases pass the inherited H4 and deep
zero-displacement tests. Their explicit full-space certificates have poor
objective levels. A stronger obstruction then excludes the desired level
for EVERY coefficient choice in a substantially larger boundary-row family,
including arbitrary dependence on the enclosing horizon and ancestors.
The obstruction is a rank-one transcript feasible for that restricted row
family, with every actual step and the actual terminal retained. It violates
an explicitly identified omitted PREFIX interpolation row. It is NOT an
interpolable primal witness, a lower bound on W, or unrestricted dual
infeasibility. The missing remote-row construction remains theorem-level.

## 1. Original problem, accepted inputs, and scope

For every integer n>=0 and every predetermined h in [0,infinity)^n,
W_n(h) is the supremum of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over
all finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, convex differentiable L-smooth
functions with an attained minimizer x_star, and x_0!=x_star. The actual
updates are x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R.

The ORIGINAL benchmark retains ALL integer splits:

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt((u+v)^2+4uv))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
    C_n=max_(integer 0<=k<n)Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),
    B_n=max_(integer 0<=k<n)G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)),
    U_n^ZJ=1/B_n.

The original question is whether lim_n B_n inf_h W_n(h)=1. An affirmative
answer must have the original uniform quantifier over every nonnegative
word and every sufficiently large actual horizon. A negative answer needs
a rigorous full-function upper bound beating the benchmark on unbounded
actual horizons. No restricted-function or restricted-row computation is
such an answer.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the normalization, the original
interpolation convention, and the full independent-vector certificate test.
In particular its deletion of incoming ACTUAL-terminal rows does not delete
any queried-prefix row. Accepted fact931b9653ce0f7201, read in full, supplies
the all-n envelope B_n<=(12/5)(n+1)^rho and the SAME-m comparison
B_(2^m-1)/D_m<47/50 for all m>=1536. Its final upper-bound statement is
conditional: W_(2^m-1)(H_m)<=17/(16D_m) would imply a 799/800 separation.
That W bound is not accepted and is not proved here. Facts042 and5fd are
not additional proof premises in this report.

Fix the SAME enclosing integer m>=1536 and set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon=1/(4m), beta=1-epsilon,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon), a=beta/c, d_j=a*c^j,
    Hword_0=(), Hword_(j+1)=(Hword_j,1+d_j,Hword_j),
    n=2^m-1, h=Hword_m, S=sum_(i<n)h_i, D=1+2S,
    b=1+a, Mleaf=1+b, Nleaf=2^(m-1).

These local hierarchy symbols do not overwrite the project glossary.
The literal indices are h_i=1+a*c^level(i), where level(i) is the exponent
of 2 dividing i+1. Thus h_(2k)=b for 0<=k<Nleaf, and the queried odd
indices 2k+1 have h_(2k+1)=1+d_(1+v2(k+1)), 0<=k<Nleaf-1. There are
exactly n physical steps, and index n is the unqueried terminal. Every
child uses these same parameters, without resetting epsilon.

The identities lambda^2=2lambda+1 and 1/lambda=lambda-2 give

    b=sqrt(2)-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)],
    1<b<sqrt(2)<3/2,
    d_1=1-epsilon,
    d_2=lambda(1-epsilon^2)>2,
    2<c<5/2.

For d_2>2 use lambda>12/5 and epsilon<1/8, which give
d_2>(12/5)(63/64)>2. For c<5/2 use lambda<17/7 and
epsilon<=1/6144. Thus steps of levels0,1 lie strictly below2;
every higher-level step lies strictly above3. No step equals2.

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Retain all ORIGINAL independent
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n, with x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t. Write

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Actual smooth-convex samples satisfy Q_ij<=0. A nonnegative row array
lambda_ij with finite flow out_i-in_i=2*1_(i=n) has a full certificate

    M_cert(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.

Its value coefficients cancel. PSD must hold on ALL original vectors.

## 2. Mechanism I: chronological storage with a last-leaf objective interface

This is a completely new original-index array; it does not use inherited
Lambda or Kbase. It starts from original optimum-sector rows and finishes
with a two-gradient objective interface on the last physical leaf.

For each physical i define the scalars and vector expression

    kap80_i=max(1,h_i-1),
    r80_i=2h_i                 if h_i<2,
        2h_i(h_i-1)          if h_i>2,
    s80_i=h_i*abs(h_i-2),
    z80_i=g_i                 if h_i<2,
        x_i-g_i             if h_i>2.

These definitions refer to the actual h_i; no gradient is identified with
another gradient. Let jlast=n-1, Dleaf=1+2b, qleaf=1/Dleaf, and

    Ppre=product_(0<=i<jlast)kap80_i^2,
    w80_i^I=qleaf*product_(i<t<jlast)kap80_t^2  (i<jlast),
    q_I=qleaf*Ppre.

Every nonzero original multiplier of Law I is

    lambda_(i,star)=lambda_(star,i)=w80_i^I*r80_i, i<jlast;
    lambda_(jlast,star)=1;
    lambda_(n,star)=1;
    lambda_(n,jlast)=1.                                  (I.1)

All other rows have coefficient zero. The support has no incoming actual
terminal edge. All signs are positive. Prefix sector pairs are cycles;
the three last rows cancel f_(jlast) and give terminal flow2, so every
finite flow is correct. The full initial point, both endpoint gradients,
and the endpoint value are present in this law.

The original-row identities are

    kap80_i^2||x_i||^2-||x_(i+1)||^2
           +r80_i(Q_(i,star)+Q_(star,i))=s80_i||z80_i||^2,    (I.2)

and, writing X=x_(jlast), u=g_(jlast), v=g_n,

    qleaf||X||^2-2f_n+Q_(jlast,star)+Q_(n,star)+Q_(n,jlast)
      =qleaf||X-Dleaf(u+v)/2||^2
                      +(3-2b)||u-v||^2/4.              (I.3)

For (I.2), Q_(i,star)+Q_(star,i)=||g_i||^2-<x_i,g_i>.
When h_i<2, direct expansion leaves h_i(2-h_i)||g_i||^2.
When h_i>2, it leaves h_i(h_i-2)||x_i-g_i||^2.
For (I.3), expanding the three rows gives

    qleaf||X||^2-<X,u+v>+||u||^2+(2b-1)<u,v>+||v||^2.

Expansion of the displayed two squares has exactly these coefficients.
Since b<3/2 both square coefficients are positive. Multiplying (I.2)
by w80_i^I and adding (I.3) proves the ENTIRE identity

    M_I(q_I)=sum_(i<jlast)w80_i^I*s80_i||z80_i||^2
       +qleaf||x_(jlast)-Dleaf(g_(jlast)+g_n)/2||^2
       +(3-2b)||g_(jlast)-g_n||^2/4.                    (I.4)

There is no omitted displacement or residual. This gives a full-function
upper-certificate draft at q_I, not at the requested q=17/(16D).

At any real original cut r<s<=jlast, the same identity reads

    [product_(r<=i<s)kap80_i^2]||x_r||^2-||x_s||^2
      +sum_(r<=i<s)[product_(i<t<s)kap80_t^2]r80_i
                              (Q_(i,star)+Q_(star,i))
      =sum_(r<=i<s)[product_(i<t<s)kap80_t^2]s80_i||z80_i||^2. (I.5)

Two consecutive blocks compose by multiplying the first identity by the
second block's product and adding, with its ACTUAL common x_s. At a
dyadic parent, the actual one-step bridge is an additional such factor.
The child displacement is always sum h_i g_i and x_s=x_r-sum h_i g_i.
These are context-dependent suffix weights, not fictitious resets.
They solve all-depth positivity for this law analytically, but the
product growth costs too much. Section7 excludes *any* useful coefficient
choice on a much richer support, without assuming scalar-only storage.

## 3. Mechanism II: dense checkpoint circulation and full terminal storage

The second family permits real mixed boundary information and all enclosing
context. Its coefficient support is much larger than Law I. Let

    Leaf={0,2,...,n-1}, Check={1,3,...,n-2}.

There are Nleaf leaves and Nleaf-1 queried checkpoints. Allow these rows:

  (a) both optimum rows for EVERY original finite index, including n;
  (b) EVERY ordered pair of distinct checkpoints;
  (c) EVERY leaf-to-checkpoint row Q_(ell,p), ell in Leaf, p in Check;
  (d) checkpoint-to-leaf rows Q_(p,ell) when |p-ell|=1;
  (e) EVERY outgoing actual-terminal row Q_(n,i), i<n.

Call this support E80. It contains both directions of every adjacent
queried-prefix pair, complete checkpoint coupling, all outgoing leaf
links to all checkpoints regardless of ancestors, and the whole terminal
fan. It permits optimum-to-terminal. It excludes incoming queried-to-
terminal rows and remote checkpoint-to-leaf / leaf-to-leaf rows.

For the support-level obstruction later, EVERY nonnegative coefficient
on E80 is free, with arbitrary dependence on m and full ancestor context.
Storage may be any quadratic form in x_0, actual boundary positions and
boundary gradients, with value terms and all real mixed inner products.
It may use arbitrarily many such boundary coordinates. The only restriction
is that its telescoped original-row certificate uses E80. No reduction
to a scalar metric is presumed.

Here is an explicit FULL feasible coefficient law inside that family, as
a starting point. It proves existence of a genuine changed base and makes
every added cost auditable. Put

    Pfull=product_(i<n)kap80_i^2,
    w80_i=product_(i<t<n)kap80_t^2,
    Kprod=product_(i<n)(1+h_i),
    alpha80=epsilon/[(n+2)^2*Kprod^2],
    eta80=alpha80/[4(S+2)(n+1)^2],
    q_II=Pfull+1.

Start with coefficients lambda_(i,star)=lambda_(star,i)=w80_i*r80_i for i<n,
lambda_(n,star)=2, and every other entry zero. To these add eta80 on
each directed edge of each of the following cycles, counting overlaps:

    A_(ell,p): ell -> p -> star -> ell,
                           for every ell in Leaf and p in Check;
    B_(p,r):   p -> r -> p, for every unordered pair in Check;
    C_(p,ell): p -> ell -> p, for every |p-ell|=1;
    T_i:       n -> i -> star -> n, for every 0<=i<n.      (II.1)

The arrow denotes the ordered Q source and receiver, not a GD update.
All cycles use original indices. Formula (II.1) specifies EVERY entry
without an optimization problem or unknown PSD block. More explicitly,
write rcheck=Nleaf-1. The finite entries are

    lambda_(p,r)=eta80                (distinct p,r in Check),
    lambda_(ell,p)=eta80*(1+1_(|p-ell|=1)),
    lambda_(p,ell)=eta80*1_(|p-ell|=1),
    lambda_(n,i)=eta80                (0<=i<n).

The optimum entries, including EVERY incoming one, are

    lambda_(ell,star)=w80_ell*r80_ell+eta80,
    lambda_(star,ell)=w80_ell*r80_ell+rcheck*eta80,
    lambda_(p,star)=w80_p*r80_p+(Nleaf+1)*eta80,
    lambda_(star,p)=w80_p*r80_p,
    lambda_(n,star)=2,
    lambda_(star,n)=n*eta80.                              (II.2)

All unlisted entries, including diagonals, are zero. Every scalar shown
is strictly positive where its indicator is one. Each cycle has zero
value flow at each vertex, and the initial array has only terminal flow2.
Hence the full original value cancellation holds exactly. In particular
there is no implicit subtraction of an incoming optimum cost.

Let Cyc be the list in (II.1), and write Q_C=sum_(i,j in cycle C)Q_ij.
The exact entire-word composition identity is

    M_II(q_II)=||x_0||^2+sum_(i<n)w80_i*s80_i||z80_i||^2
                  +||x_n-g_n||^2+eta80*sum_(C in Cyc)Q_C. (II.3)

It follows by (I.2) on ALL physical steps and
||x_n||^2-2f_n+2Q_(n,star)=||x_n-g_n||^2.
Every Q_C is kept with its original mixed terms and both original
displacements. Individual cycles are NOT asserted PSD.

For a cut or dyadic composition, apply (I.5) to each physical child and
the actual bridge, multiply by the enclosing suffix product, and then
add the cycles assigned to that parent. One unambiguous assignment is
the smallest dyadic node containing all finite vertices of a cycle;
if that set is not contained in a proper node, assign it to the root.
Rows involving n are assigned to the root. There is no need to discard
crossing cycles: their exact Q_C polynomials form the boundary coupling.
This is a complete additive identity, not a claim of local child PSD.

For completeness, the all-depth PSD expenditure is explicit. Every
w80_i>=1 and s80_i>=epsilon. At level1, s80_i=(2-epsilon)epsilon>=epsilon.
At level0 use b>1 and 2-b>1/2. At higher levels h_i>3, so s80_i>3.
Let z=x_n-g_n and let Vnorm^2=||x_0||^2+sum_(i<=n)||g_i||^2.
The triangular change of coordinates from (x_0,z80_0,...,z80_(n-1),z)
to the original vectors has the following elementary bound:

    Vnorm^2 <= (n+2)^2*Kprod^2
                   [||x_0||^2+sum_(i<n)||z80_i||^2+||z||^2]. (II.4)

Indeed, for h_i<2 one has g_i=z80_i and x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i z80_i;
for h_i>2 one has g_i=x_i-z80_i and
x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i+h_i z80_i. Induction using factors1+h_i bounds
each x_i and each g_i by Kprod times the sum of residual-vector norms
appearing up to that coordinate. The last equality g_n=x_n-z obeys the
same bound including z. Cauchy--Schwarz for n+2 terms, followed by summing
the n+2 original squared norms, proves (II.4).
Thus the first three terms of (II.3) are at least alpha80*Vnorm^2.

After deleting its value terms, every individual Q row has absolute
quadratic value at most (S+2)*Vnorm^2. For two finite indices use
||x_i-x_j||<=S*Vnorm and ||g_i-g_j||^2/2<=Vnorm^2.
For an outgoing optimum row use ||x_i||<=(1+S)Vnorm, and for an incoming
optimum row its quadratic is ||g_i||^2/2. The value terms of each cycle
cancel, so the row bound can be summed inside that cycle.

The number of row occurrences over all cycles is exactly

    Lcyc=3Nleaf(Nleaf-1)+(Nleaf-1)(Nleaf-2)
                          +4(Nleaf-1)+3n
        =4Nleaf^2+4Nleaf-5 < 2(n+1)^2.

Consequently the absolute sum of all added cycle quadratics is strictly
less than alpha80*Vnorm^2/2. Equation (II.3) proves

    M_II(q_II) >= alpha80*Vnorm^2/2.                     (II.5)

This pays ALL cross-cycle and initial costs once, on the full space, for
every m>=1536. It is a full certificate draft at the very poor q_II. It
does not suggest that cycles may be added freely at the desired tiny q.

## 4. Required original-space screens

Use exactly the earlier H4 direction: x_0=0, g_0,...,g_3=1,
g_8,...,g_11=-1, and every other original gradient, including g_n, zero.
The two active blocks have equal physical mass, so their displacement
cancels exactly. For Law I, (I.4) has all nonnegative terms and its
first term is w80_0^I*b(2-b)>0. For Law II, (II.5) is strictly positive
on this nonzero original vector. These conclusions use the FULL forms;
there is no projection to a primitive or constant-gradient subspace.

For the deep wave at every 2<=j<=m-3, let p=2^j-1, Hbridge=1+d_j,

Again b*g_0+Hbridge*g_p=0, exactly. In Law I the first nonnegative
term is w80_0^I*b(2-b)*(Hbridge/b)^2>0. Law II is positive by (II.5).
Both screens therefore PASS for both replacement bases, even if their
initial coefficient q is replaced by17/(16D): x_0=0 on both tests, so
that replacement does not change either value. Passing does not imply
a useful objective level; Section7 supplies a different test.

## 5. Full initial/common-gradient and actual-terminal accounts

put K_ij=lambda_ij for finite i!=j, mu_i=lambda_(i,star),
nu_i=lambda_(star,i), and h_n=0 as NOTATION only. The full polynomial is

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-sum_i mu_i<x_0,g_i>
                                  +sum_(i,j)C_ij<g_i,g_j>,
    C_ii=mu_i+sum_v K_iv-1_(i=n)-h_i*sum_(v>i)K_iv,
    2C_ij=-(K_ij+K_ji)-h_j*sum_(v>j)K_iv
                    +h_i[mu_j+sum_(v<=i)K_jv], i<j.    (5.1)

To check the diagonal, half the total incident multiplier mass equals
mu_i+sum_v K_iv-1_(i=n), by flow including nu_i. Forward rows out of i
contribute the additional -h_i sum_(v>i)K_iv. For i<j, squared gradient
differences give the first term, forward rows out of i crossing j give
the second, and rows out of j reaching index<=i or the optimum give
the third. Incoming optimum rows have no initial mixed term. Thus no
nu_i or displacement contribution has been silently omitted.

Let e be the all-ones gradient column and Ppos80_i=sum_(t<i)h_t. Then

    U80=sum_i mu_i=2+sum_i nu_i,
    V80=e^T C e=D+sum_i nu_i(1+Ppos80_i).                 (5.2)

For a direct check, set g_i=1 and f_i=X-Ppos80_i-1/2. All finite Q rows
and outgoing optimum rows vanish, while Q_(star,i)=1-X+Ppos80_i.
Substitution yields qX^2-U80 X+V80, proving (5.2). The initial/common
block is B80=[[q,-U80/2],[-U80/2,V80]]. In particular neither old Huber
contact derivative nor the old D/16 slack may be assumed for these bases.

For any variation v of the gradients orthogonal to e, put
u80=mu^T v and k80=e^T C v. If Delta80=q V80-U80^2/4>0, exact
elimination of the ONE initial/common block charges

    [V80*u80^2/4-U80*u80*k80/2+q*k80^2]/Delta80.       (5.3)

The remaining quadratic is v^T C v minus (5.3). This formula includes
all initial and common cross terms in one global charge. At Delta80=0
one must instead impose the range condition and use the corresponding
singular Schur complement. At the explicit q_I and q_II, the square

    M_I(q)=||g_n-Vlast||^2+Rlast,

Law II has incoming optimum-terminal mass n*eta80. Define

Its exact ACTUAL-terminal completion is

    Rprefix=q||x_0||^2+sum_(i!=j in {star,0,...,n-1})lambda_ij Q_ij
                       -eta80*sum_(i<n)delta_i-||Bterm||^2/Aterm. (5.5)

Expanding 2Q_(n,star)+eta80 sum_(i<n)Q_(n,i)+n eta80 Q_(star,n)
proves (5.5): the terminal gradient coefficient is1+n eta80, its
linear coefficient is -2Bterm, and every f_n term cancels -2f_n.
The original prefix flow cancels the remaining -eta80 sum f_i.
Both initial and terminal costs are present. The probability formula
for an incoming-terminal-free certificate is deliberately NOT applied
to Law II's different chosen support.

## 6. A complete restricted-row transcript at every physical index

This construction tests ALL coefficient choices on E80, not merely the
two explicit laws. It also shows why full boundary metrics cannot fix
missing rows by themselves. Define

    Rreset=a*c^2/Mleaf=beta*c/Mleaf,
    sbit(k)=number of ones in the binary expansion of integer k>=0,
    v80_k=(-1)^k*Rreset^k*c^(-sbit(k))/Mleaf,
                                      0<=k<Nleaf.                   (6.1)

Here sbit(0)=0. This is a closed formula, never an executed recurrence.
If r=v2(k+1), binary carry gives sbit(k+1)-sbit(k)=1-r. Therefore

    v80_(k+1)/v80_k=-Rreset*c^(r-1)
               =-a*c^(r+1)/Mleaf=-d_(1+r)/Mleaf.        (6.2)

For each leaf index2k prescribe the REAL scalar jets

    x_(2k)=Mleaf*v80_k,  g_(2k)=v80_k,
    f_(2k)=(b+1/2)*v80_k^2.

For each queried checkpoint2k+1<n prescribe

    x_(2k+1)=v80_k, g_(2k+1)=v80_k, f_(2k+1)=v80_k^2/2.     (6.3)

The leaf update gives Mleaf*v80_k-b*v80_k=v80_k. The following bridge update
gives v80_k-(1+d_(1+v2(k+1)))*v80_k=Mleaf*v80_(k+1), by (6.2).
Thus these are the EXACT original physical GD relations. In particular
x_0=Mleaf*v80_0=1; there is no freedom to change the radius in the proof.

After the final physical leaf the actual terminal position is

    t80=x_n=v80_(Nleaf-1)
       =-Rreset^(Nleaf-1)/(Mleaf*c^(m-1)).               (6.4)

The sign is negative because Nleaf-1 is odd. Its binary expansion has
m-1 ones. This gives (6.4) directly from (6.1), including the last leaf.
Complete that terminal with

    u80term=g_n=2t80/(b+2),
    f_n=t80^2/(b+2),
    x_star=g_star=f_star=0.                            (6.5)

There is no assertion of a single function interpolating these jets.
Their scalar Gram matrix is PSD because all vectors are literal scalars.

We now check EVERY row type in E80, including orientations and the
terminal; no numerical check or finite-horizon inference is used.

At a leaf with parameter v,

    Q_(leaf,star)=0, Q_(star,leaf)=-b*v^2.

At a checkpoint with parameter w, x=g=w and f=w^2/2, so both optimum
rows and all ordered checkpoint-checkpoint rows are zero. For EVERY
leaf v and checkpoint w, regardless of order or distance,

    Q_(leaf(v),check(w))=0,
    Q_(check(w),leaf(v))=b*v*(w-v).                    (6.6)

These formulas follow by substituting (6.3). They also hold with w=0
for the optimum. A neighboring checkpoint AFTER a leaf has w=v,
so both adjacent rows vanish. At a checkpoint BEFORE the next leaf,
v=-d*w/Mleaf with d>0; hence

    b*v*(w-v)=-b*(d/Mleaf)*(1+d/Mleaf)*w^2<0.          (6.7)

These are ALL adjacent prefix incidences, so all of them satisfy Q<=0.

Put u=u80term. Equation (6.5) gives

    f_n-u*t80+u^2/2=-b*u^2/4.

For each queried checkpoint, including the optimum, its outgoing
terminal row is therefore -b*u^2/4. For ANY leaf parameter v the
terminal row is exactly

    Q_(n,leaf(v))=-b*(v-u/2)^2<=0.                    (6.8)

Indeed its expression is f_n-u*t80+u^2/2+b*u*v-b*v^2.
The remaining incoming optimum-terminal row is
Q_(star,n)=-f_n+u^2/2=-b*u^2/4<=0.
This checks all row types(a)--(e), every optimum row, every leaf,
every checkpoint, and the actual unqueried terminal.

## 7. All-depth growth, exact lower obstruction for E80, and failed target

This section is entirely symbolic. Since
Mleaf=lambda-2epsilon/[lambda(1+epsilon)],

    Rreset-1
      =epsilon*[2/(lambda(1+epsilon))-lambda*epsilon]/Mleaf.

With epsilon<1/8 and lambda<5/2 the bracket is greater than
32/45-5/16=287/720>5/16. Also Mleaf<5/2. Thus

    Rreset>1+epsilon/8=1+1/(32m).                     (7.1)

The integer inequality 2^(m-1)-1>=96m^2 holds for m>=16. At16 it is
32767>=24576. If it holds at m, then
2^m-1=2(2^(m-1)-1)+1>=192m^2+1>=96(m+1)^2,
because 96m^2-192m-95>0 for m>=16. This proves the assertion by induction.
All our m are in that range. Consequently

    Nleaf-1>=96m^2>32m(2m+1).

Bernoulli's binomial inequality gives (1+1/(32m))^(32m)>=2. Together
with (7.1), this yields Rreset^(Nleaf-1)>2^(2m+1). Since Mleaf<4 and
c<4, one has Mleaf*c^(m-1)<2^(2m). Formula (6.4) now gives

    |t80|>2,
    2f_n=2t80^2/(b+2)>8/(b+2)>16/7>2.               (7.2)

The exact expression, stronger than this convenient coarse bound, is

    Qrelax80(m)=2*Rreset^(2Nleaf-2)
                      /[(b+2)*Mleaf^2*c^(2m-2)].       (7.3)

For ANY nonnegative array supported on E80 with the required original
value flow, evaluate its full polynomial on (6.1)--(6.5). Its initial
norm is1 and EVERY selected interpolation row is nonpositive. Therefore

    M_cert(q) <= q-Qrelax80(m).

Full PSD forces

    q>=Qrelax80(m)>2, for EVERY m>=1536.               (7.4)

This is a support-level impossibility proof attempt: arbitrary weights,
both optimum directions, arbitrary context, arbitrary matrix boundary
potentials, complete checkpoint couplings and the full terminal fan do
not escape it if their final row support stays inside E80. A free
nonnegative square added to a storage derivation does not change this
argument: after telescoping, the original-row certificate itself must
still be PSD and is tested by the displayed original vectors and values.

The requested q=17/(16D) is less than1 since S>=b>1 and D>3.
Thus (7.4) excludes it by a large margin for both mechanisms and their
whole specified coefficient family. This is not merely a bad choice of
eta80 or of the context weights. It is also not a contradiction with
the genuine full certificates (I.4), (II.5): their explicit levels are
necessarily at least (7.3), and the same calculation forces that fact.
No eigenvalue computation or automated recurrence was used to reach it.

At epsilon=0, Rreset=1 and (6.4) gives t80=-lambda^(-m). The growth
in (7.2) specifically comes from the small positive SAME-m deformation
repeated across all leaves; it is not an objection to the undeformed
silver schedule's full certificate.

## 8. Exact omitted prefix row and the missing boundary inequality

The transcript is provably NOT a legal primal instance. Let

    pbad=n-2=2(Nleaf-2)+1, ellbad=0,
    vfirst=v80_0=1/Mleaf,
    wbad=v80_(Nleaf-2)=-Mleaf*t80/d_1.

Here pbad is an actual queried checkpoint, and ellbad is the actual
initial leaf. Since t80<-2, d_1=1-epsilon<1 and Mleaf>2,
wbad>2Mleaf>vfirst. Formula (6.6) gives the explicit forbidden row

    Q_(pbad,0)=b*vfirst*(wbad-vfirst)>0.                (8.1)

This is a remote queried-prefix row, neither an incoming-terminal row
nor a duplicate-gradient constraint. There is no way to infer its sign
from E80: the complete transcript just checked is a counterexample to
that inference. The reverse row Q_(0,pbad) is present and equals zero.
This directional distinction is essential.

One economical new support direction is the nonnegative symmetric pair
Q_(pbad,0)+Q_(0,pbad). It has zero value flow and acts positively by
(8.1) on this transcript. But it is indefinite on the original formal
space. For ANY queried u<v its full polynomial is

    Q_uv+Q_vu=||g_u-g_v||^2
                 -<g_u-g_v,sum_(u<=t<v)h_t g_t>.      (8.2)

Setting only g_u nonzero gives (1-h_u)||g_u||^2, which is negative
when h_u>1; setting only g_v nonzero gives ||g_v||^2>0. Thus adding
this row pair is not a free PSD repair and starts a genuinely new
unallocated coefficient mechanism. No such third mechanism is attempted.

The precise unresolved boundary construction is as follows. On the SAME
Hword_m, find nonnegative original multipliers with full flow and genuine
remote checkpoint-to-leaf or other excluded prefix rows such that, with
C and mu formed by (5.1),

    C - (4q)^(-1)mu*mu^T >= 0 on ALL gradient coordinates,
    q=17/(16D),                                           (8.3)

or any other rigorously sufficient original-benchmark-beating level.
Every actual terminal and initial cost must remain in C and mu. Formula
(8.3) is the exact Schur condition for q>0. It is a theorem-level missing
inequality, not a technicality or an already constructed certificate.

At a minimum, any such law must supply enough positive action outside
E80 on (6.1)--(6.5). Writing lambda^out for its excluded rows gives the
explicit necessary boundary payment

    sum_(ij outside E80)lambda^out_ij*Q_ij(transcript)
          >= Qrelax80(m)-q
                       -sum_(ij in E80)lambda_ij*Q_ij(transcript)
          >= Qrelax80(m)-q.                            (8.4)

This payment is necessary, never sufficient: (8.2) shows the costs on
other original directions. A full solution requires one analytic all-depth
law paying (8.3) while meeting (8.4), not unknown feasible SDP blocks or
an unproved cone-invariance assertion. Allowing even all checkpoint
gradients in the boundary state does not establish those missing rows.

## 9. Retrieval, novelty boundaries, and final status

The prior H4 and deep-wave tests were recalled from max79 finding
35290b8fa6113ce5 and the earlier own backward-path report. They were used
as screens, not correctness premises. Neither old base enters this report.
The older repeated-copy template already warned about a deformation
accumulating over leaves; novelty is NOT claimed for that qualitative
warning. Here the closed transcript, every retained row orientation, its
free terminal completion, and the bound for arbitrary arrays on E80 were
derived jointly. In particular this obstruction survives changing the
entire inherited base, rather than only adding nonnegative weights to it.

Query-memory, direct-proving, construct-counterexamples, and
identify-key-failures skills were used. The mathematical portions were
kept as one unverified package because TASK.md explicitly closed formal
calls. Matlas was queried once for long-step boundary/Lyapunov certificates;
the returned bounded-step results do not apply. One web call provided
primary-literature context. The already downloaded primary text
arXiv:2309.16530, Section3, Theorem3.4 and its proof in Sections3.1--3.2,
was read for the gluing architecture. Its Q orientation differs from
ours; its result is for its own undeformed schedule and is NOT imported
as a theorem. No external theorem is used as a proof premise here.

Both analytical mechanisms are exhausted in their stated scopes. Their
literal arrays, signs, flow, all-space identities, ancestor-dependent
products, terminal completions and global mixed costs are explicit.
They pass the inherited screens and fail the target for a new, more
general reason: the restricted rows permit incompatible leaf thresholds.
The original unrestricted minimax problem remains OPEN. No theorem was
submitted, no new fact landed, no full-function competitive bound was
obtained, and no negative minimax resolution is claimed. Return this
bounded invocation; no automatic renewal or third law is authorized.

## 2. Same-enclosing-m word and all parameter guards

## 3. Static functions, complete queries, minima, and every row

For u,v>0 let

nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz. Partitioning an interval at the two

complete minimum set{0}, with f(0)=0. For general L set F=L*f.

    x_0=s, x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g(x_i),

fixed function. The initial radius about the complete minimum is
exactly |s|. All theorem statements cover this full literal trajectory,
not an auxiliary trajectory with freely chosen gradients.

One tempting ratio-free primitive envelope is

    A=A_(m-1), d=d_(m-1), S=A-1,

radius is (R^2/D_j+1)/2. Passing this enlarged symmetric interval

mechanism keeps threshold-conditioned affine exterior branches and
exact signed interval capture, rather than assuming(4.1).

each of size l_j=2^(j-1)-1, and let rootcell be its actual checkpoint.

## 9. Failure synthesis and the remaining interface

Law I has an explicit full PSD factor but no nonnegative original-row
representation with its fixed terminal pool. The first-row invariant
survives every balanced-skew re-selection preserving that exact factor.
This is an original coefficient obstruction, not a missing full-space
term, an untested child block, or failure of a restricted kernel test.

Law II allows a nonzero skew divergence and accounts for its genuine
common-gradient derivative. Its correction costs tau^2/(2kappa) ONCE,
globally. The literal correction can make a first-query edge less
positive in Nmat, but the last-to-previous-leaf edge demands a larger
detail coefficient. The two demands force the stated excessive charge.
The obstruction concerns this one skew pattern and terminal distribution,
not arbitrary chronological corrections or further coefficient re-selection.

The still-needed mechanism is an explicit full factor AND a nonnegative
original-row matching at q82<=17/(16D) for every SAME-m m>=1536. A changed
terminal distribution, a nonisotropic chronology-dependent detail system,
or a more general skew correction with an analytically bounded aggregate

# Tail-weighted full squares and an explicit balanced first-row repair

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical report, worker max, invocation83.
Original exact-profile minimax problem OPEN. No new fact or verifier verdict.

This is one joint derivation, not a sequence of accepted intermediate facts.
TASK.md and master_guidance a16df0f0aca7349e permit ONE invocation and at
most TWO substantive coefficient laws. They forbid mathematical programs,
numerical evaluations, arithmetic/trajectory/recurrence replays, solvers,
formal calls/fact_submit, installations, consults and subagents. All those
counts remain zero. All scalar inequalities below are textual mathematics.

## 1. Outcome and exact scope

The exact suffix-product scale is retained in BOTH the nonisotropic detail
metric and the actual terminal distribution. Every original queried gradient,
the actual unqueried terminal gradient, and the initial vector remain
independent. The two explicit laws use the same weighted full square and
distributed imbalance, but genuinely different original coefficient arrays.

Law A uses the canonical weighted skew for that imbalance. Throughout its
entire domain, its incoming optimum multiplier at original query1 is
negative. Independently, making its first-to-last queried multiplier
nonnegative forces its exact global square charge above the assigned
qtar=17/(16D). This quantifies why paying through an exponentially tiny
initial tail weight fails in this particular matching.

Law B adds an EXPLICIT BALANCED skew transport, with no sign-feasibility
oracle. It equalizes the entire first row, and can make all its finite
multipliers nonnegative while maintaining the full PSD factor at qtar.
Nevertheless, for EVERY member of Law B, either the original multiplier
from the last queried leaf to the preceding queried leaf is negative, or
the original incoming optimum multiplier at query1 is negative. This is
an exhaustive obstruction for this displayed balanced correction, including
arbitrary positive metric scale and arbitrary nonnegative imbalance scale.

Neither exclusion is an impossibility theorem for all balanced corrections,
all weighted variances, all terminal probabilities, or the full dual cone.
No primal interpolability or lower bound on W is inferred from a formal
negative direction or a negative signed multiplier. No full upper bound on
W, benchmark improvement, or resolution of the original problem is obtained.

## 2. Original problem and accepted inputs

For a predetermined nonnegative word h of length n and L>0, W_n(h) denotes
the supremum of 2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite
Euclidean dimension, convex differentiable L-smooth function with an
attained minimizer x_star, and x_0!=x_star, under the original recursion
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R. The original question concerns
whether W_n_star/U_n^ZJ tends to1, where W_n_star=inf_(h>=0)W_n(h) and
U_n^ZJ=1/B_n. The original benchmark retains EVERY integer split:

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(u,v)=(u+v+sqrt(u^2+6uv+v^2))/2,
    G(u,v)=2u+v/2+sqrt(v^2+8uv)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n) Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n) G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)).

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the original interpolation
orientation, full independent-vector certificate interpretation, and exact
incoming-terminal-free reduction. It deletes NO queried-prefix row.
Accepted fact931b9653ce0f7201 supplies the same-enclosing-m word below,
its mass identity and the scalar comparison B_n/D<47/50. Its implication
from W_n(H_m)<=17/(16D) to a strict benchmark improvement is CONDITIONAL;
that full-class upper hypothesis is still missing. These are the only
accepted mathematical inputs used here. Historical draft6e66efffac0795f1
is recall only; its coordinate and row identities are rederived below.

Fix ANY integer m>=1536. All children use this SAME enclosing m:

    ell=1+sqrt(2), eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps,
    c=ell(1+eps), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), 0<=j<m,
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, z=n-1,
    S=sum_(i<n)h_i, Aword=1+S, D=1+2S=2Aword-1,
    p=1/Aword, qtar=17/(16D), b=1+a.

The symbols p and q in this report mean p83 and q83; neither is a benchmark
exponent or a primal derivative. The letter B without a subscript below is
a skew matrix, not the benchmark B_n. All other hierarchy notation is local.
The actual physical step is h_i=1+a*c^v2(i+1), where v2(j) is the exponent
of2 dividing the positive integer j. The final three steps are
(b,1+beta,b). The first and last queried steps equal b; index n is the
ACTUAL terminal, distinct from z.

The elementary bounds needed below are

    12/5<c<5/2, 7/8<beta<1, 1/3<a<1/2, 4/3<b<3/2.       (2.1)

For example sqrt(2)>7/5 and sqrt(2)<17/12; hence ell>12/5 and

The accepted mass formula is

    Aword=(1-vword)2^m+vword*c^m,

    2^m<Aword<c^m, 0<p<2^(-m)<1/128.                  (2.2)

Every h_i>1, consistently with these strict mass inequalities.

## 3. Exact physical suffix products and the selected terminal law

Write sbit(L) for the binary digit sum of a nonnegative integer L, including
sbit(0)=0. For 0<=L<=n define the product of the FINAL L actual factors:

    r_L=product_(t=n-L)^(n-1)(h_t-1), r_0=1.

The index j counted backward from the final physical step has
h_(n-j)-1=a*c^v2(2^m-j)=a*c^v2(j), for 1<=j<2^m. The valuation equality
follows by factoring the exact power of2 from j: the remaining difference
from2^m is odd. For any L, sum_(j=1)^L v2(j)=sum_(t>=1)floor(L/2^t).
Writing L in binary and summing each digit's contributions gives
sum_(t>=1)floor(L/2^t)=L-sbit(L). Therefore the EXACT suffix identity is

    r_L=beta^L*c^(-sbit(L)), 0<=L<=n.                 (3.1)

No product or recurrence has been numerically evaluated. In particular
s:=r_n=beta^n/c^m, and the signed full-word product is -s since n is odd.
Define the actual terminal coefficient and its absolute scale by

    k_i=h_i product_(i<t<n)(1-h_t),
    u_i=|k_i|, U=sum_(i<n)u_i, rho_i=u_i/U.

If L=n-1-i, adding the next backward factor shows

    u_i=r_L+r_(L+1), k_i=(-1)^L u_i=(-1)^i u_i.       (3.2)

Thus all u_i are strictly positive. The last three are

    u_z=b, u_(z-1)=a(1+beta), u_(z-2)=b*a*beta,
    u_0=(b/a)s.                                      (3.3)

Expanding a product over the m binary digits gives the finite identity

    Z=sum_(L=0)^n r_L=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1+beta^(2^j)/c),
    U=2Z-1-s <2(3/2)^m.                              (3.4)

The last inequality uses beta<1 and c>2. The three distinct last terms
in (3.3), with (2.1), give

    U>4/3+5/8+7/18=169/72>7/3.                       (3.5)

Both laws use these SAME explicit terminal probabilities:

    alpha_star=p, alpha_i=(1-p)rho_i=delta*u_i,
    delta=(1-p)/U, rplus=1-delta, rminus=1+delta,
    v=k-alpha.                                       (3.6)

They sum to1 and are strictly positive on every original queried sample
and the optimum. They are probabilities on real original rows, not on a
selected child interface. Since U>7/3, one has 0<delta<3/7, rplus>1/2,
and 1<rminus<3/2. Precisely

    v_i=rplus*u_i for i even,
    v_i=-rminus*u_i for i odd.                        (3.7)

Several uniform small-initial-weight bounds will be used. The binomial
expansion implies n=2^m-1>m(m-1)/2>128m for m>=1536. Also
(1-eps)^(-n)>(1+eps)^n>=1+n*eps, so beta^n<1/33. From Aword<c^m,
s/p=beta^n*Aword/c^m<beta^n. Because b/a=1+1/a<4,

    s<p/33, u_0<4p/33<p/8,
    alpha_0<p/8, rho_0<3p/56<1/10.                  (3.8)

These are symbolic inequalities uniform in all enclosing m in the task.

## 4. Full original coordinates and the complete signed matching

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Keep arbitrary independent
vectors x_0,g_0,...,g_n, with every original position defined by

    x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t*g_t.

The residual orientation is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

Legal actual jets obey Q_ij<=0. For i<n let y_i=x_i-g_i and
Delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2, with the corresponding star quantities zero.
Let e be the all-ones column of length n, e_i its coordinate columns, and
T=T82 the lower triangular matrix T_ii=1, T_it=h_t for t<i, zero for t>i.
For vector columns g=(g_0,...,g_(n-1)) and y=(y_0,...,y_(n-1)),

    y=e*x_0-Tg, g=T^(-1)(e*x_0-y).                    (4.1)

This is invertible on the ENTIRE formal space. Explicitly, if
pi_i=product_(t<i)(1-h_t), then

    g_i=pi_i*x_0-y_i
          +sum_(j<i)h_j product_(j<t<i)(1-h_t)*y_j.  (4.2)

Substitution into x_(i+1)=(1-h_i)x_i+h_i*y_i proves

    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y, e^T k=1+s, T^T k=h.           (4.3)

For the latter identity, h_j=1-(1-h_j) telescopes on each suffix:
k_i+h_i sum_(j>i)k_j=h_i. In particular e^T v=p+s.
The cumulative terminal probabilities, distinct from detail weights below,
are Cprob_i=p+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j. Define

    R_i=h_i*Cprob_i-alpha_i,
    t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j, t=Te,
    Uclock=sum_i R_i=t^T v,
    gamma=2p/(p+s), eta=(p-s)/(p+s).

Then T^T v=R and
R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i>0. Thus Uclock>0,

    R_0=bp+a*alpha_0, H=p+s-v_0=p+alpha_0-s/a,
    bp<R_0<25p/16, 7p/8<H<9p/8.                     (4.4)

The lower bound on H follows from H=p+s-rplus*u_0>p-u_0; its upper
bound follows from the second expression in (4.4).
The actual terminal center is V=-s*x_0+v^T y.

For the moment let w_i>0 be arbitrary DETAIL weights, Ww=sum_i w_i,
and let d be any real column with e^T d=0. Define

    K=diag(w)-w*w^T/Ww,
    A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww+B, B^T=-B, Be=0,
    P=K+gamma*v*v^T, N=T^T(P+A).                     (4.5)

Thus Ke=0, A^T=-A and Ae=d. The matrices are instantiated explicitly in
Sections6 and7; an arbitrary sign-feasible B is NOT a proposed result.
Every scalar entry is

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(K_uj+A_uj)
                                      +gamma*R_i*v_j. (4.6)

The entire ORIGINAL SIGNED coefficient array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,n-1},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for i!=j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i=2p*R_i+(T^T d)_i,

                      =(Kt)_i+gamma*Uclock*v_i-(At)_i-2alpha_i,

       +(q-p^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,d^T y>.                (4.8)

## 5. Weighted completion, the real common derivative, and a row invariant

Let ybar_w=sum_i w_i*y_i/Ww. Since sum_i d_i=0, expanding the squares gives

    sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2
       +sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(d_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
       +eta||v^T y-(p+s)x_0||^2+(q-p^2-J)||x_0||^2.  (5.2)

The charge J is paid ONCE globally. No child gradient, common mode, leaf,
checkpoint, terminal square or initial cross derivative has been removed.
The detail form has kernel exactly the constant y columns, because every
