B changes neither this derivative nor the full square polynomial.

Now derive the original FIRST-ROW off-diagonal sum including d_0.
The first column of T is (1,b,...,b)^T. Since K has column sums zero,
(T^T K)_00=-a*K_00. Skewness gives A_00=0, and e^T A=-d^T gives
(T^T A)_00=-b*d_0. Meanwhile (T^T d)_0=-a*d_0. Subtracting the diagonal
from the row sum in (4.7) yields

    sum_(j>0) N_0j
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*(p+s-v_0)+d_0
       =a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H+d_0.                     (5.4)

Every balanced B leaves this sum invariant. Nonnegative finite first-row
multipliers require the right side to be <=0. A balanced correction can
redistribute that sum among entries; it cannot change the sum itself.

There is also an exact inverse-metric price for this invariant. Weighted
Cauchy--Schwarz on i>0 gives
sum_(i>0)d_i^2/w_i >=d_0^2/(Ww-w_0), since sum_(i>0)d_i=-d_0.
Consequently

    J>=d_0^2/(4*K_00), K_00=w_0(1-w_0/Ww).          (5.5)

Equality holds precisely when d_i=-d_0*w_i/(Ww-w_0) for every i>0.
Because H>0, (5.4)--(5.5) imply for any nonnegative first row

    J>=(a*K_00+gamma*R_0*H)^2/(4*K_00)
      >=a*gamma*R_0*H.                               (5.6)

The final inequality expands the nonnegative square
(a*K_00-gamma*R_0*H)^2. This is a necessary first-row screen, NOT a
sufficient certificate condition. The two selected laws now instantiate
all weights and skew matrices rather than leaving the screen unsolved.

## 6. Law A: exact tail metric with minimum-price distributed imbalance

For EVERY kappa>0 and tau>=0 choose

    w_i=kappa*u_i, Ww=kappa*U,
    d=tau*(rho-e_0),
    A_A=tau*(rho*e_0^T-e_0*rho^T), B_A=0.             (6.1)

Here A_A=(d*w^T-w*d^T)/Ww exactly, and A_A e=d. The imbalance is
negative at0 and positive at EVERY other actual queried index, not just
at one endpoint. It attains equality in (5.5). The metric is nonisotropic
because u_0<p/8 whereas u_z=b>4/3. The terminal probabilities remain (3.6).

The exact global charge and common derivative are

    J_A=tau^2*(1-rho_0)/(4*kappa*u_0),
    d^T t=tau*(tbar-1), tbar=sum_i rho_i*t_i.          (6.2)

Thus (5.2) is a fully specified factor iff q>=p^2+J_A.
For a literal scalar description of EVERY finite entry put
F_i=u_i+h_i sum_(j>i)u_j. Then

    N^A_ij=kappa*(u_i*1_(i=j)+h_i*u_j*1_(j>i)-F_i*rho_j)
          +gamma*R_i*v_j
          +tau*((F_i/U)*1_(j=0)-1_(i=0)*rho_j).      (6.3)

Together with (4.7), this is the complete array. Both optimum orientations
can also be written explicitly:

    mu_0=2p*R_0+a*tau*(1-rho_0)>0,
    mu_i=2p*R_i+tau*F_i/U>0 for i>0,
    nu^A_i=kappa*u_i*(t_i-tbar)+gamma*Uclock*v_i
                         -tau*(rho_i-1_(i=0)*tbar)-2alpha_i. (6.4)

All terminal outgoing signs and all outgoing optimum signs pass. No sign
is silently assigned to nu^A or an off-diagonal -N^A.

### 6.1 A first-row charge obstruction at the assigned target

Since v_z=rplus*u_z, the actual first-to-last queried entry is

    N^A_0z=rho_z*(a*kappa*u_0-tau)
                                +gamma*R_0*rplus*u_z. (6.5)

If lambda_(0,z)=-N^A_0z>=0, positivity of rho_z gives

    tau>=a*kappa*u_0+gamma*R_0*(U-1+p).               (6.6)

Apply (a*x+C)^2/(4x)>=a*C for x=kappa*u_0>0 and
C=gamma*R_0*(U-1+p)>0. Equations (6.2) and (6.6) imply

    J_A>=a*gamma*R_0*(U-1+p)*(1-rho_0)
       >(4/9)*p*(4/3)*(9/10)=8p/15.                (6.7)

The strict lower bounds use a*b>4/9, gamma>1, R_0>bp, U>7/3 and
rho_0<1/10. On the other hand Aword>128 gives

    qtar/p=17*Aword/[16*(2Aword-1)]<8/15,             (6.8)

because this inequality is equivalent to Aword>128. Thus no member of
Law A has both full PSD and lambda_(0,z)>=0 at q<=qtar. This argument
uses the exact SINGLE global charge and no local Schur-budget summation.

### 6.2 A stronger literal incoming-optimum failure for every q

The weighted clock is uniformly large. By (3.3)--(3.5), t_z>n and
n>2^(m-1), so

    tbar>=rho_z*t_z> b*n/[2*(3/2)^m]
                     >(1/3)*(4/3)^m>27.             (6.9)

For the last inequality m>=16 and (4/3)^4=256/81>3, so (4/3)^16>81.
Meanwhile t_1=1+b<5/2<tbar/2. Query1 has v_1=-rminus*u_1<0.
In (6.4) its metric term is strictly negative, its rank term is strictly
negative, its skew term is nonpositive, and -2alpha_1 is strictly negative.
Hence

    nu^A_1=lambda_(star,1)<0                         (6.10)

for EVERY m>=1536, kappa>0, tau>=0 and every real q. This excludes
Law A as an original-row certificate even at larger q. It does not exclude
a balanced re-selection, which can change nu_1 and (6.5). Law B performs
one such correction explicitly; it is not dismissed by (6.10).

## 7. Law B: an explicit balanced transport that repairs the entire first row

Keep the SAME w,d,alpha,p and arbitrary kappa>0,tau>=0 as in Law A.
Define the probability column on noninitial queried samples

    r_0^pool=0, r_i^pool=u_i/(U-u_0) for i>0,
    chi=e_0-r^pool,
    xi=gamma*R_0/a,
    bvec_0=0, bvec_i=xi*(v_i-H*r_i^pool) for i>0,
    B_B=chi*bvec^T-bvec*chi^T,
    A_B=A_A+B_B.                                     (7.1)

The r^pool column is distinct from the suffix product r_L. Its denominator
is positive, and its entries sum to1. Since sum_(i>0)v_i=H, both chi and
bvec have sum zero. Therefore B_B is skew AND B_B e=0. In particular
A_B e=d, and the entire factor (5.2), charge (6.2), and real derivative
(5.3) are unchanged. There is no hidden skew unknown in this law.

For complete scalar coefficients define
C_i=chi_i+h_i sum_(j>i)chi_j and
E_i=bvec_i+h_i sum_(j>i)bvec_j. Then

    N^B_ij=N^A_ij+C_i*bvec_j-E_i*chi_j.              (7.2)

Equations (4.7), (6.3), (7.1)--(7.2) specify EVERY original coefficient.
The outgoing optimum coefficients are still the strictly positive mu_i
in (6.4). The incoming optimum coefficients are

    nu^B_i=nu^A_i-chi_i*(bvec^T t)+bvec_i*(chi^T t).  (7.3)

No positivity of these incoming coefficients is assumed.

### 7.1 The entire first row is explicitly equalized

For j>0, B_B,0j=bvec_j. Because B_B has zero column sums,
(T^T B_B)_0j=-a*bvec_j. Substituting (7.1) in (6.3) yields

    N^B_0j=r_j^pool*S0,
    S0=(a*kappa*u_0-tau)*(1-rho_0)+gamma*R_0*H.      (7.4)

In particular ALL original finite first-row multipliers are nonnegative
iff S0<=0, equivalently

    tau>=a*kappa*u_0+gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).           (7.5)

This realizes the invariant (5.4), rather than assuming it can be repaired.
It changes the demanding Law A quantity U-1+p in (6.6) to the much smaller
H/(1-rho_0). Thus the Law A charge obstruction does NOT transfer to Law B.

The simultaneous first-row and full-PSD conditions at qtar are nonvacuous.
Within this same two-parameter law choose the explicit member

    kappa_0=gamma*R_0*H/[a*u_0*(1-rho_0)],
    tau_0=2*gamma*R_0*H/(1-rho_0).                    (7.6)

These are positive. Equation (7.4) gives N^B_0j=0 for every j>0, and
J_A=a*gamma*R_0*H. From (2.1), gamma<2 and (4.4),

    J_A< (25p/16)*(9p/8)=225p^2/128<2p^2.

Consequently p^2+J_A<3p^2<p/2<qtar, because p<1/128 and
qtar/p=17*Aword/[16*(2Aword-1)]>17/32>1/2. This is a strictly positive
full factor at the target with all finite first-row multipliers zero,
positive terminal probabilities, and positive outgoing optimum multipliers.
It remains a FAILED certificate because the complete array still has a
negative original coefficient, as the next subsection proves.

### 7.2 Last-to-previous-leaf versus incoming optimum1: exhaustive sign conflict

Let j=z-2, the genuine preceding queried leaf. Both z and j are even.
For i,j>0 the balanced correction has the explicit entry

    B_B,ij=xi*(v_i*r_j^pool-r_i^pool*v_j).            (7.7)

By (3.7), v_z/u_z=v_j/u_j=rplus. Therefore B_B,zj=0. Also
A_A,zj=0. The last row of T^T is the last coordinate row, so exactly

    N^B_zj=u_z*u_j*(-kappa/U+gamma*rplus^2).          (7.8)

If kappa<gamma*U*rplus^2, this entry is positive and the ORIGINAL
lambda_(z,z-2) is negative. Otherwise its sign passes and necessarily

    kappa>=gamma*U*rplus^2>7/12.                     (7.9)

The strict lower bound follows from gamma>1, U>7/3 and rplus>1/2.
We now prove that throughout this remaining domain nu^B_1 is negative.

Put tpool=sum_i r_i^pool*t_i=(tbar-rho_0)/(1-rho_0). Then
bvec^T t=xi*(Uclock-v_0-H*tpool), chi^T t=1-tpool.
For i>0, using (7.3) gives the exact expression

    nu^B_i=kappa*u_i*(t_i-tbar)
       +[gamma*Uclock-xi*(tpool-1)]*v_i
       +xi*r_i^pool*(Uclock-(p+s))-tau*rho_i-2alpha_i. (7.10)

This includes the actual initial clock t_0=1 in BOTH appearances of
(tpool-1) and (p+s); omitting it would change the optimum row.
At query1, divide by the positive u_1 and use v_1/u_1=-rminus:

    nu^B_1/u_1=kappa*(t_1-tbar)
       +[-gamma*rminus+xi/(U-u_0)]*Uclock
       +xi*rminus*(tpool-1)-xi*(p+s)/(U-u_0)
       -tau/U-2delta.                                (7.11)

All signs in this expression can be bounded uniformly. Since b/a<4,
alpha_0<p/8, and gamma<2,

    xi=gamma*(bp/a+alpha_0)<2*(4p+p/8)<9p.           (7.12)

Also U-u_0>7/3-1/8>2. With p<1/128, (7.12) implies
xi/(U-u_0)<9p/2<1<gamma*rminus. Thus the coefficient of Uclock in
(7.11) is negative; Uclock>0. The terms -xi*(p+s)/(U-u_0), -tau/U and
-2delta are nonpositive, with the first and last strictly negative.
Further,

    tpool < tbar/(1-rho_0),
    xi*rminus*tpool < (9p)*(3/2)*(10/9)*tbar
                                      =15p*tbar.    (7.13)

Since t_1<tbar/2 by (6.9), dropping the negative terms in (7.11) gives

    nu^B_1/u_1<(-kappa/2+15p)*tbar<0.               (7.14)

For the final strict sign, (7.9) gives kappa/2>7/24, whereas
15p<15/128<7/24. All denominators and u_1,tbar are positive.

Combining (7.8) and (7.14) covers EVERY kappa>0,tau>=0, with no assumption
on PSD or the first-row signs: either lambda_(z,z-2)<0, or
lambda_(star,1)=nu^B_1<0. At equality kappa=gamma*U*rplus^2, (7.9) and
(7.14) still apply. This excludes the WHOLE displayed Law B domain at any
q, in particular every full-PSD member at qtar, including (7.6).

This conflict concerns the literal balanced correction (7.1). Another
balanced matrix can change the pair (7.8), the optimum row (7.11), or both.
No universal exclusion of balanced re-selection is asserted.

## 8. Boundary, sign and scope audit

* All enclosing integers m>=1536 are treated with the SAME beta,c,a at
  every child. No finite numerical horizon test or reset is used.
* The probabilities at every original queried target and at the optimum
  are strictly positive. The actual terminal gradient remains free, with
  its exact square retained. No earlier remote row is removed.
* The variance metric controls all n-1 independent detail directions.
  The independent common direction and its real derivative are retained.
* Every finite and optimum coefficient has a literal scalar formula.
  Terminal and outgoing-optimum signs pass for both laws. Incoming-optimum
  and finite signs fail as proved; no signed row is called a certificate.
* tau=0 is allowed and covered; kappa>0 is necessary for the specified
  positive metric. Equality in PSD and in the tail sign has been covered.
* Balanced B_B e=0 is checked explicitly, and the initial clock contribution
  is retained in the exact incoming-optimum formula. This is not the old
  isotropic endpoint correction or the old physical-tree uniform pool.
* The first-row invariant includes d_0. Its inverse-metric charge is paid
  once, with an explicit global square-zero direction proving necessity.
* Formal negative directions are not actual trajectories. Failure of these
  two coefficient laws gives no lower bound on W and no global no-certificate
  theorem. Fact931's missing full-function hypothesis remains unproved.

The row identities and inequalities above have received a textual author
audit only. They are not verifier-accepted facts, and no downstream argument
may treat this report as an accepted building block.

## 9. Retrieval, failure synthesis and handoff

The query-memory, immediate-conclusions, direct-proving,
construct-counterexamples and identify-key-failures procedures guided this
bounded joint attempt. The fact search found no accepted version of the
new weighted first-row identity or these two row laws. Current guidance
was recalled by its targeted query after an empty-string query returned
count0. Oversized initial recall output was truncated; the relevant old
joint report and accepted inputs were reread in bounded portions.

A repair-mode Matlas search for full PSD weighted interpolation certificates
returned unrelated PL, stochastic and constant-step statements; none was
used. Web search located Altschuler--Parrilo, 'Acceleration by Stepsize
Hedging II: Silver Stepsize Schedule for Smooth Convex Optimization',
arXiv:2309.16530, https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16530, already read in the prior
round as exact proof-pattern background. No external theorem or proof step
is imported here. The new laws reduce to explicit coefficient identities
in that already-audited interpolation regime; no additional literature
layer or new mathematical machinery is needed for these scoped algebraic
rejections. No notebook or numerical certificate was run.

Law A's failure is not caused by forgetting tail scales: it uses them in
both the metric and terminal distribution, and its imbalance is optimally
distributed for its fixed initial component. Its literal first-to-last row
still overcharges, and the early negative-k incoming optimum row fails.

Law B demonstrates a real escape from Law A's first-row charge argument:
an explicit balanced transport repairs the entire row at affordable full
PSD cost. Its remaining failure is a different, complete-original-array
conflict: a same-sign pair of late queried leaves fixes a nonvanishing
metric scale, while the early odd query sits below the weighted mean clock
and has negative terminal coefficient. The specified transport is too
small to pay that original optimum row at that forced metric scale.

The next missing mechanism would have to alter this second conflict, for
example through a different balanced transport affecting the relevant
late pair and optimum load, a different genuinely nonisotropic metric, or
a different actual terminal law. These are uncovered freedoms, not a third
law attempted in this invocation and not a solution by an unknown matrix.
The first-row invariant (5.4) and its charge (5.5) remain necessary checks
in the stated general architecture; their sufficiency has not been claimed.

# Releasing the middle sector: exact original-row lift and two scoped failures

JOINT UNVERIFIED. Project gd-exact-profile-20260926, worker max4,
invocation81, guidance b941bd3964f8f8f6, plan8fc254f625619e19.
No formal submission was permitted or made. No new fact_id exists.

This report derives the full remainder when all middle gradients are
released at j=0,k=n-2. It gives explicit nonnegative weights on actual
rows for two natural lifts, and proves that neither lift is positive
semidefinite on the full formal space, even with the allowed objective
slack. The second mechanism tests an explicit four-sector discriminator:
its negative formal direction is not interpolable, and the most direct
single-boundary-cycle repair cannot be PSD either. These are scoped
certificate obstructions, not a counterexample to a function-class bound.

The theorem-level interface remains open: a successful lift needs a
different original-row construction with a full-space sign/Schur proof.
No uniform upper bound on W, no primal escape, and no resolution of the
original every-n/every-nonnegative-word problem is claimed.

All derivations below are joint: no new unverified lemma is imported as
an accepted premise. Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies only original
interpolation necessity/sufficiency and normalization. Accepted
931b9653ce0f7201 supplies only its hierarchy/benchmark scope, in Section12.

## 1. Same physical word, actual boundary indices, and normalization

Fix any integer m>=1536, and throughout set

    lambda=1+sqrt(2), epsilon_h=1/(4m), beta_h=1-epsilon_h,
    c=lambda(1+epsilon_h), a=beta_h/c,
    H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j),
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, S=sum h, Z=D_m=1+2S.

All children keep this SAME enclosing m and all its parameters. Index
the actual steps from0 to n-1. Put

    K=n-2, R=n-1,
    A=h_0=h_R=1+a, d=a, e=h_K-1=a*c=beta_h,
    I={1,...,K}, M=sum_(i=1)^(K-1) h_i,
    B=sum_(i in I)h_i=M+1+e=S-2A,
    v=M+1=B-e, U=1+d+v,
    w=A+1/2-A^2/2=1-a^2/2,
    D=U+e+w=S+1/2-A^2/2.

Thus 2D=Z-A^2. The singleton first sector is index0, the entire middle
sector is I, the singleton last queried sector is indexR, and n is the
actual unqueried terminal. In particular h_K has dyadic level1, not0:
K+1=2^m-2 is divisible by2 but not4. Every physical leaf remains.

Normalize a legal instance to L=1, f_star=0, x_star=g_star=0. Write
x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i)h_t g_t and use exactly the accepted orientation

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2 <=0.       (1.1)

The objective-certificate level is denoted chi, to avoid confusion with
any gradient or benchmark capacity. It would bound 2f_n/||x_0||^2.
General L follows by dividing the objective by L and translating its own
specified minimizer; the normalization stays W=2R.

Elementary bounds used below are jointly recorded here. Since
lambda<5/2 and epsilon_h<=1/6144, in fact c<5/2; for example use
sqrt(2)<10/7, lambda<17/7, and (17/7)(6145/6144)<5/2.
Also beta_h>99/100, so

    1/3<a<1/2, 1<A<3/2, 0<e<1, 7/8<w<1.             (1.2)

The upper bound on a follows from a<1/lambda=sqrt(2)-1<1/2.
For the lower bound use a>(99/100)/(5/2)=99/250>1/3.
There are n-3 ordinary middle entries, all exceeding1, so v>n-2>5.
In particular U>6 and D>18. Much weaker horizon bounds would suffice.

For later mass comparisons put X_h,j=1+sum H_j. Literal summation gives
X_h,(j+1)=2X_h,j+a*c^j, X_h,0=1, hence

    X_h,j=(1-v_h)2^j+v_h*c^j, v_h=a/(c-2).           (1.3)

Substitution verifies this symbolic formula, without evaluating a
recurrence. Since c(c-2)>lambda(lambda-2)=1>beta_h, one has 0<v_h<1.
Consequently X_h,m<c^m, S<c^m, and B<c^m.

## 2. A concrete three-sector row identity, rederived jointly

Start by imposing g_i=q for i in I, and put p=g_0, r=g_R. Define

| Row | mu |
|---|---:|

    theta=(U+e)/(U+2e+2w) <1,

## 10. What a successful next lift must actually supply

The frozen and mean-weighted identities locate the missing terms rather
than suppressing them. Neither a diagonal-variance claim nor a choice
of the available chi slack pays them.

A new proof must give nonnegative original weights with exact value
balance and a full-space bound. It could change the middle probability
law, add actual middle-to-middle rows, or recursively distribute flow,
but none of those mechanisms is completed here. For a fan with a
different probability law, even its internal two-coordinate blocks
must satisfy (6.4), and the chronological vectors P_omega,T_omega and
the independent displacement dvec still remain in (4.4). A successful
recursion cannot keep only the displacement mean while forgetting
these moments. Its boundary state and sign closure must be explicit.

The two formal tests in Section8 show why the first missing adjacent
cycle cannot simply be assigned whatever weight repairs (7.4): its
initial charge must also be paid. They do not exclude a larger network
that supplies that price through other rows. No unspecified PSD block
is offered as a theorem, and no unknown block has been assigned a
positive sign.

No new substantive mechanism is begun after these two permitted ones.

author: max3
claim: JOINT UNVERIFIED max3 invocation78: replacing common curvature by K=max(kappa_plus,kappa_minus) in the radial plateau lemma is false for an actual clipped full H_m trajectory. Terminal radius stays above7a/8 although the claimed bound is1/d_m; the actual objective has D_m*E<9/64 and is not an improving witness.
evidence: For every SAME-m m>=1536, let S=S_m, ell=1+a, and retain all steps H_m. Choose kappa_plus=1, kappa_minus=mu=1/(4S), b_plus=1, b_minus=a/(8S)=mu*a/2, and x0=1. Define ONE static derivative g(x)=min(x,1) on x>=0 and max(mu*x,-b_minus) on x<=0; f is its integral from0. This g is continuous, nondecreasing and1-Lipschitz, so f is finite differentiable convex1-smooth with complete minimum set{0}, minimum0 and own initial radius1. All ordered interpolation rows follow by integrating the nonnegative triangular lower bounds g(t)-g(x)>=max(0,g(y)-g(x)-(y-t)) and g(y)-g(t)>=max(0,g(y)-g(x)-(t-x)) for x<t<y; both integrals are at least(g(y)-g(x))^2/2. Actual scalar vectors give a PSD full Gram. The first actual leaf ell gives x1=-a. At every index1<=i<=n_m set T_i=sum_{t=1}^{i-1}h_t and x_i=-a+b_minus*T_i. Because T_i<=S-ell<S, every such radius is>7a/8>a/2, the true negative threshold. Thus g_i=-b_minus, and every physical update, repeated interval visit and terminal formula is exact on this same function. Terminal radius r=a*(7/8+ell/(8S)). True coordinate thresholds are u_plus=1 and u_minus=a/2. K=1 and s=1 satisfy s<=K*d_m*min(u_plus,u_minus), whereas r>7a/8>1/d_m; the inequalities follow from a>2/5,d_m>20, derived jointly in report Sections3,8. # Independent common square, positive incoming load, and two row-clock obstructions

JOINT UNVERIFIED analytical report. Worker max, invocation85.
Original exact-profile minimax problem OPEN. No new fact or formal submission.

## 1. Outcome and exact scope

This report jointly rederives the enlarged common-square architecture and
all its original interpolation coefficients. The paid zero-sum column is
zeta, whereas the actual skew divergence is

    d=zeta+(p-s)(v-z).

Separating z from v changes the architecture, but does not grant free
sign-feasible transport. The outgoing optimum vector depends on zeta,
not on d alone. Both the incoming total/clock moments and the complete
first-row total/clock moments are derived below for GENERAL z.

Law I uses a clock-zero endpoint common column independent of v, a
strictly positive incoming optimum load nu=(1/64)e_0 at the INITIAL
query, and an explicitly scaled positive source/last/tail metric. Its full
polynomial is PSD below the target and all optimum signs pass. Its
first-row total has the required sign. Nevertheless its endpoint clock
defect is negative uniformly in every enclosing m>=1536, for every
skew completion preserving the selected actions. In the ideal endpoint
metric, EVERY compatible endpoint incoming load cancels exactly from
this defect. The positive load in this law therefore changes individual
terms without repairing their net obstruction.

Law II changes terminal probabilities to the actual last queried index
and adds a specified metric mass1/16 at the penultimate query. It keeps
the independent clock-zero common column and the positive incoming
load1/64 at index0. This changes the failing moment: the full first-row
TWO-moment screen now passes, as do full PSD and all optimum signs.
However a different invariant, the last queried row tested against the
PENULTIMATE clock, is strictly less than -1/16. It forces a negative
original finite multiplier from the last query to an earlier-than-
penultimate query. Every balanced correction annihilating e and t
preserves this obstruction.

These are exclusions of TWO fully specified laws, including every
remaining balanced skew in each law. They are not an impossibility
result for the general architecture or for the full dual cone. No
formal residual vector or negative coefficient is presented as an
interpolable primal trajectory. No full-class upper bound on W, and
therefore no resolution of the original problem, has been obtained.

This is ONE joint proof draft. All new calculations are unverified;
none is adopted as a separately accepted premise. The only accepted
facts used are1252b8823bb5a290 and931b9653ce0f7201 at the scopes specified
below. The older reports and the main advisory supplied directions only.

## 2. Problem, accepted interfaces, and physical word

For a predetermined nonnegative word h of length n and smoothness L>0,
W_n(h) is the supremum of
2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L||x_0-x_star||^2) over every finite Euclidean
dimension, convex differentiable L-smooth f with an attained minimizer,
and x_0!=x_star, under x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Thus W=2R.
The original question is whether W_n_star/U_n^ZJ tends to1, where
W_n_star=inf_(h>=0)W_n(h), U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, and the original all-split
benchmark has

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt(x^2+6xy+y^2))/2,
    G(x,y)=2x+y/2+sqrt(y^2+8xy)/2,
    C_n=max_(0<=j<n)Omega(C_j,C_(n-j-1)),
    B_n=max_(0<=j<n)G(C_j,B_(n-j-1)).

Accepted1252b8823bb5a290 supplies the signed residual orientation and
full terminal-square certificate interpretation. Only incoming edges
at the ACTUAL unqueried terminal may be deleted; no queried-prefix
coordinate or constraint is removed. Accepted931b9653ce0f7201 supplies
the word below, its mass formula, and B_n/D<47/50. Only CONDITIONAL on
the still-missing full-class W_n(H_m)<=17/(16D) for every m>=1536 does
it imply the799/800 separation. That missing hypothesis is not proved.

Fix arbitrary integer m>=1536 and keep its parameters in EVERY child:

    eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps, c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+eps), a=beta/c,
    b=1+a, H_0=(), H_(j+1)=(H_j,1+a*c^j,H_j), j<m,
    h=H_m, n=2^m-1, l=n-1, r=l-1,
    S=sum_(i<n)h_i, D=1+2S, p=1/(1+S), qtar=17/(16D).

The indices l,r are the last and penultimate QUERIED samples, different
from the actual terminal n. We use the following short local scalar
aliases throughout this report. Their public glossary names carry85:
p=p85, s=s85, qtar=q85, T=T85, U=U85, J=J85, P=P85, H=H85,
X=X85, r=r85. These explicitly scoped aliases do not change any
existing project-glossary definition. The matrix for the chronological
coordinate change is Ltri, distinct from scalar T; a superscript T
means transpose. In Section3 only, Len is an integer suffix length.

The physical last three steps are (b,1+beta,b). Put hgap=1+beta=2-eps.
Elementary bounds from m>=1536 are

    12/5<c<5/2, 7/8<beta<1, 1/3<a<1/2, 4/3<b<3/2.

The accepted mass formula, also obtained by substitution in
1+S_(j+1)=2(1+S_j)+a*c^j, is

    1+S_j=(1-vword)2^j+vword*c^j,
    vword=beta/[c(c-2)] in(0,1).

Consequently

    2^m<1+S<c^m, c^(-m)<p<2^(-m)<2^(-20).             (2.1)

Let e be the all-ones column on the n queries and e_i its coordinate
columns. Define clocks

    t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j, T=t_l=1/p-b,
    Delta=T-1=1/p-b-1, t_r=T-hgap.

They are strictly increasing, t_0=1 and t_1=1+b. In particular

    3/(4p)<Delta<1/p, Delta-b>1/(2p),
    0<hgap/Delta<4p<1/128.                            (2.2)

## 3. Tail quantities and the bounds actually needed

Write sbit(L) for the binary digit sum. For0<=L<=n put

    rtail_L=product_(j=n-L)^(n-1)(h_j-1)
           =beta^L*c^(-sbit(L)),
    s=rtail_n=beta^n/c^m,
    k_i=h_i product_(i<j<n)(1-h_j),
    u_i=|k_i|, U=sum_i u_i, rho_i=u_i/U.

The suffix formula follows because h_(n-j)-1=a*c^v2(j), and
sum_(j=1)^L v2(j)=L-sbit(L). With L=l-i one has

    u_i=rtail_L+rtail_(L+1), k_i=(-1)^i u_i,
    u_0=(b/a)s, u_l=b, u_r=a(1+beta), u_(l-2)=ba beta,
    U>7/3.                                          (3.1)

For the last inequality the last three terms exceed4/3,5/8,7/18,
whose sum169/72 exceeds7/3. Every rho_i is strictly positive.
The following source bound is especially useful:

    0<s<u_0<p^2/64, rho_0<1/10, s<p.                (3.2)

For a symbolic proof,2^m-1>16m^2 for m>=16 by induction, starting at16.
Also beta^(-4m)>(1+1/(4m))^(4m)>=2, so beta^(4m)<1/2.
Thus beta^n<2^(-4m), while b/a<4 and p>c^(-m) yield
u_0/p^2<4 beta^n c^m<4(5/32)^m<1/64. The other inequalities follow.
No arithmetic, recurrence, or trajectory was evaluated by a program.

Telescoping the terminal update gives

    e^T k=1+s, Ltri^T k=h, t^T k=S,                  (3.3)

where Ltri_ii=1, Ltri_ij=h_j for j<i, and zero otherwise.
For Law I let tbar=sum rho_i t_i and set

    alpha=(1-p)rho, V=t^T(k-alpha)=(1-p)(1/p-tbar).

The necessary uniform bounds are

    32<V<512m^3, p V^2<1/1024.                       (3.4)

Here is the full derivation, to avoid importing the previous unverified
report. The binary product and its digit-weighted sum give

    Ztail=sum_(L=0)^n rtail_L
         =product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1+beta^(2^j)/c),
    U=2Ztail-1-s,
    Mtail/Ztail=sum_(j=0)^(m-1)
                    2^j beta^(2^j)/(c+beta^(2^j)),
    Mtail=sum_(L=0)^n L rtail_L.

Choose j with m/2<2^j<=m. Bernoulli's inequality gives beta^(2^j)>=3/4,
and c+beta^(2^j)<7/2; hence Mtail/Ztail>3m/28. Also ns<1. Therefore

    sum_i rho_i(l-i)>(Mtail/Ztail-1)/2>3m/56-1/2.

The suffix after query i has mass at least b+(l-i). As1-p>1/2,
the formula for V makes V>32 for m>=1536.
For the upper bound, Len=L+1 final steps lie in H_d where d is the least
integer with2^d>Len. Thus their mass is smaller than c^d<(2^d)^2<=4Len^2.
Since u_i<2 beta^L and U>2,

    V<4 sum_(L>=0)(L+1)^2 beta^L
      =4(1+beta)/(1-beta)^3<512m^3.

The series identity follows by multiplying by(1-beta)^3.
Finally2^m>2^30 m^6 for m>=128: the base compares2^128 with2^72,
and the induction step follows from
(1+1/m)^6<=sum_(j>=0)(6/m)^j<=64/61<2.
Using p<2^(-m) gives pV^2<2^(-12)<1/1024.

Law II instead chooses alpha=(1-p)e_l. It has

    V=b(1-p), alpha_0=0, v_0=u_0, v_l=a+p,
    0<V<3/2, pV^2<1/1024.                            (3.5)

In BOTH laws alpha_star=p, v=k-alpha, E=p+s, F=p-s>0,
eta=F/E, e^T v=E, and

    R=Ltri^T v,
    R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<=i)alpha_j)-alpha_i>0.            (3.6)

Indeed R_i=h_i(p+sum_(j<i)alpha_j)+(h_i-1)alpha_i.
Moreover0<v_0<u_0 in Law I, v_0=u_0 in Law II, and R_0<2p in both.
For Law I use alpha_0=((1-p)/U)u_0, with (1-p)/U<3/7.

## 4. FULL original-space identity with an independent common column

Normalize L=1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Keep x_0,g_0,...,g_n
arbitrary and independent, substituting ONLY the actual GD recursion.
The accepted residual is

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2.

For i<n set y_i=x_i-g_i and delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2. Then

    y=e*x_0-Ltri*g,
    g=Ltri^(-1)(e*x_0-y),
    x_n=-s*x_0+k^T y.                                (4.1)

Ltri is invertible with diagonal1. More explicitly, with
pi_i=product_(j<i)(1-h_j),

    g_i=pi_i*x_0-y_i
             +sum_(j<i)h_j product_(j<j'<i)(1-h_j')y_j.

Thus this change spans ALL original queried-gradient directions.
The actual terminal gradient remains independently free.

Choose any z with e^T z=E, positive weights w_i, and zero-sum zeta.
Let Ww=sum_i w_i and define

    K=diag(w)-ww^T/Ww,
    P=K+vv^T+eta zz^T,
    d=zeta+F(v-z),
    A^T=-A, Ae=d, N=Ltri^T(P+A).                     (4.2)

The complete signed multiplier array is

    lambda_(n,star)=2p, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(j,n)=0 for j in {star,0,...,l},
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for distinct i,j<n,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i.           (4.3)

Diagonal multipliers vanish. In scalar entries,

    N_ij=K_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(r'>i)(K_(r',j)+A_(r',j))
                          +R_i v_j+eta Zout_i z_j,
    Zout=Ltri^T z.                                  (4.4)

The formula defines every original ordered pair; none is hidden behind
an existence assertion. The finite prefix outgoing total at i is N_ii,
its incoming total is N_ii-2alpha_i, and the actual terminal adds incoming
2alpha_i. Hence finite-node divergence is zero, terminal divergence2,
and optimum divergence-2. All sampled values cancel in

    M(q)=q||x_0||^2-2f_n+sum_(i!=j)lambda_ij Q_ij.

For prefix nodes including star,
Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>; the remaining prefix quadratic is
-g^T N y. Using(4.1) it is
-<x_0,(Pe-d)^T y>+y^T P y. The terminal expansion, with -2f_n
included, is
||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2-||-s*x_0+v^T y||^2-2sum alpha_i delta_i.
Those delta terms cancel the prefix value terms. Now

    Pe=Ev+Fz,
    2s v-Pe+d=-2Fz+zeta,
    eta E^2=p^2-s^2.

Substitution proves the COMPLETE identity

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2+y^T K y
         +eta||z^T y-E*x_0||^2
         +(q-p^2)||x_0||^2+<x_0,zeta^T y>.           (4.5)

Let ybar_w=sum w_i y_i/Ww. As e^T zeta=0, completion gives

    M(q)=||g_n+s*x_0-v^T y||^2
       +sum_i w_i||y_i-ybar_w+(zeta_i/(2w_i))*x_0||^2
       +eta||z^T y-E*x_0||^2
       +(q-p^2-J)||x_0||^2,
    J=(1/4)sum_i zeta_i^2/w_i.                      (4.6)

This pays the initial charge ONCE. It retains every detail, the common
square and its derivative, and the actual terminal square.
Full PSD is equivalent to q>=p^2+J. For necessity take scalar x_0=1,
y_i=c0-zeta_i/(2w_i), where
c0=1+[sum_i z_i zeta_i/(2w_i)]/E, and g_n=-s+v^T y.
Every displayed square vanishes. Reconstruct the queried gradients by
(4.1). This is a formal-space test, not a primal interpolation claim.
In particular g_n need NOT equal p when z and v differ.

For the actual common queried-gradient direction g_i=G, y_i=x_0-t_i G.
Put V=t^T v, Z=t^T z, theta=t^T zeta, X=t^T Kt. The full prefix remainder
is exactly

    (q-p^2)||x_0||^2-theta<x_0,G>
                      +(X+eta Z^2)||G||^2.          (4.7)

The real common derivative theta has not been discarded.

## 5. General optimum moments, complete first-row moments, literal skew

From Pe+d=2p v+zeta, the outgoing optimum vector is

    mu=2pR+Ltri^T zeta.                              (5.1)

The incoming vector is

    nu=Kt+Vv+eta Zz-At-2alpha.                       (5.2)

Since e^T A=-d^T and t^T At=0, its EXACT moments are

    M0=e^T nu=2pV+theta-2(1-p),
    M1=t^T nu=X+V^2+eta Z^2-2alpha^T t.              (5.3)

A nonnegative nu necessarily has M0>=0 and M0<=M1<=T M0.
Conversely the isolated two-moment problem has the nonnegative endpoint
solution

    nu_target=((T M0-M1)/Delta)e_0
                          +((M1-M0)/Delta)e_l.      (5.4)

This is not sufficient for the finite multiplier signs.
For ANY specified compatible nu_target let

    rvec=Kt+Vv+eta Zz-2alpha-nu_target,
    tmean=(e^T t)/n, cvec=t-tmean*e, Ve=cvec^T cvec>0,
    A0=(d e^T-e d^T)/n,
    fvec=rvec-tmean*d+(d^T t)e/n,
    A=A0+(fvec cvec^T-cvec fvec^T)/Ve.               (5.5)

The two moment identities imply e^T rvec=-d^T t and t^T rvec=0.
Thus e^T fvec=0 and cvec^T fvec=0. Multiplication shows Ae=d and
At=rvec, with both terms skew. This is a literal entrywise completion.
Every other completion is A+C with C^T=-C and Ce=Ct=0.
Such C leaves the polynomial, mu,nu and all moment tests below unchanged.

For the first row define

    S0=sum_(j>0)N_0j,
    P0=sum_(j>0)(t_j-1)N_0j,
    G0=P0-Delta*S0=sum_(j>0)(t_j-T)N_0j.

The first row of Ltri^T is b e^T-a e_0^T. Write

    Lcol=Pe-d=2s v+2F z-zeta.

Then N_0j=b Lcol_j-a(P_0j+A_0j), and N_00=b Lcol_0-aP_00.
As mu_0=2pR_0-a zeta_0, the complete general first-row sum is

    S0=aP_00+zeta_0+2pR_0-2bs v_0-2bF z_0.          (5.6)

Using(P+A)t=2Pt-2alpha-nu yields the complete clock identity

    P0=b(2sV+2FZ-theta)-2a(Pt)_0
                                  +2a alpha_0+a nu_0-mu_0,
    (Pt)_0=(Kt)_0+Vv_0+eta Zz_0.                    (5.7)

These formulas explicitly include BOTH optimum directions.
If all finite lambda_(0,j)>=0, equivalently N_0j<=0, then necessarily

    S0<=0, Delta*S0<=P0<=b*S0.                      (5.8)

Indeed b<=t_j-1<=Delta for all j>0. When S0=0 all off-diagonals must
vanish. These are exact invariant screens, not sufficient row signs.

There is another invariant at the actual last query l. Its row in
Ltri^T is e_l^T, so N_ll=P_ll, (Nt)_l=2(Pt)_l-2alpha_l-nu_l.
Testing its earlier entries against t_r, the penultimate clock, gives

    Hlast=sum_(j<l)(t_j-t_r)N_lj
         =2(Pt)_l-2alpha_l-nu_l-t_r mu_l-hgap*P_ll.  (5.9)

Nonpositive N_lj require Hlast>=0, since t_j<=t_r for j<l.
A negative Hlast forces N_lj>0 at some j<r, not merely at r.

## 6. The shared explicit common column, incoming load, and paid imbalance

Both laws fix the genuinely independent common column

    z=E(T e_0-e_l)/Delta, e^T z=E, t^T z=0.          (6.1)

It differs from v: for example every odd interior v_i is negative and
nonzero, whereas z_i=0 there. The independence is not a scalar rescaling.
Set the NONZERO incoming load

    ellload=1/64, nu_target=ellload*e_0.              (6.2)

For each law's own alpha,V define

    theta0=2(1-p)-2pV=2p alpha^T t,
    theta=theta0+ellload,
    Xreq=theta0/p-V^2+ellload.                       (6.3)

Select positive base weights what_i as specified for that law and put

    tbase=sum what_i t_i/sum what,
    Vbase=sum what_i(t_i-tbase)^2,
    scale=Xreq/Vbase, w_i=scale*what_i,
    K=diag(w)-ww^T/sum w,
    zeta=(theta/Xreq)Kt.                             (6.4)

This fixes every scale from the actual word before row-sign work.
It gives t^T Kt=Xreq, e^T zeta=0 and t^T zeta=theta. Moreover

    J=theta^2/(4Xreq).                              (6.5)

Indeed(Kt)_i=w_i(t_i-tbar_w), whose squared inverse-weight sum is
Xreq. Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz shows the same law minimizes this charge
at fixed theta for its metric. By(5.3), M0=M1=ellload. Thus(6.2) is
exactly compatible. Define d by(4.2), A by(5.5), then EVERY scalar
multiplier by(4.3)--(4.4). The literal law sets C=0; our obstructions
will cover every extra skew C annihilating e and t.

### 6.1 Positive metric, full PSD, all optimum signs

For both laws1<theta0<2. In Law I use V>32 and pV^2<1/1024 to get
pV<1/32768 and then theta0>1. In Law II use V<3/2 and(2.1).
Consequently

    Xreq>(1023/1024)*theta0/p>0,
    Xreq<2/p+ellload, 1<theta<3, theta/Xreq>p.        (6.6)

The last follows because theta-pXreq=ellload(1-p)+pV^2>0.
Every base weight is positive because p^2 rho_i>0, and the two unit
endpoint masses make Vbase>0. Hence all metric weights are positive.
The full charge satisfies

    J < [theta0*p/4]*(1+ellload/theta0)^2*(1024/1023)
      < (4225/8184)p,
    p^2+J <(17/32)p<qtar.                            (6.7)

For the second line use p<1/128 and
4225/8184<67/128, equivalent to540800<548328.
Thus full PSD holds strictly below the requested target for BOTH laws.
No interpolation signs are inferred from PSD alone.

The terminal multipliers are nonnegative, and nu is exactly ellload at
index0 and zero elsewhere. All outgoing mu_i are STRICTLY positive.
To prove this, zeta_i has the sign of t_i-tbar_w, crossing only once
from negative to positive, and has zero sum. Every proper suffix sum
is positive: if i is before the crossing, use the negative preceding
prefix and zero total; if i is after it, every remaining term is
positive. If zeta_i<0 then sum_(j>i)zeta_j>=-zeta_i, whence

    (Ltri^T zeta)_i=zeta_i+h_i sum_(j>i)zeta_j
                                     >=(h_i-1)(-zeta_i)>0.

If zeta_i>=0 the same expression is positive, including i=l because
zeta_l>0. Equation(5.1) proves all mu_i>0.

## 7. Exact endpoint-clock reduction and incoming-load cancellation

For (6.1) put Y=-(Kt)_0=w_0(tbar_w-1)>0. Then zeta_0=-theta Y/Xreq.
Write

    K_00=Xreq/Delta^2+eK, Y=Xreq/Delta+eY.

Substituting(5.6)--(5.7), z_0=ET/Delta and Z=0 gives

    G0=Gendpoint+Epert,
    Epert=a(2eY-Delta eK)+theta(Delta-a)eY/Xreq,
    Gendpoint=(a/Delta)[Xreq-T theta-(p^2-s^2)T^2]
       +a nu_0+2bs(V-ET)
       +v_0[2apT+2bsDelta-2aV]-aDelta v_0^2+2a alpha_0. (7.1)

This follows by expanding the metric part as
 a(2Y-Delta K_00)+(a-Delta)zeta_0-btheta,
and using R_0=bE-a v_0 in the remaining terms.
For the endpoint reduction with zeta=(theta/Xreq)Kt and ANY
compatible endpoint load, not just(6.2), write its total M0
and moment M1, so theta=theta0+M0 and
Xreq=theta0/p-V^2+M1. Endpoint support means
M1-T M0=-Delta nu_0. Consequently

    Xreq-T theta=btheta0-V^2-Delta nu_0,
    (a/Delta)(Xreq-Ttheta)+a nu_0
                                  =(a/Delta)(btheta0-V^2). (7.2)

Thus EVERY endpoint incoming load cancels out of Gendpoint exactly.
For our fixed nonzero load, therefore,

    Gendpoint=(a/Delta)[btheta0-V^2-(p^2-s^2)T^2]
       +2bs(V-ET)
       +v_0[2apT+2bsDelta-2aV]-aDelta v_0^2+2a alpha_0. (7.3)

A positive load is not intrinsically useless: it changes other rows,
the charge, and the metric perturbation. Equation(7.2) states only this
precise endpoint cancellation and does not exclude distributed metrics.

## 8. Law I: tail terminal probabilities, source/last metric, positive load

Fix alpha=(1-p)rho and the complete choices(6.1)--(6.4) with

    omega=p^2, what=e_0+e_l+omega*rho.               (8.1)

Equations(4.3)--(4.4),(5.5) specify ALL multipliers. Full PSD and every
optimum sign already follow jointly from Section6.
For exact metric estimates put xclock_i=(t_i-1)/Delta in[0,1],
rbar=sum rho_i xclock_i, and define

## 5. Exact hexagonal image at every radius and every original step

is k(R-3/2)/2<=0; the core term is at most k. The first bound follows
directly from (5.1)--(5.2): the mixed outer branch is an average of R and
k-1/2, and the short middle branch is at most R. The largest k in H_j
is a c^(j-1), proving the second line of (7.4).

Composing the second max in (7.5) by distributivity gives the upper bound
max{R-S_j/2, max_i[3(h_i-1)/2-(mass strictly after i)/2]}.
An occurrence of a level-l bridge is followed by its complete H_l right
child, so its latter expression is at most (3a c^l-S_l)/2. Equality in
this purely affine-max comparison is possible at the last occurrence of
that level, whose suffix is exactly H_l. There is no reset of parameters.
Define T_l=(3a c^l-S_l)/2. Formula (7.1) gives

  T_l=[1+(3a-eta)c^l-(1-eta)2^l]/2.

These T_l strictly increase. Indeed 3a-eta=a[3-1/(c-2)]>a/2>1/5,
and hence (3a-eta)(c-1)>7/25>1-eta by (7.2). Also c^l>=2^l.
Subtracting adjacent displayed formulas proves T_(l+1)>T_l. The maximum
is consequently T_(j-1)=C_hex,j, proving the final explicit upper bound.
It includes every branch, but C_hex,j grows; it is not a sharp convergence
theorem and is not substituted for the desired bound.

## 8. Exact complete-word failure of the scalar relaxation

For every j>=1 choose the scalar initial radius R_0=S_j+1. At every actual
position, let A_i be the original mass already executed. Then

  R_i=S_j+1-A_i/2,
  M_(h_i)(R_i)=R_i-h_i/2,
  E_j(S_j+1)=S_j/2+1.                             (8.1)

This is a symbolic proof for every j, not an executed recurrence. Here is
why EVERY branch choice is valid. Let Hmax=1+a c^(j-1). From (7.1),

  S_j> [c/(c-2)](Hmax-1)-1 >5Hmax-6>4Hmax-5.

Thus R_i>=S_j/2+1>2Hmax-3/2>=2h_i-3/2. Also R_i>3/2 since S_j>1.
In the outer formulas (5.1)--(5.2), R-h/2 dominates the mixed branch
exactly when R>=2h-3/2. It also dominates k there, since h>1. This proves
the induction in (8.1), including the real last leaf.

Combining the separately sharp conversions (6.1)--(6.2) with this exact
scalar path gives the certificate value

  [2E_j(R_0)-1]/R_0^2=1/(S_j+1).                  (8.2)

Its ratio to the baseline1/(1+2S_j) is
(1+2S_j)/(1+S_j)=2-1/(1+S_j). It exceeds17/16 because S_j>1>1/15.
For j=m it tends to2 as m tends to infinity, since S_m>=2^m-1.
This is a precise, unavoidable loss for the relaxation that keeps only the
scalar radius, uses these exact one-step images, and applies the sharp
separate initial-norm and terminal-objective conversions. Any weaker
one-step bounds or weaker separate conversions cannot repair that loss.
It does NOT exclude a bound retaining an objective or directional state.

The incompatibility is concrete. Start the ACTUAL fixed F at
x_0=-(S_j+1)v_1. Every point is on the same physical edge-normal ray with
z_i=S_j+1-A_i/2>1/2 and y_i=0. Its actual gauge is exactly R_i, so ONE
legal trajectory attains all the scalar image radii in (8.1). But its
actual terminal value is S_j/2+3/4, not S_j+1. Its terminal point is on
an edge axis, whereas the maximizer of (6.2) is on a vertex axis. The
initial Euclidean bound is already exact on this edge ray. No orientation
switch can be inserted at the terminal of this static trajectory.

Alternatively, the actual start +(S_j+1)v_1 stays in the same vertex
through the terminal and finishes at v_1 with Psi=1. Neither of these
legal starts realizes (8.2) as its normalized objective. No full-word
triangle counterexample is claimed.

## 9. Actual fixed-face criteria, and why large radius is insufficient

For a particular vertex, order the other coordinates so its upper gap is
u_0 and the remaining gap is v_0>=0. The condition

  u_0>=S_m+1                                      (9.1)

is necessary and sufficient for that SAME vertex chart to hold at all
queries AND the terminal. Under this condition the gap at any prefix is
u_0-A_i>=1 and the other gap is unchanged. Conversely, if the chart holds
through the terminal, its affine update gives u_n=u_0-S_m>=1.

For a fixed physical edge, write x=z n_E+y t_E. The condition

  z_0>=1/2+S_m/2, |y_0|<=sqrt(3)/2                 (9.2)

is necessary and sufficient for that edge chart to be valid throughout,
including terminal. Necessity uses z_n=z_0-S_m/2>=1/2 and initial edge
membership. Sufficiency follows from z_i=z_0-A_i/2 and
|y_i|=P_i|y_0|<=|y_0| using (7.3). Boundary choices are harmless.

Both fixed-face classes have normalized payoff at most1/D_m. Indeed
D_m P_block,m^2<1 because (7.1) gives D_m<2c^m and P_block,m=beta^n c^(-m).
In a vertex chart the difference between ||x_0||^2 and D_m Psi(x_n)
is (s_0-D_m)^2+t_0^2. In an edge chart it is
(z_0-D_m/2)^2+(1-D_m P_block,m^2)y_0^2. The equalities at x_0=D_m v_1 and
x_0=-(D_m/2)v_1 are legal by (9.1)--(9.2). Thus the classes actually
attain1/D_m. This is not extended to the face-changing domain.

There is no scalar large-radius criterion for fixed faces. Choose
0<delta<a, u_0=1+delta and v_0=T with T arbitrarily large. This is a
strict vertex query. The first actual leaf1+a gives ordered gaps
U=a-delta in (0,1), V=T-a+delta. For T large enough U+2V>1, so the next
query is strictly on an edge. Meanwhile ||x_0||^2=u_0^2+u_0 T+T^2 tends
to infinity. This family rules out assuming that all large starts have
one face. Criteria (9.1)--(9.2), not radius alone, identify the histories
to which the fixed-face sharpening applies.

    C_0=B_0=1,
    Omega(x,y)=(x+y+sqrt(x^2+6xy+y^2))/2,

## 3. Tail probabilities and the exact mixed terminal clock

    |Gendpoint-a*dclock*(2a-3)|<20p^2.              (6.5)

### 6.2 Last-row clock, including the nonzero incoming-load cost

The last row of Ltri^T is e_l^T, so

    N_ll=P_ll,
    (Nt)_l=2(Pt)_l-2alpha_l-nu_l.

For the last row define

    Slast=sum_(j<l)N_lj=mu_l-P_ll,
    Jlast=sum_(j<l)(t_j-1)N_lj=(Nt)_l-mu_l-Delta*P_ll,
    Hlast=sum_(j<l)(t_j-t_r)N_lj
                  =(Nt)_l-t_r*mu_l-hgap*P_ll.

    Alast=what_l(1-M/B)/H,
    Blast=what_l(1-what_l/B)/H.

Then (Kt)_l=(Xreq/Delta)Alast, K_ll=(Xreq/Delta^2)Blast,
zeta_l=(theta/Delta)Alast. Both ratios are positive and <3.
For the auxiliary base without omega*rho,

    Alast=(1-xiM+xiM*rclock)/Dclock>=1-xiM.

Restoring omega*rho changes this ratio by at most32omega: its numerator

Using V=2, alpha_l=b-v_l, nu_l=0 and z_l=-E/Delta gives the EXACT

    Hlast=Cclock*Alast-hgap*(Xreq/Delta^2)*Blast
       +4v_l+2p(b+hgap)v_l-hgap*v_l^2-2b-hgap*eta*z_l^2,

 Cclock=2Xreq/Delta-theta+theta*(hgap-1)/Delta.

    2-ellload-20p<Cclock<3,

eta*z_l^2=(p^2-s^2)/Delta^2<4p^4.

## 7. Decisive column failure of the prescribed law

The incoming optimum equation in (4.3) is a COLUMN equation:

    sum_i N_il=nu_l+2alpha_l=2alpha_l.

If each off-diagonal N_il were nonpositive, it would imply
N_ll>=2alpha_l. But N_ll=P_ll for every skew A, not just (5.4).
The metric scale is small:

    scale<=2Xreq/Delta^2<8p,
    K_ll<=w_l=scale*(1+omega*rho_l)<12p.

Together with (3.3) and eta*z_l^2<4p^4, this gives

    P_ll=K_ll+v_l^2+eta*z_l^2<12p+1/4+4p^4<1/3,
    P_ll-2alpha_l<1/3-19/10=-47/30<-3/2.            (7.1)

Thus the putative nonnegative incoming transport masses have negative
total:

    sum_(0<=i<n, i!=l)lambda_(i,l)
      =sum_(0<=i<n, i!=l)(-N_il)=P_ll-2alpha_l<-3/2.

At least one original finite edge INTO the last queried node has a
negative multiplier. This conclusion is invariant under all Ce=Ct=0
corrections and, more generally, under any skew with the same incoming
column sum. The complete prescribed law fails for every m>=1536.
This is not a primal counterexample, an infeasibility proof for all
possible coefficient architectures, or a conclusion about W itself.

## 8. Second mechanism: transport with diagonal exclusion and the full factor

This section treats an entire family, rather than adding another metric
atom. First give the exact finite transport interface for any fixed
P,mu,nu,alpha in the architecture above. Write

    D_i=N_ii, a_ij=-N_ij for i!=j, a_ii=0,
    r_i=D_i-mu_i,
    c_i=D_i-nu_i-2alpha_i,
    b_i^clock=t_i D_i-(Nt)_i.                       (8.1)

Here a_ij denotes transport mass and is unrelated to the physical scalar
a. If the original finite multipliers are nonnegative, then a_ij>=0 and

    sum_j a_ij=r_i, sum_i a_ij=c_j,
    sum_j t_j a_ij=b_i^clock.                       (8.2)

Thus every r_i,c_j is nonnegative, sum r=sum c, and
sum_i b_i^clock=sum_j t_j c_j. A zero r_i forces b_i^clock=0.
For positive r_i the mean b_i^clock/r_i lies in the interval spanned
by {t_j:j!=i}; retaining the exclusion is essential at either endpoint.
With Kmass=sum r=sum c, the forbidden diagonal further implies

    r_i+c_i<=Kmass.                                 (8.3)

Indeed all mass from row i must land outside column i, whose total
capacity is Kmass-c_i. This is a true cut inequality.

There are elementary clock cuts as well. For any real tau,

    sum_i max(0,b_i^clock-tau*r_i)
                              <=sum_j c_j max(0,t_j-tau).       (8.4)

For each row, max(0,sum_j a_ij(t_j-tau))<=sum_j a_ij max(0,t_j-tau);
summing proves (8.4). More generally for any convex function phi on[1,T],
finite convexity gives

    sum_(i:r_i>0) r_i phi(b_i^clock/r_i)
                                      <=sum_j c_j phi(t_j).    (8.5)

This is merely the finite convex-combination inequality, provable by
induction on the number of nonzero row entries, and imports no transport
existence theorem. It is necessary, not sufficient for the original law.
The following more general elementary cut keeps the missing diagonal
visible: if real Ucut_i,Vcut_i,Zcut_j obey
Ucut_i+Vcut_i*t_j+Zcut_j>=0 for EVERY i!=j, then

    sum_i Ucut_i*r_i+sum_i Vcut_i*b_i^clock+sum_j Zcut_j*c_j>=0. (8.6)

Multiply each allowed coefficient by a_ij>=0 and sum. No condition on
Ucut_i+Vcut_i*t_i+Zcut_i is imposed, because that edge is forbidden.

Crucially, the chronological symmetric-factor constraint remains

    Ltri^(-T)N+N^T Ltri^(-1)=2P.                    (8.7)

A transport coupling satisfying row/column masses and clock conditions
alone may violate (8.7). This equality cannot be replaced by PSD of P.
For precision, given D and an array a with zero diagonal, nonnegative
off-diagonals, and the row and column sums in (8.2), define
N=diag(D)-a. If (8.7) holds, then A=Ltri^(-T)N-P is skew.
For the fixed architecture mu=2pR+Ltri^T zeta, one has
Ae=Ltri^(-T)mu-Pe=d. Moreover
(P-A)t=N^T e=nu+2alpha, so At=Pt-2alpha-nu.
Thus this system recovers exactly the required skew and all original
coefficients; the clock equations follow with

    Nt=Ltri^T(2Pt-2alpha-nu).

This is an equivalence of constraint descriptions, NOT an asserted
feasible unknown matrix or a new certificate law. We use it only to
prove the explicit family exclusion below.

### 8.1 Last-column cut and a metric concentration inequality

The last row of Ltri^(-T) is e_l^T. The (l,l) entry of (8.7) therefore
pins D_l=P_ll. The nonnegative column mass c_l gives

    K_ll+eta*z_l^2 >= 2alpha_l+nu_l-(b-alpha_l)^2.   (8.8)

This combines the transport column cut with an exact original-space
factor constraint. Allowing D_l to float freely would lose it.

For ANY strictly positive metric weights w, set X=t^T Kt and

    Qgap=sum_(i<l) w_i (T-t_i)^2 / sum_(i<l)w_i.

The weighted variance identity is

    X=(1/Ww)sum_(i<j)w_i w_j(t_i-t_j)^2.

Retaining only pairs involving l and using
K_ll=w_l(Ww-w_l)/Ww gives the exact necessary estimate

    X>=K_ll*Qgap, so K_ll<=X/Qgap.                  (8.9)

Every denominator is positive since w_i>0 and the clocks are distinct.
For d0>0 define the NONLAST far-clock fraction

    Ffar(d0)=sum_(i<l:T-t_i>=d0)w_i / sum_(i<l)w_i.

Then Qgap>=d0^2*Ffar(d0). If
 Bneed:=2alpha_l+nu_l-(b-alpha_l)^2-eta*z_l^2>0,
(8.8)-(8.9) imply the quantitative concentration requirement

    Ffar(d0)<=X/[d0^2*Bneed].                       (8.10)

This is a global statement about ALL nonlast metric weights; it does
not assume any sparse support or any special skew completion.

### 8.2 A full family excluded, including arbitrary sparse metric atoms

Fix any same-enclosing-m word as in Section2. Consider ALL choices with

 (i) alpha_i>=0, sum alpha_i=1-p, alpha_l>=1/2;
 (ii) v=k-alpha, z=E(T e_0-e_l)/Delta, eta=F/E;
 (iii) arbitrary positive w with X=t^T Kt<=3/p;
 (iv) Ffar(Delta/2)>=256p;
 (v) any skew A and any nonnegative incoming optimum vector nu
     satisfying the original equations (4.2)-(4.3).

There is no restriction to the literal skew (5.4), to nu=ellload e_0,
or to the paid minimum-energy zeta. If the divergence and PSD happen
to pass, they still cannot repair the following finite signs.

For alpha_l in[1/2,1-p], the function
2alpha_l-(b-alpha_l)^2 is strictly increasing, because its derivative
is2+2b-2alpha_l>0. Using b<17/12 gives

    2alpha_l-(b-alpha_l)^2
                >=1-(b-1/2)^2>23/144.              (8.11)

Also eta*z_l^2=(p^2-s^2)/Delta^2<4p^4<1/144.
On the other hand, (8.9) and condition(iv) yield

    Qgap>=64p*Delta^2,
    K_ll <=(3/p)/(64p*Delta^2)<1/12,                (8.12)

where Delta>3/(4p) was used. Therefore

    c_l=P_ll-nu_l-2alpha_l
       <1/12+1/144-23/144=-5/72<0.                 (8.13)

This contradicts a nonnegative column mass. Every member of the entire
precisely specified family has some negative original multiplier into
l. No existence theorem, unknown optimizer, asymptotic coefficient law,
or numerical evaluation enters this exclusion.

As a concrete sparse-metric subfamily, take ANY finite subset
Jsubset of {1,...,l-1}, arbitrary coefficients Mlast>0 and b_j>=0,
and omega0>0, with

    what=e_0+Mlast*e_l+sum_(j in Jsubset)b_j e_j+omega0*rho,
    1+sum_j b_j+omega0 <= 1/(256p).

Scale what by ANY positive scalar for which t^T Kt<=3/p. The positive
regularizer retains every coordinate. The initial atom is far from T,
and its fraction of the nonlast base weight is at least
1/(1+sum_j b_j+omega0)>=256p. Hence every such metric lies in the
excluded family whenever the terminal mass is >=1/2 and the common
column is as above. The number and positions of interior atoms and the
last weight are unrestricted. The prescribed law of Section5 belongs
to this family: alpha_l>19/20, Xreq<2/p, Mlast=1, b_r=sigma<1/3,
omega0=p^2, and1+sigma+p^2<3/2<1/(256p).

Equivalently, even without the coarse256p threshold, (8.10)-(8.11)
show that a putative law in this architecture with alpha_l>=1/2 and
X<=3/p must have Ffar(Delta/2)<140p. Indeed Bneed>11/72 and
Delta>3/(4p) give4X/(Delta^2 Bneed)<(1536/11)p<140p.
This records the quantitative missing interface rather than prescribing
another unsupported atom. It does not exclude terminal laws with less
mass at l, metrics with sufficiently little far-clock mass, another
common column, or architectures outside (4.2).

## 9. Author audit, resources, and handoff

The audit retains all original queried gradients, all prefix rows, the
actual free terminal gradient, the terminal square, the independent
common square, its derivative, and the global initial charge. The
terminal and metric mixtures have separate names xiT andxiM. The
positive omega*rho weights are never dropped from the actual law;
auxiliary endpoint formulas include an explicit restoration error.
The incoming load penalty in the last-row clock is ellload(1-xiM),
which is necessary for the stated finite margin. Both endpoint screens
pass, but the column cut fails; no sufficiency is inferred from moments.
The second mechanism retains the original factor equality (8.7), and
its exclusion covers all skews in the stated family, not just one
Euclidean completion.

Fact search found no accepted result replacing the

This is the ONE capped invocation86 with TWO mechanisms. Mathematical

The full bound W_n(H_m)<=17/(16D) and original minimax target remain

## 7. Mechanism2: explicit chronological PSD details and their global price

We now enlarge the detail term itself, instead of changing another
weight within one weighted-variance metric. The identified constraint
is the first diagonal's ability to pay a column load under a small
initial charge. Both clock-bearing and clock-annihilating details are
allowed below; the former change the paid column and all load moments.
Their price is recomputed, not assumed to vanish.

On the ORIGINAL queried indices define the literal chronological vectors

    gdetail_i=e_i-e_(i+1), 0<=i<=n-2,
    ddetail_i=h_(i+1)e_i-(h_i+h_(i+1))e_(i+1)+h_i e_(i+2),
                                           0<=i<=n-3.

They obey

    e^T gdetail_i=0, t^T gdetail_i=-h_i,
    e^T ddetail_i=0, t^T ddetail_i=0.              (7.1)

For the latter clock identity substitute
(t_i,t_(i+1),t_(i+2))=(t_i,t_i+h_i,t_i+h_i+h_(i+1));
each term cancels. Thus zero sum alone does NOT imply zero clock energy.

    gamma_i=Xreq/[2(n-1)h_i^2], 0<=i<=n-2,
    tau_i=p/[1+h_i+h_(i+1)]^2, 0<=i<=n-3,
    Hclock=sum_(i=0)^(n-2) gamma_i gdetail_i gdetail_i^T,
    Hnull=sum_(i=0)^(n-3) tau_i ddetail_i ddetail_i^T,
    Qdetail=K/2+Hclock+Hnull.                      (7.2)

    t^T Hclock t=sum_i gamma_i h_i^2=Xreq/2,

### 7.2 Moment accounting for the surviving enlargement freedoms

A general sum H=sum gamma_i gdetail_i gdetail_i^T
+sum tau_i ddetail_i ddetail_i^T, with nonnegative scalar weights,

necessary bound requires nu_0+2alpha_0=O(p) at the target scale.

c<(29/12)(1001/1000)<5/2. These are uniform exact inequalities,
not computed horizon checks.

## 2. Scalar envelope, boundaries, gradient, and minimum

Let L>=0, K=[0,L]e_1 in R^2, lambda=(1,T) with T>0. Minimizing in
Y=(y,0) gives

    Phi(x,z)=phi_L(x)+z^2/2,
    phi_L(x)= min_(0<=y<=L) [y+(x-y)^2/2],
    y(x)=clip(x-1,0,L),
    g_L(x)=phi_L'(x)=x-y(x).                           (3)

Here L denotes normalized segment length, not the advertised smoothness
constant. All calculations use advertised smoothness1. Multiplying Phi
by any original smoothness constant L_orig>0 and using steps h_i/L_orig
leaves the trajectory and the normalized W=2R score unchanged.

The minimizer y(x) follows either from the derivative 1+y-x or from the
projection normal. Substitution gives the complete formula

    phi_L(x)=x^2/2,                  x<=1,
             x-1/2,                1<=x<=1+L,
             L+(x-L)^2/2,          x>=1+L.             (4)

At x=1 the adjacent values are1/2 and the adjacent derivatives are1.
At x=1+L the adjacent values areL+1/2 and the derivatives again are1.
For L=0 the two exterior formulas coincide with x^2/2 and the middle
interval is a point. Thus g_L is continuous and nondecreasing, with
successive slopes1,0,1. Integrating its slope on a partition at the two
breakpoints proves global1-Lipschitz continuity. Consequently phi_L is
convex, differentiable, and1-smooth. Its unique minimizer is0, its
minimum is0, and

    0<=phi_L(x)<=x^2/2                                (5)

because y=0 is always an available trial in (3).

The projection statement retains ALL normals: for every x, the selected
y(x) satisfies (x-1-y(x))(v-y(x))<=0 for every v in[0,L]. The vertical
component of X-lambda does not affect projection onto this horizontal
segment. Hence grad Phi=(g_L(x),z)=X-P_K(X-lambda) at every point,
including every original query, the terminal, and0. One fixed global
function is used throughout, so no separate row-feasibility oracle is
needed. The unique minimum of Phi is also0 at(0,0).

## 3. All exposed segments in all dimensions and exact orthogonality

Every nondegenerate segment allowed by the accepted representation has
the form K=[0,ell]e with ell>0 and e a unit vector. In fact0 cannot be an
interior point of a nondegenerate segment on which a linear functional is
strictly positive away from0: the two opposite directions would have
opposite heights. Thus0 is an endpoint. Write

    lambda=alpha*e+w, w perpendicular to e, alpha>0,
    X=alpha*(x*e+z), z perpendicular to e,
    L=ell/alpha, u=w/alpha.

Direct substitution into the defining minimum, with y=alpha*t, yields

    Phi(X)=alpha^2*(phi_L(x)+||z||^2/2).               (6)

The normalized coordinates obey exactly the original advertised
smoothness1 updates

    x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_L(x_i),
    z_(i+1)=(1-h_i)*z_i.                             (7)

The factor alpha^2 cancels in the normalized objective/radius quotient.
Initial orthogonality is precisely

    x_0+<u,z_0>=0.                                   (8)

This accounts for all dimensions and all orientations, as follows.

* If u=0, (8) forces x_0=0. The horizontal coordinate stays0 and any
  admissible nonzero initialization is purely perpendicular quadratic.
  In dimension1 there is no such nonzero initialization.
* If u!=0, put T=||u||. All solutions of (8) with x_0=s are
  z_0=-(s/T^2)u+v, where v is perpendicular to u. Therefore
  ||z_0||^2=s^2/T^2+||v||^2. The canonical two-dimensional realization
  is v=0: lambda=(1,T), X_0=(s,-s/T).
* If s=0, horizontal motion is identically0. Every admissible nonzero
  z_0, including one perpendicular to u in higher dimension, has the
  pure quadratic score.
* For K={0}, the function is ||X||^2/2 regardless of lambda. Every
  admissible nonzero orthogonal initialization has that same score.
  If a particular ambient dimension and lambda admit no such point,
  they simply contribute no instance.

In particular a one-dimensional nondegenerate interval with scalar
orthogonality is not an admissible nonzero start. The extra direction
and its norm payment cannot be omitted.

## 4. The full-word quadratic factor and the exact weighted score

Define

    p_j=beta^(2^j-1)*c^(-j), p_0=1,
    Q=p_m^2.

For j>=1 the SIGNED product of all quadratic factors1-h in H_j is
-p_j. Indeed the length is odd, the leaf factor is-a, and
p_(j+1)=d_j*p_j^2, which is satisfied by the displayed formula.
Every nonempty prefix of H_j has product modulus at most a<1.
To prove this, the leaf case is a; a prefix lying in the first child
uses the induction hypothesis, and one passing its bridge has modulus
at most

    p_j*d_j = c^(-1)*beta^(2^j) <=a

times a prefix modulus at most1 of the last child. Empty prefixes have
modulus1. In particular this also proves the weaker all-prefix bound1.

Let x_n(L,s) be the actual scalar output of all H_m. For s!=0 put

    q(L,s)=2*phi_L(x_n(L,s))/s^2.

Equations (6)-(7), the true minimum0, and the full product give exactly

    score = [s^2*q(L,s)+||z_0||^2*Q]/[s^2+||z_0||^2]. (9)

This is a weighted average with the TRUE squared initial radius. The
canonical two-dimensional score is

    q_T(L,s)=[T^2*q(L,s)+Q]/[T^2+1].                 (10)

Extra dimensions only add quadratic weight. Equations (8)-(10), and
the s=0 cases above, show that the unrestricted exposed-segment supremum
is exactly the supremum of q(L,s) over L>=0 and real s!=0. One direction
uses the weighted average and the fact that L=0 already supplies Q;
the other uses finite T tending to infinity for each fixed scalar
instance. This equality is only for the segment subclass.

There is also an explicit FINITE tilt rule for a potential strict
witness. If q(L,s)=q_*>b, then

    T^2=1+2*(b-Q)_+/(q_*-b)                          (11)

gives q_T>b. This follows on multiplying by T^2+1 from
T^2(q_*-b)>b-Q. Also
|q_T-q_*|=|Q-q_*|/(T^2+1). A limiting scalar score alone is not
presented as a strict admissible witness.

## 5. Complete small-start and degenerate-plateau regimes

For every L>=0 and |s|<=1, all pure quadratic candidate iterates have
absolute value at most |s| by the prefix product bound. They therefore
remain in x<=1, where (3) has g_L(x)=x. This verifies the candidate
trajectory by induction through EVERY physical step. Its terminal is

    x_n=-p_m*s, q(L,s)=Q for 0<|s|<=1.               (12)

For L=0 this identity holds for every real s!=0. The zero scalar start
is handled by Section3 and does not require dividing by s.

Equation (1) also gives

    D*Q <2*c^(-m)<1/4, and p_m<1/(2*sqrt(D)),         (13)

because beta<1, c>2 and m>=1536>=3. Thus these complete regimes are
strictly below1/D, and (9) preserves this assertion in all dimensions.

## 6. Every no-crossing or one-crossing trajectory, all L and amplitudes

Here a strict crossing means consecutive nonzero iterates with opposite
signs; a zero hit remains0 thereafter. The argument is supplied jointly
and actually applies to any one-dimensional convex1-smooth function
with unique minimizing point0 and minimum value0. We apply it only to
the present family.

On either fixed ray let t be the radius and G(t) the positive gradient
magnitude. For a ray sign sigma in{-1,1}, write f_sigma(t)=f(sigma*t)
and G(t)=sigma*f'(sigma*t). Then G is nondecreasing,1-Lipschitz,
G(0)=0 and G(t)<=t.
If q=G(t), one has G(v)<=min(v,q) for0<=v<=t, whence

    2*f_sigma(t)<=2*t*q-q^2.                        (14)

For a segment of actual updates staying on that ray, with total physical
mass T, initial radius R and final radius t, radii decrease. All queried
gradient magnitudes are at least q=G(t), so R>=t+T*q. The identity

    (t+T*q)^2-(1+2T)*(2*t*q-q^2)
                         =(t-(T+1)*q)^2>=0

proves

    2*f(terminal)<=R^2/(1+2T).                     (15)

This includes intervals wholly in the outer quadratic region, intervals
that traverse either boundary, and arbitrary L. It is not a substitution
of a clipped-gradient formula for g_L.

Suppose there is exactly one strict crossing, at physical step h=1+d_k.
Let P,T be the COMPLETE masses before and after that step. If its query
has radius y and gradient magnitude v, the no-crossing prefix gives
|s|>=y+P*v>=(1+P)*v. Its crossing landing has radius
z=h*v-y<=d_k*v. Applying (15) to its actual no-crossing suffix yields

    q(L,s)<= d_k^2/[(1+P)^2*(1+2T)].                (16)

The chronological hierarchy pays this denominator at every possible
physical occurrence. Put A=A_k, d=d_k,
N=S_m-S_(k+1)>=0 and x=P-S_k. The full adjacent H_k children imply

    0<=x<=N, T=S_k+N-x,
    (1+P)^2*(1+2T)=(A+x)^2*(2A-1+2N-2x),
    D=4A+2d-1+2N.

The derivative of the denominator expression is
2(A+x)(A-1+2N-3x). It has no interior minimum. Its value at N minus
its value at0 is

    N*[2A(A-1)+N*(2A-1)]>=0.

Hence the denominator is at least A^2*(2A-1+2N). Since d/A<1/2,

    d^2*(4A+2d-1) <(A^2/4)*(5A-1)
                            <=A^2*(2A-1),

where the last inequality is equivalent to A>=1. Adding the2N terms
preserves strictness since d^2<A^2. Thus (16) is strictly less than1/D.
A trajectory with no strict crossing uses (15) on the whole word and
has score at most1/D. A zero hit gives zero scalar terminal value.

This closes ALL finite-L trajectories with at most one strict crossing,
without prescribing where either curvature boundary is visited. It does
not cover arbitrary repeated crossings: even the small-start quadratic
trajectories in (12) cross at every positive step, so crossing counts
must not be silently assumed small.

## 7. Complete forcing identity and uniform thin-segment bounds

For each physical query let y_i=clip(x_i-1,0,L), so0<=y_i<=L. The
actual recurrence can be unrolled algebraically, with no branch selected
or evaluated:

    x_n=-p_m*s+sum_(i<n) w_i*y_i,
    w_i=h_i*product_(i<t<n)(1-h_t).                  (17)

Let E_j be the sum of absolute values of these forcing coefficients for
the complete word H_j. Literal concatenation gives E_0=0 and

    E_(j+1)=(1+d_j*p_j)*E_j+(1+d_j)*p_j.

This recurrence is SOLVED here, not left as a quantitative answer. Put

    C_j=product_(0<=k<j)[1+c^(-1)*beta^(2^k)].        (18)

C_j in this report is the local segment forcing product, distinct from
the project's primitive benchmark capacities C_n. Its shared glossary
entry is C_seg_j.

Using p_(j+1)=d_j*p_j^2 shows

    E_(j+1)+p_(j+1)+1
               =(1+d_j*p_j)*(E_j+p_j+1),
    E_j=2*C_j-1-p_j.                                (19)

The signed sum telescopes to1- product(1-h)=1+p_j for j>=1.
Consequently the total POSITIVE coefficient mass in (17) is C_m,
and the total magnitude of its NEGATIVE coefficients is C_m-1-p_m.
Keeping these signs gives, for every actual scalar trajectory,

    -p_m*s-L*(C_m-1-p_m) <=x_n<= -p_m*s+L*C_m,
    |x_n|<=p_m*|s|+L*C_m.                            (20)

The y_i were not independently optimized to claim realizability: (20)
is only an upper bound on the actual coupled sequence.

The product (18) has the following completely evaluated uniform bound:

    C_m<6*sqrt(m).                                   (21)

To prove it take K=ceil(log_2(4m)). Since2^m>=4m for m>=4, K<=m.
Also2^K<8m. For k<K, each factor in (18) is at most1+1/c<sqrt(2),
so their product is less than sqrt(8m). For k=K+t,

    c^(-1)*beta^(2^k) <(1/2)*exp(-2^t),

using log(1-eps)<=-eps and2^K>=4m. The tail product is at most
exp((1/2)*sum_(t>=0)exp(-2^t)). Since2^t>=t+1, the sum is at most
1/(exp(1)-1)<1. Its exponential is therefore less than exp(1/2)<2.
These elementary exponential bounds follow for instance from the series
2<exp(1)<3<4. The full product is less than2*sqrt(8m)<6*sqrt(m).
If the tail is empty the same bound holds.

Combining (5), (12), and (20) proves the all-start bound

    sup_(s!=0) q(L,s) <= [p_m+L*C_m]^2.              (22)

For |s|>=1 use (20) divided by |s|; for |s|<1 use (12).
This is a quantitative bound for EVERY L, but it is not the desired
profile when L is large. In particular it closes the entire thin-segment
regime

    0<=L<=1/(12*sqrt(m*D)):
                 sup_(s!=0) q(L,s)<1/D.             (23)

Indeed (21) bounds L*C_m by1/(2sqrt(D)), and (13) gives the other
strict half. Equations (9) and (13) transfer (23) to all exposed-segment
dimensions with this normalized length.

For any L, the additional complete large-radius regime

    |s|>=1 and |s|>=2*L*C_m*sqrt(D)                 (24)

also has q(L,s)<1/D. One may replace the second threshold by the
explicit larger threshold12*L*sqrt(m*D). These conclusions allow L
and s to depend arbitrarily on the enclosing m.

## 8. Exact benchmark approach with a finite orthogonal tilt

The segment class is not uniformly below the scalar Huber benchmark.
For each enclosing m choose

    L=2S, s=D, T=sqrt(D),
    K=[0,2S]e_1, lambda=(1,sqrt(D)), X_0=(D,-sqrt(D)).

Every scalar query and the terminal lie in[1,1+L]. In fact at prefix
mass P_i the scalar coordinate is D-P_i, which lies in[S+1,D].
Thus the entire horizontal run is linear with gradient1,

    x_n=S+1, 2*phi_L(x_n)=D, q(L,s)=1/D.

Initial orthogonality is D-sqrt(D)*sqrt(D)=0 and the true initial
radius squared is D^2+D. The vertical terminal is p_m*sqrt(D), with
the sign obtained from z_0=-sqrt(D) and full product-p_m. Therefore

    2*Phi(X_n)/||X_0||^2=(1+Q)/(D+1)<1/D.            (25)

The relative deficit from1/D is (1-DQ)/(D+1), a positive number
less than1/(D+1). More generally increasing finite T in (10) makes
this score arbitrarily close to1/D. This is a legal lower approach
for the segment supremum, not a strict improvement over1/D or17/(16D).

## 9. Actual all-m upper-wing reactivation after a strict plateau query

This construction refutes the proposed shortcut:
"After an actual iterate enters the finite plateau, replace all future
gradients by the one-sided unbounded Huber gradient min(x,1)."
The static finite plateau can be left through its upper boundary again.
It does not refute the desired segment objective bound.

For every enclosing m>=1536 choose explicitly

    L=1/10, y=1+L/2=21/20,
    M=a*(1+beta)+a^2*beta*(1+d_2)
                      +a^3*beta*d_2*(1+beta),
    r=(y+L*M)/p_3, s=-r,
    T=1, lambda=(1,1), X_0=(-r,r).                  (26)

All quantities are finite and positive, and this is one legal segment
instance with initial squared radius2r^2. The scalar first seven steps
are the literal H_3 prefix of H_m. Its exact queried coordinates can be
specified in reverse order solely to prove the explicit forward law:

    x_7=y, x_6=-y/a,
    x_5=L+(L+y/a)/beta, x_4=-x_5/a,
    x_3=L+(L+x_5/a)/d_2, x_2=-x_3/a,
    x_1=L+(L+x_3/a)/beta, x_0=-x_1/a.                (27)

Substitution or multiplication of the three negative forcing
coefficients gives x_1/a=(y+L*M)/p_3=r, so (27) agrees exactly with
the completely explicit initial choice (26). Each negative query uses
gradient x. Every positive query among x_1,x_3,x_5 is STRICTLY above
1+L, hence uses gradient x-L:

* x_5>L+y/a>2, because y>1, a<1/2 and beta<1.
* a*d_2<5/4 and x_5>2 give
  x_3>L+x_5/(a*d_2)>L+8/5>L+1.
* x_3>1, a<1/2 and beta<1 give x_1>L+2>L+1.

These guards verify every update in (27), without a feasibility oracle.
The next actual query x_7=y lies STRICTLY inside[1,1+L]. Its step is
the original level3 bridge1+d_3, so

    x_8=L/2-d_3<0,
    x_9=a*(d_3-L/2)=beta^2*c-a/20.                 (28)

Here x_8 is followed by the original leaf1+a. From (2),
beta^2*c>2 and a/20<1/40. Therefore

    x_9>79/40>11/10=1+L.                           (29)

Thus x_9 is a genuine new upper-wing query after the strict plateau
query x_7. The physical next step at index9 is1+beta. Continuing from
the common state x_7, the proposed unbounded-Huber replacement agrees

differs from the actual one by

    x_10(actual)-x_10(replacement)
                   =-(1+beta)*(x_9-L-1)<0.          (30)

The original full H_m continues on the same globally defined function;
every remaining projection and its normal is fixed by (3). The vertical
coordinate follows its full quadratic product, and no radius is dropped.
This report does NOT supply an evaluated terminal payoff for (26), and
does NOT present it as an improving worst-case witness. Its concluded
claim is exactly the finite-prefix failure (29)-(30) inside a legal
full-word instance for every allowed m.

## 10. What has and has not been closed

The complete geometric reduction includes every dimension, all exposed
segments, zero horizontal starts, parallel height vectors, degenerate
segments, boundaries, the actual full quadratic factor, and the true
orthogonality/radius payment. The finite-T strict-witness conversion
(11) is explicit if a scalar witness is later found.

The quantitatively closed regimes are:

1. L=0 or0<|s|<=1: exact score Q.
2. Any L and amplitude with no or one strict sign crossing: at most1/D.
3. Every start for normalized L<=1/(12sqrt(mD)): strictly below1/D.
4. Every L and the large radii in (24): strictly below1/D.
5. The explicit plateau law in Section8: scalar score exactly1/D and
   a legal finite-tilt score (25) approaching it.

None of the following attempted simplifications closes the remaining
regime. Replacing all scalar motion by its quadratic product fails on
Section8. Replacing future motion after a plateau visit by an unbounded
Huber trajectory fails on Section9. Optimizing the bounded variables
y_i independently in (17) loses their common-body guards and yields
only (22), not a sharp family profile. These are failures of proposed
proof transfers, not evidence that the desired full upper bound is false.

Any as-yet-unexcluded scalar witness q(L,s)>1/D must in particular have

    L>1/(12sqrt(mD)),
    1<|s|<2L*C_m*sqrt(D),
    at least two strict sign crossings and no zero hit.

This is a necessary residual domain, not a claim of existence and not an
unevaluated branch list advertised as closure. Repeated returns with
reactivated positive outer curvature remain quantitatively uncontrolled
