kappa=B=1, j=m, and w_m=A_(m-1)/d_m. Then

    0<w_m<beta<1,
    G(M_m(d_m*w_m))=theta=a*beta>a*w_m.             (1.4)

These are exact complete-word interval images attained by compatible
actual starts. This is not a local-step comparison failure.

For a possible repair, the necessary coefficient loss on this witness is

    L_m=beta*d_m/A_(m-1),
    1<L_m<1+3/(2m),
    lim_(m->infinity) m*(L_m-1)=(3+2sqrt(2))/4.     (1.5)

Thus a proposed universal coefficient a*(1+C/m) requires
C>=(3+2sqrt(2))/4. This is a NECESSARY loss, not a sufficient upper
bound for all amplitudes or for the general kink law.

The counterexample has first inner reversing level J=0. It refutes
the assertion quantified over arbitrary J, but does not settle positive J.
No third mechanism or asymmetric family is entered.


## 2. Actual function, objective areas, and all interpolation rows

The radial objective is exactly

    2F(r)=kappa*r^2,                         0<=r<=1,
    2F(r)=(r-v)^2+kappa*v,                   1<=r<=u,
    2F(r)=2B*r-C_tail,                       r>=u,
    C_tail=B^2+v*(2B-kappa).                       (2.1)

Values and first derivatives agree at both knots. At B=kappa the
middle interval disappears and u=1. At kappa=1 this is the Huber law
with cap B; the family kink radius has not been changed.

The odd derivative g is continuous and nondecreasing, with piecewise
slopes kappa,1,0. Partitioning an interval at the knots proves
|g(x)-g(y)|<=|x-y|. Hence f is finite, convex, differentiable, and
globally1-smooth. Since G(r)>0 for r>0, its unique minimizer is0 and
its minimum is0. The true initial distance is |s|.

All ordered smooth-convex rows of actual samples hold directly. For x<y
put Delta=g(y)-g(x), so0<=Delta<=y-x. On[x,y],

    g(t)-g(x)>=max(0,Delta-(y-t)),
    g(y)-g(t)>=max(0,Delta-(t-x)).

Integrating gives both directed convexity remainders at least Delta^2/2.
Consequently, with g_i=g(x_i), f_i=f(x_i), for EVERY ordered pair of
physical, terminal, or optimum points,

    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+g_i*(x_j-x_i)+(g_i-g_j)^2/2<=0.   (2.2)

Repeated points have identical values/derivatives. The Gram matrix is
positive semidefinite because each quadratic form is a square of a real
linear combination of the actual scalar vectors. No terminal gradient
or physical leaf is deleted.

At radius r, put p=G(r). Since p<=r and G(t)<=min(t,p) on[0,r],

    2F(r)<=2r*p-p^2.                               (2.3)

Also G(r)<=min(r,B), so F(r)<=J_B(r), where J_B denotes the Huber
function with derivative sign(x)*min(|x|,B). This value comparison does
NOT imply a universal comparison of individual kink-function steps.

For advertised smoothness L>0, objective L*f and steps h_i/L give
the same points and normalized payoff. A smaller actual core curvature
never changes the physical schedule.


## 3. Exact same-m masses and uniform elementary bounds

Throughout,

    0<epsilon<1/1000, beta>99/100,
    12/5<c<17/7<5/2, 2/5<a<1/2,
    0<theta<1/2, c*theta=beta^2<1.                 (3.1)

Use7/5<sqrt(2)<17/12 and epsilon<1/1000 for
12/5<c<(29/12)*(1001/1000)<17/7.
Then a>(99/100)*(7/17)>2/5, while a<1/2 since c>2.

Define

    t=c*(c-2), eta=a/(c-2)=beta/t.

Since lambda*(lambda-2)=1 and c>lambda, t>1>beta and0<eta<1.
The literal word recursion and its exact solution are

    A_(j+1)=2A_j+d_j,
    A_j=(1-eta)*2^j+eta*c^j, j>=0.                 (3.2)

Substitution verifies the formula and A_0=1. Hence

    A_j<c^j for j>=1,
    A_j>d_j/(c-2), d_j/A_j<c-2<1/2 for j>=0.      (3.3)

The second strict inequality follows from the positive term
(1-eta)*2^j.

Let d=d_(m-1). By(3.1), d>(2/5)*2^(m-1)=2^m/5.
For all integers m>=8, 2^m>20m: it holds at8, and doubling preserves
the inequality because2m>=m+1. Thus

    d>4m=1/epsilon, 1/d<epsilon,
    D=2A_m-1<2c^m=2d_m/a.                         (3.4)

The exact expansion

    t=1+2lambda*(lambda-1)*epsilon+lambda^2*epsilon^2

and6<2lambda*(lambda-1)=4+2sqrt(2)<7, lambda^2<6 give

    1+6epsilon<t<1+8epsilon.                       (3.5)

Here epsilon<1/6 bounds6epsilon^2 by epsilon.

At every physical level-k bridge, the actual original prefix mass P
satisfies P>=S_k, because its full left H_k child is present.
The actual suffix after that bridge is H_k followed by zero or more
pairs(h_l^lev,H_l) with strictly increasing ancestor levels l>k.
Ascend the binary tree, retaining an ancestor exactly when its bridge
and right child remain ahead. This accounts for every remaining physical
leaf, including the terminal leaf, without resetting m.


## 5. Complete unit-Huber reference, proved jointly

First set B=1 and use J_1. Its exact one-step interval radius for
h=1+d_h>=1 is

    V_h(R)=max(d_h*min(R,1), R-h).                 (5.1)

The odd continuous step map has extrema at an endpoint or a knot.
It maps[-R,R] ONTO the symmetric interval with this radius.
Let U_j(R) be the exact interval radius for complete H_j. Then

    U_(j+1)=U_j composed with V_(h_j^lev) composed with U_j. (5.2)

All radius maps are nondecreasing. Composition is exact, since a continuous
odd map has a connected symmetric interval image. Thus no incompatible
choice of separate child starts occurs.

First prove by induction

    U_j(A_j)=1,
    U_j(R)=R-S_j for R>=A_j,
    U_j(R)<=max(1,R-S_j) for R>=0.                  (5.3)

The empty word has these properties. At input A_(j+1)=2A_j+d_j,
the first child gives A_j+d_j+1. The bridge has staying output A_j
and crossing output at most d_j<A_j. The second child gives1.
A positive exterior start R>=A_(j+1) stays saturated at every query
and through the terminal, giving R-S_(j+1). Monotonicity bounds smaller
interval inputs by1. This proves(5.3).

Next prove simultaneously, for every integer r>=0,

    U_j(d_j*theta^r)<=theta^(r+1), j>=1.            (5.4)

For j=1, d_1=beta<1 and the output is exactly
a*beta*theta^r=theta^(r+1). At the unscaled parent input c*d_j,
(5.3) bounds the first child by max(1,c*d_j-S_j). The bridge's
crossing term is at most d_j. Its staying term is at most d_j because

    c*d_j-S_j-(1+d_j)<=d_j
    iff (c-2)*d_j<=A_j,

which follows from(3.3). Apply the second child's r=0 bound.
For r>=1, c*theta<1 gives
c*d_j*theta^r<=d_j*theta^(r-1). The first child gives at most theta^r<1,
the bridge at most d_j*theta^r, and the second child at most
theta^(r+1). This proves the full family(5.4).

For0<R<=d_m, choose r>=0 with
d_m*theta^(r+1)<R<=d_m*theta^r. Monotonicity implies

    U_m(R)<=theta^(r+1)<R/d_m.                    (5.5)

For an actual strict crossing at level k, the landing radius is at most
d_k. If k>=1, the following full H_k gives radius<=theta<a by(5.4);
if k=0, the landing itself is<=a. At each later retained ancestor l,
an incoming radius<=a<1 becomes at most a*d_l<=d_l at the bridge,
and the full right H_l gives<=theta. The exact suffix from Section3
therefore proves

    any strict crossing in H_m => terminal radius<=a. (5.6)

All repeated crossings and all remaining leaves are included.

For R<=d_m use2J_1(r)<=r^2 and(5.5) to bound payoff by1/d_m^2.
For R>=d_m with a crossing use(5.6) to bound it by a^2/d_m^2.
Both are less than1/D, since D<2d_m/a and d_m>2/a by(3.1),(3.4).
No-crossing histories obey(4.1), giving1/D.
Thus the complete all-start Huber profile is<=1/D.

The start R=D=1+2S stays saturated through terminal radius1+S
and has payoff[2(1+S)-1]/D^2=1/D. The exact profile is therefore1/D.
Scaling this reference Huber function by B gives the same profile for
every cap B>0 on the same physical word. This reference calculation does
not change the cap or kink of an actual outward-kink trajectory.


## 8. Mechanism2: an exact complete-word counterexample

Set kappa=B=1. Then G(r)=min(r,1), the actual function is J_1,
and M_j=U_j. This is one fixed member of the required family.
The first inner reversing level J is0 because ell>1.

We first prove the exact identity

    U_j(d_j)=theta for EVERY j>=1.                 (8.1)

Its upper bound is(5.4), proved in this joint report.
At j=1 equality holds since d_1=beta<1.
Put Delta_j=d_j-A_(j-1). At j=2,

    Delta_2=beta*c-2-a
           =epsilon*(2/c-lambda*epsilon)>0.       (8.2)

Substitute c=lambda*(1+epsilon), a=(1-epsilon)/(lambda*(1+epsilon))
and lambda-1/lambda=2 to check the equality. For the sign,
c<5/2 gives2/c>4/5, while lambda*epsilon<1/400.
For every j>=2 the exact recursion gives

    Delta_(j+1)=2Delta_j+(c-2-1/c)*d_j>0,          (8.3)

because t=c*(c-2)>1. Thus d_j>A_(j-1) for j>=2.

Assume(8.1) at j-1. At interval input A_(j-1), the first H_(j-1)
gives radius1 by(5.3), the bridge gives d_(j-1) by(5.1), and the
second child gives theta by induction. Hence U_j(A_(j-1))=theta.
Monotonicity and d_j>A_(j-1) give the lower bound in(8.1).
In particular,

    U_m(A_(m-1))=theta.                            (8.4)

Set q=2/c<5/6. Since d_m=beta*c^(m-1), the proposed amplitude is

    w_m=A_(m-1)/d_m
       =[eta+(1-eta)*q^(m-1)]/beta.                (8.5)

From(3.5) and epsilon<1/1000,

    eta=beta/t>1/2,
    0<1-eta=(t-beta)/t<9epsilon,
    beta*t-1>(1-epsilon)*(1+6epsilon)-1
                  =5epsilon-6epsilon^2>4epsilon.

It follows that

    beta^2-eta=eta*(beta*t-1)>2epsilon.             (8.6)

Furthermore(5/6)^4<1/2 and m-1>=12 give

    (1-eta)*q^(m-1)<9epsilon/8<2epsilon.            (8.7)

Thus eta+(1-eta)*q^(m-1)<beta^2 and0<w_m<beta<1=B.
The actual interval input is d_m*w_m=A_(m-1), and theta<1.
Equation(8.4) yields

    G(M_m(d_m*w_m))=G(theta)=theta=a*beta>a*w_m,

proving(1.4) for every enclosing m in the assignment.

Exact interval composition in Section5 ensures compatible actual starts,
not adversarially reset child inputs. An actual nonzero start in
[-A_(m-1),A_(m-1)] attains terminal magnitude theta. For a precise
selection take the least s in[0,A_(m-1)] with |Psi_m(s)|=theta.
The set is nonempty by(8.4) and oddness, compact by continuity, and
its minimum is positive since Psi_m(0)=0. This specifies a single
complete trajectory on the fixed function. No objective claim replaces
that true s by the interval radius.


## 9. Exact necessary coefficient price; no sufficient repair claimed

The witness's ratio to the asserted right-hand side is

    L_m=theta/(a*w_m)=beta/w_m
       =beta^2/[eta+(1-eta)*q^(m-1)].              (9.1)

Section8 gives L_m>1. Since the second denominator term is positive,

    L_m<beta^2/eta=beta*t.

The exact expansion, using lambda^2=3+2sqrt(2), is

    beta*t=1+lambda^2*epsilon-epsilon^2-lambda^2*epsilon^3
           <1+6epsilon=1+3/(2m).                 (9.2)

This proves the finite necessary witness loss in(1.5).
Direct subtraction gives

    0<beta*t-L_m
      =beta^2*(1-eta)*q^(m-1)
         /[eta*(eta+(1-eta)*q^(m-1))]
      <36epsilon*(5/6)^(m-1),                    (9.3)

using eta>1/2 and1-eta<9epsilon. Multiplying this error by m sends it
to0, while

    m*(beta*t-1)=lambda^2/4-1/(16m)-lambda^2/(64m^2).

Therefore lim m*(L_m-1)=lambda^2/4. Any universal amplitude estimate
with coefficient a*(1+C/m) must have L_m<=1+C/m on this witness,
hence C>=lambda^2/4 is necessary.

This does not establish a sufficient paid amplitude theorem or control
accumulated losses through arbitrary inner reversals. It is impermissible
to compound an unproved per-level estimate using this calculation.

The complete objective profile of this same function is exactly1/D by
Section5. Consequently this counterexample does not violate17/(16D)
and is not an improving objective witness.

x_star, x_0!=x_star, and the original updates
x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L)grad f(x_i). Let R_n(h) denote the same supremum
without the numerator factor2, so W=2R. The current sufficient route in
accepted931b9653ce0f7201 still requires the full-function inequality
W_(2^m-1)(H_m)<=17/(16D) for EVERY m>=1536. Nothing in this report proves
or disproves that inequality.

of h_i-1 over the final r steps, with R_0=1. If pop(r) denotes the number
of1 digits in the binary expansion of r, the hierarchy gives

    R_r=beta^r*c^(-pop(r)),
    s=R_n, k_i=h_i product_(u>i)(1-h_u),

## 3. Complete first-law metric and original polynomial

The common column and required clock energy are

    z=(E/a)(b e_0-e_1), Z=t^T z=-E/a, e^T z=E,
    Xreq=D/17-(pi^2-s^2)/a^2=D-pi^(-2)-eta Z^2.

Xreq>D/17-425/(64D)>0 and Xreq<D/17<S/5.
Define physical-mass moments and the clock metric by

    Qmass=sum h_i^2, Rmass=sum h_i^3,
    t_mass=(sum h_i t_i)/S,
    Vmass=sum h_i(t_i-t_mass)^2,
    rho_clock=Xreq/Vmass,
    Kclock=rho_clock[diag(h)-hh^T/S].

All sums are finite symbolic expressions. The level-count identity is
sum h_i^d=sum_(u=0)^(m-1)2^(m-1-u)(1+a*c^u)^d for d=1,2,3.
Palindrome reversal sends the prefix mass p_i=t_i-1 to S-p_i-h_i.
It gives sum h_i p_i=(S^2-Qmass)/2 and
sum h_i^2 p_i=(S Qmass-Rmass)/2. Summing
(p_i+h_i)^3-p_i^3 yields
sum h_i p_i^2=S^3/3-S Qmass/2+Rmass/6. Therefore

    t_mass=1+(S^2-Qmass)/(2S),
    Vmass=S^3/12+Rmass/6-Qmass^2/(4S).              (3.1)

In particular this is the variance for the actual unequal steps.
The level formula gives

The mass formula gives S>=vword*c^m-1. Also

For the second strict inequality, (c-2)^2/(c^2-2) is increasing on

## 4. General orientation of a symmetric-factor cut

Let Gamma be any original n-by-n matrix with zero diagonal, all entries
nonnegative, and B=Ltri Gamma symmetric. For any symmetric P and skew A,

    sum_(i,j)Gamma_ij N_ij
      =tr(Gamma^T Ltri^T(P+A))
      =tr(B^T(P+A))=tr(BP).                        (4.1)

The last equality follows by pairing B_ij A_ij+B_ji A_ji=0 and A_ii=0.
It is an equality on the FULL original arrays. If all original finite
multipliers lambda_ij=-N_ij are nonnegative, its left side is nonpositive.
Therefore tr(BP)<=0 is necessary. Neither Ae nor At is used. Conversely,
a positive trace proves only that the displayed fixed P has no sign-feasible
skew completion; it gives no primal function or minimax bound.

## 1. Verdict and precise scope

The whole assigned class with arbitrary global compatible skew remains OPEN.
No unknown feasible matrix is presented as a construction, and no obstruction
for local skew changes is presented as an obstruction for arbitrary skew.
The following are jointly derived partial conclusions, not accepted facts.

1. No nonzero nonnegative combination of the two old symmetric-factor cuts
   is positive semidefinite on the four-dimensional detail space. Thus that
   particular cone-separation attempt cannot exclude the whole metric cone.
2. The old second cut has the exact general-metric requirement

       2 beta R03+g R33 >= g(1-a)/b+Cstar/b^2.

   Its order-1/eps amplitude requirement was specific to the correlation
   R03=-R33. It does not apply to an arbitrary positive semidefinite R.
3. A bounded explicit metric R_test below passes BOTH old cuts, both endpoint
   screens, the source and last capacities, and C2,C3. It is only a test of
   those selected necessary conditions, not a passing original certificate.
4. For EVERY positive semidefinite R, no correction to the prescribed
   canonical skew that is supported in the final six queries and annihilates
   the original e,t can make all thirty local off-diagonal entries nonpositive.
   One literal strictly positive weighted sum of those entries is invariant
   under every such metric and skew change, and exceeds127.
5. Any full feasible completion therefore requires nonlocal skew changes.
   Section8 gives their exact necessary boundary-flux inequality and all
   thirty local inequalities, with every outside interaction retained.

    eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps, c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+eps), a=beta/c,

Let e be the all-ones column in R^n, and e_i the original coordinate column.

    t=Ltri e, t_i=1+sum_(j<i)h_j,

Elementary exact enclosures used below are

    12/5<c<5/2, 99/100<beta<1,

For an integer suffix length r in{0,...,n} define R_r to be the product

### A3. Complete first-law metric and original polynomial

### A4. General orientation of a symmetric-factor cut

Let Gamma be any original n-by-n matrix with zero diagonal, all entries
nonnegative, and B=Ltri Gamma symmetric. For any symmetric P and skew A,

    sum_(i,j)Gamma_ij N_ij

      =tr(B^T(P+A))=tr(BP).                        (4.1)

The last equality follows by pairing B_ij A_ij+B_ji A_ji=0 and A_ii=0.

# Quadratic occupation common column: passing global tests and an exact two-anchor failure

Status: JOINT UNVERIFIED. Worker max, invocation93, guidance7a99c4006b2edc8d.
This is one joint analytical draft, not a verifier-accepted result. TASK permits
zero formal calls. No fact_submit was made and none of the new claims has a fact
ID. All uses of earlier unverified algebra are rederived below. The original
minimax problem remains OPEN, with W=2R throughout.

## 1. Outcome, correction, and exact scope

The literal first common-column law in TASK preserves both original source
coordinates and the complete sum and clock moments. It passes the specified
necessary tests for every integer m>=M0, where the absolute threshold used here
is M0=2^26:

    T_w < -10q,                 T_t < -(S+1)^2/10.

Both original endpoint capacity/moment tests, the weighted first-source pair,
both terminal-six symmetric-factor cuts, and C2,C3 pass for the prescribed
Rtest metric. These tests do NOT prove simultaneous finite signs.

There is a sign typo in TASK's proposed expansion of Csrc. The literal law has
p1=-ga/(1+s) and w1=-a, so p1*w1=+ga^2/(1+s). The correct expansion is

    (1+s)Csrc=b+ga^2+(a beta+s)a beta.                 (1.1)

We corrected this calculation; we did NOT change p,u,uhat,gamma,z or the metric.

The sole second mechanism is an explicit skew supported on edges incident to
the ORIGINAL root query and the ACTUAL lower alpha-bracket query. Every one of
its coefficients is specified in Section9. Its two moment equations hold, but
its original finite entry satisfies

    N04=b^2 s^2/(a^2 beta^3)+(q/2)b^2 a beta^3
                             +a rho_clock b^2/S > q/3.       (1.2)

Therefore lambda04=-N04<0: that completion is excluded. This is a certificate
array obstruction, not a primal adversary or a minimax lower bound. The same
common column with a different global skew is NOT excluded. No third mechanism
or second common column was tried.

Accepted fact1252b8823bb5a290 is used only for the original interpolation
orientation and full terminal-square certificate interface. Accepted
931b9653ce0f7201 retains its conditional scope: it supplies benchmark comparison,
not the missing full-function bound. No original function-class upper bound is
asserted here.

## 2. Original coordinates, products, and actual alpha bracket

Fix the SAME enclosing integer m>=M0 in every child, and put

    eps=1/(4m), beta=1-eps, c=(1+sqrt(2))(1+eps), a=beta/c,
    H_0=(), H_(r+1)=(H_r,1+a c^r,H_r), h=H_m,
    n=2^m-1, l=n-1, S_r=sum H_r, S=S_m, D=1+2S,
    q=17/(16D), pi=sqrt(q), b=1+a, g=1+beta.

The original queried indices are0,...,l, and n is the unqueried terminal.
e is the all-ones column in R^n; e_i denotes its standard coordinate columns.
L=Ltri has diagonal1 and L_ij=h_j for j<i, zero for j>i. Set

    t=L e, t_i=1+sum_(u<i)h_u, T=t_l=S-a,
    Delta=T-1=S-b, Utotal=S+1, ell=L t.

Here L is a matrix after smoothness normalization, not the original smoothness
constant. Utotal is a scalar; U below is a six-by-four detail matrix.

Useful elementary enclosures are

    12/5<c<5/2, 99/100<beta<1, 41/100<a<5/12,
    7/5<b<17/12, 199/100<g<2, 17/5<H:=1+a c^2<7/2.

For the lower bound on a, sqrt(2)<99/70 gives
(70/169)(6143/6145)>41/100. The upper bound uses sqrt(2)>7/5.
For H=1+(1+sqrt(2))(1-eps^2), use sqrt(2)>141/100 and eps<1/100.
All remaining bounds follow directly from eps<=1/6144.

Put vword=a/(c-2). Summing the two children gives, by substitution,

    1+S_r=(1-vword)2^r+vword c^r.

The identity c(c-2)=1+2(2+sqrt(2))eps+(1+sqrt(2))^2 eps^2
implies c(c-2)<1+7eps+6eps^2. Thus
vword>(1-eps)/(1+7eps+6eps^2)>1-8eps=1-2/m>4/5,
where the second comparison follows by multiplying positive denominators.
Also c(c-2)>1>beta, so vword<1. Consequently

    2^m-1<S<c^m<2^(2m), 1/(4S)<q<1/S,
    2^(-2m-2)<q<2^(-m), pi<2^(-m/2)<1/1000,
    17/(48S)<q<17/(32S), D/S<201/100.              (2.1)

For q<2^(-m), use D>2^(m+1)-1 and 2^(m+1)-1>(17/16)2^m.

Let pop(i) count binary1 digits. The physical level at index i is the exponent
of2 dividing i+1. Counting multiples of2^r shows that the sum of these levels
in the first i steps is i-pop(i). Hence

    w_i=product_(u<i)(1-h_u)=(-1)^i beta^i c^(-pop(i)),
    s=product_(i<n)(h_i-1)=beta^n c^(-m)>0,
    w_n=-s, |w_i|<=beta^i.

Palindrome reversal gives the same formula for unsigned suffix products.
Define k_i=h_i product_(u>i)(1-h_u). Finite product telescoping gives

    e^T k=1+s, L^T k=h, t^T k=S,
    |k_i|<=2, k_i w_i=s h_i/(h_i-1), L w=e.       (2.2)

For the last identity, w_(i+1)-w_i=-h_i w_i gives
w_i+sum_(u<i)h_u w_u=1. At the source and final pair these identities give

    w0=1,w1=-a,w2=a beta,w4=a beta^3,
    w_l=s/a, w_(l-1)=-s/(a beta),
    k0=bs/a,k1=-gs/(a beta),k_l=b.                (2.3)

Set E=pi+s, F=pi-s, eta=F/E, V=(1-pi)/pi. Smallness estimates below
prove 0<s<pi. The actual terminal distribution is

    tbar=(S-V)/(1-pi), j=min{i:t_(i+1)>=tbar},
    alpha_j=(1-pi)(t_(j+1)-tbar)/h_j,
    alpha_(j+1)=(1-pi)(tbar-t_j)/h_j,
    alpha_i=0 otherwise, v=k-alpha.

The mean is in the queried clock range: tbar>S-1/pi>1, while

    (1-pi)(T-tbar)=15/(32pi)-b+(a+1/2)pi>0.

Thus alpha>=0, e^T alpha=1-pi, t^T alpha=S-V, e^T v=E, t^T v=V.
Ties use the stated earlier bracket with zero earlier coefficient.

For later bounds define drem_i=Utotal-t_i, the actual remaining step mass,
and D_r=sum_i alpha_i drem_i^r. Direct use of the mean gives

    D_1=1/pi-pi Utotal,
    dbar=D_1/(1-pi)=(15/32-q/2)/(pi(1-pi)),
    1/(3pi)<dbar<1/(2pi).                        (2.4)

The upper bound is equivalent to1/32-pi/2+q/2>0; the lower follows from
pi<1/1000. If h_j=1+a c^r, the suffix after j contains an H_r block.
Since a c^r=(c-2)vword c^r<(S_r+1)/2, one has
h_j<3/2+drem_(j+1)/2. The actual bracket and (2.4) now give

    drem_(j+1)<=dbar<=drem_j,
    drem_j<(3/2)dbar+3/2<2/pi.                   (2.5)

In particular t_j>S-2/pi>3S/4. The original root index
rroot=2^(m-1)-1 has t_rroot=1+S_(m-1)<S/2+1, so j>rroot and
j>=2^(m-1). Conversely drem_(j+1)>(2/3)(dbar-3/2)>1/(5pi)>200.
Thus both alpha coordinates are outside the final six, whose remaining mass
is less12. They are also beyond all fixed early source coordinates.

We will use explicit superexponential guards, not an asymptotic slogan.
For every integer m>=64, 2^(m-1)>16m^3: at64 this is
2^63>16(2^6)^3=2^22, and the induction uses
2m^3>(m+1)^3 for m>=4. Since
beta^(-4m)>(1+1/(4m))^(4m)>2, both alpha-support prefix amplitudes and s obey

    Btail:=beta^(2^(m-1))<2^(-4m^2),
    |w_i|<=Btail on and after alpha's support, s<Btail.     (2.6)

These finite inequalities also prove s<pi and every smallness assertion below.

## 3. Literal full-space metric and its clock energy

Put Z=-E/a and

    X=Xreq=D-pi^(-2)-eta Z^2=D/17-(q-s^2)/a^2.

The bounds a>2/5 and D>11 give 0<X<D/17<S/5. Let

    Qmass=sum h_i^2, Rmass=sum h_i^3,
    tmass=(sum h_i t_i)/S,
    Vmass=sum h_i(t_i-tmass)^2,
    rho_clock=X/Vmass,
    Kclock=rho_clock[diag(h)-hh^T/S], yclock=Kclock t.

These are the actual nonuniform physical moments. If pclock_i=t_i-1,
palindrome reversal sends pclock_i to S-pclock_i-h_i. Pairing reversals and
then telescoping (pclock_i+h_i)^3-pclock_i^3 yields

    sum h_i pclock_i=(S^2-Qmass)/2,
    sum h_i^2 pclock_i=(S Qmass-Rmass)/2,
    sum h_i pclock_i^2=S^3/3-S Qmass/2+Rmass/6.

Substitution proves

    tmass=1+(S^2-Qmass)/(2S),
    Vmass=S^3/12+Rmass/6-Qmass^2/(4S),
    M2:=sum h_i t_i^2
       =S+S^2-Qmass+S^3/3-S Qmass/2+Rmass/6.       (3.1)

Level counts give Qmass=2S-n+a^2(c^(2m)-2^m)/(c^2-2).
Since S>(99/100)a c^m/(c-2),
Qmass/S^2<2/S+(100/99)^2(c-2)^2/(c^2-2)<1/15.
Indeed (c-2)^2/(c^2-2)<1/17 for2<c<5/2,
(100/99)^2/17<1/16, and2/S<1/500.
Thus (3.1) gives Vmass>2S^3/25 and rho_clock<125/S^2.
Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz and multiplication now prove

    Kclock>=0, Kclock e=0, t^T Kclock t=X,
    yclock_i=rho_clock h_i(t_i-tmass).             (3.2)

For 0<=i<=n-3 define the original three-query details

    d_i=h_(i+1)e_i-(h_i+h_(i+1))e_(i+1)+h_i e_(i+2),
    omega0=(3q-(Kclock)00)/g^2,
    omega_i=8(q+v_i^2+v_(i+1)^2+v_(i+2)^2)/(h_i+h_(i+1))^2, i>=1.

Each detail annihilates e and t because the two actual consecutive clock
increments are h_i,h_(i+1). Also (Kclock)00<250/S^2<3q, so omega0>0;
the remaining coefficients are positive by their definitions.

Set I=l-5. Local coordinates0,...,5 below mean original I,...,l. Their
physical steps are (g,b,H,b,g,b). The columns of U, extended by zero outside
this set, are

    u0=(b,-g-b,g,0,0,0)^T,
    u1=(0,H,-b-H,b,0,0)^T,
    u2=(0,0,b,-H-b,H,0)^T,
    u3=(0,0,0,g,-b-g,b)^T.

Their sums and their products with the actual local clocks

    tau=(0,g,g+b,g+b+H,g+2b+H,2g+2b+H)^T

vanish. With ehat_r the coordinate columns in R^4, freeze exactly

    Rtest=3(ehat0-ehat1)(ehat0-ehat1)^T+ehat3 ehat3^T,
    Knew=Kclock+sum_(i=0)^(I-1)omega_i d_i d_i^T+U Rtest U^T.  (3.3)

This is a sum of PSD matrices. The preceding products and the support of
all details prove, without an unknown metric,

    Knew>=0, Knew e=0, Knew t=yclock,
    t^T Knew t=X, (Knew)00=3q.                    (3.4)

Only d0 reaches source0. The unchanged source off-diagonal is

    Knew01=-rho_clock bg/S-(b+g)(3q-(Kclock)00)/g. (3.5)

Also Knew04=-rho_clock b^2/S: no retained detail or U column reaches both
original0 and4. All tail support statements in later sections refer to the
full original metric (3.3), including the two crossing details before I.

## 4. The frozen occupation law and absolute moment bounds

Use the literal signed weights and source subtraction

    p_i=h_i w_i/(1+s),
    p0=b/(1+s), p1=-ga/(1+s), r2=1-p0-p1=(a beta+s)/(1+s),
    u=p-p0 e0-p1 e1-r2 e2,
    Mu=t^T u, uhat=u-(Mu/g)(e_l-e_(l-1)),
    gamma=q(1+s)/(2(q-s^2)),
    zsrc=(E/a)(b e0-e1), dz=E gamma uhat, z=znew=zsrc+dz.     (4.1)

The p_i are signed, not probabilities. Since h_i w_i=w_i-w_(i+1),
sum_i p_i=(1-w_n)/(1+s)=1. Therefore e^T u=0 and u0=u1=0.
The physical last clock gap is t_l-t_(l-1)=g, so

    e^T uhat=t^T uhat=0, uhat0=uhat1=0,
    e^T z=E, t^T z=Z=-E/a,
    z0=Eb/a, z1=-E/a.                            (4.2)

Thus X and BOTH source coordinates are exactly preserved.

Here are explicit bounds that will pay every new error. At each original i,
2^level<=i+1 and c<4 give

    h_i<=2(i+1)^2, t_i<=2(i+1)^3, ell_i<=6(i+1)^6.

For the last bound sum h_u t_u over u<i, using
h_u t_u<=4(u+1)^5 and sum_(u<i)(u+1)^5<=(i+1)^6.
For an integer d>=0 and 0<beta<1,

    sum_(i>=0)(i+1)^d beta^i <= d!/(1-beta)^(d+1).

Indeed (i+1)^d<=d!*binom(i+d,d); expanding a product of d+1 geometric
series proves the displayed generating sum. No recurrence was executed.
In particular |p0|<2, |p1|<1, 0<r2<1, so the source subtraction has
clock absolute moment less10 and ell absolute moment less20. It follows that

    |Mu|<=480(4m)^6+10 < Bm:=2^22 m^6,
    |ell^T u|<=12*8!*(4m)^9+20 < Bell:=2^40 m^9.  (4.3)

For every integer m>=1024, m^6 and m^9 are at most2^(m/4). At1024 the
larger is2^90<2^256. For the induction,
(1+1/m)^9<=sum_(k>=0)(9/1024)^k=1024/1015<8/7,
and (8/7)^4<2. Thus multiplying by the next factor preserves the bound.
Combining (2.1),(2.6),(4.3) gives

    s^2/q<1/100, s<1/10, 0<gamma<1,
    delta:=4pi Bm=2^24 pi m^6 <2^(24-m/4)<2^(-20). (4.4)

This is an explicit absolute threshold proof. No dependence on a function,
dimension or initial point is present.

The added final-two entries are exactly

    z_l=E gamma[b s/(a(1+s))-Mu/g],
    z_(l-1)=E gamma[-g s/(a beta(1+s))+Mu/g].       (4.5)

At the other four final-six indices, z_i=E gamma p_i. As E<2pi and each
physical tail step is less4, (4.3)--(4.4) prove

    |z_i|<delta for all I<=i<=l.                 (4.6)

This bounds even the moment correction, which must not be discarded just
because the uncorrected terminal p entries are small.

Finally the source product (1.1) follows directly from (2.3),(4.1). The exact
last-prefix relation (w_l-w_(l-1))/g=s/(a beta) gives

    w^T uhat=Tquad/(1+s)-Csrc-s Mu/(a beta),
    Tquad=sum_(i<n)h_i w_i^2.                    (4.7)

## 5. Complete original polynomial, skew compatibility, and coefficients

With the fixed Knew and z from (3.3),(4.1), define

    P=Knew+vv^T+eta zz^T,
    dvec=F(v-z), rvec=Knew t+Vv+eta Zz-2alpha,
    A^T=-A, Ae=dvec, At=rvec, N=L^T(P+A).         (5.1)

The necessary skew compatibility identities all hold:

    e^T dvec=0,
    e^T rvec=-dvec^T t,
    t^T rvec=X+V^2+eta Z^2-2(S-V)=0.             (5.2)

For the middle identity use E-2pi=-F and eta E=F. For the last insert
X=D-pi^(-2)-eta Z^2 and V=pi^(-1)-1. Thus compatible skews exist.
For example let tmean=e^T t/n, cvec=t-tmean e, Ve=cvec^T cvec, and
fvec=rvec-tmean dvec+(dvec^T t)e/n. Then

    Acan=(dvec e^T-e dvec^T)/n
               +(fvec cvec^T-cvec fvec^T)/Ve.     (5.3)

Equations (5.2) imply e^T fvec=cvec^T fvec=0; multiplying (5.3) proves
both required moments. Every other compatible A is Acan+C with
C^T=-C, Ce=Ct=0.

Every original coefficient, including those outside the terminal block, is

    N_ij=P_ij+A_ij+h_i sum_(u>i)(P_uj+A_uj),
    lambda_(i,j)=-N_ij for queried i!=j,
    lambda_(i,star)=mu_i=(Ne)_i,
    lambda_(star,i)=nu_i=(N^T e)_i-2alpha_i,
    lambda_(n,star)=2pi, lambda_(n,i)=2alpha_i,
    lambda_(i,n)=lambda_(star,n)=0.               (5.4)

From (P+A)e=2pi v and (P-A)t=2alpha one gets

    mu=2pi L^T v,
    mu_i=2pi[h_i(pi+sum_(u<i)alpha_u)+(h_i-1)alpha_i]>=2q h_i,
    nu=0, N^T e=2alpha.                         (5.5)

Thus all terminal and optimum signs pass. Finite off-diagonal signs remain
separate obligations.

For full accounting of the change from zsrc with the SAME metric, put
Psrc=Knew+vv^T+eta zsrc zsrc^T. For the canonical skew change,

    DeltaP=eta(zsrc dz^T+dz zsrc^T+dz dz^T),
    Deltadvec=-F dz, Deltarvec=-(F/a)dz,
    DeltaAcan=F(e dz^T-dz e^T)/n
       +F(tmean-1/a)(dz cvec^T-cvec dz^T)/Ve,
    DeltaN_ij=(DeltaP+DeltaAcan)_ij
                       +h_i sum_(u>i)(DeltaP+DeltaAcan)_uj.  (5.6)

No untouched-row assumption is made: (5.6) describes every original pair.
For an additional global C its full change is L^T C with the same entry rule.

To connect these arrays to the certificate interface of fact1252b8823bb5a290,
normalize smoothness to1 and x_star=g_star=f_star=0. Write
Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,
y_i=x_i-g_i, delta_i=f_i-||g_i||^2/2, and Gpre=(g_0,...,g_l).
Then y=e x0-L Gpre, x_n=-s x0+k^T y, and
Q_ij=delta_i-delta_j+<g_i,y_j-y_i>. The change of original coordinates is
invertible. Flow (5.4)--(5.5) cancels all sampled function values. Expanding,
using Pe-Ae=2s v+2Fz and q=s^2+eta E^2, gives the FULL identity

    q||x0||^2-2f_n+sum lambda_ij Q_ij
       =||g_n+s x0-v^T y||^2+y^T Knew y
                              +eta||z^T y-E x0||^2.        (5.7)

The initial cost q is paid once, and g_n remains a free formal gradient.
The right side is PSD. It is an upper certificate only if ALL lambda signs
also hold; no positivity claim about the polynomial substitutes for them.

## 6. Both global costs, with the new terms retained

For any original real column x let Gamma_x,ij=(x_i-x_j)^2. Row and column
sums (5.5), with both orientations included, give

    <Gamma_x,N>=(x^2)^T mu+2alpha^T(x^2)
                               -2(Lx)^T(P+A)x.          (6.1)

All Gamma entries are nonnegative and diagonal entries zero. Hence a valid
finite-sign array must have each such cost nonpositive. For x=t,w,

    T_t=(t^2)^T mu+2alpha^T(t^2)
                         -4ell^T(Knew t+Vv+eta Zz-alpha),
    T_w=(w^2)^T mu+2alpha^T(w^2)-4s v^T w-4F z^T w.       (6.2)

The second formula uses Lw=e and e^T(P+A)=2s v^T+2Fz^T.
A global neutral skew C changes neither cost: the remaining pairings are
ell^T Ct=0 and e^T Cw=0. A symmetric e,t-null detail also changes neither.
T_w has no K at all provided its moments and compatible A are maintained.
These are full-array equalities; symmetry of L Gamma_t or L Gamma_w is not
assumed.

### 6a. Exact occupation cancellation and the sign of T_w

Let Aprev_i=sum_(u<i)alpha_u and define the nonnegative actual tail remainder

    Ralpha=2pi sum h_i Aprev_i w_i^2
            +2pi sum(h_i-1)alpha_i w_i^2+2sum alpha_i w_i^2.

By (5.5), the first two terms of T_w are 2q Tquad+Ralpha. Moreover
zsrc^T w=E(1/a+2). Substituting (4.7) and the FROZEN gamma yields exactly
